title: Aligned coherent pair
summary: The complete positive-density pair action has an aligned coherent stationary set with an explicit ambient Hessian and finite-mode nonlinear orbital stability.
text: Summary: The complete positive-density pair action has an aligned coherent stationary set with an explicit ambient Hessian and finite-mode nonlinear orbital stability. Stationary branch of the common action Use the complete canonical component action and notation of coherent pair deformation: E=\frac\kappa2\int(|s_a|^2+|s_b|^2)^2d\nu_{\rm FS}, \quad \lambda_R=\frac{D_R^2}{D_{2R}}, \quad C=\frac{D_ND_M}{D_{N+M}}. This is a declared positive-density action in a mode fibre, with orthogonal bundle components and a specified kinetic metric. It is not the full scalar Dirac action or a physical spatial bound-state theorem. Coefficient indices add no physical spatial dimensions. For fixed positive norms J_a,J_b, choose the same unit ray z in both families. The complete equations admit \begin{aligned} a(t)&=\sqrt{J_a}e^{-i\omega_at}z^{\otimes N}, &\omega_a&=\kappa(\lambda_NJ_a+CJ_b),\\ b(t)&=\sqrt{J_b}e^{-i\omega_bt}z^{\otimes M}, &\omega_b&=\kappa(\lambda_MJ_b+CJ_a). \end{aligned} \tag{1} The self and cross gradients each point along the occupied tensor. Their independent carrier phases are allowed by the two norm symmetries. All transverse mode blocks Choose z=e_0 and rotate out the two frequencies in (1). Label an occupation by its transverse degree j. Define r_{N,j}=\frac{(N)_{\underline j}}{(2N)_{\underline j}}, \qquad p_j=\frac{(N)_{\underline j}}{(N+M)_{\underline j}}, \qquad q_j=\frac{(M)_{\underline j}}{(N+M)_{\underline j}}. For 1\le j\le\min(N,M), each transverse occupation carries the two-by-two complex-linear equation i\frac d{dt} \begin{pmatrix}\eta_{a,j}\\\eta_{b,j}\end{pmatrix} =\kappa\begin{pmatrix} J_a\lambda_N(2r_{N,j}-1)+J_bC(p_j-1) &C\sqrt{J_aJ_bp_jq_j}\\ C\sqrt{J_aJ_bp_jq_j} &J_b\lambda_M(2r_{M,j}-1)+J_aC(q_j-1) \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}\eta_{a,j}\\\eta_{b,j}\end{pmatrix}. \tag{2} For j present in only one family, keep its diagonal entry. The multiplicity of each transverse occupation block is \binom{j+d-1}{d-1}. Summing these multiplicities over each family recovers its entire band dimension. To derive (2), differentiate both factors of the density and retain both components' variations. The self blocks are the single-family Hessian. In the cross term, multiplication by the other coherent density gives the ratios p_j and q_j. The mixed derivative gives their geometric mean. Projected phase selection permits anomalous, conjugate-linear terms only in the two j=0 carrier components. No such terms are discarded in the transverse equation. At j=1, (2) reduces to \frac{\kappa C}{N+M} \begin{pmatrix} -J_bM&\sqrt{J_aJ_bNM}\\ \sqrt{J_aJ_bNM}&-J_aN \end{pmatrix}. \tag{3} Its eigenvalues are 0,\qquad -\frac{\kappa C(J_bM+J_aN)}{N+M}. \tag{4} The zero eigenvector (\sqrt{J_aN},\sqrt{J_bM}) rotates both coherent rays together. The other mode changes their relative orientation. For j\ge2, p_j+q_j<1. Thus the cross part of (2), divided by \kappa C, has negative trace and determinant J_aJ_b(1-p_j-q_j)>0. The self diagonal terms also have negative sign because r_{R,j}<1/2. All nonzero transverse frequencies are therefore real and have sign opposite to \kappa. The only transverse zero modes are the d common coherent rotations. The j=0 sector contains the two phase zero modes and carrier drifts caused by varying the conserved norms; fixed norms remove those radial changes. Nonlinear orbital stability in the full finite space Orthogonal symmetrization obeys I(a,b)=C\|T_{NM}(a\otimes b)\|^2\le CJ_aJ_b. \tag{5} Equality requires the product tensor to be fully symmetric. Swapping one index between the two normalized factors then gives \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\rho_a\widehat\rho_b)=1, where both contractions are positive with trace one. Equality forces both to be the same rank-one projector, hence a and b are coherent tensors on the same ray. The converse is immediate. Together with the sharp self bounds, this shows that the aligned set is exactly the global energy maximum at fixed norms for \kappa>0, and the global minimum for \kappa<0. The nonnegative deficit \mathcal D= \frac{\lambda_NJ_a^2+\lambda_MJ_b^2}{2}+CJ_aJ_b -\left[\frac{A(a)+B(b)}2+I(a,b)\right] \tag{6} vanishes precisely on that set. The product of the two fixed-norm spheres is compact. On any closed subset separated from the aligned set, (6) has a positive minimum. Conservation of both norms and the energy therefore proves nonlinear orbital stability of the entire aligned set for either nonzero sign of \kappa. This argument retains all ambient coefficients, including perturbations outside a prepared two-dimensional generating subspace. It supplies a finite-mode result stronger than the absence of growing linear modes. It remains separate from stability of physical spatial profiles, omitted bands and complete Dirac polarizations. Stability does not imply capture into alignment The conserved rotation moment is S=N\rho_a+M\rho_b. A pair of nonparallel coherent rays has a rank-two S, whereas an exactly aligned coherent pair has rank one. The former cannot evolve into the latter under these equations while preserving all its moments. The deformation calculation shows how contact can nevertheless increase: the patterns can depart from the coherent subset and retain their conserved moments in shape modes. An energy extremum alone does not justify an alignment or relaxation law. Physical time scales require the actual kinetic normalization, and a physical capture process requires its own allowed outgoing modes. Verification The normal-source contact calculation uses this aligned family at a large normal degree and derives its complete target operator limit. A separate fixed-norm bound there extends the energy-maximum argument to both scalar Dirac signs when the spatial kinetic operator is zero, retaining its explicitly finite mode scope. coherent_pair_variation_checks.py compares (2) against the complete differentiated action in all ambient occupation sectors, including the anomalous blocks and both stationary equations. Exact rational inequalities and combinatorial multiplicities cover large degrees without allocating their enormous matrices.

title: Coherent normal sources and the contact limit

A field realization of a narrow coherent source The coherent contact construction has the required simplex eigenvalue when a point current on the occupied mode ray is assumed. With \Delta=N_2-N_1, \delta_M=1- rac{D_{M+N_1}}{D_{M+N_2}} = rac{d\Delta}{M}+O(M^{-2}). 	ag{7} At depth six, the unchanged assignments are N_1=12, N_2=34, with target ratio 3515/17. A physical kinetic contribution or background-energy prescription would have to be calculated in the same master action before any cancellation or subtraction is used. The operator limit alone does not establish a finite-energy particle. There is also a separate retained self-term. At finite M, aligned target and normal fields with norms J,q have  egin{aligned} E_*&= rac g2\left[J^2\lambda_N+2JqC_{NM}+q^2\lambda_Might],\ \omega_N&=g(J\lambda_N+qC_{NM}),& \omega_M&=g(q\lambda_M+JC_{NM}),\ \lambda_L&=D_L^2/D_{2L},& C_{NM}&=D_ND_M/D_{N+M}. \end{aligned} 	ag{9} The rank-one limit makes C_{NM}	o D_N but does not remove J\lambda_N. Aligned coherent tensors with one common scalar sign attain (10), with arbitrary allowed spinor polarizations in that sign space. The complete scalar gradients preserve both occupied tensors and give (9). Opposite common scalar signs give the same energy maximum; no antiparticle interpretation is assigned to them. The equality conditions are common coherent coefficient direction and common scalar sign. On the finite product of the fixed-norm spheres, conservation of energy and both norms therefore gives nonlinear orbital stability of this entire maximizing set. This includes the scalar-sign and spinor variations in the declared zero-spatial-kinetic mode system. It establishes neither capture into that set nor stability of omitted spatial modes. In particular, it is not a finite-energy theorem for the singular M	o\infty limit. A general positive source has the same moment obstruction The finite coherent family is not the only possible normal preparation. Let ho\ge0 be any fixed integrable normal scalar ray density, and let t=|u^\dagger z|^2 relative to a coherent target. Its normalized source coefficient is c_N(z)=\intho(u)t^N\,d

u \ge rac{gc^2}{8\eta^d}, \qquad \eta=1-(1-2\delta)^{1/\Delta}.} 	ag{14} At fixed positive c and fixed coupling, this lower bound grows as \delta^{-d} when the family deficit tends to zero. Equation (14) is a bound on the positive scalar self-energy term; it does not assert that uncalculated terms in an arbitrary master action cannot contribute to the total energy. The exact minimum at two fixed moments can also be found in the enlarged class of all nonnegative square-integrable ray densities. Rotational averaging around z preserves the moments and decreases the quadratic norm, so an optimizer depends only on t. For moment ratios sufficiently close to one, it has the form  oxed{ho_*(t)=A\,t^{N_1}(t^\Delta-h)_+,} \qquad A>0,\quad 0<h<1. 	ag{14a} Here (x)_+=\max(x,0), and A,h are fixed by \intho_*t^{N_1}=c and \intho_*t^{N_2}=c(1-\delta). title: Coherent pair deformation
summary: A common positive-density quartic drives two coherent mode patterns into shape deformations, with reciprocal changes in contact fixed by conserved energy and rotation moments.
text:
Summary: A common positive-density quartic drives two coherent mode patterns into shape deformations, with reciprocal changes in contact fixed by conserved energy and rotation moments. The specified component action At a common projective mode fibre of dimension d, retain complete bands \mathcal H_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^{d+1}) and \mathcal H_M=\operatorname{Sym}^M(\mathbb C^{d+1}), with N,M\ge1. Set D_R= inom{R+d}{d} and use normalized coherent transforms s_a(u)=\sqrt{D_N}\langle u;N|aangle, \qquad s_b(u)=\sqrt{D_M}\langle u;M|bangle. Assume the two retained families are orthogonal bundle components of the same field, with the declared positive density ho=|s_a|^2+|s_b|^2 and canonical coefficient kinetic form. The action is S=\int dt\left[  rac i2(a^\dagger\dot a-\dot a^\dagger a +b^\dagger\dot b-\dot b^\dagger b) - rac\kappa2\intho^2d
u_{m FS}ight]. 	ag{1} The line bundles of degrees N and M need not be identified to add their Hermitian densities. Orthogonality and the kinetic metric are assumptions of this component action; spatial nesting alone supplies neither. A coherent scalar sum with interference is a different current. The positive density here is also different from the indefinite scalar Dirac bilinear  ar\Psi\Psi. This calculation retains all complex coefficients of its two families. It tests mode-pattern deformation in a specified action, rather than claiming a full particle-pair interaction on the physical base. The projective fibre adds no physical spatial dimensions. Different physical depths additionally require actual normal-bundle maps and spatial kinetic normalization. No independent field or mediator particle is introduced. A single symmetric product gives both reciprocal forces Let T_{NM}:\mathcal H_N\otimes\mathcal H_M	o\mathcal H_{N+M} orthogonally symmetrize every tensor index. In normalized occupations, T_{NM}(|\alphaangle\otimes| etaangle) =\sqrt{ rac{ inom N\alpha inom M eta} { inom{N+M}{\alpha+ eta}}}\,|\alpha+ etaangle. 	ag{2} The multi-index Vandermonde identity gives T_{NM}T_{NM}^\dagger=I. Define C_{NM}= rac{D_ND_M}{D_{N+M}},\qquad q=T_{NM}(a\otimes b),\qquad A_bh=T_{NM}(h\otimes b),\qquad B_ak=T_{NM}(a\otimes k). The cross-density overlap is exactly  oxed{I(a,b)=\int|s_a|^2|s_b|^2d
u_{m FS} =C_{NM}\|q\|^2.} 	ag{3} Its two derivatives are C_{NM}A_b^\dagger q and C_{NM}B_a^\dagger q. If F_N is the complete unit-coupling single-family quartic gradient, (1) gives  oxed{ i\dot a=\kappa igl(F_N(a)+C_{NM}A_b^\dagger q igr),\qquad i\dot b=\kappa igl(F_M(b)+C_{NM}B_a^\dagger q igr).} 	ag{4} Both responses, their relative coefficient and their self-interactions come from the same \kappa. No pair-specific force coefficient has been chosen. Independent component phases conserve J_a=\|a\|^2 and J_b=\|b\|^2. Coherent overlap and the missing shape directions For unit coherent preparations a=z^{\otimes N}, b=w^{\otimes M}, let 	au=|z^\dagger w|^2. Symmetrizing the two products gives the finite polynomial  oxed{I(z^{\otimes N},w^{\otimes M}) = rac{C_{NM}}{ inom{N+M}{N}} \sum_{j=0}^{\min(N,M)} inom Nj inom Mj	au^j.} 	ag{5} One derivation groups permutations by the number j of indices exchanged between the two tensor blocks. Those terms have overlap 	au^j and multiplicity  inom Nj inom Mj; their total number at 	au=1 is  inom{N+M}{N} by Vandermonde. Equation (5) is an overlap identity, not a proof that the coherent subset is dynamically invariant. The graph-ray benchmark demonstrates the constant-overlap precession obtained in a specified two-ray reduction. To test invariance, use common mode-frame covariance and component phases to set z=e_0 and w=ce_0+se_1, where c,s>0 and c^2+s^2=1. The component of the cross-gradient on |N-j,jangle is  egin{aligned} G_j={}& rac{D_ND_M\sqrt{ inom Nj}\,d!}{(N+M+d)!} \sum_{r=0}^{M-j} inom Mr inom M{r+j} c^{2M-2r-j}s^{2r+j}\ &\hspace{27mm}\cdot(N+M-r-j)!\,(r+j)!, \qquad 0\le j\le\min(N,M). \end{aligned} 	ag{6} Components with j>M vanish. Expanding the two powers of w in the projected current and using the FS monomial integral proves (6). Every summand is positive in the stated nonaligned preparation. In particular, G_2>0 whenever N,M\ge2. At a coherent tensor, its phase and norm occupy j=0, and its coherent ray tangents occupy j=1. Therefore the j=2 force lies outside that tangent space. The self-gradient contributes only the carrier direction, so it cannot cancel this force. The reciprocal calculation gives the same conclusion for the other pattern. Thus the coherent product manifold is not invariant for a generic nonaligned pair with N,M\ge2. A calculation that varies only the two rays discards genuine solutions of the retained coefficient equations. When \min(N,M)=1, the cross-force has only j=0,1 in either adapted frame. In that special case the coherent pair manifold is invariant. Aligned and orthogonal coherent preparations are also stationary rays. Changing contact follows from conservation Write A(a)=\int|s_a|^4, B(b)=\int|s_b|^4, and \lambda_R=D_R^2/D_{2R}. The single-family sharp bounds give A(a)\le\lambda_NJ_a^2, \qquad B(b)\le\lambda_MJ_b^2, with equality exactly for coherent tensors. Prepare both patterns coherently and evolve the complete equations (4), with \kappa
e0. Conservation of E=\kappa(A+B)/2+\kappa I then gives  oxed{I(t)-I(0) = rac{\lambda_NJ_a^2-A(a(t)) +\lambda_MJ_b^2-B(b(t))}{2}\ge0.} 	ag{7} Loss of individual coherence is balanced by increased cross-density contact. Equation (7) is an exact bound relative to this particular initial preparation. It does not say that I(t) increases monotonically. The first time derivative vanishes initially. Resolve the initial coefficient velocities into each coherent frame and let v_{a,j}, v_{b,j} denote the full vectors of degree-j transverse components. The complete single-family Hessian gives  oxed{I''(0)=2\sum_{j\ge2}\left[ \lambda_NJ_a(1-2r_{N,j})\|v_{a,j}\|^2 +\lambda_MJ_b(1-2r_{M,j})\|v_{b,j}\|^2ight],} 	ag{8} where r_{R,j}=(R)_{\underline j}/(2R)_{\underline j} and absent components are zero. Since 1-2r_{R,j}>0 for j\ge2, (6) makes (8) strictly positive for a generic nonaligned coherent pair. The actual velocities include \kappa, so this curvature is proportional to \kappa^2. Other preparations can evolve toward less contact. In the real occupation convention, the Hamiltonian obeys F( ar a, ar b)=\overline{F(a,b)}. Complex-conjugating a later state therefore initiates its reversed trajectory, along which the earlier contact increase becomes a decrease. This is a mathematical time-reversal test of (4); it assigns no physical meaning to antiparticles. Rotation moments give a second compatibility balance Let ho_a,ho_b be the positive one-index contractions of |aangle\langle a| and |bangle\langle b|, with traces J_a,J_b. title: Coherent quartic variation
summary: A smooth quartic action has exactly coherent extrema, an explicit complete mode Hessian and finite-mode orbital stability, with the smooth-contact frequency multiplier.
text:
Summary: A smooth quartic action has exactly coherent extrema, an explicit complete mode Hessian and finite-mode orbital stability, with the smooth-contact frequency multiplier. A specified action on the complete mode band The cumulative tangent-mode carrier at physical depth d is \mathcal H_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^{d+1}), \qquad D_N= inom{N+d}{d},\qquad N\ge1. Its generating space consists of d complexified spatial tangent directions and one homogenizing coefficient. Its projective ray space is an auxiliary mode fibre. It does not add physical spatial dimensions, or replace the actual electron spatial manifold by \mathbb{CP}^6. The self-contact module defines the physical base and mode fibre separately. At a fixed spatial base point, or after a separately specified spatial profile reduction, retain every coefficient c\in\mathcal H_N. For a unit generating vector u, write |u;Nangle=u^{\otimes N} and define the normalized coherent transform s_c([u])=\sqrt{D_N}\langle u;N|cangle, \qquad \int |s_c|^2\,d
u_{m FS}=\|c\|^2=J, 	ag{1} where the Fubini--Study measure has total volume one. The phase of this transform depends on the lift of [u]; its absolute square is well defined. Specify the canonical finite-mode action S_N[c]=\int dt\left[  rac i2(c^\dagger\dot c-\dot c^\dagger c)-E_N(c)ight], \qquad E_N(c)= rac{\kappa}{2}\int |s_c|^4\,d
u_{m FS}, \qquad \kappa\in\mathbb R. 	ag{2} The coefficient kinetic metric in (2) is part of this declared action. Equation (1) alone does not prove that a physical spatial Dirac reduction has this metric; its canonical normalization must be derived separately. No omitted spatial kinetic term or spinor component is silently identified with (2). Exact symmetric product formula Let T:\mathcal H_N\otimes\mathcal H_N	o\mathcal H_{2N} be orthogonal symmetrization of all 2N tensor indices, with the target identified with its symmetric subspace. It satisfies TT^\dagger=I and T^\dagger T=\Pi_{2N}, the projector onto that subspace. Put \lambda_N= rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}},\qquad Q(c)=T(c\otimes c),\qquad A_c h=T(h\otimes c). Applying the coherent resolution of identity at degree 2N gives  oxed{\int |s_c|^4\,d
u_{m FS} =\lambda_N\|Q(c)\|^2,\qquad i\dot c=\kappa\lambda_N A_c^\dagger Q(c).} 	ag{3} Indeed, the product of the two degree-N coherent transforms is (D_N/\sqrt{D_{2N}})s_{Q(c)}, and \delta Q=2A_c\delta c. Varying (2) with respect to \overline c produces the second identity, including its coefficient. It is the complete cubic vector field on \mathcal H_N, not its evaluation on a frozen ray. For an orthonormal occupation basis |\alphaangle, |\alpha|=N, the map can be computed without a tensor of four mode indices: T(|\alphaangle\otimes| etaangle) =t_{\alpha eta}|\alpha+ etaangle, \qquad t_{\alpha eta} =\sqrt{ rac{ inom N\alpha inom N eta} { inom{2N}{\alpha+ eta}}}. 	ag{4} The multi-index Vandermonde identity makes the sum of t_{\alpha eta}^2 at any fixed \alpha+ eta equal to one. This checks the coisometry normalization independently. Coherent states are precisely the sharp extrema Orthogonal projection cannot increase a norm. Consequently  oxed{\int|s_c|^4\,d
u_{m FS} \le\lambda_N\|c\|^4.} 	ag{5} For nonzero c, equality holds exactly when c is a coherent tensor, c=\sqrt J e^{i\phi}z^{\otimes N} with \|z\|=1. Here is a direct proof of the equality condition. Normalize c and suppose c\otimes c lies in the fully symmetric 2N-index subspace. Exchanging one index between the two copies then has expectation one. That expectation is \operatorname{tr}(ho_1^2), where ho_1 is the one-index contraction of |cangle\langle c|. Since ho_1 is positive with trace one, it must have rank one. A tensor with a pure one-index contraction factors across that index; symmetry forces all remaining indices to carry the same vector. The converse follows immediately from z^{\otimes N}\otimes z^{\otimes N}=z^{\otimes2N}. For N=1 every vector is already coherent. This is the fourth-moment instance of coherent-state concentration. The broader convex-function inequality is due to Lieb and Solovej, with equality and quantitative results developed by Nicola, Riccardi and Tilli. The elementary projector proof above supplies the particular result needed for the action without an entropy argument. At fixed J, the coherent orbit is therefore the complete set of global energy maxima for \kappa>0, and global minima for \kappa<0. This is variational selection in the specified finite coefficient space; it does not establish the preferred sign of a physical scalar interaction. Exact coherent branch and nonlinear frequency For c_0=\sqrt J z^{\otimes N}, (3) gives  oxed{c(t)=e^{-i\Omega_N t}c_0,\qquad \Omega_N=\kappa J\lambda_N =\kappa J rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}.} 	ag{6} Every coefficient equation is satisfied. The ray [z] is stationary and only its common phase evolves. Coherence therefore supplies an exact stationary branch of the smooth action, without replacing its spectrum by that of a point insertion. The norm J is conserved by the phase symmetry. All mode-frame rotation moments are also conserved. In tensor notation, ho_1= rac1N igl(\langle c,a_j^\dagger a_i cangle igr)_{ij}, \qquad \operatorname{tr}ho_1=J, \qquad \dotho_1=0. 	ag{7} The operators a_j^\dagger a_i act on the symmetric occupation indices. Equation (7) follows from the U(d+1) invariance of (2). This mode-fibre symmetry is an assumption of the isotropic completion, not an additional set of physical spatial rotations. In particular, conservative evolution does not generally capture an arbitrary pattern into a coherent minimum: its energy and the one-index contraction are fixed. Complete perturbation equation Choose z=e_0 by mode-frame covariance and use a frame rotating with \Omega_N. For c=e^{-i\Omega_Nt}(c_0+\eta), define the normalized Toeplitz eigenvalue ratio r_j= rac{N(N-1)\cdots(N-j+1)} {2N(2N-1)\cdots(2N-j+1)},\qquad r_0=1, \qquad 0\le j\le N. 	ag{8} Here j counts occupations outside coordinate zero. Its complex multiplicity is  inom{j+d-1}{d-1}. The full linearized equation is  oxed{  egin{aligned} i\dot\eta_0&=\kappa J\lambda_N(\eta_0+\overline\eta_0),\ i\dot\eta_j&=\kappa J\lambda_N(2r_j-1)\eta_j, \qquad 1\le j\le N. \end{aligned}} 	ag{9} To obtain it directly, write V for multiplication by |s_{c_0}|^2 followed by projection. Its eigenvalue in sector j is J\lambda_Nr_j, as follows from the exact FS monomial integral. The variation of |s|^2s has both terms \delta(|s|^2s)=2|s|^2\delta s+s^2\delta\overline s. The second term has a nonzero projected matrix entry only when the two occupation multi-indices sum to 2Ne_0, so only the radial entry survives. Subtracting the rotating-frame frequency gives (9). Dropping this conjugate term would give an incorrect radial equation. Since r_1=1/2, the d complex tangent directions to the coherent ray are zero modes. For j\ge2, 0<r_j<1/2, and all remaining frequencies are real and have the same sign opposite to \kappa. When N\ge2, the smallest nonzero absolute frequency is |\Omega_{m transverse,min}| =|\kappa|J\lambda_N rac{N}{2N-1}. 	ag{10} The radial equation contains the phase zero mode and the phase drift caused by changing the conserved norm. On a fixed-norm space modulo phase this does not supply an exponentially growing perturbation. Finite-mode nonlinear orbital stability At fixed nonzero J, the state sphere is compact. For N\ge2 the nonnegative deficit \mathcal D(c)=\lambda_NJ^2-\int|s_c|^4\,d
u_{m FS} vanishes exactly on the compact coherent orbit. It has a strictly positive minimum on every closed subset a positive distance from that orbit. Norm and energy conservation therefore imply nonlinear orbital stability of the coherent set under (3), for either nonzero sign of \kappa. The polynomial vector field exists globally because the norm remains bounded. This argument supplies finite-mode nonlinear stability, rather than inferring it solely from real linearized frequencies. The conclusion concerns the whole coherent set, including phase and ray rotations. It is not attraction to one prepared ray. Physical spatial variation, omitted bands, Dirac components, nuclear sources and additional interaction terms require their own stability analysis. Consequence for the mass construction For unit coefficient norm and a band-independent \kappa, the derived frequency multiplier is D_N^2/D_{2N}. The occupied point-contact multiplier is D_N. Their ratio is  rac{\lambda_N}{D_N} = rac{D_N}{D_{2N}} =\prod_{r=1}^d rac{N+r}{2N+r}, which depends on N and tends to 2^{-d} for large N at fixed d. At the specified electron and muon bands (12,34) in depth six, (6) gives the smooth-action ratio 137.029686760779, while the point count gives 206.764705882353. These are the distinct prescriptions compared in the contact-kernel audit. Thus coherent extrema and finite-mode stability can be established for a specific action while its mass-sequence multiplier remains different. Converting (6) into a physical rest mass additionally requires the spatial Dirac equation, its normalized profile and the identification of its pole. The homogeneous coherent action uses a normalized square root of the quartic current integral to obtain the occupied coefficient D_N. Its full variation has a different response, with a cancellation of the radial conjugate term. It supplies exact nonconstant spatial solutions for the specified independent bundle, while the changed functional and its normalization require a master origin. This does not alter the quartic action's result (6). Reciprocal extension The complete pair action retains both full mode families. A generic pair leaves the coherent subset, and conservation relates its shape deformation to changing density contact. The aligned stationary set has a separate complete stability calculation. Verification and related The current projection identity now expresses this same smooth quartic as an exact weighted sum of all reduced tensor-current purities. It identifies the coefficients supplied by the projection, including signed full-spinor currents and different grades. This gives a direct operator comparison with the shell-weighted self-mass action, rather than inferring that action from the coherent count alone. coherent_contact_variation_checks.py checks independent FS quadrature, the full nonlinear gradient and both Hessian blocks, symmetric-product normalization, the coherent stationary equation, all perturbation sectors and complete finite-mode evolution. Exact rational formulas also cover large bands without allocating their matrices. The supporting algebra is in coherent_mode_algebra.py. Canonical coupling normalization — specifies the physical kinetic metric needed before interpreting the coefficient frequency. Bilateral polarization coupling — separates conservative orientation evolution from encounter-driven changes in compatibility.

title: Consistent band contacts
summary: A fixed bare kernel must have compatible cumulative compressions, while coherent projective contact changes under the standard band inclusion and effective kernels obey a different Schur consistency law.
text: Summary: A fixed bare kernel must have compatible cumulative compressions, while coherent projective contact changes under the standard band inclusion and effective kernels obey a different Schur consistency law. What a common bare operator requires At fixed spatial depth d, let \mathcal B_N=\bigoplus_{k=0}^N\operatorname{Sym}^k\mathbb C^d with normalized oscillator occupations |\alpha\rangle, |\alpha|\le N. Let I_N:\mathcal B_N\hookrightarrow\mathcal B_{N+1} preserve each existing occupation. These are mode labels on the same specified spatial sector, not additional physical dimensions. If a fixed bare operator or quadratic form A is defined on the union of these spaces, its compressions A_N=P_NAP_N satisfy \boxed{I_N^\dagger A_{N+1}I_N=A_N.} \tag{1} This follows by testing the two forms on any pair of vectors already in \mathcal B_N. Conversely, a Hermitian family satisfying (1) defines a unique form on finite occupation sums. Boundedness, closability and an infinite-space operator domain require additional control; finite consistency alone does not establish them. The spatial point form at a fixed position and width satisfies (1): its matrix entries \overline{h_\alpha(X)}h_\beta(X) remain the same when more modes are admitted. Its growing nonzero eigenvalue is consistent with an unchanged lower matrix block. Test the normalized homogenized coherent family Identify \mathcal B_N with \operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C^d) using normalized occupation states. For a fixed unit vector z=(z_0,z_1,\ldots,z_d), the coherent coefficients are (v_N(z))_\alpha= \sqrt{\frac{N!}{(N-k)!\,\alpha!}}\, z_0^{N-k}z_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots z_d^{\alpha_d}, \qquad k=|\alpha|\le N. \tag{2} The standard cumulative inclusion adds one unused, or zeroth, occupation. Direct comparison of (2) at two consecutive bands gives I_N^\dagger v_{N+1}(z)=z_0 C_Nv_N(z), \qquad (C_N)_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{N+1}{N+1-k}}. \tag{3} For \Lambda_N(z)=D_N|v_N(z)\rangle\langle v_N(z)| and D_N=\binom{N+d}{d}, the resulting compression is \boxed{I_N^\dagger\Lambda_{N+1}(z)I_N =D_{N+1}|z_0|^2C_N|v_N(z)\rangle\langle v_N(z)|C_N.} \tag{4} It is generally different from \Lambda_N(z). At z=e_0, the same ground matrix entry is D_{N+1} on the left and D_N on the right. For N\ge1 and a ray with nonzero z_0 and a nonzero transverse coordinate, C_N changes the relative ground and degree-one amplitudes, so even the compressed rank-one direction changes. A scalar rescaling alone cannot repair that directional difference. At z_0=0, the left side vanishes completely. Consequently, the projective point-contact family is not the sequence of compressions of one fixed linear form under this fixed-ray, normalized cumulative identification. Each individual projective contact theorem remains exact. The family uses a different homogeneous line bundle and evaluation map at each N. This is a test of a particular proposed operator bridge. If N labels different physical branches rather than a common cutoff, if the master operator depends on the full field, or if the spatial embedding and kinetic metric depend on N, their actual relations must replace (1). Such data cannot be inferred from equality of dimensions alone. Effective operators have Schur consistency Compression and effective reduction are different operations. Let D(\zeta)=A-\zeta I in a finite complete mode space, and split retained modes P_N from the complement Q_N. When the indicated inverses exist, eliminating the complement gives F_N(\zeta)=D_{NN}-D_{NQ}D_{QQ}^{-1}D_{QN}, \qquad \boxed{F_N(\zeta)^{-1}=P_ND(\zeta)^{-1}P_N.} \tag{5} The identity follows by solving the complementary block equation and substituting it into the retained equation. Hence it is the inverse effective operator that has the compression relation I_N^\dagger F_{N+1}(\zeta)^{-1}I_N=F_N(\zeta)^{-1}. \tag{6} Equivalently, taking a Schur complement through an intermediate band gives the same result as direct elimination. For a positive static Hessian, the eliminated block also fixes the sign of the correction: F_N=D_{NN}-B D_{QQ}^{-1}B^\dagger\le D_{NN}. Thus failure of (1) is not by itself a failure of an effective master reduction. A proposed effective family must instead supply the complementary modes, its frequency dependence and the consistency in (5)–(6). These are modes of the same field \Psi_\infty; no mediator particles have been introduced. The common field response also tracks its kinetic normalization and retarded boundary conditions. A controlled local limit of the coherent evaluation map There is a useful mathematical connection to an ordinary bosonic coherent coefficient sequence. In the affine chart set z=\frac{(1,a/\sqrt N)}{\sqrt{1+|a|^2/N}},\qquad a\in\mathbb C^d. For fixed occupation \alpha of degree k, (2) becomes (v_N)_\alpha= \sqrt{\frac{N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1)}{N^k}} \left(1+\frac{|a|^2}{N}\right)^{-N/2} \frac{a^\alpha}{\sqrt{\alpha!}} \longrightarrow e^{-|a|^2/2}\frac{a^\alpha}{\sqrt{\alpha!}}. \tag{7} The measure must transform as well. Unit-volume FS measure in this chart is d\nu_{\rm FS}= \frac{d!}{\pi^dN^d}\left(1+\frac{|a|^2}{N}\right)^{-d-1} d^{2d}a. Since D_Nd!/N^d=\prod_{j=1}^d(1+j/N), its contact measure satisfies \boxed{D_Nd\nu_{\rm FS}\longrightarrow\pi^{-d}d^{2d}a} \tag{8} at fixed a. The coherent operator density then has a finite limit per unit a volume. Equations (7)–(8) are a local large-band limit, not an exact finite-band identification. The coordinates a describe mode amplitudes; they do not replace any physical spatial dimensions. Changing the measure in an action also transforms its delta functions and source coefficients. A normalization factor cannot simply be discarded while holding those other ingredients fixed. Finite ray resolution separately quantifies how a specified smooth symbol approaches point contact at fixed N. Verification coherent_kernel_consistency_checks.py checks (3)–(4) in every retained occupation, fixed spatial point compression, direct and staged complex Schur elimination, compressed resolvents and the coefficient/measure limits in (7)–(8).

title: Contact-kernel audit
summary: Point-contact and smooth-density spectra are compared without identifying their operators.
text:
Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Point-contact and smooth-density spectra are compared without identifying their operators. NOT A PHYSICS MODULE. These are exact finite-band comparison calculations and an action-level audit. The graph-supported point-contact construction remains a live hypothesis; no alternative tested here is silently substituted for it. 1. The source distinction that motivated the test The self-contact source, Section 6.2, explicitly lifts the scalar current onto the graph of a chosen projective ray: \mathcal J_d(q,[u])=J_d(q)\delta_{m FS}([u],[z_{\Psi_d}(q)]), \qquad J_d= ar\Psi_d\Psi_d. It then writes the scalar interaction \mathcal L_{m sc}=-(\kappa_d/2)J_d^2, whose scalar Euler--Lagrange term is -\kappa_dJ_d\Psi_d. Its diagonal kernel is local multiplication. Later in the same subsection, the self-field insertion is identified with a delta concentrated at the selected ray. Section 6.3 proves the finite-band projection theorem for that point insertion, and Section 6.4 applies it to the proposed nonlinear Dirac term. The distinction is important: a kernel f(u)\delta(u,u') specifies multiplication by f, whereas a coefficient f(u)=\delta(u,z) specifies a point-supported multiplier. Locality of the diagonal kernel alone does not choose that coefficient. The graph lift is explicitly an additional part of the written construction; it must neither be ignored nor mistaken for an already completed derivation of the action's projected dynamics. Merely integrating J(q)^2 against the normalized graph delta returns J(q)^2. It does not automatically insert a new finite-band pairing kernel into the action. Establishing that pairing is the remaining dynamical step identified by this audit, not a request for an amplitude measurement. 2. The exact point-contact theorem survives For \mathcal H_N=H^0(\mathbb{CP}^d,\mathcal O(N)), \qquad D_N= inom{N+d}{d}, use unit Fubini-Study measure and the specified homogeneous Hermitian normalization. The reproducing kernel has constant diagonal K_N(z,z)=D_N. Its normalized coherent line is |z;Nangle=K_{N,z}/\sqrt{D_N}. The point-symbol quadratic form is \langle s,T_{\delta_z}tangle=\overline{s(z)}t(z). It gives T_{\delta_z}=P_N\delta_zP_N =|K_{N,z}angle\langle K_{N,z}| =D_N|z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Its nonzero eigenvalue is exactly D_N. This result depends on the stated ray, finite band, measure, and covariance assumptions. It is not the claim that every algebraic scalar interaction has this spectrum. The source itself makes isotropic projective completion a necessary premise and separately requires a band-blind normalized coefficient; see Sections 6.3--6.4 and 9. 3. Three different local multiplier prescriptions In the same finite Hilbert space, compare the following unit-normalized symbols: Symbol on the ray space Projected operator spectrum Constant 1 Eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity D_N Point source \delta_z Eigenvalue D_N once, otherwise zero Smooth coherent density j_z(u)=D_N|\langle u,zangle|^{2N} Full positive spectrum below, with largest eigenvalue D_N^2/D_{2N} All three have projected trace D_N. Equal trace therefore does not imply equal spectrum. The smooth case has rank D_N, whereas the point case has rank one. These are different operators, not alternative normalizations of the same eigenvector. The smooth symbol is normalized because \int_{\mathbb{CP}^d}|\langle u,zangle|^{2N}d
u(u)= rac{1}{D_N}. It is a comparison prescription: the source graph lift selects a point symbol, not automatically this smooth density. 4. Full smooth-symbol spectrum Choose z along coordinate zero. On normalized degree-N monomials, let k be the occupation of that coordinate. The remaining d occupations sum to N-k. Unit-FS monomial moments obey \int \prod_{r=0}^{d}|u_r|^{2m_r}d
u(u) = rac{d!\prod_rm_r!}{(d+\sum_rm_r)!}. The normalized monomial of multi-index \alpha, |\alpha|=N, has squared normalization (N+d)!/(d!\prod_r\alpha_r!). Multiplication by D_N|u_0|^{2N} therefore gives the diagonal eigenvalue  oxed{\lambda_k =D_N rac{(N+d)!}{(2N+d)!} rac{(N+k)!}{k!}}, \qquad 0\le k\le N, with multiplicity  oxed{m_k= inom{N-k+d-1}{d-1}}. Phase invariance makes the off-diagonal monomial integrals vanish. The largest eigenvalue occurs at k=N and simplifies to  oxed{\lambda_{\max}= rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}}. The checks verify positivity, \sum_km_k=D_N, and \sum_km_k\lambda_k=D_N for the tested bands, using exact rational arithmetic. They do not require constructing the largest matrices explicitly. N,d D_N Smooth largest eigenvalue Smooth largest eigenvalue divided by D_N 1,1 2 4/3 2/3 2,2 6 12/5 2/5 3,3 20 100/21 5/21 2,4 15 45/14 3/14 12,6 18564 580.391724138 0.0312643678161 34,6 3838380 79530.8961572 0.0207199120872 For example, at (N,d)=(3,3) the complete spectrum is 5/21, 20/21, 50/21, 100/21, with multiplicities 10,6,3,1, respectively. 5. A same-sector shape test, not a scale fit Using the already specified electron and muon bands, N_e=12, N_\mu=34, d=6, a common band-independent coefficient cancels in either prescription. The point prescription gives  rac{D_{34}}{D_{12}}= rac{3515}{17} \approx206.764705882353. The smooth-symbol occupied-line prescription gives  rac{D_{34}^2/D_{68}}{D_{12}^2/D_{24}} = rac{9441729375}{68902802} \approx137.029686760779. These are calculated spectral ratios under two different prescriptions, not new experimental measurements. An overall electron unit conversion cannot make the prescriptions identical. This demonstrates the importance of the operator choice. It does not disprove the graph-supported point construction by imposing the smooth construction in its place. No experimental precision or significance claim is made in this note. 6. Single contact evaluation versus double smearing The finite-band coherent pairing kernel is B_N(z,w)=\langle z;N|T_{\delta_w}|z;Nangle =D_N|\langle z,wangle|^{2N}. It satisfies \int B_N(z,w)d
u(w)=1, \qquad B_N(z,z)=D_N. A point source evaluated at its own ray uses the coincident value of this one kernel. Replacing the source by its smooth coherent density and averaging the test coherent density against it instead gives \int B_N(z,w)^2d
u(w)= rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}. This is the previously undocumented explanation of the two eigenvalues. A graph-source interaction with one such finite-band pairing can retain the linear simplex count; two smoothings yield a different quantity. Neither operation may be silently substituted for the other. What remains open is the action-level origin and ordering of the pairing: the proposed graph current, the nonlinear variation, and the finite-band projection have to be joined in one specified construction. The test establishes a consistent mathematical distinction, not that the full master action has already supplied this joining. 7. Moving self-consistent ray: the limited cancellation that is exact Differentiate P^2=P for a differentiable orthogonal projector: (\delta P)P+P(\delta P)=\delta P. Multiplying by P on both sides gives  oxed{P(\delta P)P=0.} For a normalized u on the occupied line, \langle u,\delta P\,uangle=0. This was checked with a complex ray u=(3/5,4i/5)^T and a Hermitian generator of projector motion. It removes the automatic objection that every change of the self-consistent ray must shift the occupied eigenvalue at first order. It does not imply (\delta P)u=0, erase off-diagonal variations, or prove the full nonlinear Euler--Lagrange equation. In particular, derivative dependence of the ray, variation of the contact coefficient, kinetic contributions, and stability of the coherent branch remain separate questions. No claim of complete variational closure follows from the diagonal projector identity. 8. Findings to carry forward Graph contact variation supplies a defined measure-pairing action with one finite-band kernel. Its self-contraction retains D_N, while its full ray-dependent variation cancels self-orientation stiffness. The remaining scalar coefficient still needs a normalized spatial solution before it can be interpreted as a rest mass. Coherent quartic variation gives the complete action-level calculation for the smooth prescription. Coherent tensors are its sharp fourth-moment extrema, and its full conjugate-linear Hessian and finite-mode orbital stability can be derived. Its nonlinear frequency still contains D_N^2/D_{2N}. Thus the existence of a coherent stationary branch does not by itself select the point-contact mass sequence. Checked: the point-contact identity; the constant, point, and smooth comparison spectra; the exact smooth-symbol family ratio; normalization and coincidence of the single pairing kernel; its squared-kernel integral; and the diagonal moving-projector cancellation. Not established: that ordinary diagonal locality alone forces the graph symbol; that the graph lift by itself supplies the required action pairing; that double smearing is the correct V2 prescription; that the chosen coherent branch solves and is selected by the full projected dynamics; or that these calculations determine a baryon frequency. No current magnitude, field amplitude, or profile parameter was fitted. The unknowns are operator identification and the derivation or cancellation of their physical coefficients. The regression script reproduces the finite tests; the source passages are self-contact Sections 6.1--6.4 and 9. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and correction guidance. Band consistency and finite resolution Consistent band contacts tests how the coherent family changes under the specified cumulative oscillator inclusion. A fixed bare kernel has one compatibility law; an effective kernel obtained by eliminating same-field modes has a different Schur consistency law. Finite ray resolution independently varies the symbol width and retained band, giving the complete spectrum and an exact operator-norm error relative to the point contact.

title: Finite ray resolution
summary: A normalized coherent symbol of specified finite width has an exact full Toeplitz spectrum and a controlled point-contact error, with distinct fixed-width and fixed-band limits.
text: Summary: A normalized coherent symbol of specified finite width has an exact full Toeplitz spectrum and a controlled point-contact error, with distinct fixed-width and fixed-band limits. Specify a width independently of the retained band On the auxiliary mode-ray space \mathbb{CP}^d, use unit FS measure, \mathcal H_N=H^0(\mathbb{CP}^d,\mathcal O(N)) and D_N=\binom{N+d}{d}. These are the mode fibres of the projective contact comparison, not additional physical spatial dimensions. For a specified ray z and integer p\ge0, define the positive symbol f_{p,z}(u)=D_p|u^\dagger z|^{2p},\qquad \int f_{p,z}d\nu=1, \qquad T_{N,p}=P_N f_{p,z}P_N. \tag{1} Here p fixes the source width independently of the band N. p=0 is uniform; increasing p concentrates the source about z. It is a prescribed comparison symbol. Its width and source variation would need to follow from the master action in a physical application. Exact full spectrum Choose z=e_0. Phase integration makes T_{N,p} diagonal on normalized monomials. If their zeroth occupation is k, the FS moments are \int\prod_{r=0}^{d}|u_r|^{2m_r}d\nu =\frac{d!\prod_r m_r!}{(d+\sum_r m_r)!}. These follow from iterated Euler beta integrals on the unit simplex. Substitution into (1) gives \boxed{\lambda_k(N,p) =D_p\frac{(N+d)!}{(N+p+d)!}\frac{(p+k)!}{k!}, \qquad m_k=\binom{N-k+d-1}{d-1}.} \tag{2} For p>0 these eigenvalues increase with k. In particular, \boxed{\lambda_{\rm top}(N,p)=\frac{D_ND_p}{D_{N+p}}, \qquad \frac{\lambda_{N-j}}{\lambda_{\rm top}} =\frac{N(N-1)\cdots(N-j+1)} {(N+p)(N+p-1)\cdots(N+p-j+1)}.} \tag{3} Every eigenvalue is positive at finite p, and \sum_k m_k\lambda_k=D_N. At p=0, (2) gives the identity operator. At p=N, (3) reproduces the smooth coherent-density coefficient D_N^2/D_{2N} used in the complete quartic action. Exact distance from point contact At fixed N\ge1, p\to\infty gives T_{N,p}\to D_N|z;N\rangle\langle z;N|. The coherent line is its top eigenvector for every p. The sum of all complementary eigenvalues is D_N-\lambda_{\rm top}, so no complementary eigenvalue exceeds that deficit. Therefore \boxed{\frac{\|T_{N,p}-D_N|z;N\rangle\langle z;N|\|}{D_N} =\varepsilon_{N,p} =1-\frac{D_p}{D_{N+p}} =1-\prod_{i=1}^d\frac{p+i}{p+N+i}.} \tag{4} Writing each factor as 1-N/(p+N+i), the product bound \prod(1-a_i)\ge1-\sum a_i and 1-a_i\le e^{-a_i} give \boxed{1-\exp\left[-\frac{dN}{p+N+d}\right] \le\varepsilon_{N,p}\le\frac{dN}{p+N+1}.} \tag{5} The upper bound may exceed one; (4) gives the exact value. These formulas state quantitatively how narrow a specified symbol must be for the point operator to be a useful approximation. For two bands N_2>N_1 with the same p, \frac{\lambda_{\rm top}(N_2,p)}{\lambda_{\rm top}(N_1,p)} =\frac{D_{N_2}}{D_{N_1}} \prod_{i=1}^d\frac{p+N_1+i}{p+N_2+i}. \tag{6} Its relative correction to the point-contact ratio is independent of an overall common scale and remains nonzero at every finite p. This is an operator comparison; extracting particle frequencies still requires the complete normalized spatial field equation. Limits with different physical inputs At fixed p and N\to\infty, \lambda_{\rm top}(N,p)\to D_p=\|f_{p,z}\|_\infty. It stays bounded while D_N grows. More generally, \|P_N fP_N\|\le\|f\|_\infty for any fixed bounded multiplier. A bounded symbol of fixed amplitude and width cannot produce an unbounded simplex eigenvalue merely by increasing the cutoff. If instead p/N\to a>0, then \frac{\lambda_{\rm top}(N,p)}{D_N} \longrightarrow\left(\frac a{1+a}\right)^d. \tag{7} The leading simplex power can therefore coexist with a shrinking source width, but (7) is asymptotic. It does not make the finite-band coefficient exactly independent of N. A prescribed N-dependent width must be explained by the same action and normalization as the other field data. There is also an exact extremal statement. For any positive unit measure \mu on the ray space, define T_\mu=D_N\int|u;N\rangle\langle u;N|\,d\mu(u). Then \|T_\mu\|\le D_N. Equality for a normalized vector v requires |\langle v,u;N\rangle|=1 for \mu-almost every u. For N\ge1, distinct projective rays give distinct coherent lines; thus equality holds exactly when \mu is a point measure. This statement uses the positive unit-measure convention. Signed symbols, different total source strength or additional operator terms change its hypotheses. Consistent band contacts addresses the separate requirement that a proposed family arise from one common bare operator or a specified effective reduction. Verification coherent_kernel_consistency_checks.py checks (2) by independent beta quadrature and complete CP1 matrices, the exact trace and full error spectrum, both bounds in (5), finite band ratios, and the distinct limits in (3) and (7).

title: Graph contact variation
summary: A defined graph-measure pairing retains the simplex coefficient, but its full self-variation cancels ray stiffness and does not select a coherent pattern.
text: Summary: A defined graph-measure pairing retains the simplex coefficient, but its full self-variation cancels ray stiffness and does not select a coherent pattern. A well-defined graph pairing At a point of the physical spatial manifold Q_d, use the homogenized mode carrier \mathcal H_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^{d+1}), D_N=\binom{N+d}{d}, with normalized coherent vectors |z;N\rangle. The projective mode fibre describes oscillator-symbol data; it adds no physical spatial dimensions. The physical base and fibre are distinguished in the self-contact module. Write P_z=|z;N\rangle\langle z;N| and define the single pairing kernel B_N(z,w)=D_N\operatorname{tr}(P_zP_w) =D_N|z^\dagger w|^{2N},\qquad \int B_N(z,w)d\nu_{\rm FS}(w)=1. \tag{1} For a real scalar current J(q) and a specified field-dependent ray z_\Psi(q), the finite signed measure \mu_q=J(q)\delta_{[z_\Psi(q)]} is well defined. A candidate interaction is E_{\rm graph} =\frac\kappa2\int_{Q_d} \int\!\int B_N(u,v)d\mu_q(u)d\mu_q(v)\,d\mu_{Q_d}(q). \tag{2} Equation (2) pairs two measures against a smooth finite-band kernel. It never multiplies two delta distributions at the same integration variable. The kernel family, its normalization and this pairing are specified additions to the action; ordinary locality of J^2 does not derive them. This supplies a precise candidate completion of the graph-contact construction. Exact total variation of one occupied graph The coincident value B_N(z,z)=D_N is constant. Therefore (2) is exactly \boxed{E_{\rm graph} =\frac{\kappa D_N}{2}\int_{Q_d}J(q)^2d\mu_{Q_d}(q).} \tag{3} Every variation of the ray cancels before any field equation is imposed. This remains true if z_\Psi depends on derivatives of the physical field, provided it is a well-defined differentiable ray along the variation. The residual variation comes from J, the physical measure and any additional action terms. On a fixed physical geometry, \delta E_{\rm graph}=\kappa D_N\int J\,\delta J\,d\mu_{Q_d}. \tag{4} For J=\bar\Psi\Psi, an interaction Lagrangian equal to minus (3) contributes -\kappa D_NJ\Psi to the Euler--Lagrange equation obtained by varying \bar\Psi. In Hamiltonian form its contribution is \kappa D_N(\Psi^\dagger\beta\Psi)\beta\Psi. The simplex factor survives as a nonlinear scalar coupling coefficient. A normalized stationary spatial profile, its kinetic contribution and its frequency must still be solved; (3) does not identify that frequency with a rest mass proportional to D_N. Why the apparent self-orientation stiffness cancels Hold J fixed and let P(\theta) be a moving coherent projector. At one physical point, (2) is \kappa D_NJ^2\operatorname{tr}(P^2)/2. Its second derivative is \frac{d^2E}{d\theta^2} =\kappa D_NJ^2\left[ \operatorname{tr}\bigl((P')^2\bigr) +\operatorname{tr}(PP'')\right]=0. \tag{5} For the unit generating curve z(\theta)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,0,\ldots), at zero, \begin{aligned} |z;N\rangle'&=\sqrt N\,|N-1,1\rangle,\\ |z;N\rangle''&=-N|N,0\rangle +\sqrt{2N(N-1)}\,|N-2,2\rangle. \end{aligned} The last term is absent for N=1. Substitution gives \operatorname{tr}((P')^2)=2N, \qquad \operatorname{tr}(PP'')=-2N. \tag{6} The positive source-Gram contribution and the curvature of the moving source cancel exactly. Keeping only the first term in (5) would supply an artificial self-orientation stiffness. The weaker identity P(\delta P)P=0 already removes a diagonal first variation; (5) accounts for both terms at second order. Occupied frequency does not determine the response operator For a finite coefficient illustration only, choose J=c^\dagger c and the canonical time-kinetic term. Equation (3) becomes E(c)=\frac{\kappa D_N}{2}(c^\dagger c)^2, \qquad i\dot c=\kappa D_N(c^\dagger c)c. \tag{7} Every coefficient pattern rotates by the same phase at a fixed norm. Every projective direction is stationary. In particular, this action does not distinguish the coherent tensors from other vectors in \mathcal H_N. The complete derivative of the right-hand side is \delta F=A\eta+B\bar\eta,\qquad A=\kappa D_N(JI+cc^\dagger),\qquad B=\kappa D_Ncc^{\mathsf T}. \tag{8} After subtracting the carrier frequency \Omega=\kappa D_NJ, all directions orthogonal to c have zero frequency. By contrast, freezing the rank-one matrix \kappa D_Ncc^\dagger would give the same occupied frequency but a transverse rotating-frame frequency -\Omega. When that matrix depends on the evolving c, its derivative restores exactly (8). Its instantaneous rank does not determine the nonlinear response spectrum. Here the arbitrary coefficient ray [c]\in\mathbb P(\mathcal H_N) must not be confused with the smaller coherent subset [z^{\otimes N}]. Nor is the positive coefficient norm in (7) a replacement for the scalar Dirac current used in (4). For another distinct prescription, fix z and vary E=\kappa|s_c(z)|^4/2, where s_c(z)=\sqrt{D_N}\langle z;N|c\rangle. On c=\sqrt J|z;N\rangle, its frequency is \kappa D_N^2J. This quartic evaluated density is different from the graph current J\delta_z in (2). The number of evaluations matters. The smooth quartic action, in contrast, has nonzero restoring frequencies for departures from the coherent set. Its occupied multiplier is D_N^2/D_{2N}. Matching one occupied eigenvalue is therefore insufficient to identify either action's complete response or its pattern-selection properties. Two graph rays retain a reciprocal orientation interaction At one common mode fibre, replace the single measure by \mu=J_a\delta_{z_a}+J_b\delta_{z_b}. For fixed positive coefficient norms J_a,J_b, (2) gives E=\frac{\kappa D_N}{2} \left[J_a^2+J_b^2+2J_aJ_b\tau^N\right], \qquad \tau=|z_a^\dagger z_b|^2. \tag{9} There is a cross-ray force although the isolated self-ray force vanishes. To make its time evolution explicit, restrict both degree-N coefficient patterns to coherent tensors and pull back their canonical kinetic form. The two ray symplectic weights are NJ_a and NJ_b. In a horizontal phase gauge, with s=z_a^\dagger z_b, the equations are \begin{aligned} i\dot z_a&=\kappa D_NJ_b\tau^{N-1}\bar s\,(z_b-sz_a),\\ i\dot z_b&=\kappa D_NJ_a\tau^{N-1}s\,(z_a-\bar s z_b). \end{aligned} \tag{10} Both objects respond to the same energy. Direct differentiation gives \dot\tau=0,\qquad \frac d{dt}\left(J_a z_az_a^\dagger+J_bz_bz_b^\dagger\right)=0. \tag{11} Indeed, put S=J_a z_az_a^\dagger+J_bz_bz_b^\dagger and \omega=\kappa D_N\tau^{N-1}. The ray projectors obey \dot P_a=-i\omega[S,P_a] and the same equation for P_b; their exact solution is common conjugation by e^{-i\omega St}. These P_a,P_b act on the generating vectors, rather than on \mathcal H_N. A common unitary change of mode frame preserves all equations. Its physical rotation subgroup also preserves them. Thus this specified first-order two-ray reduction produces reciprocal precession, with constant relative overlap. It does not by itself implement changing compatibility of complete physical spatial patterns. The bilateral orientation benchmark has a related conservation law. Full coefficient deformations, spatial transport, spinor structure and kinetic normalization remain separate parts of a particle-pair calculation in the one field \Psi_\infty. Physical spatial profile Complete local scalar response also separates rank from occupied-ray self-contact at an actual physical point. Its scalar-null source derivative has one real responsive direction, but that direction is orthogonal to the occupied complex ray and gives zero after projection onto it. This does not derive the graph kernel or its simplex normalization. Local scalar normalization tracks the remaining spatial equation: virial and fixed-norm constraints make the nonlinear coefficient and its frequency distinct. In the flat massless local reduction, the standard regular radial ansatz has no nonzero finite-norm stationary solution. The actual physical geometric and bundle terms must be retained when testing a particle profile. The direct derivative calculation gives the local scalar term before adding the graph pairing. Its coefficient count repeats local source eigenvalues; it does not generate the factor in (3). This makes the extra interaction premise explicit even when the graph ray is described by field derivatives. Verification graph_contact_variation_checks.py checks kernel normalization, complete moving-projector curvature, both coefficient Hessian blocks, fixed and varying rank-one matrices, reciprocal ray derivatives and the exact pair trajectory. It includes depths six and ten without constructing their large occupied-band matrices. Canonical normalization explains the additional physical metric needed to interpret the finite coefficient frequencies.

title: Local scalar contact on physical field derivatives
summary: Prolonging the written local scalar interaction to physical field derivatives repeats its local source blocks without generating a simplex coupling, and finite derivative data do not close the spatial kinetic equation.

Summary: Prolonging the written local scalar interaction to physical field derivatives repeats its local source blocks without generating a simplex coupling, and finite derivative data do not close the spatial kinetic equation. Test the local interaction before changing its action The mass-operator construction identifies the filtered derivative symbols of the physical field with a cumulative symmetric carrier. That identification gives the correct Hockey-Stick rank. It does not yet determine how the written interaction acts on those derivatives. This calculation applies the actual product rule to the local scalar term. It uses the same smooth physical spinor field throughout. Its coordinate directions are ordinary spatial directions on Q_d; Taylor coefficients introduce no additional physical dimensions and require no compactification. The result is local and does not choose a global spatial topology. In a local orthonormal spin frame, write \mathcal E_{m sc} = rac{\kappa}{2}\int(\psi^\dagger eta\psi)^2d\mu,\qquad \mathcal N(\psi)=\kappa(\psi^\dagger eta\psi) eta\psi, \qquad  eta^\dagger= eta,\quad eta^2=I. 	ag{1} The metric,  eta and \kappa are fixed background data in the variation. The full equation also contains its spatial Dirac operator. No occupied profile or physical mass follows from the algebraic source alone. Derivative counting and its exact product rule Choose local real coordinates centred at q. For a multiindex \alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d), put |\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j and \alpha!=\prod_j\alpha_j!. The divided Taylor coefficients through order N are c_\alpha= rac{\partial^\alpha\psi(q)}{\alpha!}, \qquad j_N\psi=(c_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le N}. 	ag{2} The name jet means this finite collection of derivatives. A field of such coefficients is holonomic when the coefficients actually are the derivatives of one field. At one point, arbitrary finite coefficients can be realized by a polynomial; across space they obey derivative compatibility conditions. The coordinate-independent jet definition and its Taylor description are given in Kolář, Michor and Slovák, Sections 12.1–12.5. Per spinor component, the rank is exactly D_{N,d}=\sum_{k=0}^N inom{k+d-1}{d-1}= inom{N+d}{d}. 	ag{3} For a fixed smooth real scalar current J, denote its divided derivatives by J_\gamma. The Leibniz rule gives [j_N(J\psi)]_\alpha =\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}J_\gamma c_\delta. 	ag{4} Thus multiplication induces a truncated convolution matrix [M_N[J]]_{\alpha\delta}=  egin{cases} J_{\alpha-\delta},&\delta_j\le\alpha_j\ 	ext{for every }j,\ 0,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} 	ag{5} Order the indices by total degree. Every diagonal entry is J_0=J(q); every other nonzero entry raises degree. Consequently M_N[J]=J_0I+K,\qquad K^{N+1}=0, 	ag{6} and  oxed{ \det(\lambda I-M_N[J])=(\lambda-J_0)^{D_{N,d}}, \qquad \operatorname{tr}(M_N[J]^r)=D_{N,d}J_0^r. } 	ag{7} The integer in (3) appears as a multiplicity and in a trace. The sole scalar eigenvalue remains J_0. When J_0
e0, the jet multiplier has full rank. Equation (7) is a statement about this particular local operator; it does not bound a separately derived spatial effective action. Changing to coherent coordinates preserves this distinction Using unscaled derivatives instead of (2) conjugates (5) by the diagonal matrix with entries \alpha!. The usual degree-N homogeneous coherent normalization is another invertible diagonal transformation, S_\alpha=\sqrt{ rac{N!\,\alpha!}{(N-|\alpha|)!}}, \qquad \widetilde c_\alpha=S_\alpha c_\alpha,\qquad \widetilde M=SM_N[J]S^{-1}. 	ag{8} It leaves (7) unchanged. It is a change of coefficient coordinates, not a derivation of their kinetic metric. There is a useful exact complex example. With fixed spinor u, amplitude a and real spatial wavevector k, let \psi(x)=aue^{ik\cdot x},\qquad c_\alpha=au rac{(ik)^\alpha}{\alpha!}. 	ag{9} At the coordinate origin, (8) turns the scalar coefficient sequence into the homogeneous coherent occupation sequence generated by (1,ik). Its squared coefficient norm is proportional to (1+|k|^2)^N, rather than being an independent physical norm of the original field. Retaining the conjugate phase gives J(x)=|a|^2u^\dagger eta u,\qquad J_\gamma=0\quad(|\gamma|>0), 	ag{10} because the derivative sum in every coordinate contains \sum_{\ell=0}^r(-1)^\ell inom r\ell=\delta_{r0}. 	ag{11} Therefore the complete source satisfies  oxed{j_N\mathcal N(\psi)=\kappa J_0\, eta\,j_N\psi} 	ag{12} at every retained order, before and after (8). This local plane wave is an operator example, not a proposed localized particle. At the assigned six-dimensional cumulative indices: Degree N Coefficient slots per spinor component Scalar coefficient in (12) 12 18\,564 \kappa J_0 34 3\,838\,380 \kappa J_0 This comparison holds the physical background fixed; a separate nonlinear branch could have a different current profile. Include the full variation of the self-consistent current For the nonlinear source in (1), the current is not fixed. Its actual Taylor coefficients and those of its source are J_\alpha=\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}c_\gamma^\dagger eta c_\delta, \qquad \mathcal N_\alpha =\kappa\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}J_\gamma eta c_\delta. 	ag{13} All J_\alpha are real; conjugate terms pair under \gamma\leftrightarrow\delta. The B term and the additional term in A are the response of the current itself. Freezing the current would omit them. For any matrices A,B, the real matrix of \eta\mapsto A\eta+B ar\eta, using real and imaginary parts, is \mathcal R(A,B)=  egin{pmatrix} \operatorname{Re}(A+B)&-\operatorname{Im}(A-B)\ \operatorname{Im}(A+B)&\operatorname{Re}(A-B) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{15} Interleave the real and imaginary parts at each derivative index. Equation (14) is block lower triangular, with the same local block \mathcal R_0=\mathcal R(A_0,B_0) on every diagonal. Hence the full real source Jacobian \mathcal J_N obeys  oxed{ \det(\lambda I-\mathcal J_N) =\det(\lambda I-\mathcal R_0)^{D_{N,d}}. } 	ag{16} Again the count repeats local response eigenvalues. Spatial derivatives appear in the off-diagonal blocks and can change Jordan structure. Neither this algebraic source Jacobian nor (7) is the full time-evolution generator, which also includes multiplication by -i, the spatial Dirac term, and any rotating-frame subtraction. The local eigenvalues can also be written explicitly. Let the complex +1 and -1 eigenspaces of  eta have dimensions r_+ and r_-, both positive, and set Q_0=c_0^\dagger c_0,\qquad S_0=c_0^\dagger eta c_0. In real coordinates the source derivative is \kappa[S_0 eta_{\mathbb R}+2v_{\mathbb R}v_{\mathbb R}^{\mathsf T}]. Its eigenvalues are  egin{array}{c|c} 	ext{Eigenvalue}&	ext{Multiplicity}\ \hline \kappa S_0&2r_+-1\ -\kappa S_0&2r_--1\ \kappa\left(Q_0+\sqrt{Q_0^2+3S_0^2}ight)&1\ \kappa\left(Q_0-\sqrt{Q_0^2+3S_0^2}ight)&1 \end{array}. 	ag{17} To derive the last two values, remove the directions orthogonal to the positive and negative parts of c_0. Their squared norms are (Q_0+S_0)/2 and (Q_0-S_0)/2. On the remaining real two-dimensional span, the trace is 2\kappa Q_0 and the determinant is -3\kappa^2S_0^2. Formula (17) also holds by continuity when one part vanishes. At a scalar-null field, S_0=0, the only nonzero local eigenvalue is 2\kappa Q_0. A sign of  eta or an eigenvalue in (17) is not an assignment of particle versus antiparticle. Curvature and the physical kinetic norm On a curved spatial manifold, a connection splits the finite derivative filtration into symmetrized covariant derivatives. The change from ordinary coordinate derivatives to this splitting is triangular and invertible, with the same highest-order symbols. A connection preserving the spinor pairing obeys the covariant product rule. The associated graded operator of scalar multiplication remains J(q) on every degree, so (7) survives. The full source variation transforms with the same fixed linear change of jet coordinates, preserving (16). Curvature does not turn a coordinate transformation into a new scalar coupling. There is a useful warning about the norm implicit in such a rewriting. If some retained derivative of J is nonzero, K in (6) is a nonzero nilpotent matrix. Then M_N[J] is not diagonalizable and cannot be self-adjoint in any positive definite metric on the independent finite jet fibre. For example, at d=N=1 and J=1+x, M= egin{pmatrix}1&0\1&1\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{18} The equation GM=M^\dagger G forces G_{22}=0, which excludes a positive definite G. Ordinary real multiplication on the physical L^2 field space is nevertheless self-adjoint. There is no contradiction: the Taylor map is not a unitary identification of that space with an independent finite coefficient fibre at one point. The original canonical norm remains Q[\psi]=\int\psi^\dagger\psi\,d\mu. 	ag{19} Expressing its field through holonomic derivatives does not replace (19) with an independent sum over all derivative slots. A positive norm that weights all spatial derivatives defines a different, usually Sobolev, metric; its induced operator and constraints must be transformed as well. The canonical normalization calculation explains why the physical kinetic metric must accompany a projected interaction. There is also a kinetic closure issue. Already for a flat first-order Dirac operator \mathscr D=-i\sum_j\mathsf a_j\partial_j, [j_N(\mathscr D\psi)]_\alpha =-i\sum_j\mathsf a_j(\alpha_j+1)c_{\alpha+e_j}. 	ag{20} The highest retained derivative needs order N+1 of the field. For example, \psi_1=u and \psi_2=u+\epsilon x_1^{N+1}v have identical N-jets at zero, but their degree-N Dirac jets differ by -i\epsilon(N+1)\mathsf a_1v. Thus a finite jet at one point does not define a closed algebraic kinetic matrix. A spatial PDE on jet fields can retain their derivatives and compatibility equations; a finite oscillator reduction instead needs an actual projection and control of its complementary spatial modes. Consequence for the mass-operator derivation The count in (3) is exact. The prolonged local action gives (13) and (14), rather than the auxiliary rank-one contact. Deriving the latter requires an additional physical reduction, such as a specific source pairing and its canonical normalization. The defined graph pairing supplies one conditional action with a simplex coefficient, but its kernel is an additional premise. This also clarifies the scope of the coherent curved mode-bundle fields and their physical contact spectrum. Those calculations use sections of a specified independently twisted kinetic bundle. Realizing them as derivatives of the master field would require the holonomic constraints and the actual induced kinetic operator. Equality of carrier ranks alone does not provide that realization. The result concerns the written local scalar term and changes of its derivative coordinates. It does not exclude different nonlinear spatial branches, a derived interaction from complementary modes of the same field, or a different master term. It leaves the assigned particle dimensionalities and mode indices unchanged. Verification local_current_jet_checks.py compares (13) with independently expanded complex spatial polynomials. It checks the complete real-linear variation, trace identities, both signs of  eta, scalar-null fields, and covariance when all spin data are rotated together. The largest explicit real Jacobian has dimension 448, retaining every derivative through order two in six dimensions for an eight-component spinor. A nonflat metric-compatible connection is checked in two independent ways: symmetrized ordered covariant differentiation and a matrix exponential along radial lines. Their current jets and full nonlinear variations agree. Exact binomial identities verify the plane-wave cancellation at arbitrary multiindices through the assigned degrees, without constructing millions of coefficient entries. Symbolic differentiation also verifies the kinetic counterexample (20).

title: Simplex counts in a physical projective spectral band
summary: A fixed-line cumulative spatial band on CP3 has exactly twenty times the simplex rank and a corresponding polarized point eigenvalue, while its full Dirac pair and smooth scalar self-source retain additional components and nonconstant coefficients.
text:
Summary: A fixed-line cumulative spatial band on CP3 has exactly twenty times the simplex rank and a corresponding polarized point eigenvalue, while its full Dirac pair and smooth scalar self-source retain additional components and nonconstant coefficients. An actual spatial band has the simplex count On physical \mathbb{CP}^3 with the specified line connection \mathcal O(3), retain every zero-form spatial spectral shell from 0 through N=n-1. The complete band has dimension  oxed{ \mathscr D_N= inom{N+3}{3} inom{N+6}{3} =20 inom{n+5}{6}=20S(n,6). } 	ag{1} Its physical point evaluation in the zero-form polarization is rank one and has nonzero eigenvalue \mathscr D_N/\mathcal V, where \mathcal V is the physical volume. Thus a specified point contact has an exact simplex coefficient with a single factor of twenty independent of the band. This is a different space of spatial fields from the holomorphic tangent-mode band: the line degree here stays fixed while nonholomorphic spatial harmonics are added. It also uses a different connection from the \mathcal O(2) derivative polynomial. The two calculations should not be combined without a map between their bundles and actions. The count and evaluation operator can be derived. A smooth local scalar current has not thereby become a point insertion. The explicit reproducing state below has a different self-contact expectation and drives complementary components. The geometry is conditional actual CP3 with ordinary macroscopic spatial directions, no compactification and unknown FS scale R. The calculations at CP5 below use a separately specified actual ten-dimensional geometry. Line and spectral labels are field data, not additional physical dimensions or charge assignments. Sum all fixed-line spatial shells For complex dimension m and L\ge0, consider the zero-form sections in the full bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L). Their spatial squared-Dirac eigenvalues are X_k=k(k+L+m),\qquad X= rac{R^2\mathscr D_L^2}{4},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots. 	ag{2} The complete projective spectrum includes this family and all the other spinor families. Here the cumulative zero-form subspace is \mathcal K_N= igoplus_{k=0}^N\mathcal H_k. There is a direct polynomial count. A shell can be represented by a trace-free homogeneous polynomial of holomorphic and antiholomorphic degrees (k+L,k), with its line homogeneity retained. Taking a trace lowers both degrees by one. The harmonic decomposition of the complete polynomial space gives d_k=\dim\mathcal H_k = inom{k+m}{m} inom{k+L+m}{m} - inom{k+m-1}{m} inom{k+L+m-1}{m}. 	ag{3} The subtracted product is zero at k=0. The same dimensions follow from the SU(m+1) Weyl formula. Summing the differences in (3) yields  oxed{ \mathscr D_N=\dim\mathcal K_N = inom{N+m}{m} inom{N+L+m}{m}. } 	ag{4} Multiplication by |Z|^2 in the homogeneous polynomial description realizes the nested cumulative inclusions. On unit homogeneous coordinates it preserves the existing spatial section. The band therefore has one fixed connection and compatible spatial inclusions. title: Spatial oscillator point contact
summary: A point contact on actual flat spatial oscillator waves has a position-dependent reproducing strength, whose central value is a weighted Hockey-Stick count rather than the projective simplex dimension.
text: Summary: A point contact on actual flat spatial oscillator waves has a position-dependent reproducing strength, whose central value is a weighted Hockey-Stick count rather than the projective simplex dimension. The physical spatial evaluation operator Fix ordinary spatial coordinates x\in\mathbb R^d, Lebesgue measure, oscillator width w>0, and the cumulative normalized Hermite band \mathcal B_{N,d} of oscillator modes. Let P_N be its orthogonal projector. Point evaluation at X defines a finite positive quadratic form \langle f,A_N(X)f\rangle=|f(X)|^2, \qquad A_N(X)=P_N\delta_XP_N. \tag{1} No untruncated bounded delta multiplication operator is assumed. In the real normalized Hermite basis, the finite matrix is A_{\alpha\beta}=h_\alpha^w(X)h_\beta^w(X). It has rank one and its sole nonzero eigenvalue is \boxed{K_{N,d}^w(X,X)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le N}|h_\alpha^w(X)|^2.} \tag{2} This strength has physical units of inverse spatial volume and depends on position and width. Integrating (2) over X gives the dimension D_d(N)=\binom{N+d}{d}, because each basis mode is normalized. The dimension is therefore the integrated trace density, not its value at an arbitrary spatial point. Mehler's formula and the central count Apply Mehler's formula to each spatial coordinate, including the Gaussian factors in the normalized modes. The shell generating function is \sum_{\alpha\ge0}|h_\alpha^w(X)|^2t^{|\alpha|} =\left(\frac w\pi\right)^{d/2}(1-t^2)^{-d/2} \exp\left[-w|X|^2\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right]. \tag{3} Multiplication by (1-t)^{-1} sums all shells through N: \boxed{\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}K_{N,d}^w(X,X)t^N =\frac{(w/\pi)^{d/2}}{(1-t)(1-t^2)^{d/2}} \exp\left[-w|X|^2\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right],\quad |t|<1.} \tag{4} This depends on X only through |X|, as required by physical rotation covariance of the complete isotropic band. The evaluation vector itself retains all spatial mode amplitudes. At the oscillator center, odd occupations vanish. For M=\lfloor N/2\rfloor, the coefficient in (4) becomes \boxed{K_{N,d}^w(0,0)=\left(\frac w\pi\right)^{d/2} \sum_{r=0}^{M}\frac{(d/2)_r}{r!} =\left(\frac w\pi\right)^{d/2}\binom{M+d/2}{M}.} \tag{5} This is the weighted Hockey-Stick identity derived in oscillator source marginals. At fixed d,w and large N, the gamma-function ratio gives K_{N,d}^w(0,0)\sim \frac{(w/\pi)^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)} \left(\frac N2\right)^{d/2}, \qquad D_d(N)\sim\frac{N^d}{d!}. \tag{6} For example, at d=6 and the same width, \frac{K_{34,6}^w(0,0)}{K_{12,6}^w(0,0)} =\frac{\binom{20}{17}}{\binom{9}{6}} =\frac{95}{7}\simeq13.5714, \qquad \frac{D_6(34)}{D_6(12)}\simeq206.7647. \tag{7} These are operator comparisons, not predicted particle mass ratios. An independently derived width w_N changes (5); choosing it to fit a desired power is additional structure. Even restoring a leading power would not prove the exact finite-band simplex law. Fourier duality with the normal marginal For q normal coordinates, define the restriction (Ef)(x)=f(x,0) and the scaled unitary Fourier transform (\mathcal F_w f)(y)=\left(\frac w{2\pi}\right)^{q/2} \int e^{-iw y\cdot y'}f(y')dy'. Direct Fourier transformation of the Hermite generating function gives \mathcal F_w h_\beta^w=(-i)^{|\beta|}h_\beta^w. At zero normal position, h_{2m}^w(0)=\left(\frac w\pi\right)^{1/4} (-1)^m\sqrt{\frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{4^m}}, \qquad h_{2m+1}^w(0)=0. Evaluation of the Fourier integral at zero therefore proves, on the finite band, \boxed{R=\left(\frac{2\pi}{w}\right)^{q/2}E\mathcal F_w.} \tag{8} The Fourier transform preserves total oscillator degree. Consequently, the restriction and marginal have the same singular spectrum after their displayed dimensional factors are removed. Their even-mode phases differ. Equality of singular strengths does not make them the same response to a fixed complex spatial preparation. Relation to projective ray contact The projective contact calculation uses H^0(\mathbb{CP}^d,\mathcal O(N)) with a homogeneous unit-volume Fubini–Study measure. Its point contact has constant strength D_d(N). The point in that construction is a mode ray; the point X in (1) is a position in an actual flat spatial chart. An equality of finite dimensions does not identify the two evaluation operators or measures. There is an elementary vector test. Under the usual normalized homogenization of occupations, the spatial vector at X=0 has a nonzero ground coefficient, zero degree-one coefficients and nonzero degree-two coefficients whenever N\ge2. A Veronese coherent vector z^{\otimes N} with nonzero ground coefficient and vanishing all degree-one coefficients must have z_1=\cdots=z_d=0, which also eliminates every degree-two coefficient. Thus central spatial evaluation is not a projective coherent ray in that identification. The unfinished coordinate-to-ray kernel bridge must specify the actual transform, measure, field-dependent data and kinetic normalization. Equations (1)–(8) give a fully specified spatial comparison against which such a bridge can be tested. They do not replace the proposed compact physical geometry of an IDWT particle. Verification spatial_oscillator_projection_checks.py checks direct Hermite evaluation against (3)–(5), integrates the trace density, verifies physical rotation covariance and Fourier phases, and constructs the full marginal and restriction matrices independently.

title: Physical contact on the tangent-mode band
summary: The complete holomorphic tangent-mode band has an exact polarization-dependent physical point-contact spectrum, whose largest eigenvalue differs from the auxiliary simplex count.
text:
Summary: The complete holomorphic tangent-mode band has an exact polarization-dependent physical point-contact spectrum, whose largest eigenvalue differs from the auxiliary simplex count. Project the actual spatial sections The coherent spatial mode-bundle construction puts the tangent-mode carrier and the spatial Dirac field on the same curved geometry. Its natural spatial evaluation map can now be computed, including the full holomorphic coefficient space and its kinetic norm.
