This is a conditional diagnostic of a particular twisted-Dirac interpretation, not a compactification premise imposed on V2. It prevents declaring a complete particle spectrum merely from the 16-dimensional exterior fibre. 5. What this does and does not solve The global group and charge-table construction is now explicit and avoids the tangent splitting obstruction. It does not derive why this bundle is selected, how it is tied to the single master spinor, which differential operator gives occupied modes, gauge kinetic terms, coupling strengths, or the cross-depth charged-current blocks. Treat it as an admissible candidate against which the missing master-to-gauge map can be tested, not a replacement axiom silently added to V2. title: CP5 tangent splitting obstruction
summary: The complex tangent bundle of CP5 admits no global rank-three plus rank-two splitting, even without imposing determinant one.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The complex tangent bundle of CP5 admits no global rank-three plus rank-two splitting, even without imposing determinant one. Why this matters Gauge selection §15 already excludes determinant-one tangent holonomy because c1(T CP5)=6H. The obstruction is stronger: a global complex 3+2 tangent splitting itself is impossible. Keeping the determinant connection does not cure that failure. 1. Exhaust the possible Chern factors Let E=T^(1,0) CP5. The Euler sequence gives c(E)=1+6H+15H^2+20H^3+15H^4+6H^5, \qquad H^*(\mathbb{CP}^5;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[H]/(H^6). Suppose E=A_3 direct-sum B_2. The Whitney product formula says c(E)=c(A)c(B). Since both factors have degree at most their ranks, their product has degree at most five. Equality modulo H^6 is therefore an exact polynomial equality. The top coefficient is nonzero, so the degrees must be exactly three and two. Over the rationals the polynomial factors as c(E)=(1+2H)(1+H+H^2)(1+3H+3H^2). The two quadratics are irreducible (discriminant -3), and the linear factor occurs only once. Normalizing constant terms to one, the only possible rank-two Chern factors are c(B)=1+H+H^2\quad\hbox{or}\quad c(B)=1+3H+3H^2. 2. Both factors fail a necessary bundle condition Restrict B to a linear CP3 inside CP5. A complex rank-two bundle on CP3 with c1=aH and c2=bH^2 must satisfy ab=0 modulo 2. This is the classical Atiyah–Rees/Schwarzenberger condition; see Opie, Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.3. The two candidates have (a,b)=(1,1) and (3,3), hence ab odd in both cases. Neither is the Chern class of such a bundle. The supposed splitting cannot exist. An independent check uses K(CP3)=Z[t]/(t^4), t=[O(1)]-1, and ch(t)=exp(H)-1. The rank-two candidate characters are \operatorname{ch}(B)=2+aH+\frac{a^2-2b}{2}H^2 +\frac{a^3-3ab}{6}H^3. Their coefficients in the integral K-theory basis (1,t,t^2,t^3) would be (2,1,-1,1/2) and (2,3,0,-1/2), respectively. Half-integral final coefficients are impossible. The K-theory basis is established in Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, §2.2. 3. Precise consequence for V2 No unitary connection on T^(1,0) CP5 can have its full holonomy contained in a conjugate U(3) times U(2): such a reduction would produce the excluded rank-three and rank-two subbundles. This conclusion does not assume the connection is Levi–Civita, holomorphic, or determinant one. Tensoring the tangent bundle by a line bundle cannot help with the splitting: a split of E tensor L would untwist to a split of E. Separately its first Chern class would be (6+5k)H for L=O(k), never zero for integer k. The pointwise exterior-algebra branching, charge normalization, and local stabilizer calculations remain valid. What fails is promoting that local split to the literal global tangent bundle. An auxiliary gauge bundle, a different effective carrier, or a properly specified non-global construction is required. This theorem does not forbid the Standard Model group on CP5 or every possible V2 gauge completion. The normal-spinor calculation provides a compatible distinction: the tangent/normal splitting along an embedded CP3 exists and has an explicit induced connection. It is not a rank-three plus rank-two splitting over the entire CP5 base. Verification cp5_gauge_bundle_checks.py factors the Chern polynomial exactly, exhausts the rank-two factors, and independently computes their forbidden K-theory coefficients. The cited bundle theorem is an input; finite arithmetic alone is not a replacement for it. Related Auxiliary gauge carrier — explicit separate bundle that avoids this obstruction without identifying it with the tangent carrier. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Projective nesting and intermediate spatial depths
summary: Normal characteristic classes obstruct odd intermediate depths in standard projective nesting and obstruct a full sequence of one-dimensional depth increments between any embedded CP spaces whose lower complex dimension is at least two.
text:
Summary: Normal characteristic classes obstruct odd intermediate depths in standard projective nesting and obstruct a full sequence of one-dimensional depth increments between any embedded CP spaces whose lower complex dimension is at least two. A partial inclusion is not a complete spatial chain IDWT requires its physical sectors to be nested submanifolds of one ordinary spatial manifold. The geometry premise audit already distinguishes that requirement from assigning a name to each spatial depth. Here a normal-bundle calculation determines when the standard projective inclusions can contain intermediate spatial depths. The calculation concerns actual spatial embeddings, not projectors on field coefficients. It assumes the stated global projective topologies. It introduces no compactification or small spatial scale. Changing the metric radius, interaction strength or occupied spinor does not change the characteristic classes used below. Consider the standard inclusion \mathrm{CP}^a\hookrightarrow\mathrm{CP}^{a+q},\qquad [Z]\longmapsto[Z,0],\qquad a,q\ge1. 	ag{1} Its spatial depths are 2a and 2(a+q). The normal-bundle derivation gives N=\mathcal O(1)\otimes\mathbb C^q,\qquad H^*(\mathrm{CP}^a;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[h]/(h^{a+1}), 	ag{2} where h=c_1(\mathcal O(1)). Writing N_{\mathbb R} for the real rank-2q normal bundle,  oxed{c(N)=(1+h)^q,\qquad e(N_{\mathbb R})=h^q,\qquad p(N_{\mathbb R})=(1+h^2)^q.} 	ag{3} All expressions are truncated in the cohomology of the lower base. In particular e(N_{\mathbb R})
e0 when q\le a, and p_1(N_{\mathbb R})=qh^2
e0 when a\ge2. Odd intermediate depths are obstructed Suppose (1) factored through an embedded intermediate spatial submanifold Y of dimension 2a+r, where 0<r<2q: \mathrm{CP}^a\hookrightarrow Y^{2a+r} \hookrightarrow\mathrm{CP}^{a+q}. 	ag{4} Restrict its tangent and normal bundles to \mathrm{CP}^a. An ambient Riemannian metric supplies an orthogonal splitting N_{\mathbb R}=A_r\oplus B_{2q-r}. 	ag{5} Here A is the normal of the lower space in Y, and B is the normal of Y in the higher space, restricted to the lower space. Every real bundle over \mathrm{CP}^a is orientable because H^1(\mathrm{CP}^a;\mathbb Z_2)=0. If r is odd, both ranks in (5) are odd. Their Euler classes lie in odd-degree cohomology of \mathrm{CP}^a, which vanishes. The Euler product formula therefore requires e(N_{\mathbb R})=e(A)e(B)=0. 	ag{6} This contradicts (3) whenever q\le a. Consequently  oxed{q\le a\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 	ext{no odd-dimensional intermediate }Y	ext{ in (4)}.} 	ag{7} The Euler product and odd-rank facts follow from Thom classes; see Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles, Corollary 3.12 and Proposition 3.13. Equations (5)–(7) apply those standard results to the actual spatial inclusion. The intermediate space need not itself be projective or have a prescribed metric. Standard lower-to-higher inclusion Spatial depths Nonzero normal Euler class Excluded intermediate depths \mathrm{CP}^1\subset\mathrm{CP}^2 2	o4 h 3 \mathrm{CP}^2\subset\mathrm{CP}^3 4	o6 h 5 \mathrm{CP}^3\subset\mathrm{CP}^5 6	o10 h^2 7,9 \mathrm{CP}^1\subset\mathrm{CP}^3 2	o6 h^2=0 on \mathrm{CP}^1 none from this Euler test For codimension two, this has a simple geometric meaning. A one-dimensional intermediate normal direction would be a real line subbundle of \mathcal O(1)_{\mathbb R}. Over the simply connected lower base that line would be trivial and would give a nowhere-zero normal vector. Its nonzero Euler class prevents such a vector. A normal direction exists in every coordinate chart, but these directions cannot be chosen consistently over the entire lower space. Every one-dimensional increment requires a real normal frame There is a stronger condition if every intermediate depth is required: M^d=Y_d\subset Y_{d+1}\subset\cdots\subset Y_D=X^D. 	ag{8} Restrict each successive normal line to M. Their sum is N_MX. If H^1(M;\mathbb Z_2)=0, each line is trivial, so  oxed{	ext{A full chain (8) implies }N_MX\cong \mathbf1^{D-d}	ext{ as a real bundle}.} 	ag{9} Conversely, a real normal frame and a tubular neighborhood give intermediate images of M times coordinate balls of every dimension. This supplies smooth intermediate submanifolds near M; it does not require them to be closed or geodesically complete, or turn the whole ambient space into a product. The criterion concerns existence of the stated embeddings, not their dynamics or physical selection. For the standard projective inclusion with a\ge2, p_1(N_{\mathbb R})=qh^2 already contradicts (9), including when q>a and the top Euler class vanishes for dimensional reasons. Vanishing of the Euler obstruction alone is not sufficient. Changing the projective embedding does not restore a full chain The full-chain obstruction extends to any smooth embedding i:\mathrm{CP}^a\hookrightarrow\mathrm{CP}^b, with b>a\ge2. No holomorphic assumption is needed for this part. Let H be the ambient hyperplane class and write i^*H=u h for some integer u. For the real tangent bundle of \mathrm{CP}^m, the Euler sequence gives p_1(T\mathrm{CP}^m)=(m+1)H^2: equivalently use p_1=c_1^2-2c_2 with c_1=(m+1)H and c_2= inom{m+1}{2}H^2. The real tangent-normal splitting therefore gives  oxed{p_1(N_i)=\left[(b+1)u^2-(a+1)ight]h^2.} 	ag{10} The characteristic-class rules and real complexification convention are detailed in Cohen, chapter 3, section 5. There is no torsion ambiguity on the cohomology of \mathrm{CP}^a. The coefficient in (10) cannot vanish: for u=0 it is -(a+1), while for |u|\ge1 it is at least b-a>0. Since h^2
e0 for a\ge2, no such smooth embedding has a trivial real normal bundle. Hence  oxed{b>a\ge2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{CP}^a\hookrightarrow\mathrm{CP}^b 	ext{ cannot be refined through every intermediate spatial depth}.} 	ag{11} For example, an arbitrary smooth CP3-to-CP5 embedding would have p_1(N_i)=(6u^2-4)h^2. Changing the embedding cannot supply a full 6,7,8,9,10 sequence of smooth nested spatial submanifolds. This statement is stronger than, and distinct from, the obstruction to a complex tangent splitting over all of CP5 in the CP5 tangent audit. A constructive control where intermediate spaces do exist The lower-dimensional exception is useful. For \mathrm{CP}^1\subset\mathrm{CP}^3, the real normal bundle underlying \mathcal O(1)\oplus\mathcal O(1) has an explicit global orthonormal frame, despite being nontrivial as a complex bundle. Let z\in\mathbb C^2 be a unit representative of [z]\in\mathrm{CP}^1, let \sigma_j be the Pauli matrices, and set A_0=I,\qquad A_j=i\sigma_j\quad(1\le j\le3),\qquad W(z)=(A_0z,A_1z,A_2z,A_3z). 	ag{12} These four normal columns obey \operatorname{Re}[W(z)^\dagger W(z)]=I_4,\qquad W(e^{i	heta}z)=e^{i	heta}W(z). 	ag{13} The second identity makes them well-defined sections of \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Cz,\mathbb C^2). The first follows because A_i^\dagger A_j is anti-Hermitian for i
e j. They are a real frame, not four independent complex columns. The normal connection can still have curvature; a topological frame is not a frame of parallel vectors. For actual physical metric radius R, the normal exponential is explicit. For real y\in\mathbb R^4, r=|y|<\pi R/2, put \Phi([z],y)= \left[\cos(r/R)z,\  rac{\sin(r/R)}r W(z)yight], 	ag{14} using its continuous value at r=0. The projective representative has unit norm and (13) makes (14) independent of the phase choice of z. For a sufficiently small tubular radius, restricting y successively to \mathbb R^1,\mathbb R^2,\mathbb R^3 gives compatible smooth submanifolds of real dimensions three, four and five containing the same CP1 inside CP3. These intermediate spaces are tubular constructions, not CP2 or an assigned nuclear geometry. No measured length or small extra-dimensional scale is attached to the tube parameter. The example shows precisely why (7) and (11) retain their hypotheses; it does not select physical sectors or their global completeness. Consequences for the coupling construction The complete CP1 normal-frame criterion The same construction classifies the standard inclusions with lower space \mathrm{CP}^1. Their normal bundle is \mathcal O(1)\otimes\mathbb C^q: here q is complex codimension, and the ordinary real normal dimension is 2q. For q=2m, group its complex lines into m pairs. Each pair has the real frame (12)–(13), so their direct sum gives a global real frame of rank 2q: N_{\mathbb R}\cong  igoplus_{j=1}^{m} \left(\mathcal O(1)\oplus\mathcal O(1)ight)_{\mathbb R} \cong\mathbf1^{2q}. 	ag{15} For odd q, triviality is obstructed. The equatorial transition of \mathcal O(1) over \mathrm{CP}^1\cong S^2 is one full rotation of its real two-plane. For q copies, the lift of this transition loop to \operatorname{Spin}(2q) ends at (-1)^q=-1: each plane contributes its spin half-angle sign. It is therefore not a contractible loop in SO(2q), whereas a trivial real bundle has a contractible clutching loop. Equivalently its second Stiefel–Whitney class is w_2(N_{\mathbb R})=qh mod2
e0. Together with (15), this proves  oxed{\mathrm{CP}^1\subset\mathrm{CP}^{1+q} 	ext{ has a trivial real normal bundle exactly when }q	ext{ is even}.} 	ag{16} Equation (9) and the tubular construction then give the corresponding criterion for a full sequence of intermediate depths near CP1. In particular, CP1 inside CP5 permits such tubular intermediate spaces; it does not make its depth-six intermediate a global CP3. The full CP3-to-CP5 obstruction above remains unchanged. These existence statements neither select physical sectors nor establish completeness of the tubular intermediate spaces. Keep the actual nesting hypotheses The standard CP3-to-CP5 pair remains a valid partial inclusion with its computed normal connection and reciprocal specified kernel. It cannot simultaneously be declared the complete spatial chain through all the intervening depths. If only selected depths are retained in a calculation, its scope must say so. The obstruction at 2	o3	o4 and at 4	o5	o6 directly affects the alternating sphere/projective candidate list. Merely replacing the odd-dimensional sphere by another smooth odd-dimensional manifold does not fix a standard projective inclusion on either side. Compatible geometries and embeddings need a new construction. The parallel two-state normal spinor factor in the six-to-ten branching also does not provide a real normal frame. For that inclusion, \Sigma^-N is a trivial complex doublet while e(N_{\mathbb R})=h^2
e0. Spinor components and ordinary spatial normal directions are different bundles. On a contractible spatial chart these global obstructions disappear. Using such a chart is a different domain from the entire projective space and needs its own field domain, boundary conditions and normalization. Local mode counting by itself supplies neither the missing global embeddings nor a physical geometry. Verification projective_nesting_checks.py runs 1,385 checks. Exact tangent-bundle quotients and real complexification recover the characteristic classes independently. Finite differences of the actual normal connection and improper spatial curvature integrals verify the primitive characteristic numbers and their independence of R. The code also checks the global phase covariance, real orthonormality, explicit inverse and induced metric of the constructive tube. The topological conclusions rely on the proofs above and the cited bundle theorems. A finite scan of dimensions or integer degrees is a consistency check, not a substitute for the all-degree argument. No empirical geometry or particle coupling is identified by this result.

title: Geometric probe selection
summary: Exact CP3 section integrals give a conditional low-order probe coupling and show that four orbit modes can miss a nonzero weak-field response.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Exact CP3 section integrals give a conditional low-order probe coupling and show that four orbit modes can miss a nonzero weak-field response. Candidate and assumptions Continue the selected spinor-line lift and its explicitly added Killing drive. Test observer coordinate symbols built from the smooth projective functions f_ij = conjugate(Z_i) Z_j / (Z†Z). A real coordinate is a Hermitian combination of these functions times a length ℓ. This is a geometric candidate for an electromagnetic readout, not the nonlinear petal detector map and not a derivation of physical spatial coordinates. The demo and its actual coefficient trajectories are unchanged. With density q|Φ|², its dipole operator is q times the section-space compression of multiplication by the chosen coordinate. There are now explicit matrix elements, rather than arbitrary four-by-four probe matrices. All results below are conditional on this source assignment and on restricting to the holomorphic section sector. Other spatial spinor modes remain outside this calculation and may contribute to a fully physical probe response. Exact matrix elements Normalize the FS measure to unit volume and use |Z| = 1 representatives. For an occupation multi-index n with Σ_i n_i = L, normalized monomials are s_n(Z)=\sqrt{\frac{(L+3)!}{6\prod_i n_i!}}\prod_i Z_i^{n_i}, \qquad \int\prod_i|Z_i|^{2n_i}d\mu=\frac{6\prod_i n_i!}{(L+3)!}. Integrating an additional f_ij factor gives T_{ij}=\Pi_L f_{ij}\Pi_L =\frac{a_j^\dagger a_i+\delta_{ij}I}{L+4} on the degree-L symmetric representation. The a symbols implement monomial occupation changes; no physical flat oscillator is introduced. In particular, Σ_i T_ii = I, ensuring that normalized total charge does not grow with L. For i ≠ j, the only nonzero matrix element moves one unit of occupation from i to j and equals √(n_i(n_j+1))/(L+4). These identities follow by the displayed monomial integral; the diagnostic compares every matrix entry against that integral for L = 1, 2, 3. What this candidate sees on the actual orbit In the monomial eigenbasis, the four occupied states are u=(L,0,0,0),\quad v=(0,L,0,0),\quad w=(0,0,1,L-1),\quad r=(0,0,0,L), with initial coefficients (A,A,B,B)/√2, A²+B² = 1. Their frequencies are ν(L,−L,−1,0), so this is the same orbit as the amplitude/clock construction. For L ≥ 2, a one-occupation transfer cannot connect either u or v to any other selected state. Only the w↔r clock pair remains off-diagonal: \langle r|T_{34}|w\rangle=\frac{\sqrt L}{L+4}. Thus low-order geometric dipoles need not reveal all the frequencies permitted by an arbitrary four-state matrix: family full section dimension possible nonzero unforced frequencies for this symbol class two petals, L = 1 4 ν, 2ν four petals, L = 2 10 ν six petals, L = 3 20 ν For the complex dipole choice d_x+i d_y = qℓ⟨T_34⟩, the signal is qℓ B²√L e^{iνt}/[2(L+4)]. It can trace a circle even when the detector shows petals. This is not a statement that the actual multidimensional orbit has become a circle; the two probes retain different information. Nor does an unobserved petal frequency prove no radiation: the clock signal is still time dependent under this particular charge readout. A symbol polynomial of bidegree (k,k) can transfer at most k occupations. Connecting either extremal state to another selected state requires k ≥ L. That is a projective-coordinate degree threshold, not automatically an ordinary electromagnetic multipole order or a number of photons. A response that four modes miss entirely Choose the real coordinate X = ℓ Re(conjugate(Z_1)Z_3)/(Z†Z), giving D=C(a_1^\dagger a_3+a_3^\dagger a_1),\qquad C=\frac{q\ell}{2(L+4)}. Let P retain just {u,v,w,r}. For L ≥ 2, PDP = 0, but (1−P)DP ≠ 0. A four-mode calculation would predict no dipole or linear response for this probe. The full section-space generator is h = ℏν(N₁−N₂−N₃). Using [a₁†a₃,a₃†a₁] = N₁−N₃ gives the exact retarded response to −E(t)D: \chi(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle[D(t),D(s)]\rangle =-\frac{C^2}{\hbar}(A^2L-B^2)\sin(2\nu(t-s)),\qquad t>s. Here ⟨N₁−N₃⟩ = (A²L−B²)/2. For the demo's A = 0.6 and B = 0.8 this response is nonzero at L = 2 and 3 despite PDP = 0. The intermediate states are real members of the 10- or 20-dimensional section space, not additional fitted energy levels. An exact small impulse independently reproduces this kernel in the diagnostic. Its sign depends on the prepared populations; it is not a fitted absorption rate or a passivity claim. This particular commutator depends only on conserved occupations and t−s, even though the prepared orbit is not stationary. That simplification is special to this probe and generator, not a license to replace every orbit response by an equilibrium susceptibility. Consequence for the previous frequency test The earlier finite-generator frequency bounds remain correct for an unforced dipole within that specified four-state model. They do not alone bound a physical absorption spectrum when the probe can excite omitted modes. Exact preservation of the unforced orbit is insufficient; probe closure or a controlled elimination of omitted modes is also needed. The conditional line lift, density, current, and these matrix elements form a calculable candidate chain. V2 still has to select the twist, Killing term, observer symbols and scale, photon normalization, and nuclear state. The separate ring sector is not derived by setting L = 0 here. No atomic spectrum or independent evidence for extra spatial dimensions is claimed. Reproduction projected_current_checks.py checks exact monomial integration, charge normalization, the unforced selection rule, the occupation-distance threshold, omitted-mode coupling, and the full response against an independently evolved impulse. title: Two different notions of encounter
summary: Research record, section 2: Two different notions of encounter.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Research record, section 2: Two different notions of encounter. Provenance Preserved from interaction notebook section 2, recorded 2026-09-05 and corrected 2026-09-06. Original sequence contents. This is an exploratory research record, not an independently established V2 result. Read the related later audits before using an intermediate conclusion. 2. Two different notions of encounter A crucial distinction is required. 2.1 Full-depth direct encounter For two particles of the same depth d, let their relative coordinate be \Delta X_d\in Q_d. A genuinely local same-depth interaction samples the full relative geometry. In a locally Euclidean model, R_d^2=\sum_{i=1}^d(\Delta x_i)^2. If the interaction is central, V=V(R_d), then F_i=-\frac{dV}{dR_d}\frac{\Delta x_i}{R_d}. Thus all nonzero components of the one separation vector evolve together. The uncontrolled coordinates are not automatically independent random variables. The correct probabilistic object for an observer resolving only a subspace is therefore P(\Delta X_\perp\mid\Delta X_{\rm obs}), not the unconditional P(\Delta X_\perp). A correlation law such as \mathbb E\!\left(|\Delta X_\perp|^2\mid r\right) =\alpha r^2 would imply \mathbb E(R_d^2\mid r)=(1+\alpha)r^2, so full coincidence follows as the visible separation r\to0. 2.2 Interaction through a lower-depth carrier The current V2 cross-depth theorem gives a different mechanism. For κ = +0.7 the ratios are approximately 5.29, 5.42, and 5.48 for the two-, four-, and six-petal initial preparations; for κ = −0.7 they are 1.90, 1.86, and 1.84. These are dimensionless transient test results, not physical atomic power estimates. Initial nuclear relaxation was not assumed; the induced free oscillation contributes. Reversing the coupling sign changes interference without changing the electron state. The simulation does not include radiative backreaction itself. A fixed-radius proton benchmark For an illustrative ordinary electron at fixed distance R from a small proton, its quasistatic field at the proton is E_e = e r̂/(4πε₀R²), whereas its relative dipole is d_e = −eR r̂. Define the nuclear electric polarizability volume α_V by p_N = 4πε₀α_V E_e. In the static-response regime, p_N=-\frac{\alpha_V}{R^3}d_e,\qquad d_{\rm total}=\left(1-\frac{\alpha_V}{R^3}\right)d_e. This is the favorable sign for partial electric-dipole cancellation. As a versioned benchmark, the PDG 2024 proton listing gives α_V = (11.2±0.4)×10⁻⁴ fm³. The NIST CODATA 2022 table gives a₀ = 5.29177210544×10⁴ fm. Their central values give \frac{\alpha_V}{a_0^3}=7.56\times10^{-18}. Thus ordinary static proton polarization is much too small to cancel an ordinary fixed-radius Bohr-scale electron dipole in this benchmark. This is an amplitude ratio, not the size of every nuclear correction to atomic spectroscopy. It is not a prediction that the atomic electron follows a classical Bohr circle. The older versioned polarizability is used solely for reproducibility of an order-of-magnitude comparison, not as a claim of the latest recommended average. Limits of that estimate Do not average R^{-3} over the ideal displayed petal center crossings: the detector map has not been identified as electric charge position, and the point-source/nuclear-dipole approximations fail at nuclear overlap. A proper calculation uses the finite source, spatially varying nuclear response, physical frequency dependence, and the electromagnetic propagator. Near nuclear resonances, static polarizability is insufficient and absorption must be included. Magnetic and spin channels have not been bounded here. If V2 predicts a much stronger response through its extra-dimensional projection, it must derive that enhancement and check it against nuclear response and atomic measurements. The existence of feedback is established within the candidate model; the enhancement and orbit stabilization are not. Reproduction and related nuclear_feedback_checks.py checks the neutral-pair dipole identity, interference algebra, and the versioned fixed-radius numerical ratio, separately from its dimensionless simulations. Nuclear response feedback — reciprocal action and coupled electron–nucleus evolution. Orbit electromagnetic spectrum — why a detector trajectory cannot automatically be used as an electromagnetic point source. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Nuclear response feedback
summary: A reciprocal electron–nuclear polarization model produces retarded feedback and coupled modes, with energy-checked evolution of circular and petalled preparations.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A reciprocal electron–nuclear polarization model produces retarded feedback and coupled modes, with energy-checked evolution of circular and petalled preparations. Scope and missing physical input This is a possible feedback extension of the already existing orbit-plus-precession construction, not the origin of its petals. The unperturbed h₀ below already supplies the selected exchange and clock; the induced response perturbs that prescribed motion. These calculations do not derive the precession lock from Coulomb binding or establish that nuclear feedback is necessary for it. In particular, this electric-dipole model does not calculate induced magnetic feedback; that requires a magnetic/current response and its reciprocal coupling. This extends the actual-orbit coefficient dynamics with a responding nuclear electric dipole. It is a semiclassical mean-field model: c describes the electron's section amplitudes and p a collective nuclear polarization. It is not a microscopic proton calculation or a replacement by stationary orbitals. Magnetic/spin response, nuclear recoil, and radiative damping need distinct terms; the recoil and combined-source issues are treated separately. The nucleus responds to the electron's local electric field, not necessarily to its far-field dipole. Let F_i be the Hermitian matrix for that local field in the full retained electron section space, so E_{e,i} = c†F_i c. Once the physical observer charge matrix R(x) is known, a quasistatic nonoverlapping source would give F_i=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\int R(x)\frac{(R_N-x)_i}{|R_N-x|^3}\,d^3x. Finite nuclear size and overlapping charge require a regularized source calculation. Retardation requires the electromagnetic Green function and current, not this instantaneous Coulomb expression. The V2 current map still has to determine F_i; it cannot generally be inferred from a dipole matrix D_i alone. For the explicit diagnostic below we assume one channel F = κD and leave κ uncalibrated. One reciprocal action For one nuclear electric-polarization component, choose strength s_N > 0 and frequency Ω_N > 0. Its static polarizability is α_N(0) = s_N/Ω_N². With c†c = 1, the action is S=\int dt\left[i\hbar c^\dagger\dot c-c^\dagger h_0c +\frac{\dot p^2-\Omega_N^2p^2}{2s_N}+p\,c^\dagger Fc\right]. Both equations follow from the same interaction: i\hbar\dot c=(h_0-pF)c,\qquad \ddot p+\Omega_N^2p=s_Nc^\dagger Fc. Thus the nucleus is driven by the electron, while its induced dipole enters the electron Hamiltonian as −pF. Keeping only the first effect would not be a backreaction model. The conserved energy is E=c^\dagger h_0c+\frac{\dot p^2+\Omega_N^2p^2}{2s_N} -p\,c^\dagger Fc. In the static mean-field limit, minimizing over p gives p = α_N(0)⟨F⟩ and energy shift −α_N(0)⟨F⟩²/2. The factor one half is required because energy is stored in the polarized nucleus. This is not the operator shift −α_N(0)F²/2 obtained in a suitable fast, quantized oscillator elimination: electron–nuclear correlations and fluctuations distinguish that quantum treatment from the present mean-field model. Adding an internal damping term γ_N ṗ with γ_N ≥ 0 gives Ė = −γ_N ṗ²/s_N. Nuclear polarization does not provide an inexhaustible energy supply. This phenomenological damping is not the coherent radiation reaction of the complete atom, which must be derived from the combined source. Induced charge and current A nuclear polarization density P_N(x,t) = p(t)G_N(x−R_N) along the selected axis, with a normalized centered finite profile G_N, supplies ρ_pol = −∇·P_N and j_pol = ∂_tP_N. These satisfy continuity identically and carry zero net charge but dipole p. For a moving R_N, differentiating the full translated profile includes its motion. The nuclear net charge and center-of-mass current are additional sources, not part of this zero-net-charge polarization term. A magnetic response would add ∇×M_N to the current and require its own response function. Retarded response and return field With e^{-iωt} convention, the nuclear susceptibility is \alpha_N(\omega)=\frac{s_N}{\Omega_N^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_N\omega}. For positive ω and nonnegative damping its imaginary part is nonnegative. A harmonic local field F_ω deposits average power ω Im(α_N)|F_ω|²/2 in this damped oscillator. Resonant enhancement therefore cannot be considered without phase, absorption, and backreaction. On the unperturbed actual orbit, the electron's response to −pF is \chi_{FF}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}c_0^\dagger[F(t),F(s)]c_0, \qquad \delta\langle F\rangle=\chi_{FF}*p. Here the star denotes the causal time integral. Hence p = α_N*(F₀+χ_FF*p). The companion expression δd_i = χ_{D_iF}*p gives the change in the electron's measured dipole. For a nonstationary orbit these are generally two-time kernels. A scalar frequency denominator is justified only for a time-translation-invariant channel, a justified orbit-phase average, or a Floquet generalization. In the scalar stationary channel F = κD, write the electron susceptibility as χ_e. Solving the two response equations gives p=\frac{\alpha_N\kappa}{1-\alpha_N\kappa^2\chi_e}\,d_0, \qquad d_{\rm total}=\frac{1+\alpha_N\kappa}{1-\alpha_N\kappa^2\chi_e}\,d_0. The denominator determines feedback and coupled poles. The numerator determines electron–nucleus electric-dipole interference. They are distinct: changing κ to −κ leaves the feedback denominator unchanged but changes the radiation amplitude. Any use of this formula also needs the physical conversion between local field and dipole represented by κ. Coupled frequencies and stability are calculable, not automatic For a positive-response oscillator approximation χ_e = s_e/(Ω_e²−ω²), s_e > 0, and zero damping, the coupled frequencies obey \omega_\pm^2=\frac{\Omega_e^2+\Omega_N^2 \pm\sqrt{(\Omega_e^2-\Omega_N^2)^2+4\kappa^2s_es_N}}2. Both squared frequencies are positive precisely when κ²s_es_N < Ω_e²Ω_N². Near resonance the modes mix; at stronger coupling this particular quadratic model becomes unstable. Conservative mode mixing does not by itself attract preparations into a preferred locked orbit. The previously calculated electron response can have either sign depending on its prepared occupations, so positivity of s_e must not be assumed for every orbit channel. Direct reciprocal evolution on the actual section model The executable diagnostic uses the full section spaces at L = 1, 2, 3, not just the four initially occupied modes. Its h₀ = ℏνĜ_L and D = (T_34+T_43)/2 in chosen dipole units are the earlier geometric candidate. It also initializes the three-state ring embedded at degree 2. No field frequencies are fitted to experimental lines. Illustrative dimensionless parameters are ℏ = ν = 1, Ω_N = 1.3, s_N = 0.8, κ = ±0.7, γ_N = 0. The initial polarization and its velocity are zero. These parameters are deliberately visible-response test values, not estimates of the proton's response. Evolution runs to t = 20. The integrator alternates exact half-steps of the free electron/nucleus flow and an exact coupling step. During the latter p is fixed and ⟨F⟩ is conserved, so c → exp(iΔt pF/ℏ)c and ṗ → ṗ+s_NΔt⟨F⟩. This preserves coefficient norm; the second-order splitting's energy error is checked by halving the step from 0.02 to 0.01. preparation maximum nuclear dipole magnitude final 1−fidelity to unforced orbit maximum energy error two petals 0.102915 0.0003331 5.2×10⁻⁸ four petals 0.122709 0.0016087 7.4×10⁻⁸ six petals 0.129525 0.0023806 8.3×10⁻⁸ ring embedded at degree 2 0.122709 0.0016087 7.4×10⁻⁸ The degree-2 ring and four-petal preparations give the same active clock response for this particular single-channel probe; it does not distinguish their spectator amplitude occupations. That is a property of the chosen coupling, not an identification of their actual orbits. Changing κ's sign gives the same evolved electron state and opposite nuclear dipole. Postprocessing the combined dipole acceleration changes the radiation diagnostic, as expected. Both signs give nonzero radiation diagnostics in these transient runs; no cancellation or attracting stable atom is found. Radiation is not fed back into this conservative integrator, so its excellent energy conservation must not be presented as proof of radiative stability. Outcome This provides a reciprocal, energy-audited electric-polarization feedback model. It can shift and mix modes and change the combined radiation. Whether it selects V2's observed orbit families depends on the actual nuclear susceptibility, local-field matrices, and radiation reaction. The companion benchmark tests the scale of ordinary proton polarization without claiming it bounds every multidimensional source map. Reproduction and related nuclear_feedback_checks.py checks the feedback algebra, passive nuclear response, coupled-mode threshold, four orbit integrations, norm/energy convergence, sign reversal, and total-dipole diagnostics. No microscopic nuclear response is derived by these tests. Geometric probe selection — section-space matrices used for the explicit diagnostic. Nuclear radiation benchmark — recoil, source interference, and a sourced proton-scale comparison. Ring section embedding — three-state circular preparation in the degree-2 carrier. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Nuclear stability test
summary: Coherent radiation and passivity impose a precise dark-mode condition for persistent dipole motion, while the ordinary proton benchmark falls far short of cancellation.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Coherent radiation and passivity impose a precise dark-mode condition for persistent dipole motion, while the ordinary proton benchmark falls far short of cancellation. Question and present verdict This is a conditional radiation/polarization test, not a test of whether precession can produce petals: the visualization already contains that construction. It also does not evaluate induced nuclear magnetic feedback. Its dipole cancellation conditions must not be promoted to necessary conditions for every physical realization of the 6D precessing orbit. Can the induced nuclear response stabilize V2's actual electron orbits? The preceding simulations demonstrated feedback but did not establish this. This note adds coherent electric-dipole radiation to the harmonic response equations and tests necessary conditions for persistent passive motion. It is not a fully nonlinear Maxwell–Dirac–nucleus solution. The ordinary, low-frequency, fixed-Bohr-radius proton-polarization mechanism is too weak to cancel that benchmark electron dipole. A nonradiating coupled mode is mathematically possible in the ideal two-dipole model, but requires specific matching and absence of loss. Existing V2 equations have not selected those conditions or supplied the physical local-field matrix and nuclear susceptibility. Thus this is a conditional exclusion plus an exact target for the remaining calculation, not a general no-go for 6D orbits. Periodic motion must pass an energy test For a passive isolated system with no incident power, Poynting balance gives \Delta E_{\rm recoverable} =-\int_0^T(P_{\rm outward}+P_{\rm internal\ loss})\,dt. Take a sphere surrounding the source in the radiation zone and a complete period, so periodically stored near-field energy returns to its original value. A genuinely periodic state with the same stored energy after T requires zero average outgoing radiation and zero irreversible internal loss. Nuclear feedback can exchange energy within the system, but cannot replace energy escaping to infinity indefinitely. A metastable orbit with slow decay is a different target; it needs a calculated lifetime. This argument does not forbid a moving multidimensional state whose physical electromagnetic source is nonradiating. It also does not apply classical moving-charge radiation to a stationary quantum atomic source. The physical current, rather than the visual outline, is what matters. Coherent radiative response Use one spatial dipole channel with electron dipole d and nuclear dipole p, and time dependence Re[(d,p)e^{-iωt}]. For a passive two-oscillator diagnostic, let s_e,s_N > 0, bare frequencies Ω_e,Ω_N, real reciprocal coupling κ, and internal damping γ_e,γ_N ≥ 0. Neither susceptibility here already includes radiative damping. To leading electric-dipole order, both sources radiate through d+p. Define r_rad = 1/(6πε₀c³). The inverse response is M(\omega)= \begin{pmatrix} (\Omega_e^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_e\omega)/s_e&-\kappa\\ -\kappa&(\Omega_N^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_N\omega)/s_N \end{pmatrix} -ir_{\rm rad}\omega^3 \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}. The last term is the common dipole radiation field, not two independent radiative damping terms. It retains electron–nucleus interference. This frequency-domain test avoids integrating an unregularized third-derivative radiation-reaction equation with runaway solutions. Finite spatial phase, higher multipoles, and the full causal high-frequency response are outside this leading-order model. For v = (d,p), direct multiplication gives -\operatorname{Im}(v^\dagger Mv) =r_{\rm rad}\omega^3|d+p|^2 +\frac{\gamma_e\omega}{s_e}|d|^2 +\frac{\gamma_N\omega}{s_N}|p|^2. Multiplication by ω/2 yields the time-averaged radiated and absorbed power. The radiation normalization agrees with the dipole-power derivation in UT Austin's radiation notes. Every term is nonnegative for positive ω. Therefore a real-frequency source-free mode Mv = 0 must have d+p = 0 and no internal loss in either occupied component. If γ_N > 0, a nonzero nuclear cancellation dipole cannot give an exactly persistent passive mode in this model. This positivity calculation is for passive positive-response electron and nuclear oscillators. Some prepared section-space electron responses have population-dependent signs; those require their full dynamical treatment. The isolated-system energy requirement remains applicable without assuming an equilibrium susceptibility. An exact dark-mode condition Set γ_e = γ_N = 0 and p = −d ≠ 0. The remaining real equations require \omega_d^2=\Omega_e^2+\kappa s_e =\Omega_N^2+\kappa s_N>0. Equivalently, Ω_e²−Ω_N²+κ(s_e−s_N) = 0. A positive-definite conservative energy and this matching condition admit a dipole-dark normal mode. The diagnostic constructs one explicitly, then shows that changing a frequency or adding nuclear absorption destroys that exact dark solution. This proves mathematical possibility, not physical selection or attraction. Even a perfect dipole-dark mode can radiate through omitted multipoles. It is not automatically the prepared petalled trajectory. Every actual nonzero source harmonic and radiation channel must pass the corresponding test; petal count alone does not tell us which electromagnetic harmonics are present. For constant κ and a single lossless Lorentz nuclear response, the driven cancellation equation 1+κ α_N(ω) = 0 has at most one positive squared frequency. Arbitrary multi-harmonic cancellation is not automatic. How far the ordinary proton benchmark is from cancellation For the previously derived fixed-radius electrostatic geometry, κ = −1/(4πε₀R³), and α_N(0) = 4πε₀α_V. Cancellation requires an induced dipole comparable to the electron dipole, hence |κ α_N(ω)| approximately 1 with the correct phase. The versioned benchmark has η = α_V/a₀³ = 7.56×10⁻¹⁸. Relative to its static response, this requires an enhancement of approximately 1.32×10¹⁷. The inputs are the PDG 2024 proton polarizability and CODATA 2022 Bohr radius, as documented in the companion benchmark. This is not a bound on all nuclear corrections to spectroscopy or on an unspecified V2 projection. In the one-pole nuclear model, normalized cancellation amplitude is \frac{d+p}{d}=1-\frac{\eta} {1-\omega^2/\Omega_N^2-i\gamma_N\omega/\Omega_N^2} when electron backreaction is temporarily excluded solely to test the required nuclear amplitude and phase. For zero damping it vanishes at 1−ω²/Ω_N² = η, or relative detuning (Ω_N−ω)/Ω_N ≈ 3.78×10⁻¹⁸. For small residual amplitude, γ_Nω/Ω_N² must be much smaller than η as well. At the same real detuning with imaginary part equal to η, the residual amplitude is 1/√2, not near zero. The exact source-free mode must additionally satisfy the coupled matching condition above; a zero of the driven amplitude alone is insufficient. These numbers do not propose an actual ultra-narrow nuclear resonance. They quantify what would be required to rescue this particular benchmark using the assumed one-pole response. Ordinary proton Compton measurements constrain its electric and magnetic polarizabilities; an independently measured example is the MAMI result. No matching atomic-frequency nuclear response has been derived here. Replacing the ordinary response with a resonant or multidimensional one without deriving its spectrum would merely introduce the desired answer as a parameter. What is now determined, and what is not Determined: mere induction does not establish stability; coherent radiation and internal absorption give explicit loss conditions; the two-dipole model has a sharply specified exceptional dark mode; the ordinary static proton benchmark misses the required cancellation amplitude by about 17 orders of magnitude. The prior conservative feedback simulations cannot be cited as evidence for radiative stabilization. Not determined: whether V2's actual projected source, nuclear spectrum, magnetic response, and full coupled field dynamics produce a nonradiating or sufficiently long-lived bound orbit. The current project leaves those physical quantities unspecified. This cannot be decided uniquely by further tuning the illustrative oscillator. The next substantive task is to derive the local-field/current map and nuclear response from the proposed action, or identify a measured response with the same physical coupling. Reproduction and related nuclear_stability_checks.py verifies the coherent loss identity on complex amplitudes, the tuned dark mode and its failure under absorption/mismatch, and the single-frequency cancellation condition. High-precision arithmetic resolves the small benchmark detuning. It does not claim a complete radiative time evolution or a V2 stability proof. The diagnostic uses explicit runtime checks that remain active under Python optimization. It reports 88 executed numerical evaluations across ten named conditions, plus the measured loss-identity residual, not a bare PASS label. An in-memory mutation reversing the response matrix's dissipative sign failed at the loss-identity check with exit status 1 under both normal and optimized Python. The correct script also runs its checks under optimization. This verifies that the checks can reject that error, not that they exhaust all possible errors. Constructed matching examples and algebraic identities remain internal model-consistency tests, not independent physical evidence. Nuclear response feedback — reciprocal dynamics whose earlier simulations excluded radiative feedback. Nuclear radiation benchmark — source geometry, recoil, and versioned numerical inputs. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Orbit current projection
summary: A conserved electromagnetic source requires a specified current projection, not identification with the detector-averaged orbit image.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A conserved electromagnetic source requires a specified current projection, not identification with the detector-averaged orbit image. Scope This starts the electromagnetic test of the actual multidimensional orbits in the demo, including the circle and two-, four-, and six-petal cases. It does not replace them with stationary orbitals. The coefficient ray [c], the sector point [Z], and the Dirac field on physical space remain distinct until a physical bridge is specified. Bound within, free without, section 8, already proposes a fibre-integrated electron current coupled to the photon. Higher-dimensional polarization, sections 3 and 6, adds the invariant representation filter. These specify a route to a vertex, not the numerical source produced by a particular c(t). The depth-two photon sector must also be related to the electromagnetic field seen by an ordinary spatial observer; its spatial depth is not a license to replace ordinary Maxwell propagation by a two-space-dimensional wave equation. Conserved pushforward Let a density n and tangent current J on a fixed sector manifold Q obey ∂t n + div_Q J = 0. Assume no boundary flux, or sufficient decay, and a smooth physical charge readout X_t: Q → R³. This is a conditional source construction, not an identification of X_t with the demo's apparatus map. For charge e* (negative for an electron), define distributions \rho(t,x)=e_*\int_Q n(t,u)\delta^{(3)}(x-X_t(u))\,d\mu(u), j(t,x)=e_*\int_Q \left[dX_t(J)(t,u)+n(t,u)\partial_tX_t(u)\right] \delta^{(3)}(x-X_t(u))\,d\mu(u). For every compactly supported smooth test function f, integration by parts gives \frac{d}{dt}\int\rho f\,d^3x =e_*\int_Q\left[J\cdot d(f\circ X_t) +n\nabla f(X_t)\cdot\partial_tX_t\right]d\mu =\int j\cdot\nabla f\,d^3x. Thus ∂tρ + ∇·j = 0, with total charge e*∫n. The term involving ∂_tX_t is required for a moving readout/frame. This proof allows many-to-one maps; it needs neither an inverse map nor a choice of one point on each fibre. Gauge invariance of ∫(j·A − ρφ) dt d³x follows, up to boundary terms, from this continuity equation. Gauge invariance alone does not select X_t. For a point trajectory U(t) with n = δ_U and J = U̇δ_U, these equations reduce to ρ = e_*δ(x−Γ(t)), j = e_*Γ̇δ(x−Γ(t)), where Γ = X_t(U(t)). This is precisely the extra assumption needed before a displayed curve can be treated as a moving electromagnetic point charge. An invariant polarization filter acting on a spinor current needs its own covariant conservation check. Arbitrarily deleting current components does not inherit this proof. A concrete projected action must provide the conserved source, its normalization, and its observer-space interpretation. Why the exposure image is insufficient The demo's registration density is a full-period average of G_σ(x−Γ(t)). Its being stationary does not make the instantaneous source stationary. For a fixed normalized centered spatial kernel, the conditional source ρ = e_*G_σ(x−Γ), j = e_*Γ̇G_σ(x−Γ) conserves charge, but still has electric dipole d(t) = e_*Γ(t). Spatial broadening alone does not smooth that dipole's time dependence. A physical frequency-dependent form factor can affect high-frequency radiation; that is additional source physics, not a consequence of plotting a blurred exposure. A complete-period average of a periodic conserved source has divergence-free mean current. It discards nonzero time harmonics. Computing radiated power from that mean is not computing the mean power of the original source. Calculation to close Derive the charged projected action and its current; evaluate it on the actual bound orbit; push it to the physical electromagnetic observer with its polarization filter; then compute its multipoles and response to a probe. The source must include the nucleus and any compensating field contribution, not only the electron, when testing a complete bound system. The follow-up spectrum test gives explicit constraints for several orbit shapes and separates a literal point-source assignment from a fixed bilinear current assignment. Neither assignment is selected by the current V2 text. Related Orbit electromagnetic spectrum — applies this distinction to the circle, petalled orbits, and detuned cases. title: Orbit electromagnetic spectrum
summary: Circle, petalled, and detuned actual orbits give distinct conditional radiation diagnostics and finite-generator constraints on electromagnetic probes.

Summary: Circle, petalled, and detuned actual orbits give distinct conditional radiation diagnostics and finite-generator constraints on electromagnetic probes. Two explicit source hypotheses The current projection audit identifies a missing physical map, not a reason to stop calculating. Here we test two conditional assignments, without claiming either follows from V2: The displayed trajectory is the electromagnetic point-charge position. The current is bilinear in a fixed linear field lift of the coefficient vector c, so its dipole is c†D_i c for fixed Hermitian matrices D_i. These hypotheses generally disagree. For L ≥ 1, z(\theta)=\Gamma_x+i\Gamma_y=R|\cos L\theta|e^{i\theta}. The circle is the separate ring sector z = Re^{iθ}. This comparison is not a claim that different physical atomic states have equal radii or clocks. For ordinary nonrelativistic electromagnetic point sources, or the long-wavelength electric-dipole approximation to an extended source, \langle P\rangle=\frac{\langle|\ddot d|^2\rangle}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}, \qquad P_{\rm circle}=\frac{e_*^2R^2\nu^4}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}. The external electromagnetic formula and its assumptions are derived in UT Austin's dipole-radiation notes, equation 15. All orbit substitutions and spectral results below are calculations here. The exact Fourier expansion is \frac zR=\frac2\pi e^{i\theta} +\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n \left[e^{i(1+2nL)\theta}+e^{i(1-2nL)\theta}\right], \qquad a_n=\frac{2(-1)^{n+1}}{\pi(4n^2-1)}. Both senses of rotation contribute to the planar acceleration norm. With the first N sideband pairs retained, Parseval gives \frac{P_N}{P_{\rm circle}}=\frac4{\pi^2} +\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n^2 \left[(1+2nL)^4+(1-2nL)^4\right]. Each summand tends to 8L⁴/π², not zero. The formal sum diverges. Equivalently, at each center crossing the one-sided velocity jump has magnitude 2RLν; the raw displayed curve has no square-integrable acceleration. Therefore it cannot be inserted unregularized into a finite-power point-charge calculation. This excludes that unregularized source prescription, not the smooth 6D coefficient orbit. The absolute-value observer readout creates the cusp. For an extended source the dipole approximation cannot be extended to arbitrarily high frequencies; the divergence is not a calculated infinite physical power for V2. The source's form factor and temporal regularity must be specified before taking that limit. Detuned multi-maximum cases For the exchange perturbation, put a = Ω/ν and m = (g/Ω)². Then z/R=r(\theta)e^{i\theta},\qquad r=\sqrt{1-m\sin^2(a\theta)}, r'=-\frac{ma\sin2a\theta}{2r},\qquad r''=-\frac{ma^2\cos2a\theta}{r} -\frac{m^2a^2\sin^22a\theta}{4r^3}, \frac{\langle P\rangle}{P_{\rm circle}} =\left\langle(r''-r)^2+4(r')^2\right\rangle. Choose the demo's +1-maximum alignments g/ν = L, a = L + 1/2, δ/ν = √(L+1/4): starting ideal case detuned maxima per clock turn δ/ν conditional planar P/P_circle circle, separate sector no radial modulation — 1 two petals, L = 1 3 1.11803399 1.88272246 four petals, L = 2 5 1.50000000 16.80500000 six petals, L = 3 7 1.80277564 85.88942381 The detuned images close in one clock turn; their full coefficient rays need two turns when ε = 0. The numbers use quadrature independently checked against Fourier acceleration and a coarser grid. They are not measured atomic emission rates. With a nonzero depth readout Γ_z, its squared acceleration adds to the planar result if it is also identified as physical charge position. No nuclear recoil or radiation reaction is included. Detuning removes the cusp but does not supply a nonradiating bound state. Fixed bilinear source: an exact frequency constraint Suppose a time-independent linear lift ψ(u,t) = Σ_a c_a(t)s_a(u) into an admissible Dirac field on physical space bundle has actually been supplied. title: Projected Dirac current
summary: Varying a minimally gauged diagnostic action fixes the current form and normalization identities, while projection exposes missing-mode contributions.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Varying a minimally gauged diagnostic action fixes the current form and normalization identities, while projection exposes missing-mode contributions. What the written action permits The six-dimensional electron module, section 8, supplies a diagnostic Dirac action with unspecified physical connections and nuclear interaction. The scalar self-contact term is algebraic in ψ̄ψ. It does not itself determine an electromagnetic connection. Conditional on a charged U(1) connection a, take ℏ = c = 1 and D_A=\nabla_A+iq a_A,\qquad \mathcal L_m=\bar\psi(i\gamma^AD_A-m-V_N)\psi -\frac\kappa2(\bar\psi\psi)^2. Here q is signed charge, A is a spacetime/sector index, and V_N is the scalar term in that diagnostic action, not an already-derived Coulomb field. Under ψ → e^{-iqχ}ψ and a → a+dχ the action is invariant. Variation gives J^A=-\frac{\delta S_m}{\delta a_A}=q\bar\psi\gamma^A\psi. The field equations and their adjoints give ∇_A J^A = 0. Algebraic neutral scalar interactions contribute no additional derivative with respect to a. Derivative interactions, a-dependent projectors, or added orbit-driving terms must instead be varied too. This is the usual minimal-coupling construction; see Tong's QED section. It derives a current from an assumed charged action, not electric charge or the physical U(1) identification from the master theory. The coefficient Z in −ZF²/4 also matters: canonical normalization of the photon gives coupling q/√Z. A current formula alone does not predict the fine-structure constant. Projection and total charge For fixed admissible mode sections s_a with ψ = Σ_a c_a s_a, define the Gram matrix G_ab = ∫s_a†s_b dμ. The kinetic action is ∫dt [iℏ c†G ċ − c†h c]. The local charge matrix is R_ab(u) = q s_a(u)†s_b(u), and therefore \int R(u)d\mu=qG. In orthonormal coordinates b = G^{1/2}c, total charge is q b†b. Multiplicity of modes does not multiply a normalized particle's electric charge. A moving orthonormal basis S(t) adds −iℏ S†Ṡ to the energy Hamiltonian; its response to a probe cannot be omitted if the basis depends on that probe. After a specified conserved pushforward to observer space, the dipole and integrated current matrices satisfy D_i=\int x_iR(x)d^3x,\qquad I_i=\int j_i(x)d^3x=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h,D_i] for time-independent matrices, no boundary flux, and a closed projected subspace. This is a consistency condition, not a way to determine D_i from h alone. Choosing D_i arbitrarily and defining I_i by this equation does not derive the physical charge distribution. Exact truncation defect Let P be an orthogonal projector and Q = 1−P. Suppose the full local operator identity is (i/ℏ)[h,R]+div j = 0. Direct compression gives \frac{i}{\hbar}[PhP,PRP]+P(\operatorname{div}j)P =-\frac{i}{\hbar}PhQRP+\frac{i}{\hbar}PRQhP. All operators here act on the retained space where appropriate. The right side vanishes if h preserves that space. Merely preserving charge globally is weaker than satisfying local conservation after projection. Even if QhP = 0 without a probe, a dipole D can have QDP ≠ 0. Then the unforced orbit is exactly retained but its weak-field response need not be. Projecting D to PDP before calculating response discards intermediate Q modes. Integrating those modes out consistently produces additional, generally frequency-dependent response terms. For a linear probe with QhP = 0 at zero field, these include terms quadratic in the applied field in the effective action; their variation contributes to linear response. One cannot infer their absence from PDP = 0. The geometric example below demonstrates this explicitly without fitting a spectrum. Charge versus degree The degree L of O(L) is not automatically the electric charge of a particle in that section space. If every connection is the Lth tensor power of one physical fluctuating connection, its infinitesimal coupling scales with L. That is not a universal electron charge across orbit families. A model can instead specify different background fluxes and a universally normalized electromagnetic perturbation, or distinguish a geometric twist from the electromagnetic bundle. Which interpretation V2 uses must be stated in the action. Representation degree alone does not settle it. Reproduction and boundary projected_current_checks.py checks the projection-defect identity, its disappearance for an invariant subspace, and charge normalization with a nonorthogonal Gram metric. The selected-line and geometric-probe notes apply this framework to actual orbit evolution. The remaining physical inputs are the master-selected bundle, orbit-driving term, electromagnetic observer map, nuclear contribution, and normalization. Related Orbit current projection — conserved pushforward and distinction from the exposure image. Selected spinor line current — a global candidate lift and the current required by its orbit drive. Geometric probe selection — exact mode integrals and an explicit missed response under four-mode truncation. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Balanced spatial branches with an exact linear frequency
summary: Balanced holomorphic fields on the specified physical CP3 geometry have an exact normalized linear frequency for the smooth moment kernel and no exponential modes in their complete spatial linearization.
text:
Summary: Balanced holomorphic fields on the specified physical CP3 geometry have an exact normalized linear frequency for the smooth moment kernel and no exponential modes in their complete spatial linearization. A spatial solution of the normalization problem A nonconstant spatial field can produce a constant scalar potential without requiring the interaction kernel itself to be constant. The distinction matters for the source-preservation theorem: its whole-band degeneracy conclusion assumes a coherent holomorphic section. Certain noncoherent holomorphic superpositions instead balance their source moments and preserve an exact linear branch for the already specified smooth spatial moment kernel. The result below constructs such fields and treats their complete spatial linearization, including the entire holomorphic multiplet and the excited source modes. It solves a conditional spatial normalization and spectral stability problem. The kernel's origin in the master action and its causal completion remain open. Use the specified physical CP3 geometry, with its undetermined Fubini–Study radius R. Its six spatial directions are ordinary and macroscopic; there is no compactification. The calculation uses the canonical Spin^c bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L) and spatial Dirac operator \mathscr D_L=\sqrt2( ar\partial_L+ ar\partial_L^\dagger). The degree L is a geometric input, not the cumulative mass-band label N=n-1. No identification of L with the electron or muon mode index is made. Write m=3 and r=m+1=4 for CP3; the mathematical formulas extend to CPm. Work first in radius units and unit spatial measure d
u. For the one field, define  egin{aligned} \sigma_\psi&=\psi^\dagger eta\psi,& M_\psi&=\int P_Z\sigma_\psi(Z)\,d

Equation (1) is the normalized kernel K_1(Z,W)=r|Z^\dagger W|^2 on unit homogeneous representatives, with the physical measure understood as above. Balanced holomorphic sections give exact branches Let H_L=H^0(\mathcal O(L)) be the complete holomorphic zero space. For a unit section \chi\in H_L, impose the balance condition  oxed{M_\chi= rac{I_r}{r}.} 	ag{2} Then V_\chi=1 at every spatial point, while \mathscr D_L\chi=0 and  eta\chi=\chi. Consequently  oxed{\psi(t)=e^{-igt}\chi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=1,\qquad \omega=g,\qquad \mathcal E_g(\chi)= rac g2.} 	ag{3} This is an exact nonlinear spatial solution for every real g, not a small-coupling expansion or a frozen-potential calculation. The case L=1 does not satisfy this argument. For any pure degree-one section, the moment is (I_r+aa^\dagger)/(r+1) with a unit, so it is not isotropic when r>1. Balance does not make the field density spatially constant. At a coordinate pole its density is D_L/r, whereas at Z=(1,e^{i\pi/L},0,\ldots,0)/\sqrt2 the polynomial in (4) vanishes. The higher spatial harmonics retain a definite shape. Physical unitary isometries rotate that shape while preserving (2). Their real spatial functions are f_a(Z)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_ZT_a),\qquad u_a=f_a\chi. Let P_0 project onto all of H_L and set v_a=P_0u_a, w_a=(I-P_0)u_a. All three Gram matrices can therefore be treated as real symmetric matrices without discarding any complex field perturbation.
