title: Scalar Dirac branch on proposed CP3
summary: The specified twisted Dirac field on physical CP3 admits an exact spatial symmetry reduction and a small scalar-contact branch, with opposite chirality and an explicit cubic frequency correction.
text:
Summary: The specified twisted Dirac field on physical CP3 admits an exact spatial symmetry reduction and a small scalar-contact branch, with opposite chirality and an explicit cubic frequency correction. Physical geometry, bundle and normalization The proposed electron \mathbb{CP}^3 is an actual six-dimensional physical spatial manifold. This calculation tests a stationary scalar contact field on that geometry. It does not replace the electron–nucleus orbit construction with a stationary orbital. IDWT has no compactified dimensions. Its six electron directions are ordinary macroscopic spatial dimensions of the same kind as the three shared with an ordinary observer. The global CP3 topology and FS metric used here are explicit geometric hypotheses. Mathematical compactness of that candidate does not make any direction hidden, curled up, or small; the physical scale remains undetermined. Results using its finite volume or discrete spatial spectrum are conditional on those geometric hypotheses. Use the specified spinor-line lift: the spin twist \mathcal O(L+2) gives the full bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L) and the spatial Dirac operator \mathscr D_L=\sqrt2( ar\partial_L+ ar\partial_L^\dagger). The integer L\ge0 and its Chern connection remain inputs. This selected construction preserves the full spinor-bundle obstruction. For the derivation, write m for complex dimension, with m=3 in the physical comparison. On \mathbb{CP}^m, the same formulas use the specified canonical Spin^c bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L). Let the FS metric have holomorphic sectional curvature 4/R^2 and physical volume \mathcal V=\pi^mR^{2m}/m!. Its unit-volume measure is d
u=d\mathrm{vol}/\mathcal V. Fix the positive phase norm Q, which is not an assigned electric charge. Write the physical stationary field as \Psi=e^{-i\omega t}\sqrt{Q/\mathcal V}\,\varphi, with \int|\varphi|^2d
u=1. For zero bare mass and local scalar coefficient g, define \varepsilon= rac{gQR}{\mathcal V},\qquad \Omega=R\omega,\qquad  eta=(-1)^{	ext{exterior degree}}. The unit-radius stationary equation and energy per Q/R are  oxed{\Omega\varphi=(\mathscr D_L+\varepsilon\sigma eta)\varphi, \qquad \sigma=\varphi^\dagger eta\varphi,\qquad \mathcal E=\langle\varphi,\mathscr D_L\varphiangle + rac\varepsilon2\int\sigma^2d
u.} 	ag{1} This is a specified spatial reduction of the scalar contact action. Its geometry and connection change the hypotheses of the flat radial theorem. An exact spatial symmetry class Choose a projective center and normalized coherent holomorphic section \chi=\sqrt{D_L}Z_0^L, with D_L= inom{L+m}{m},\qquad t= rac{|Z_0|^2}{|Z|^2},\qquad ho_0=|\chi|^2=D_Lt^L. The radial measure weighted by this section is w(t)dt=ho_0\,m(1-t)^{m-1}dt = rac{t^L(1-t)^{m-1}}{\mathrm B(L+1,m)}dt. 	ag{2} Retain the complete complex functions in the spinor class  oxed{\varphi=\chi\,[F(t)+G(t) ar\partial t].} 	ag{3} The two terms have exterior degrees zero and one. They are spatial spinor components, not two extra dimensions. Smooth F,G give global sections, including at the zeros of \chi. The relevant operator domain is the closure of smooth global sections of this form. Since  ar\partial\chi=0 and  ar\partial(G ar\partial t)=0, the two-form part of the Dirac derivative vanishes identically. The scalar source in (1) also preserves (3). This is therefore an exact invariant class of the spatial field equation, not merely a two-coefficient truncation. For the stated metric, a(t)=| ar\partial t|^2=2t(1-t). The norm and scalar are \|\varphi\|^2=\int_0^1w(|F|^2+a|G|^2)dt, \qquad \sigma=ho_0(|F|^2-a|G|^2). 	ag{4} Adjointness in this weighted measure gives the full Dirac action:  oxed{\mathscr D_L(F\chi)=\sqrt2F'\chi ar\partial t, \qquad \mathscr D_L(G\chi ar\partial t) =- rac{\sqrt2}{w}(waG)'\chi.} 	ag{5} It can also be checked in physical complex coordinates on the chart Z_0
e0. There t=(1+|z|^2)^{-1}, the line metric is t^L, and g^{i ar j}=t^{-1}(\delta_{ij}+z_i ar z_j). For a line-valued one-form \eta, the adjoint is  ar\partial_L^\dagger\eta=-2g^{i ar j} (\partial_i\eta_{ ar j}-Lt ar z_i\eta_{ ar j}). Substituting \eta=G ar\partial t\chi gives \mathscr D_L(G\chi ar\partial t) =-2\sqrt2\,[t(1-t)G'+(L+1-(L+m+1)t)G]\chi. 	ag{6} This independent coordinate formula fixes the metric factors and keeps all components of the spatial derivative. Complete Jacobi modes and the complementary gap On the zero-form part, (5) squares to \mathscr D_L^2(F\chi) =-4[t(1-t)F''+(L+1-(L+m+1)t)F']\chi. 	ag{7} Let p_n be P_n^{(m-1,L)}(2t-1) normalized in w(t)dt, so p_0=1. Jacobi's differential equation gives \mathscr D_L^2(\chi p_n)=\lambda_n^2\chi p_n, \qquad \lambda_n=2\sqrt{n(n+L+m)}. 	ag{8} This agrees with the corresponding twisted Dirac spectral family in Ginoux and Habib, Theorem 4.5, using tautological twist exponent -L-(m+1)/2 when m is odd. Equation (7) derives the needed family directly; no other spectral family is removed from the physical theory by this calculation. For n\ge1, define the normalized one-forms q_n=\mathscr D_L(\chi p_n)/\lambda_n. Then \mathscr D_Lq_n=\lambda_n\chi p_n. The complete basis in (3) consists of \chi, these zero-form modes and their one-form partners. Their energies are zero and \pm\lambda_n. The zero mode is simple in this fixed symmetry class, and the complement has gap \lambda_1=2\sqrt{L+m+1}. In calculations, write F=\sum f_np_n and \sqrt aG=\sum_{n\ge1}h_nQ_n, where Q_n=2\sqrt{t(1-t)}p_n'/\lambda_n. Both coefficient families have the ordinary positive kinetic norm \sum|f_n|^2+\sum|h_n|^2; the scalar source retains their opposite signs. A normalized branch exists at small coupling At \varepsilon=0, \varphi=\chi and \Omega=0 solve (1). Fix its overall phase and add the unit-norm constraint. The linearized stationary map on a perturbation h and frequency change b is (h,b)\longmapsto (\mathscr D_Lh-b\chi,\,2\operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,hangle). It is invertible in the real profile class: the complementary equation uses \mathscr D_L^{-1}, the component along \chi fixes b, and the last equation fixes the remaining amplitude. On spatial Sobolev spaces above the multiplication threshold, this inverse gains one derivative. The cubic source is analytic. The implicit function theorem therefore gives a unique nearby normalized branch in this fixed symmetry class and phase. Elliptic regularity makes it smooth. Its complex extension supplies the allowed time-dependent perturbations. Common physical FS isometries rotate the center and the entire spinor construction together, giving the corresponding family of branches. No preferred electron position relative to a nucleus has been selected. The first correction necessarily includes opposite chirality Set A=\intho_0^2d
u= rac{D_L^2}{D_{2L}},\qquad q=(ho_0-A)\chi,\qquad \eta=-\mathscr D_{L,\perp}^{-1}q. 	ag{9} The projected source has zero component along \chi. For L>0 it is nonzero, and \eta is an odd-chirality one-form. Because ho_0 is a polynomial of degree L, only Jacobi levels 1 through L enter this first correction. The full branch has the expansion \varphi=\chi+\varepsilon\eta+\varepsilon^2\xi+O(\varepsilon^3), \qquad \langle\chi,\xiangle=-	frac12\|\eta\|^2. 	ag{10} The symmetry \varphi(-\varepsilon)= eta\varphi(\varepsilon) makes the frequency odd in \varepsilon. Expanding (1) gives \mathscr D_L\xi=(A+ho_0)\eta. Hence \langleho_0\chi,\xiangle =- rac{3A}{2}\|\eta\|^2-\intho_0|\eta|^2d
u. Projection of the next order onto \chi yields  oxed{\Omega=\varepsilon A-4\varepsilon^3J+O(\varepsilon^5), \qquad \mathcal E= rac{\varepsilon A}{2}-\varepsilon^3J +O(\varepsilon^5), \quad J=A\|\eta\|^2+\intho_0|\eta|^2d
u.} 	ag{11} J>0 for L>0. The vanishing second-order massless correction in the orbit-drive analysis therefore does not imply all-order protection for this nonlinear source. For m=3,L=1, p_1=5t-2 and direct beta integrals give A= rac85,\quad \|\eta\|^2= rac4{125},\quad \intho_0|\eta|^2d
u= rac{48}{875},\quad  oxed{\Omega= rac85\varepsilon- rac{1856}{4375}\varepsilon^3 +O(\varepsilon^5).} 	ag{12} For L=0, the constant section instead solves the full equation exactly with \Omega=\varepsilon. The finite volume of this proposed global geometry supplies the normalization absent from the flat infinite-space comparison. That conclusion is conditional on the global CP3 model and does not invoke compactification. Interpretation and verification The physical frequency is \omega=\Omega/R, with \varepsilon=gQR/\mathcal V. It depends on the specified spatial geometry, norm and complete profile, as in local scalar normalization. The count D_L= inom{L+3}{3} belongs to physical CP3 sections; it is distinct from the auxiliary six-direction cumulative mass count  inom{N+6}{6}. Neither L=N nor a particle mass assignment follows. Existence also does not imply stability. The local-contact instability detects an unstable Dirac complement for every L>0 at sufficiently small nonzero coupling. A smooth physical moment kernel gives a different controlled stability comparison. cp3_scalar_dirac.py retains all complex coefficients in successive finite approximations to (3), with exact quartic quadrature and normalized branch continuation. cp3_scalar_dirac_checks.py checks independent coordinate derivatives, complete component closure, Jacobi normalization, the frequency expansion, conjugate response and uncompressed spatial residuals on refined grids.

title: A trace contribution to the mass current
summary: Adding a trace contraction preserves coherent simplex frequencies and the common core, removes a high-momentum secular degeneracy, and gives a positive conserved norm for the constant far-field linearization; master selection and full spatial stability remain open.
text:
Summary: Adding a trace contraction preserves coherent simplex frequencies and the common core, removes a high-momentum secular degeneracy, and gives a positive conserved norm for the constant far-field linearization; master selection and full spatial stability remain open. The freedom left by the frequency calculation The localized current action produces its simplex frequencies on an isotropic partner current carried by a coherent oscillator ray. Its Hilbert–Schmidt current norm is one inverse choice. The frequency calculation does not fix how the action curves away from that ray. That curvature matters for perturbations and coupling. Let r be the partner rank and let R be any Hermitian retained current. Its matrix size can exceed r because it also retains oscillator indices. Consider the invariant norm  egin{gathered} F_q(R)=\sqrt{qr\operatorname{Tr}(R^2) +(1-q)[\operatorname{Tr}R]^2},\ 0<q\leq1. \end{gathered} 	ag{1} This is positive for every nonzero Hermitian R and smooth there, including when individual eigenvalues vanish. The entire zero current remains a nonsmooth point. At q=1, (1) is the original \sqrt r\|R\|_{\mathrm{HS}}. Use the same complete doubled spinor, partner and oscillator fields as in the localized action. For each retained order k, the current R_k sums the scalar-insertion currents of all grades N\geq k, tracing only their discarded oscillator spectators. Keep the same canonical and spatial Dirac terms and the same binding interaction. Replace only the mass potential by U_{\mathrm{mass},q}=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k\geq0}h_{k,d}F_q(R_k), \qquad h_{k,d}= inom{k+d-1}{d-1}. 	ag{2} One q applies to every grade at the given depth. There is no separate electron or muon mass coefficient in this replacement. The sums are taken on finite grade support, or on a convergent domain where their stated variations exist. Complete variation and the unchanged frequency branch Define a linear map on Hermitian matrices, \mathcal L_q(X)=qrX+(1-q)\operatorname{Tr}(X)I. 	ag{3} The identity has the full retained matrix size. Differentiating the potential, rather than selecting its eigenvalue variations, gives  egin{aligned} 
abla F_q(R)&= rac{\mathcal L_q(R)}{F_q(R)},\ D
abla F_q(R)[X] &= rac{\mathcal L_q(X)}{F_q(R)} - rac{\mathcal L_q(R)\operatorname{Tr}[\mathcal L_q(R)X]} {F_q(R)^3}. \end{aligned} 	ag{4} These formulas retain every matrix direction. In the full field equation, each gradient is lifted back through the same current-splitting map that defined R_k. Its variation includes both the changed field and (4). On the solved coherent core, R_k=ho I_r\otimes P_{z,k}, with P_{z,k} a unit-rank projector. Consequently F_q(R_k)=rho,\qquad 
abla F_q(R_k)=q(I_r\otimes P_{z,k})+(1-q)I. 	ag{5} The occupied field lies in the range of this projector. Both terms in the second expression therefore act on it as their scalar coefficients. Every retained order supplies its original contribution to the frequency:  oxed{\omega_N=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k=0}^Nh_{k,d} =\omega_{0,d} inom{N+d}{d}.} 	ag{6} The complete isolated mass source is unchanged. The lower-spinor sustaining equation and its smooth binding are also unchanged. Thus the same unit-norm core serves every occupied grade, with the same spatial size and the same fixed-point magnitude. The magnitude is not a separate mass variable. The isolated energy and canonical inertia remain E_0=\hbar\omega_NQ and M=\hbar\omega_NQ/c^2. The scalar insertion currents are invariant under the displayed spinor boosts. Since both the potential and its complete source agree on the boosted coherent branch, the localized action's boost and stress argument continues to apply. The common Q=1 condition and the identification of core gap with frequency unit remain independent inverse premises. The change appears in the full occupied-ray Hessian. Write \phi=\sqrtho U and let \mathcal B'_\phi be the complete real-linear spatial binding derivative. In the rotating frame, \mathcal H'_q=  egin{pmatrix}\mathcal A_q&\mathcal B'_\phi\ \mathcal B'_\phi&-2\omega_N I\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathcal A_q(UX)=2q\omega_N U \left(\operatorname{Herm}X-  rac{\operatorname{Tr}\operatorname{Herm}X}{r}Iight). 	ag{7} All complex and conjugate directions remain. The change is a definite partner curvature in the same action, rather than a rescaling of a reported response by its particle mass. Equal trace and exchange contractions Two invariant quadratic expressions in a Hermitian current are \operatorname{Tr}(R^2) and (\operatorname{Tr}R)^2. They are quartic in the original field. Let \mathsf S exchange the two factors of the retained component space. Direct index contraction gives \operatorname{Tr}[(I+\mathsf S)(R\otimes R)] =\operatorname{Tr}(R^2)+(\operatorname{Tr}R)^2. 	ag{8} Giving these two contractions equal coefficients and requiring (5) produces F_*(R)=\sqrt{ rac r{r+1}} \sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(R^2)+(\operatorname{Tr}R)^2}, \qquad q= rac1{r+1}. 	ag{9} At depth six, r=8 and this comparison has q=1/9. At even depth ten, r=32 gives q=1/33. These ranks count field components, not extra spatial dimensions. Equation (8) is finite component algebra; it does not impose a statistical ensemble or a physical compact space. Equal coefficients in (8) are a declared inverse choice. Invariance alone allows the whole family (1), and the master field has not been shown to select (8), its square root, or the shell weights. Thus (9) supplies a concrete comparison without tuning q to the particle masses; it is not a forward derivation of a unique interaction. The limiting wave problem and its exact reduction Use natural units. In the decaying tail of the smooth common-gap core, the nonlinear binding coefficients vanish and the core gap m_c remains. Freeze the limiting direction and the partner frame. A unitary change on the partner index takes the upper background matrix to I_r. The complex-linear spatial block then has the form \mathcal D_p X=(\alpha\cdot p)X+m_c eta X B, \qquad B^\dagger=B,\quad B^2=I, \qquad \mathcal D_p^2=(|p|^2+m_c^2)I. 	ag{10} The last equality follows from \{\alpha_a, eta\}=0; no commuting assumption between independent matrix currents is used. Put \varkappa=\sqrt{|p|^2+m_c^2}. Multiplying each lower component by its corresponding \mathcal D/\varkappa is unitary. Transposing the conjugate matrix component is another unitary change. The entire frozen generator then splits into one trace block G_0(\varkappa) and r^2-1 traceless blocks G_q(\varkappa)=  egin{pmatrix} q\omega&\varkappa&q\omega&0\ \varkappa&-2\omega&0&0\ -q\omega&0&-q\omega&\varkappa\ 0&0&\varkappa&2\omega \end{pmatrix},\qquad \omega=\omega_N. 	ag{11} The evolution convention is e^{-i\Omega t}. Its squared frequencies are  oxed{\Omega_\pm^2=\varkappa^2+2\omega^2 \ \pm\ 2\omega\sqrt{\omega^2+(1-q)\varkappa^2}.} 	ag{12} Both are positive for 0<q\leq1 and \varkappa>0. The trace block has the real frequencies \pm(\sqrt{\omega^2+\varkappa^2}\pm\omega). Both frequency signs have been retained. These statements concern the complete constant limiting operator, not only a radial restriction. For numerical work, the slow root in (12) should be evaluated as \Omega_-^2= rac{\varkappa^2(\varkappa^2+4q\omega^2)} {\varkappa^2+2\omega^2+2\omega\sqrt{\omega^2+(1-q)\varkappa^2}}. 	ag{13} This avoids subtracting large nearly equal numbers. Direct diagonalization at the assigned muon coefficient can otherwise create spurious small imaginary frequencies. The unitary reduction and (13) determine the exact limiting operator's frequencies independently of that conditioning. Real frequencies can still hide amplification At large \varkappa, remove the common fast phase and compress (11) to one propagation direction. The remaining two-component matrix is N_q= rac\omega2  egin{pmatrix}q-2&q\-q&2-q\end{pmatrix},\qquad N_q^2=\omega^2(1-q)I. 	ag{14} For the original norm, q=1, this is nonzero but nilpotent. Its exact propagator is I-itN_1, with largest singular value  oxed{\|I-itN_1\|_2 = rac{\sqrt{4+(\omega t)^2}+|\omega t|}{2}.} 	ag{15} The full finite-wave-number frequencies are real, yet this response grows with elapsed time in the high-momentum limit. It prevents a bound uniform in both time and momentum for the original constant limiting evolution. It does not prove nonlinear instability of the localized core: the coefficient limit, spatially varying core and vacuum regularity are distinct questions. For 0<q<1, the positive matrix H_q= egin{pmatrix}1-q/2&-q/2\-q/2&1-q/2\end{pmatrix} 	ag{16} satisfies H_qN_q=N_q^\dagger H_q. Its eigenvalues are 1 and 1-q, so the compressed response obeys \|e^{-itN_q}\|_2\leq rac1{\sqrt{1-q}}. 	ag{17} For (9) at depth six this bound is 3/\sqrt8=1.060660\ldots. It is a bound for the compressed high-momentum response, not a bound of six percent on every disturbance of a particle. A positive conserved norm for the complete frozen operator There is also a full finite-momentum result. Let \Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-1,-1) and \mu=\varkappa^2+2\omega^2. Define K_q(\varkappa)= rac1{2\omega} \Sigma G_q(\mu I-G_q^2). 	ag{18} Direct multiplication gives K_q^\dagger=K_q and K_qG_q=G_q^\dagger K_q. Its eigenvalues fall into two real quadratic pairs \lambda^2-T_i\lambda+D_i=0, where  egin{aligned} T_1&=(2-q)\varkappa^2+2\omega^2,\ D_1&=(1-q)\varkappa^4+\varkappa^2\omega^2,\ T_2&=(2-q)\varkappa^2+2(q+1)\omega^2,\ D_2&=(1-q)\varkappa^4+[1+4q(1-q)]\varkappa^2\omega^2 +4q\omega^4. \end{aligned} 	ag{19} For 0<q\leq1 and \varkappa>0, each sum and product is positive. The Hermitian matrix K_q is therefore positive. For q<1 and a nonzero gap, \varkappa\geq m_c, elementary bounds further give  rac{1-q}{2-q}I\ \leq\  rac{K_q(\varkappa)}{\varkappa^2} \ \leq\ \left[2-q+2(q+1) rac{\omega^2}{m_c^2}ight]I. 	ag{20} Integrating this conserved Fourier norm proves a bound uniform in time and momentum for the constant limiting evolution. The bound is not uniform in \omega/m_c, nor does it apply automatically to the variable core coefficients. This positive perturbation norm is not the physical Hamiltonian. The regular fixed-norm family with energy unbounded below survives (1), since its current is proportional to I_r and (5) still holds. Reciprocal coupling retains the common-target identity For two independently solved cores of distinct grades N>M at one depth, let ho(x),\sigma(x) be their local partner densities and s=|z^\dagger w|^2 their coherent-ray overlap. Their initial root cross energy becomes V_q(x)=\omega_{0,d}r\sum_{k=1}^Mh_{k,d} \left[\sqrt{(ho+\sigma)^2-2qho\sigma(1-s^k)} -ho-\sigmaight]. 	ag{21} It depends on both rays and remains independent of the larger grade. Every shared current and trace is identical when that target grade changes. The complete finite probe source and reciprocal initial translation forces therefore retain the common-target identity. The unchanged binding also retains its nonzero shape response for aligned coincident cores. Subsequent target deformation and encounter trajectories need not be identical. Equation (21) is a same-depth initial interaction, not an observed gauge vertex or a cross-depth photon–neutrino calculation. The new norm changes its angular dependence while preserving the assigned masses. Scope and verification partner_current_metric_checks.py checks arbitrary indefinite and singular-eigenvalue currents, complete potential mixed second variations on the actual smooth core, full oscillator source variations, and the finite interaction of two solved cores. It verifies the complete frozen unitary reduction in depths four and six, the exact characteristic compression, direct matrix exponential gains, and the positive conserved form. The implementation is partner_current_metric.py, used by localized_partner_tower.py. The higher angular calculation also tests the revised complete Hessian on the localized electron and muon branches. Its finite scans do not prove full spatial nonlinear stability. The physical mode carrier, shell weights, common normalization, core-frequency relation and master origin of the interaction remain open. The separate principal defect of the polarized rest-frame carrier is a kinetic issue and is unchanged by this potential replacement. Alignment is an angular energy maximum for the prepared pair Equation (21) vanishes when the two coherent rays align, s=1, although each isolated core keeps its nonzero mass frequency. That algebraic zero does not by itself provide a persistent weak encounter. Rotate one ray by a small physical polarization angle 	heta, so s=\cos^2	heta=1-	heta^2+O(	heta^4). For coincident equal-norm cores of distinct grades N>M, equation (21) gives  rac{V_q(	heta)}{\omega_M} =- rac{q}{2} rac{\sum_{k=1}^{M}k h_{k,d}} { inom{M+d}{d}}	heta^2+O(	heta^4) =- rac{q dM}{2(d+1)}	heta^2+O(	heta^4), \qquad h_{k,d}= inom{k+d-1}{d-1}. 	ag{22} The second equality uses the exact identity \sum_{k=1}^{M}k h_{k,d}=d inom{M+d}{d+1}. For q>0 and M>0, the coefficient in (22) is negative. The maintained particle index is n=M+1; the depth-three index-one state has M=0 and no shared positive-order mass-current term. Along this prepared upper-field polarization path, the zero-cross-energy alignment is an angular maximum, and a small rotation lowers the energy. The full binding energy is zero on these upper-only initial data, though its complete field derivative can still drive lower-spinor shape response. Equation (22) is an energetic direction, not a derived collision trajectory. The six-depth alignment check evaluates the exact sum and the closed form for all sixteen maintained indices, using M=n-1, then compares each coefficient with the finite-angle pair energy at 	heta=10^{-3}. Its report contains the full table. With the conditional equal-trace/exchange choice q=1/(r_d+1), examples of the coefficient of 	heta^2 relative to the smaller core's mass frequency are -0.75000 at depth five, particle index ten; -0.57143 at depth six, particle index thirteen; and -0.30303 at depth ten, particle index twenty-three. Thus this same-law mass current permits a vanishing initial pair energy with nonzero isolated masses. For every tested M>0, free alignment does not explain weak reactivity: the aligned preparation has a negative angular energy curvature. A stable suppression would need a derived selection or locking mechanism, or a different current geometry, in the same complete action. The pair formula concerns one depth and distinct grades; it does not calculate a neutrino's interaction with ordinary three-dimensional matter. The sign cannot be reversed inside the globally positive quadratic-root family (1) by choosing q<0. Any nonzero traceless Hermitian test current X would then have F_q(X)^2=qr\operatorname{Tr}(X^2)<0. At q=0 the same direction has zero norm and loses its polarization response. Hence every nondegenerate real norm of this form on all Hermitian currents requires q>0, which fixes the negative angular coefficient in (22). This is an obstruction for this invariant root family, not a claim about every possible same-field interaction or the complete spatial dynamics.

title: Spatial compatibility and reciprocal adjustment under the mass current
summary: The mass current gives orientation-dependent overlap and substantial fast adjustment, but spatial refinements expose an unresolved downhill direction in the depth-five moving pair.
text: The homogeneous current law gives more than isolated frequencies. Applying that same local action to two spatial patterns produces a reciprocal response that depends on their relative phase and physical polarization. Holding both original patterns fixed can greatly overstate the cost of their overlap: a small adjustment of the faster field components reduces that cost substantially. The later stability refinement is essential to the result: the present depth-five moving trial retains a downhill fast direction. Lowering the overlap energy has not yet produced a stable coupling reduction. The calculations here are conditional tests on the stated geometry. They evaluate two-mode fields on one round reference geometry. Constructing two spatially separated particle structures and following their encounter requires an extension of this calculation. They do not yet give a scattering trajectory, a cross-depth vertex, observed force strengths, or neutrino neutrality. The frequencies remain the mass variables throughout; amplitudes enter through canonical phase normalization and the coupled field equations. Use the same action for one pattern and for a pair Let \psi_a=\phi_a\otimes u_a and \psi_b=\phi_b\otimes u_b be normalized individual spatial eigenfields, with F[\psi_i]=\omega_i\psi_i. Different spatial degrees are orthogonal, including after physical rotation of either field. Fix each isolated canonical phase charge to one: \Psi_0=\frac{\psi_a}{\sqrt{2\omega_a}} +e^{i\theta}\frac{\psi_b}{\sqrt{2\omega_b}},\qquad \Pi_0=-i\sqrt{\frac{\omega_a}{2}}\psi_a -i e^{i\theta}\sqrt{\frac{\omega_b}{2}}\psi_b. \tag{1} The complete initial energy and its excess are E_{\rm pair}=\|\Pi_0\|^2+\|F[\Psi_0]\|^2,\qquad \Delta E=E_{\rm pair}-(\omega_a+\omega_b). \tag{2} Equation (2) evaluates the full nonlinear source in physical space. It does not insert an independent pair potential or assume that a superposition remains a solution. A common rotation of the two fields and their geometry preserves this action. The model is reciprocal because both patterns belong to the same varied field functional. This establishes a common source law; a dynamical encounter still requires their coupled evolution. Interference can change the current channel For normalized component rays, define k_a=\phi_a^\dagger K\phi_a<0,\qquad k_b=\phi_b^\dagger K\phi_b<0,\qquad k_{ab}=\phi_a^\dagger K\phi_b. \tag{3} At a point, write the spatial spinor directions as \zeta_a and \zeta_b, with overlap s=\zeta_a^\dagger\zeta_b. For local complex coefficients a,b, the current is j=k_a|a|^2+k_b|b|^2 +2\operatorname{Re}(\bar a b\,k_{ab}s). \tag{4} Although both individual currents are negative, the pair current can be positive in some interference regions. The exact condition that prevents this for every a,b is \boxed{|s k_{ab}|^2\le k_a k_b.} \tag{5} It is the negative-semidefiniteness condition for the full two-ray current matrix. A signed current is not particle inertia. For \eta\to0, the source coefficient approaches G=-g\operatorname{sign}(j). Thus interference can change the local component coupling substantially, even when regularization shifts each isolated frequency only slightly. The zero-regularizer limit is nonsmooth at j=0; it is not a globally smooth replacement for the finite-\eta action. A physical rotation gives a calculable compatibility threshold For the actual highest-weight spinor, let (\Gamma_1+i\Gamma_2)\zeta=0. Rotate its oscillation plane toward the third coordinate by an angle \alpha, transporting the spinor with the same ordinary spatial rotation: \zeta_\alpha=e^{\alpha\Gamma_3\Gamma_1/2}\zeta,\qquad \left(\cos\alpha\,\Gamma_1+ \sin\alpha\,\Gamma_3+i\Gamma_2\right)\zeta_\alpha=0. \tag{6} Direct Clifford differentiation gives \zeta^\dagger\zeta_\alpha=\cos(\alpha/2). \tag{7} Combining (5) and (7), the sign-changing channel is excluded when \boxed{ \alpha\ge\alpha_c, \qquad \alpha_c=2\arccos\!\left[ \min\left(1,\frac{\sqrt{k_a k_b}}{|k_{ab}|}\right)\right]. } \tag{8} This follows from the actual polarization transport. It is not a chosen neutral projector or an inference from shared spatial support alone. Beyond a strict threshold, the saturated negative-current law is linear on the pair span. Its two-frequency superposition then has no nonlinear interaction within that channel. Finite \eta retains a smaller response through the varying magnitude of the current, so (8) is not a general zero-interaction theorem. At the illustrative common strength gR/c=100, using the same within-depth regularizer as the mass calculation, selected thresholds are approximately: Depth and pair Rotation excluding the sign-changing channel 3: down / strange 63.1^\circ 4: up / charm 121.5^\circ 5: first / second neutrino mode 43.7^\circ 6: electron / muon 115.9^\circ 10: index 23 / neighboring index 24 10.4^\circ The depth-ten second index is an unassigned mathematical control. It is not a proposed additional particle. These angles describe this current law and this family of spatial patterns, not measured cross sections. Depth-two forms have a different physical bound The bosonic form fields use their own rotation law. For the electric family at index n, write a_n=\sqrt{\frac{n+1}{2n+1}},\qquad c_n=\frac{n}{\sqrt{(2n+1)(n+1)}}. \tag{9} After reversing the oscillation plane by an ordinary half-turn, the local form overlap, with scalar harmonic factors removed, is a_na_m-c_nc_m. Its normalized magnitude is bounded everywhere by \boxed{ |s_{\rm form}(x)|\le \frac{|a_na_m-c_nc_m|} {\sqrt{(a_n^2+c_n^2)(a_m^2+c_m^2)}}. } \tag{10} For the W/Z indices this bound is about 0.01267. It is below the current threshold in (5), so that actual form configuration also excludes the sign-changing channel. The scalar and vector companions are both included. The spinor half-angle in (7) is not being assigned to a boson. This remains a massive-mode polarization control, not a photon derivation. A fixed superposition can be a poor encounter state For coaxial patterns with the same spinor polarization, direct evaluation of (2) gives a large positive overlap cost at the higher depths. At gR/c=100, the down/strange example costs roughly 4.3\times10^4 times the isolated pair energy. In the tested fixed-ratio regularizer family, the unadjusted cost grows approximately as g^{2d-2} in the large-gap regime. This is an initial-state calculation. It does not establish that an actual pair must retain its original faster components throughout an encounter. A small change in those components can cancel a large source that was exposed by the overlap. To test that possibility, retain a spatial trial space invariant under H_0, while evaluating F in the full physical space. Hold the slow component coefficients fixed and vary the faster component directions: \boxed{\min_{\delta\Psi_f}\ \|F[\Psi_0+\delta\Psi_f]\|^2.} \tag{11} The fast directions are orthogonal to the two occupied rays, so the initial phase charges in (1) remain fixed in this static adjustment test. The norm in (11) includes the part of the nonlinear source outside the trial space. Projecting that source away before minimization would artificially reduce the cost. The actual spinor basis includes negative azimuths and its full moving spinor frame. Depth two instead uses all four differential-form types. No extra spatial dimensions or independent interaction field are added. In the first common trial space, the down/strange fast field changes by only about 9.5\times10^{-5} in relative norm, while its excess energy falls to about 6.52 times the isolated pair energy. Enlarging the spatial basis reduces that ratio to 5.61 and then 3.65. The up/charm control falls from about 1.46 to 0.864 when the spatial basis is enlarged. Thus the large reduction is established, but the remaining interaction has not reached a demonstrated infinite-space limit. The larger trial keeps axial radial cutoff three and two sidebands on each side of the occupied pair. Its refined excess-energy ratios are 3.65, 0.864, 0.688, 0.504 and 0.209 at depths three, four, five, six and ten respectively. Independent integration uses 256 radial nodes and 384 phase nodes. The depth-five optimizer reached its iteration limit, and all these values remain dependent on the spatial trial space. These ratios describe energy costs. They are not physical coupling constants obtained by dividing an interaction by mass, and they do not yet establish the observed grouping of responses by depth. Include the actual motion of the adjusted pattern For coaxial indices n,m, nonlinear spatial response generates azimuths n+k(m-n). Phase covariance and spatial rotation force the corresponding frequency to be \boxed{\omega_k=\omega_a+k(\omega_b-\omega_a).} \tag{12} The fast correction therefore moves. If c_k are its orthonormal spatial coefficients, the full kinetic and potential energies are T=\sum_k\omega_k^2\|c_k\|^2,\qquad V=\|F[\Psi]\|^2. \tag{13} The fast stationary functional at these prescribed frequencies is V-T, rather than V alone. The moving calculation varies that complete expression. Its phase actions are \boxed{ J_a=2\sum_k(1-k)\omega_k\|c_k\|^2,\qquad J_b=2\sum_k k\omega_k\|c_k\|^2. } \tag{14} Consequently, \boxed{E=V+T,\qquad E-\omega_aJ_a-\omega_bJ_b=V-T.} \tag{15} Equation (15) retains the complete positive energy and the phase normalization. Some signed contributions to (14) can oppose one another; that does not imply negative particle inertia. The faster components remain modes of the same field. In the smaller common trial space, the extra kinetic energy is about 1.3\times10^{-7} of the isolated pair energy for down/strange, 1.1\times10^{-5} for up/charm, and 1.3\times10^{-5} for electron/muon. The phase-action changes are explicitly retained and reach roughly 2.7\times10^{-5} in these controls. They are not silently absorbed into the amplitudes or identified with new masses. The moving and static adjustments remain close in those tests. The electron/muon moving optimization reached its iteration limit, so its reported state is a variational trial with a nonzero optimization residual. The full low-mode Euler equations and an encounter trajectory remain to be solved. The pair Hessian has an additional term An isolated eigenfield has the useful second-variation identity \tfrac12\delta^2V=\|DFh\|^2. A general pair does not satisfy that simplification. Its full moving quadratic form is \boxed{ \frac12\delta^2(V-T)[h,h] =\|DFh\|^2+ \operatorname{Re}\langle F,D^2F[h,h]\rangle -\|\Lambda h\|^2, } \tag{16} where \Lambda c_k=\omega_k c_k. For the local interaction map N=F-H_0\Psi, put v=(K-kI)\Psi and define k_h=\frac{2\operatorname{Re}(v^\dagger h)}{\rho},\qquad k_{hh}=\frac{2\operatorname{Re}[h^\dagger(K-kI)h]}{\rho} -\frac{4k_h\operatorname{Re}(\Psi^\dagger h)}{\rho}. \tag{17} Then the required derivative is \boxed{ D^2N[h,h]=2f''k_h(K-kI)h-f''k_h^2\Psi +f'''k_h^2v+f''v k_{hh}, } \tag{18} with f(k)=-g\sqrt{k^2+\eta^2}. This term cancels in the quadratic form when F=\lambda\Psi, as it should. Retaining it for an adjusted pair is necessary before claiming a stable fast response. Two independent implementations evaluate (16): direct application of the full derivative, and assembly from local current moments. They agree at the same spatial quadrature, including actual forms at depth two. The kinetic metric is canonical in both. At 128 radial and 192 phase nodes, every tested fast Hessian is positive. That observation alone is insufficient: its spatial integration must also be resolved. Independent refinement gives the following smallest fast stiffnesses for the same smaller-space moving trial fields, in the dimensionless frequency units of the calculation: Depth 128 by 192 nodes 256 by 384 nodes 512 by 768 nodes 2 17,452.548 17,452.547 not run 3 8,984.699 8,984.694 not run 4 6,448.757 6,448.757 not run 5 6,781.546 -6,359,848 -4,491,109 6 82.332 1,021.770 1,020.584 10 4,045.296 4,045.431 not run Depth five reverses sign, and its derivative is still poorly resolved. The coarse-grid positivity therefore does not establish a stable pair response. Its background also ceases to be a fast stationary point on the finer quadrature. This is a failure of the claimed numerical reduction for that pair trial, not a demonstrated instability of the isolated depth-five mass branch. An independent directional calculation holds the most negative 512-by-768 perturbation fixed and integrates its complete quadratic form directly, in bounded memory. Its curvature is approximately -4.49\times10^6, -4.26\times10^6, -4.29\times10^6 and -4.46\times10^6 on grids 512 by 768, 512 by 1536, 512 by 3072, and 1024 by 3072 respectively. The original grid agrees with the matrix calculation independently. The persistent negative direction strengthens the diagnosis for this trial field, while the remaining variation prevents calling the exact continuum curvature numerically certified. Depth six remains positive, but the full matrix still changes much more than its smallest eigenvalue even at the last refinement. Its moving optimizer had already reached its iteration limit. A converged small eigenvalue alone is not a norm bound for omitted integration or spatial channels. At depths two and four, the reported matrix integration is much better resolved. The depth-three and depth-ten matrices still have larger relative changes despite their positive minima. For a positive frozen fast stiffness with minimum \kappa_f, a bound on its gyroscopic coefficient gives the conditional frequency gap \Omega_f\ge\sqrt{\Omega_{\max}^2+\kappa_f}-\Omega_{\max}, \qquad \Omega_{\max}=\max_k|\omega_k|. \tag{19} Even at the coarse positive depth-two trial, this bound is only about twice the larger particle frequency. It does not justify a strong separation of timescales there. At other depths the coarse bound is larger, but it must not be used to bypass the integration and stationarity failures just described. Full coupled stability and encounter dynamics remain open. What is established and what remains One explicit local law now supplies isolated spatial frequencies, an orientation-sensitive current channel, and a reciprocal fast adjustment of overlapping patterns. The adjustment can be small in field norm and large in its effect on the overlap energy. Its forced motion and phase normalization are calculable from the same action. The residual interaction still depends on the retained spatial space. The supporting geometry, the low-mode encounter dynamics, cross-depth maps, physical sector scales, observed vertices and complete translational inertia remain unresolved. In particular, a same-depth neutrino-pair test does not derive its interaction with ordinary matter. Verification current_pair_response_checks.py passes 88 checks of initial pair energy and local current compatibility. current_polarization_filter_checks.py passes 92 checks of actual spinor rotation, the separate form bound, and the finite-regularizer orthogonal-pair response. current_fast_relaxation_checks.py checks the full spatial gradient, fixed phase normalization and energy decrease of the static trial. current_fast_refinement_checks.py enlarges its physical spatial basis and independently refines integration. current_pair_motion_checks.py passes 30 checks of the moving action and complete energy bookkeeping. current_fast_hessian_moments_checks.py checks the complete real second variation against an independent derivative and verifies canonical symmetry and angular normalization. current_fast_hessian_quadrature_checks.py retains the independent integration refinements, including the depth-five sign reversal. Passing its algebraic checks does not mean the reported quadrature convergence or pair stability has passed. current_pair_directional_quadrature_checks.py independently follows the fixed depth-five downhill direction through finer spatial integration without constructing another full matrix. Optimizer termination, spatial basis dependence and quadrature error are recorded separately from those algebraic checks.

title: Same-field current support, causal response and complete energy
summary: A polynomial current supplies a regular kinetic interaction and a local causal window with negative signed binding contribution; localization, complete energy and helical motion remain conditional tests of the same action.
text:
An interaction can change the time kinetic coefficient of an oscillating field while its supporting components respond reciprocally. A useful local candidate uses a current built polynomially from derivatives of those components. This avoids division by a current that can vanish. It supplies testable equations, but its local characteristic calculations and imposed background wells do not establish a self-supported particle. 1. Canonical frequency and complete energy For a stationary symmetry orbit with reduced action L_\omega=\omega^2K[u]-V[u], define its actual Noether charge by Q=2\omega K,\qquad E=\omega^2K+V,\qquad E-\omega Q=V-\omega^2K. On a differentiable stationary branch, dE/dQ=\omega. This does not generally imply E=\omega Q: the derivative of a nonlinear energy function differs from its ratio to charge. Equality is an additional normalization target when a model identifies this particular phase frequency and charge with the complete particle energy. A positive E-\omega Q tests that identification; by itself it is not a no-go theorem for localized massive states. The physical conversion \omega_m=E_{m rest}/\hbar=mc^2/\hbar is unchanged. A classical candidate must establish that its chosen oscillation has this physical identification with the appropriate action and charge normalization. No arbitrary rescaling or omission of supporting energy establishes it. Complete boost inertia also requires the complete stationary stress and energy, not a wave contribution on frozen coefficients. For a quadratic wave on a static neutral supporting texture, E_{m total}=Q\omega+E_{m support}. If an admissible common amplitude variation decomposes the action into homogeneous terms of degree p, its exact amplitude virial gives E-\omega Q=V_0+\sum_p(1-p/2)(V_p-\omega^2K_p). A positive spatial quartic with quadratic time norm therefore contributes -V_4 to this difference. The inherited weak standing Hodge interaction has the opposite sign in this ledger. These are different actions and cannot be substituted silently. A constrained unit target may forbid the amplitude variation entirely. 2. A regular local kinetic interaction Let Y^i, i=1,\ldots,d, be neutral components of the same field in ordinary physical spacetime, with metric signature (+,-,\ldots,-). Define the current by the dual of their derivative volume form, j=* (dY^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dY^d), with indices raised by that metric. More general polynomial amplitudes multiplying the form are possible, but need not preserve current conservation. The minimal block is \mathcal L=  rac{\kappa_x}{2}|\partial X|^2+  rac{\kappa_s}{2}\sum_i|\partial Y^i|^2 - rac\lambda2 j_\mu j^\mu + rac\alpha2|j^\mu\partial_\mu X|^2-U(X,Y), where all displayed coefficients are positive. The complex wave is a two-real-component field; the phase generator acts on X and leaves Y neutral. Every component is varied. This is a proposed local block of one field, not a new exchanged particle or a derived master action. On a static support, j=(J,0), the wave time coefficient is \kappa_x+\alpha J^2, while its canonical spatial coefficient is \kappa_x. The frozen wave slows. This does not settle the coupled principal symbol because perturbations of Y change j. The prior inverse support target asks for two different coefficient gradients. On a round feature m=d-2, a pinned current with J\propto R^{-m} gives \partial_{\log R}\log(\kappa_x+\alpha J^2)=-m at \alpha J^2=\kappa_x. This is a partial match only. It does not supply the required spatial gradient or gap response, and that reference equality must arise from the normal equations. A related two-scalar coefficient construction already saturated at speed c cannot have a nonzero derivative of its speed ratio and remain bounded by c on a two-sided open neighborhood. Determinant cofactor kinetics can provide causal margin, but the tested fixed tangent stretches give a radius derivative of their spatial/time ratio below 2, versus the high-gap inverse target 2d. These scoped coefficient tests do not exclude anisotropic or derivative-mixed completions. 3. Negative signed binding can coexist with a causal local response Freeze a diagonal support-gradient patch \partial_iY^j=s_i\delta_i^j, a wave velocity v, and zero wave spatial gradient. Put S=\prod_i s_i and c_i=\prod_{h
e i}s_h. After removing determinant second variations that are constant-coefficient divergences, the exact quadratic principal Lagrangian is  egin{aligned} L_2={}& rac{\kappa_x}{2}(x_t^2-|
abla x|^2) + rac{\kappa_s}{2}\sum_i(b_{i,t}^2-|
abla b_i|^2)\ &+ rac\lambda2\left[\sum_i c_i^2b_{i,t}^2- \left(\sum_i c_i\partial_i b_iight)^2ight] + rac\alpha2\left[Sx_t+v\sum_i c_i\partial_i b_iight]^2. \end{aligned} The Hamiltonian cancels the mixed time-space term. Its support spatial Fourier matrix is \kappa_s|k|^2I+(\lambda-\alpha v^2)c(k)c(k)^T, \qquad c(k)_i=c_i k_i. For nonzero cofactors it is positive for every direction whenever \alpha v^2<\lambda+ rac{\kappa_s}{\max_i c_i^2}. The time matrix is positive. For a timelike real covector every canonical principal contribution is positive, the minor term is nonnegative by Cauchy–Schwarz, and the last term is a square. Thus there is no real superluminal characteristic. The positive quadratic Hamiltonian supplies real frequencies for this constant-coefficient block. Consequently the interval \lambda<\alpha v^2<\lambda+ rac{\kappa_s}{\max_i c_i^2} permits a negative signed current-pair contribution (\lambda-\alpha v^2)J^2/2 to E-\omega Q, while retaining positive perturbation energy and causal local propagation. It is not negative total energy or negative inertia. One exact common witness at every maintained depth has s_i=\kappa_x=\kappa_s=\lambda=\alpha=1, v^2=3/2. The signed contribution is -1/4; the coupled squared front speeds are 1 and 1/8, with transverse support modes at 1/2. The second real wave quadrature has its own positive slowed block. The 1/8 here is a characteristic-speed ratio in this chosen patch, not the earlier Hodge directional contact coefficient or a neutrino rate. No special depth-five term was inserted, and this example has no depth-five-specific effect. 4. Localization and concentration are different tests On a prescribed static current, the massive scalar wave obeys (-\Delta+M^2)u=\omega^2[1+(\alpha/\kappa_x)J^2]u. A trial satisfying \int|
abla u|^2<(\alpha/\kappa_x)M^2\int J^2|u|^2 has frequency below the exterior continuum and supplies a sufficient bound-state test for a smooth localized coefficient. This is not a solution of the reciprocal support equations. A compact kinetic bump alone has no positive-frequency square-integrable massless scalar state in an otherwise free exterior. An explicit smooth trial Y_i=sx_i e^{-r^2/(2L^2)} has J=s^d e^{-dr^2/(2L^2)}(1-r^2/L^2). For a Gaussian wave of width \sigma, t=\sigma^2/L^2, its weighted current is  rac{\int J^2u^2}{\int u^2} =s^{2d} rac{1+dt+d(d+2)t^2/4}{(1+dt)^{d/2+2}}. This realizes a conditional well with regular fields. Adding only canonical neutral support energy nevertheless allows a fixed-charge concentration sequence with energy tending to zero. A positive current minor blocks that first sequence, but for d>2 another exists even with any fixed finite polynomial wave potential. Take common compact shapes, support amplitude b=L^{1/2+\delta}, wave amplitude A=L^{-2d\delta}, and 0<\delta<\min\{(d-2)/(4d),1/(4q),1/4\}, where 2q is the largest wave-potential power. The positive energy terms scale as L^{2d\delta}, L^{d-2-4d\delta}, L^{d-4qd\delta}, and L^{d-1+2\delta}, all tending to zero. This excludes a positive-energy global minimum in that unrestricted variational class. It neither excludes local stable states nor proves that the sequence stays inside the full causal field domain. A bounded target removes this particular large-amplitude path; global coercivity and the actual stationary equations still need proof. 5. Exact static and helical energy ledgers For ordinary positive spatial gradients T, derivative-free potential U, ordinary phase norm K_0, current norm K_J=(\alpha/2)\int J^2h(X), and static minor S=(\lambda/2)\int J^2, a common spatial dilation of a smooth stationary state gives E-\omega Q= rac{2T}{d}+2(S-\omega^2K_J). The stronger sufficient local bound \lambda\ge\alpha\omega^2h makes this positive. Section 3 shows that this stronger bound is not necessary for local causal positive-energy perturbations. It must not be used to close the entire current-support route. There is, however, a stronger bound for this particular static action. Put \delta=\alpha\omega^2|X|^2-\lambda and let s_i be the singular values of the support gradient. Positivity of its spatial Fourier block requires \delta\max_i c_i^2<\kappa_s wherever \delta>0. Since J^2/\max_i c_i^2=\min_i s_i^2, \delta J^2<\kappa_s\min_i s_i^2, \qquad S-\omega^2K_J\ge- rac{T_Y}{d}. Here T_Y=(\kappa_s/2)\int\sum_i s_i^2. Rank-deficient points have zero negative-pair density. Combining the bound with the stationary virial yields E-\omega Q\ge rac{2T_X}{d}>0 for a nontrivial localized charged wave with canonical wave gradient energy T_X>0. Strict principal margin strengthens the inequality on a nonzero-current region. Thus even the enlarged local negative-pair window cannot achieve the additional equality target in this simple static-support action with a positive Hamiltonian. Its supporting gradient energy costs at least what the permitted negative contribution can offset. This preserves the local witness while ruling out an overextension of it to a complete stationary equality. It is not a general exclusion of states with E>\omega Q, moving currents, mixed Hodge terms, or a different derivative action. For a synchronized physically rotating pattern, Y(t,x)=Y_0(e^{-\omega t A}x), X(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}X_0(e^{-\omega t A}x), where A is antisymmetric, the current is j=(J,J\omega Ax). The generator combines phase and physical rotation; call its charge Q_{m hel}, distinct from phase charge alone. Let K_{m rot}=(\lambda/2)\int J^2|Ax|^2. Its dilation degree is 2-d, yielding E-\omega Q_{m hel} = rac{2T}{d}+2(S-\omega^2K_J) - rac{2(d-1)}d\omega^2K_{m rot}. This is a candidate balance, not a rotating solution. In the timelike current rest frame the old sufficient bound becomes \alpha\omega^2|X|^2\le\lambda(1-|\omega Ax|^2). It implies S-\omega^2K_J\ge\omega^2K_{m rot}, keeping the ledger positive. The negative-pair window is therefore essential to any proposed escape within this architecture. Spatial wave gradients, rank defects, radiative tails and light-cylinder behavior are untested. For the Hodge square there are additional mixed derivative-gap terms. With a gap scaling as L^{-s}, its normalized wave contribution is 2V_2+(1+s)V_1+2sV_0=-\kappa\,d\Omega^2/d\log L. This is strictly positive on the lowest nonzero finite-chain branch for 0\le s\le1: every entry of the sign-adjusted inverse increases as L^{1+(1-s)(j-i)}. For larger exponents this proof stops. Using this in an ambient virial requires an actual ambient embedding with those dilation powers, not just the surface matrix. Remaining physical bridge The constructive result is a reciprocal local current interaction with an explicitly checked causal window, including negative signed binding. It still needs one smooth finite-energy stationary texture and wave, the actual simplex spectrum, the complete principal symbol on that inhomogeneous solution, its relaxed stability, physical normalization, boost inertia and a particle-pair response. The local block does not yet derive a physical mass or coupling operator. Independent verification checks the characteristic factorization at depths 2,3,4,5,6,10 and the exact negative-pair witness and cofactor bound; the remaining identities above were reviewed by direct variation and homogeneous scaling, without a new PDE run.

title: Exact scale balance and the remaining spatial supporting force
summary: Independent angular stresses obstruct scalar local curvature support for the stated nonuniform states, while a constant-density n=1 spinor supplies an explicit stationary first metric variation under the trial law.
text:
The local current action gives an exact oscillating field on the specified spatial geometry. A further calculation is needed if that geometry is to be sustained by the occupied field itself. Its size and its nonuniform deformations must both satisfy the complete variation. The results here concern stated supporting models. They do not exclude the common characteristic size within a depth, which remains a physical working premise, or require a common size across different depths. Exact pressure of the finite carrier Let \epsilon_n(R,G) be the smallest positive frequency of the complete component chain with diagonal entries c(n+j)/R and common adjacent coupling G. Put \gamma=GR/c. Its homogeneity gives the exact identity  oxed{-R\epsilon_R+G\epsilon_G=\epsilon.} 	ag{1} Define the radius exponent and its logarithmic gap derivative by p=- rac{R\epsilon_R}{\epsilon},\qquad p'= rac{dp}{d\log\gamma}. 	ag{2} The complete inverse of the triangular chain has positive magnitudes proportional to \gamma^{j-i}. Let its normalized left and right Perron singular vectors assign weights w_{ji}>0 to these entries, with \sum w_{ji}=1. Differentiation of its largest singular value gives p=1+\sum_{j\ge i}(j-i)w_{ji},\qquad  oxed{1<p<d,\quad p'\ge\operatorname{Var}_w(j-i)>0.} 	ag{3} The curvature bound follows by holding the maximizing singular vectors fixed while differentiating the logarithm of their positive bilinear sum. That fixed-vector expression is a log-sum-exp function, with second derivative equal to the stated variance. Allowing the maximizing vectors to move can only increase the curvature at their smooth maximum. Thus the finite carrier interpolates from a radius exponent near one to the leading simplex exponent d. This is an exact statement about the whole finite matrix, not an assumption that its leading determinant term is already accurate. What an additive stationary support can and cannot do Consider the particular total energy E(R,G)=\mathcal Q\epsilon_n(R,G)+U(R,G), 	ag{4} where U is the same additive supporting potential for every occupied mode. At a joint stationary point in R and G, equation (1) implies  oxed{\mathcal Q\epsilon=R U_R-G U_G.} 	ag{5} If all particles were assigned the same full stationary supporting configuration (R,G), the right-hand side and U would be the same for each. Their complete energies in (4) would therefore coincide. This remains true even if different values of \mathcal Q were allowed. The scope is the common full support state in this additive model. Common radius alone does not impose a common G, supporting motion, field texture, or supporting energy. For the monomial trial U=A R^dG^a, joint stationarity requires p= rac{d}{d-a}. 	ag{6} Where a finite stationary point exists, its Hessian in (\log R,\log G), divided by \mathcal Q\epsilon, has determinant  oxed{\det\!\left( rac{
abla^2E}{\mathcal Q\epsilon}ight) =-(d-a+1)p'<0.} 	ag{7} It is a saddle. Adding a monomial supporting term and solving only one of its balance equations would miss this independent direction. The current fixed point retains a nonzero radius force For the homogeneous current, let k=\epsilon_G, s=\sqrt{k^2+\eta^2}, G=f'(k), and C=f(k)-kf'(k), with f(k)=-g\sqrt{k^2+\eta^2}. The selected positive branch is \lambda=\epsilon+C. Hold the physical strength g and \eta fixed while varying the radius. The complete derivative is  oxed{ -R rac{d\lambda}{dR} =\langle\phi,H_0\phiangle =\epsilon-Gk=p\epsilon>0. } 	ag{8} The induced derivatives of G and C cancel. In particular,  rac{dG}{d\log R} = rac{f''G\epsilon_{GG}}{1-f''\epsilon_{GG}},\qquad  rac{\partial\lambda}{\partial g}=-s. 	ag{9} These relations agree with independent finite differences of the full fixed point at every maintained index. Differentiating only \epsilon(R,G(R)) would omit the cancellation from C. For the positive action at fixed phase charge, its standing-wave energy is \mathcal Q\lambda. Equation (8) is therefore a real remaining radius force. The current law has closed the spatial field equation on the given geometry, while leaving the size as an input. A radial minimum from a stated curvature law It is useful to test a single bounded geometric coupling rather than assigning separate particle radii. As an explicit inverse trial, choose g(R)= rac{g_0}{1+(R/R_0)^4}. 	ag{10} Equivalently, with curvature scale \kappa=1/R, this is g(\kappa)=g_0\kappa^4/(\kappa^4+\kappa_0^4), \kappa_0=1/R_0. This function and its scales are inputs; they are not derived by writing them in curvature notation. First examine the saturated current branch, \eta=0, where the occupied current is strictly negative. Then G=g, C=0, and \lambda=\epsilon. Set q_g=-d\log g/d\log R. The radius equation becomes  rac{d\log\epsilon}{d\log R}=-p+q_g(p-1)=0. 	ag{11} At a stationary point its logarithmic second derivative is  rac{d^2\log\epsilon}{d(\log R)^2} =q_g'(p-1)-(q_g-1)^2p'. 	ag{12} For (10), the tested roots are radial minima. In the leading large-gap limit their common radius within a depth is  oxed{ rac{R_*}{R_0} =\left( rac{d}{3d-4}ight)^{1/4}.} 	ag{13} The exact finite-chain radii retain mode dependence. At the illustrative g_0R_0/c=1000, the depth-two controls give radii from about 1.0118R_0 to 1.0185R_0; the depth-three controls range from 0.880114R_0 to 0.880238R_0. Consequently, even the radial test does not establish an exactly common finite radius. The complete nonuniform metric variation The decisive additional test is a conformal deformation of the actual spatial metric, g_{ab}\mapsto e^{2\sigma(x)}g_{ab}. Work in units c=R_0=1, and transport the spinor canonically so its L^2 inner product is fixed. The transported Dirac operator is \widetilde D_\sigma=e^{-\sigma/2}D e^{-\sigma/2}. 	ag{14} For the positive Laplacian \widehat\Delta=R^2\Delta, the curvature scale becomes \kappa_\sigma=\kappa e^{-\sigma} \sqrt{1+ rac2d\widehat\Delta\sigma - rac{d-2}{d}|\widehat
abla\sigma|^2}, \qquad \delta\kappa=\kappa\left(-\sigma+ rac{\widehat\Delta\sigma}{d}ight). 	ag{15} The stated small variations keep the square root real. Define component expectations b_n=\langle\phi,\chi_1\phiangle,\qquad a_n=\left\langle\phi, \chi_1\operatorname{diag}(j-d/2)\phiightangle, \qquad  eta=n+d/2. 	ag{16} For a normalized spatial eigenfield with density ho(x), put C_n=a_n-sg_\kappa. Its full first variation is \delta E_1=\kappa\intho\left[ - eta b_n\sigma+C_n\left(-\sigma+  rac{\widehat\Delta\sigma}{d}ight)ight]dV. 	ag{17} At the radial stationary point, C_n=- eta b_n. What remains is  oxed{\delta E_1=  rac{\kappa C_n}{d}\int\sigma\widehat\Deltaho\,dV.} 	ag{18} For the highest-weight density ho=q^n/M(n), choose the smooth variation \sigma=q-\langle qangle_ho. Then \left\langle\widehat\Delta qightangle_ho = rac{2(d-1)n}{n+(d+1)/2}>0. 	ag{19} Since b_n>0, equations (18)--(19) exhibit a nonzero direction that lowers the energy. The radial minimum is not stationary against this ordinary spatial deformation. For a positive standing branch, the positive action gives the corresponding force at fixed phase charge; it does not remove (18). This argument applies to the stated highest-weight family and this curvature trial. It does not exclude other geometries, other local interactions, constant-density eigensections, or supporting motion. Depth-two forms require their own metric transport The bosonic form parent does not use the spinor weight in (14). Let P_{m even} and P_{m odd} project form parity. Its exact canonical conformal transport on the two-sphere is \widetilde D_{{\mathrm f},\sigma} =E_\sigma D_{\mathrm f}E_\sigma,\qquad E_\sigma=e^{-\sigma}P_{m even}+P_{m odd}. 	ag{20} For the electric family in the form construction, write its densities as ho_e and ho_o, and let ho=ho_e+ho_o. The complete transported generating energy is  egin{aligned} E_1(\sigma)={}&2n\kappa b_n\int e^{-\sigma}ho_e\,dV\ &+\int\kappa_\sigma \left[a_{0,n}ho+ rac{b_n}{2}(ho_e-ho_o)ight]dV -s\int g(\kappa_\sigma)ho\,dV, \end{aligned} 	ag{21} where a_{0,n}=\langle\chi_1\operatorname{diag}(j-1/2)angle. Direct variation of (21) agrees with independent spatial quadrature and also leaves a nonzero force at the radial minimum. The conclusion is therefore not an artifact of assigning a spinor transformation law to a bosonic field. Independent angular stresses constrain local curvature support The nonuniform force is not specific to the bounded example (10). Keep the round reference geometry, the highest-weight spatial state, and a coupling depending only on the local scalar curvature scale g(\kappa). Allow an additional rotationally invariant functional of the geometry. At a round reference metric its first variation is isotropic, so it contributes only to the constant angular channel. This includes local scalar-curvature supporting terms; it excludes support with its own nonuniform field pattern or motion.
