For any smooth field data with the same fixed winding and finite transverse energy, completion of the full stress gives, for s=\pm1,  egin{aligned}  rac{\mathcal E-s\mathcal P_y-\mathcal T}{Z} =\int igg[&|D_0W+sD_yW|^2+|(D_1+iD_2)W|^2\ &+\left( rac B2-1+|W|^2ight)^2+ rac14F_{0y}^2\ &+ rac14\sum_{i=1}^2(F_{0i}+sF_{yi})^2 igg]d^2x\ge0. \end{aligned} 	ag{14} Only the ordinary finite-energy boundary term of the static completion has been integrated out. The inequality holds before imposing the field equations, so it retains arbitrary phases, source disturbances and connection motion. The traveling solution saturates it in its propagation direction. The bound explains precisely which cancellation occurs: the time and propagation derivatives satisfy a null relation while the positive topological tension remains. Physical polarizations and the higher-depth control The displacement X=a\cos\omega u+b\sin\omega u describes a line, ellipse or circle in the actual normal plane. Its two directions are normalizable translation modes, protected by translation symmetry. This protection survives a nonradial change of the static profile. It differs from the formal n=0 zero of the retained massive matrix, which an allowed shape perturbation lifts. The full geometric kernel contains more than the center motion: P(z)=z^d+\sum_{k=1}^d\alpha_kz^{d-k},\qquad \alpha_k\longmapsto e^{ik	heta}\alpha_k. 	ag{15} There are 2d real zero modes, with one complex pair at each normal rotation weight k=1,\ldots,d. Only k=1 translates the whole profile. All have positive kinetic metrics. A flat critical geometric action permits their linear null waves; occupation or curvature can change the centered modes. Their different weights do not make them identical spectator channels of the mass operator. The actual multiplicity calculation tests that distinction. This particular construction has two normal translation directions at every tested depth because its feature has codimension two. It therefore does not select depth two as the only possible null sector. A physical photon identification still requires the appropriate global background, state and rotation content, localization in the available directions, and its coupling to other particles. The massive carrier's simplex frequencies and sustaining source are additional constraints on that same-field realization. Verification linked_geometric_dynamics.py implements the full fields and uncompleted stress. linked_null_stress_checks.py passes 942 conditions at all six depths, including independent Cartesian field derivatives, both propagation directions, three polarizations, complete boosts and all geometric mode weights. linked_topological_stress_checks.py passes 263 conditions. It checks (14) on arbitrary smooth field data and solves nonradial configurations at two independent spatial resolutions. The latter retain their positive translation metric and fixed tension. Both reports preserve exact code hashes and separate raw spatial arrays. The complete results are the null-stress report and topological-stress report.

title: Self-mass from a hierarchy of currents
summary: One canonically normalized nonlinear action generates a simplex self-source and a common lower-order probe response; its shell weights and physical carrier remain inverse-model premises.
text: Summary: One canonically normalized nonlinear action generates a simplex self-source and a common lower-order probe response; its shell weights and physical carrier remain inverse-model premises. A self-interaction that also determines coupling The target is a single field law that gives different masses and similar coupling responses within a spatial depth. The construction below generates its self-source from the same nonlinear interaction used for a second field pattern. It contains no separately prescribed quadratic mass term. Its weighting is reconstructed from the desired simplex rule, however; it has not been derived from the existing master scalar interaction. The fixed-order current construction supplies the exact contractions used here. Retaining the whole hierarchy allows those currents to generate the isolated self-source as well. Let Q_d be an actual d-dimensional spatial sector and use the bundle W=\mathbf1\oplus(T^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C),\qquad E_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N W,\qquad D_N=\binom{N+d}{d},\qquad N=n-1. \tag{1} The first summand homogenizes the cumulative oscillator occupations. The other d directions describe ordinary spatial tangent components. Tensor coefficients and their projective rays add no physical dimensions. Only the spatial sectors are nested; the particles are not nested objects. For a finite set of occupied grades, declare canonical spinor fields \Psi_N\in\mathcal S_d\otimes E_N with action S=\int dt\,dV\left[ \sum_N\frac i2\bigl(\Psi_N^\dagger\dot\Psi_N -\dot\Psi_N^\dagger\Psi_N\bigr) -\sum_N\Psi_N^\dagger\mathscr D_N\Psi_N-U\right]. \tag{2} Here \mathscr D_N is the full covariant spatial Dirac operator, including the coefficient-bundle connection. This independent canonical grade decomposition needs an origin in \Psi_\infty. It is not implied by an equality of representation dimensions or by sector inclusion. An infinite grade sum would additionally require a domain and convergence estimates. Exact reduced currents Splitting k symmetric indices from the remaining N-k gives the natural isometry T_{Nk}:E_N\longrightarrow E_k\otimes E_{N-k}. In normalized occupation bases its only nonzero coefficient is (T_{Nk})_{\alpha,\gamma;\alpha+\gamma} =\sqrt{\frac{\binom k\alpha\binom{N-k}\gamma} {\binom N{\alpha+\gamma}}}. \tag{3} Let \beta be the Hermitian scalar insertion of the spatial Dirac equation. Trace the spectator indices and contract the complete spinor indices with \beta, defining a Hermitian matrix \rho_{N,k} on E_k. For example, with Y=T_{Nk}\Psi_N, (\rho_{N,k})_{ab} =\sum_{q,s,t}\overline{Y_{t,bq}}\,\beta_{ts}Y_{s,aq}, \qquad \operatorname{Tr}\rho_{N,k} =J_N=\Psi_N^\dagger\beta\Psi_N. \tag{4} At k=0, the current is the scalar J_N. These currents can have either sign; no spinor component has been removed to make them positive. Their adjoint insertion is B_{Nk}(H)=T_{Nk}^\dagger(H\otimes I)T_{Nk},\qquad B_{Nk}(I)=I. \tag{5} For a coherent coefficient field \Psi_N=\chi\otimes z^{\otimes N}, \|z\|=1, every contraction has the particularly simple form \rho_{N,k}=J\,P_{z,k},\qquad J=\chi^\dagger\beta\chi,\qquad P_{z,k}=|z^{\otimes k}\rangle\langle z^{\otimes k}|. \tag{6} This identity is about a full spinor field at a physical point. It does not assert that an arbitrary spatially varying coherent field solves the Dirac equation. The common action and the Hockey-Stick sum Combine the grades before varying the action: R_k=\sum_{N\ge k}\rho_{N,k},\qquad h_{k,d}=\binom{k+d-1}{d-1},\qquad \boxed{U=\sum_{k\ge0}h_{k,d}\,\Phi(\|R_k\|_{\rm HS}).} \tag{7} The same weights and scalar function \Phi apply to every grade at this depth. For an isolated coherent field, \|R_k\|_{\rm HS}=|J|, and the complete source is \boxed{\frac{\delta U}{\delta\overline\Psi_N} =D_N F(J)\,\beta\Psi_N, \qquad F(J)=\operatorname{sgn}(J)\Phi'(|J|).} \tag{8} Indeed, the matrix derivative in each channel is proportional to P_{z,k}, and B_{Nk}(P_{z,k})z^{\otimes N}=z^{\otimes N}. The coefficient is therefore \sum_{k=0}^N h_{k,d}=\binom{N+d}{d}=D_N. \tag{9} Conversely, within the class of common weighted current sums, demanding (9) at every N forces h_{N,d}=D_N-D_{N-1}, with D_{-1}=0. This uniqueness is an inverse statement. The counting identity does not show that the master dynamics assigns these weights to its interaction channels. The projection calculation derives the different weights actually supplied by a smooth coherent scalar projection and keeps its kinetic normalization explicit. Three self-interaction laws The polynomial choice \Phi(r)=\kappa r^2/2 gives M_N(J)=\kappa D_NJ,\qquad U_N=\frac\kappa2D_NJ^2. \tag{10} Its mass-like source is the simplex count times a self-current scale. That scale remains continuous unless the spatial dynamics selects J. At fixed canonical density, changing the spinor's scalar balance changes the self-source without necessarily making its other response directions small. The homogeneous root \Phi(r)=\mu r, with \mu>0, instead gives M_N=\mu D_N\quad(J>0),\qquad U_N=\mu D_NJ. \tag{11} The complete law is nonsmooth at a zero matrix current. In particular, nonzero scalar-null spinors require attention; the positive-current formula is not a globally smooth full-Dirac action. Other homogeneous coherent actions retain the same occupied mass while giving different complete responses. The chosen self-mass sequence does not uniquely specify the interaction. A smooth comparison uses one positive density scale \sigma: \begin{aligned} \Phi_\sigma(r)&=\mu\bigl(\sqrt{r^2+\sigma^2}-\sigma\bigr),\\ \boxed{M_N(J)}&=\boxed{\mu D_N\frac{J}{\sqrt{J^2+\sigma^2}}},\\ U_N&=\mu D_N\bigl(\sqrt{J^2+\sigma^2}-\sigma\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{12} The subtraction fixes the vacuum energy in the same action. It is not adjusted separately for different branches. With canonical density units, \sigma has units of J, \mu has frequency units, and \kappa in (10) has frequency divided by density units. For a zero-kinetic positive-\beta spatial field of uniform density \rho=Q/\mathcal V, the total energy and phase frequency are E_N=\mathcal V D_N\Phi(\rho),\qquad \omega_N=D_N\Phi'(\rho)=\frac{dE_N}{dQ}. \tag{13} Both ratios are D_M/D_N at a common physical norm and volume, but energy and frequency are different quantities except at the homogeneous root. The norm Q has not been identified with electric charge or particle number. Physical radius, norm selection and the rest-energy interpretation remain part of the mass problem. The fixed depth-six assignments are N=12,34, with D_{12}=18564, D_{34}=3838380 and ratio 3515/17. The same algebra applies at the assigned depth-five and depth-ten grades; it does not select a common scale between different physical depths. Full coherent response Choose a local mode frame with z=e_0. Let j count occupations outside that ray, and put D_j=\binom{j+d}{d}. Two exact contraction sums are \begin{aligned} \sum_{k=0}^N h_{k,d} \frac{\binom{N-j}{k}}{\binom Nk}&=\frac{D_N}{D_j},\\ \sum_{k=0}^N h_{k,d} \frac{\binom kj}{\binom Nj}&=D_N\frac d{d+j}. \end{aligned} \tag{14} Unavailable binomials are zero. The first is the falling-factorial moment of one occupation in a uniform composition of N into d+1 slots. For the second, combine h_{k,d}\binom kj into a constant times \binom{k+d-1}{d+j-1} and apply Hockey-Stick again. For (10), a complete perturbation \eta_j has source derivative \begin{aligned} \delta\mathcal N_0 &=\kappa D_N\left[J\beta\eta_0 +2\operatorname{Re}(\chi^\dagger\beta\eta_0)\beta\chi\right],\\ \delta\mathcal N_j &=\kappa D_N\left[\frac J{D_j}\beta +\frac d{d+j}\beta\chi\chi^\dagger\beta\right]\eta_j, \qquad j\ge1. \end{aligned} \tag{15} Thus the occupied block retains a conjugate variation. The transverse blocks are complex-linear and Hermitian. For (12), replace \kappa by \mu/\sqrt{J^2+\sigma^2}, and multiply the second term of the occupied block by \sigma^2/(J^2+\sigma^2). At the positive root endpoint \sigma=0, that occupied term cancels exactly. Every coherent Hessian block is then complex-linear and Hermitian. On a smooth nonvanishing coherent spatial solution, the complete linearized Dirac evolution therefore conserves its perturbation norm under the stated self-adjoint boundary conditions. This includes spatial and spinor perturbations outside the occupied ray; it is not a nonlinear stability theorem or a statement at scalar-null fields. The known holomorphic spatial fields give nonconstant root solutions with E_N=\omega_NQ=\mu D_NQ on the specified physical CP3 bundle. CP3 is a conditional actual six-dimensional geometry with undetermined metric scale, not compactification. Their smooth continuations and distinct uniform controls require the separate spatial selection and stability calculation. Coupling and the remaining operator question Because the grades enter the combined currents R_k in (7), the action also fixes their reciprocal interaction. A fixed probe of degree M sees an identical coherent target current through every order it can access whenever N\ge M. The complete probe calculation states the required density and ray conditions, the full target response, and the root law's delicate vacuum limit. This supplies a joint inverse model for mass and coupling. It still needs the master field to produce the canonical carrier, the shell weighting, the scalar law and the selected spatial states. Merely counting independent copies of a field does not do so: those copies contribute to the kinetic norm as well as to the potential. The full-field localization condition now excludes flat finite-norm stationary fields in the convex hierarchy's positive-current cone under its stated virial hypotheses. A fixed split into positive and negative insertion channels has the same obstruction. The calculation retains spatially changing sign projectors explicitly, giving a necessary geometric term for a possible textured solution. Verification The later localized current construction retains the hierarchy while adding matrix partners and a local binding interaction. It supplies actual localized spatial solutions, their complete boost stress and an exact frequency-proportional canonical inertia at a common norm. This is a different reconstructed action: it does not remove the positivity obstruction for the action studied above, nor derive the shell weights or physical mode carrier from the master field. An explicit complementary Dirac reduction now derives a spectral square-root source from specified canonical normal occupations and checks its complete response. Its actual scalar projection counts the populated normal band; restoring both self-terms identifies the remaining band matching, energy and occupation questions. graded_current_tower_checks.py checks the exact sums, complete complex gradients, both reciprocal responses, spinor and spatial-frame covariance, the fixed assignments, and scalar-null controls. graded_current_actions_checks.py checks the root and smooth variations, every coherent response block, and arbitrary full-spinor weak probes. The executable laws are in graded_current_tower.py and graded_current_actions.py.

title: Holomorphic binding and its responsive-frame test
summary: A holomorphic inverse binding map gives a regular localized model with unitary full fixed-frame linear response, while its simplest responsive-frame extension has refined growing spatial modes at depths three and four.
text:
There is a useful exact alternative to the polarization-current binding law. Its complete fixed-frame linearization is a complex-linear self-adjoint Dirac operator, so it preserves the spatial norm of every linear disturbance. Allowing the defining frame to respond changes that conclusion: the simplest positive frame kinetic extension has genuine resolved growing radial controls. This comparison identifies which part of the construction supplied the apparently stable response. It does not derive the simplex mass weights or a stable physical mass operator. Mass remains the selected frequency, and the physical directions remain ordinary and uncompactified. An analytic map with the same localized branch Write the full field as \Psi=(\phi,\chi)^T, where each block is an s	imes s complex matrix. In a specified component frame, define f_0= rac{\operatorname{Tr}\phi}{s},\qquad a= rac{\operatorname{Tr}\phi^2}{s},\qquad b=2f_0^2-a,\qquad t_h= rac{a}{b}. 	ag{1} The map F(\phi)=m_c eta\phi eta-\kappa t_h(\phi)\phi 	ag{2} is holomorphic and homogeneous of degree one wherever b
e0. On the radial field \phi=fI_s+i h\alpha_{\hat x}, with real f,h, a=f^2-h^2,\qquad b=f^2+h^2,\qquad t_h= rac{f^2-h^2}{f^2+h^2}. It therefore reproduces the lower-block binding source of the original polarization profile exactly. Use the real potential U_h=\omega(\|\phi\|_F^2-\|\chi\|_F^2) +2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\chi^\dagger F(\phi)). 	ag{3} The first term is a signed linear scalar current. It agrees with the q=0 current root on the positive-trace core branch, but is an explicit linear continuation outside that branch. It is not the nonsmooth absolute value \omega|\operatorname{Tr}C|. The complete source is S_\phi=\omega\phi+DF(\phi)^\dagger\chi,\qquad S_\chi=-\omega\chi+F(\phi). 	ag{4} Here the adjoint acts on the complete matrix space, not just scalar and vector coefficients. The stationary field \Psi=e^{-i\omega t}(\phi_0,0)^T has the same radial equations and Bessel-ratio solution as the original core. Its shape is independent of \omega and of a common normalization multiplier. The assigned \omega_{N,d}=\omega_{0,d} inom{N+d}{d} values still enter through prescribed inverse weights. Full spatial fixed-frame linearization At \chi_0=0, the rotating-frame Hessian is \mathcal H=  egin{pmatrix}0&L^\dagger\L&-2\omega\end{pmatrix}, \qquad L=-i\alpha_a\partial_a+DF(\phi_0(x)). 	ag{5} No conjugate disturbance is suppressed in obtaining (5); its absence is an actual consequence of holomorphicity at this branch. The derivative coefficient is uniformly bounded along the full core. For example, writing t=(f^2-h^2)/(f^2+h^2) and s_p=2fh/(f^2+h^2), one sufficient estimate is \|DF\|\le m_c+\kappa(t+2s_p)\le m_c+\sqrt5\kappa. Thus (5) is a self-adjoint bounded perturbation of the free Dirac operator on its H^1 domain. Its entire spatial linear evolution is unitary in canonical L^2, including every angular and partner component. A useful factorization is (\mathcal H+\omega)^2= \operatorname{diag}(L^\dagger L+\omega^2, LL^\dagger+\omega^2). 	ag{6} This is an analytic fixed-frame result, stronger than a finite local spectrum scan. It is not yet a statement about the complete moving particle. Removing off-branch poles The holomorphic quotient has poles away from the displayed core. Put ho=(\|\phi\|_F^2+\|\chi\|_F^2)/s, and multiply only the binding ratio term in (3) by the common cutoff \eta(|b|^2/ho^2). Use the same twice continuously differentiable cutoff that is zero below 1/16 and one above 1/4, described in Regular polarization binding. At the core its argument equals one. The profile, source, and entire linearization (5) are therefore unchanged. Away from the core the regularized potential is no longer holomorphic, but it is regular on the unit field sphere and homogeneous of degree two. Its source extends as a globally Lipschitz map at the total-field origin. All density and cutoff derivatives are retained in the source. The fixed-frame nonlinear Dirac equation consequently has global canonical L^2 mild evolution, conserved norm and finite propagation. These facts do not imply nonlinear orbital stability of the core. In particular, pointwise linearization around an exponentially decaying profile does not by itself prove uniform Frechet differentiability of the flow in the unweighted spatial L^2 topology. Covariance requires the frame to be included The traces in (1) identify spinor and partner components in a specified frame. They are not by themselves a Lorentz-covariant interaction. A conditional completion evaluates them on \Psi_u=B(u)^{-1}\Psi, where u is a retained future unit timelike orientation of the same proposed field. Under a Lorentz transformation, B(u')^{-1}S_\Lambda B(u)=\operatorname{diag}(R,R), \qquad \Psi'=S_\Lambda\Psi R^\dagger. The rest-frame matrices transform by unitary conjugation, under which (1)–(3) are invariant. The induced partner connection must also be included in the kinetic term. This orientation and its realization in the master field are inverse premises; no additional interacting particle is being introduced. The first frame source vanishes on the radial core because \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\phi_0^\dagger\alpha_aF(\phi_0))=0. Uniformly boosted cores therefore remain conditional solutions, with E_0=\omega Q and positive canonical inertia \omega Q. The mixed second variation, however, is not zero. In the component-frame convention, DF^\dagger(\alpha_a\phi_0)+\alpha_aF(\phi_0) =-2\kappa t\alpha_a\phi_0. 	ag{7} The wave and frame must both respond to this same mixed term. One explicit completion uses the Lorentz scalar frame action \mathcal L_u=- rac{I_f(u\cdot j)}2  igl[c_f^2\eta^{\mu
u}+(1-c_f^2)u^\mu u^
u igr] \partial_\mu u^\alpha\partial_
u u_\alpha, \quad u^2=1,\quad I_f>0,\quad 0<c_f<1. It has no alignment potential. At the unboosted core, its quadratic term is I_fho_{m total}(|\dot v|^2-c_f^2|
abla v|^2)/2. Equation (7) adds the reciprocal quadratic energy 2\kappa t\,v^a\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr} (\delta\phi^\dagger\alpha_a\phi_0). Its complete rotationally invariant channel consists of four complex radial wave coefficients and the radial frame displacement and velocity. With m_c=1, \kappa=2, I_f=1, c_f=1/2, it has: Depth Assigned count used as \omega Refined growing rate 3 Down: 1 approximately 0.5116 4 Up: 15 approximately 1.0859 The rates are in the common test units. Meshes of 160, 320 and 640 points, and outer radii 20 and 28, give convergent values. The eigenfunctions have bounded spatial derivative norms, finite central extent, and eigen-equation residuals below 8	imes10^{-14}. They are not alternating grid modes. These results exclude this particular responsive-frame extension as a stable particle model; they do not exclude every possible support action. The full branch inertia remains positive despite the growing shape mode. Collective drift is a different requirement A free localized particle must also admit its translation–boost pair. If T=\partial_a\Phi is a translation zero mode and b is the boost tangent, the time generator has \mathcal A b=-T, up to the chosen translation sign. A complex-linear self-adjoint \mathcal H with \mathcal A=-i\mathcal H could not have both this generalized mode and \mathcal H T=0: its range is orthogonal to its kernel, whereas the required \mathcal H b is a nonzero multiple of iT. Thus fixed-frame unitarity cannot simply be promoted to uniformly bounded motion of the complete free particle. Legitimate drift has to be treated through the responding support or the full real Hamiltonian structure, and stability assessed modulo collective motion. This observation does not explain away the radial growing modes above: those are actual shape/frame disturbances in a separate invariant spatial channel. Reproducible calculations holomorphic_core_binding.py and regular_holomorphic_binding.py contain the complete analytic and regularized sources. The 1,110-check report verifies stationary Cartesian equations, full variations, adjoints, regularization, and frame covariance across depths 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10. The 38-check spatial frame report retains the refined growing eigenfunctions and all reciprocal frame terms. The independent nonlinear Cartesian control uses holomorphic_spatial_evolution.py; its finite periodic boxes are numerical approximations, not compactified physical dimensions or a proof of nonlinear particle stability. The 25-check nonlinear refinement report compares the complete disturbance fields across grids and time steps. Relative differences are about 0.172% for the depth-three grid comparison, 0.120% for the depth-four grid comparison, and 0.0314% for the depth-four time-step comparison. Canonical norm drift remains below six parts in a billion in the tested trajectories. These controls use a common illustrative frequency of one; they are not separate fitted particle assignments.

title: Normal stress and translation of the gapped spatial carrier
summary: Complete normal modes and independent spatial forces reveal an unresolved wave stress, including a negative directional response, which persists under the exact contracted boost.
text:
The gapped carrier produces the simplex frequency under its stated inverse premises, but its partial wave momentum response has a negative direction in the large-coupling regime. This is a limitation of the wave in a prescribed spatial background. The field that generates and sustains that background has not been supplied, so the result is not the inertia of a complete IDWT particle. This calculation continues the gapped normal carrier. It retains every normal mode forced at first order and does not infer inertia from a truncated kernel momentum matrix. Mass remains the selected frequency in equivalent units. The purpose of the calculation is to test whether the proposed spatial dynamics has the required inertial response. An exact relation between partial momentum response and wave stress Fix a surface frequency parameter beta. In dimensionless normal coordinates, the complete trial Hamiltonian has the form H=\Lambda\alpha_i p_i+B(x),\qquad p_i=-i\partial_i,\qquad \{\alpha_i,\alpha_j\}=2\delta_{ij},\qquad \{B,\alpha_i\}=0. 	ag{1} Repeated normal indices run over x and y. B includes the prescribed normal matrix texture and all bounded pair terms of the carrier. Lambda converts normal momentum to the common surface frequency unit. Assume a localized normalized eigenstate H psi = omega psi with zero mean momentum, and an isolated eigenvalue for the response under examination. The gap estimates in the carrier note provide one conditional regime where this assumption can be checked. The anticommutator and position commutator give \{H,\alpha_i\}=2\Lambda p_i,\qquad [H,x_i]=-i\Lambda\alpha_i. 	ag{2} Combining them on the stationary state yields an exact response vector: (H-\omega) \left( rac{\alpha_i\psi}{2} + rac{i\omega x_i\psi}{\Lambda}ight) =\Lambda p_i\psi. 	ag{3} A component along psi can be removed without changing the response to momentum. For translation of the prescribed background, the moving-frame operator is H(w)=H-w_i Lambda p_i, where w is speed divided by the normal wave speed. Second-order stationary perturbation theory gives \omega(w)=\omega(0)- rac12 M^{m wave}_{ij}w_iw_j+O(|w|^3). 	ag{4} Substitution of (3), followed by integration by parts, gives  oxed{M^{m wave}_{ij}=\omega Q\delta_{ij}+T_{ij},\qquad T_{ij}=\Lambda\operatorname{Re} \langle\psi,\alpha_jp_i\psiangle.} 	ag{5} Here M^wave names the signed derivative of partial wave momentum with respect to the imposed velocity, not the inertia of the complete particle. Q is the canonical wave norm; Q=1 in the comparisons below. T is integrated wave stress. Equation (5) already includes the response of the complete eigenfunction. It is not a prescription for discarding the normal complement. In physical units, the dimensionless M in (5) has the units of mass times the squared normal wave speed divided by hbar times the surface frequency unit. This dimensional conversion does not identify it with the physical inertia of the complete particle. In a local reference product, both normal coordinates can be translated. For a round feature embedded in ordinary space, its radial normal coordinate describes a profile displacement; translating that coordinate alone is not a Cartesian translation of the entire feature. The axial normal direction is an ordinary translation. A completed curved spatial construction must respect this distinction. Independent complete normal control For winding n=1 the square of D_1 is the two-dimensional oscillator plus a constant Clifford matrix with eigenvalues -2, 0, 0 and 2. With total oscillator degree N, its complete invariant grades are g=N,\quad N+1,\quad N+1,\quad N+2, \qquad D_1^2=2g. 	ag{6} Keeping whole grades retains an exactly invariant Dirac space. The bounded spatial multiplier still forces higher grades, so its actual unretained source is calculated in ordinary position space and checked as the grade bound increases. Stress is assembled as the projection of the full product alpha_j p_i; multiplying separately projected factors would omit intermediate components outside the grade bound. For beta=2 and coupling gamma=2, the largest control gives: Lambda Frequency M_xx M_yy 30 1.99715209389 1.99841825066 1.99794789104 100 1.99974350946 1.99985750606 1.99981532704 300 1.99997149931 1.99998416600 1.99997948095 Independent moving-frame eigenfrequencies at speeds 0.001 and 0.002 agree with (5). The unperturbed control, with the additional bounded polarization and hopping removed, has exactly M=omega I. These controls verify the response identity, but do not imply the same limiting stress at higher winding. The full normal complement at general winding Let psi_0 be the canonically normalized projected small-frequency state. At fixed beta and gamma, the first full normal correction is \psi=\psi_0+\Lambda^{-1}\eta+O(\Lambda^{-2}),\qquad \eta=-D_n^{-1}(I-P)V\psi_0. 	ag{7} The inverse acts on the complete orthogonal complement. Since psi_0 has negative chirality and eta has positive chirality, the leading wave stress is T_{ij}^{(0)}=2\operatorname{Re} \langle\alpha_jp_i\psi_0,\etaangle. 	ag{8} The explicit partner factorization reduces the inverse to scalar radial operators for every forced angular integer m: K_m=-\partial_r^2-r^{-1}\partial_r+m^2r^{-2}+r^{2n}. 	ag{9} Write x_r=r^(n+1)/(n+1) and nu=|m|/(n+1). The full regular, decaying half-line inverse is  egin{aligned} (K_m^{-1}f)(r)= rac1{n+1} igg[&K_
u(x_r) \int_0^r I_
u(x_s)f(s)s\,ds\ &+I_
u(x_r)\int_r^\infty K_
u(x_s)f(s)s\,ds igg]. \end{aligned} 	ag{10} This expression includes the full radial domain. The numerical evaluation retains all forced Fourier powers and both positive-chiral spinor components. Differentiating (10) gives a separate check of the original first-order equation D_n eta=(omega-B)psi_0. Thus a check of only the squared equation cannot hide an incorrect first-order component. The constant-polarization source has a useful exact inverse. For the normalized kernel mode with radial functions U_l and V_l, D_n^{-1}(I-P)S\Phi_l = rac r{n+1} \left(e^{i(l-n)	heta}V_l,0,0, i e^{i(l+1)	heta}U_light)^T. 	ag{11} The bounded hopping sources are obtained by differentiating h=z/sqrt(1+r^2). Their scalar inverses in (10) have independent adaptive quadrature controls. Tiny canonical chain coefficients are retained with relative accuracy; they are necessary because the frequency is much smaller than individual spatial source terms. A negative wave-inertia direction survives a large normal gap At gamma=10000, the leading complete normal result is: Winding n Beta Frequency M_xx / frequency M_yy / frequency 6 15.5 8.72769605e-13 265109.3235 -265107.6577 6 37.5 1.80452918e-10 44066.2103 -44064.5444 10 27.5 5.90247175e-21 110296.6624 -110295.0492 All frequencies use the common dimensionless surface unit of the trial. The depth-ten unit has not been physically related to the depth-six unit. The two normal axes in the table are principal axes of the chosen polarized texture. Rotating the entire geometric data rotates the full stress tensor and preserves its eigenvalues. Increasing Lambda reduces the size of the complementary field correction eta/Lambda. It does not suppress (8): the momentum in (5) contributes the compensating factor Lambda. Thus the positive normal spectral gap and the identity P p_i P=0 are insufficient to establish acceptable wave inertia. There is an independent check on the much smaller stress trace. Let h_l' be the derivative of the projected hopping when h(z) is replaced by h(kappa z), at kappa=1: h_l'=2\pi\int_0^\infty  rac{r^2[U_{l+1}U_l+V_{l+1}V_l]}{(1+r^2)^{3/2}}\,dr. 	ag{12} Normal dilation and the Hellmann-Feynman identity give, at leading order in the large normal gap, \operatorname{Tr}T^{(0)}=  rac{2\gamma}{n+1}\sum_l h_l' \operatorname{Re}(v_{l+1}^*u_l). 	ag{13} Here u and v are the two complete, jointly normalized chain vectors. In the large-gamma simplex regime this becomes  rac{\operatorname{Tr}T^{(0)}}\omega \longrightarrow- rac1{n+1}\sum_l rac{h_l'}{h_l}. 	ag{14} The mean of the two partial momentum-response eigenvalues divided by frequency is approximately 0.8329 at winding six and 0.8066 at winding ten. This positive mean coexists with a negative individual eigenvalue. The trace was integrated directly before numerical cancellation of the large opposite directional contributions, and agrees with (13). What a supporting field must supply The normal coefficient is prescribed in the present trial. A closed same-field solution must instead derive both that coefficient and its momentum and stress. Static stress balance can require a supporting contribution opposite to the wave stress, but asserting such cancellation does not construct the supporting solution or determine its energy. Its canonical norm and boundary conditions also matter. The earlier matrix-current spatial response provides a concrete warning: the changing norm of a stationary background affects excess energy and inertia. Subtracting its phase-weighted norm without stating the physical ensemble does not establish a complete particle energy. The present normal carrier has not supplied those missing quantities. The next source test must use the actual spinor currents of (7), retain their angular dependence, and assess whether they generate the assumed texture. No independent scalar interaction or exchanged particle is part of this calculation. Independent check from every spatial force The complete stationary equation also gives a force-based check of the integrated wave stress. Taking the expectation of i[H,x_j p_i] and integrating by parts gives  oxed{T_{ij}=\int x_j\,\psi^\dagger(\partial_iB)\psi\,d^2x.} 	ag{15} Both coordinate-dependent coefficients must be included: the normal texture W and the bounded hopping h. The constant surface and polarization terms have no normal position derivative in this reference operator. For W, its coefficient Lambda multiplies the first current j^(1)/Lambda, so the contribution remains finite in the large-gap limit. For h, the leading kernel pair already gives the required source. Write k(x)=sum phi_(1)^dagger phi_(0), summing every normal spinor component. The two contributions are  egin{aligned} T^W_{ij}&=\operatorname{Re}\int x_j (j_1^{(1)}+i j_2^{(1)})^*\partial_iW\,d^2x,\ T^h_{ij}&=2\operatorname{Re}\int x_j\, \gamma e^{-i\vartheta}k\,\partial_i h\,d^2x. \end{aligned} 	ag{16} Here vartheta is the retained normal orientation. The sum agrees independently with the kinetic calculation (8), including the full off-diagonal tensor entries and their rotation. The trace additionally obeys Tr T^W=-n Tr T and Tr T^h=(n+1) Tr T in this limit. Keeping only one coefficient's force would therefore give the wrong stress. Lorentz contraction does not remove the partial wave stress There is a useful distinction between a rigidly translated prescribed coefficient and the explicitly contracted coefficient appropriate to the normal Lorentz transformation of this trial equation. It does not separate mass from frequency; it concerns which part of the field and its supporting structure is included in momentum. For a boost along normal direction i, put gamma_w=(1-w^2)^(-1/2). The contracted moving-frame operator uses B(gamma_w x_i,x_perp) and subtracts w Lambda p_i. The complete boosted eigenfunction can be written \varphi_w= \exp\!\left( rac{\operatorname{arctanh}w}{2}\alpha_iight) \exp\!\left( rac{i\omega\gamma_w w x_i}{\Lambda}ight) \psi(\gamma_w x_i,x_\perp). 	ag{17} The anticommutation relations of (1) verify directly that its moving-frame phase frequency is omega/gamma_w. The stationary internal oscillation has not stopped. At first order, (17) has exactly the response vector (3). Its wave momentum derivative is therefore still omega+T_ii at unit canonical norm. The second derivative of the contracted coefficient contributes x_i partial_i B to the frequency curvature. Combining (15) with the rigid-coefficient result gives \left. rac{d^2\omega_{m contracted}}{dw^2}ight|_0 =-M^{m wave}_{ii}+T_{ii}=-\omega. 	ag{18} Thus the expected contracted phase frequency and a nonzero partial wave stress coexist. Reading only the curvature of the contracted phase would miss the explicit velocity dependence of the supporting coefficient. It would not compute the momentum of the complete supporting field. In fact, (17) also gives an exact finite-velocity momentum identity. For a localized stationary state, the commutator with x_i gives the integrated current <alpha_i>=0, so the boost preserves its canonical norm Q. Define Pi_i=Lambda <p_i>. Changing variables to x_i'=gamma_w x_i and using the square of the spin boost gives \Pi_i(w)=\gamma_w\Pi_i(0) +\gamma_w w igl(\omega Q+T_{ii} igr). 	ag{19} In a reference with Pi_i(0)=0 and Q=1 this is gamma_w w (omega+T_ii). The wave stress therefore persists in the full boost formula, not only in a first-order expansion. This identity concerns the same prescribed coefficient and does not supply the missing momentum of its physical source. The complete-grade n=1 control verifies the small-velocity limits directly. At Lambda=30, its base frequency is about 1.99715209. The contracted phase has that curvature, while the x momentum response approaches 1.99841825, including the independently calculated stress 0.00126616. Both normal directions and increasing complete grades agree with (18). For a closed localized same-field particle, the sustaining degrees of freedom must supply their own energy, momentum and stress. The present prescribed-background calculation does not determine them. The negative wave-only direction found above is therefore a source requirement to resolve, rather than a demonstrated negative inertia of a complete IDWT particle. Reproducible evidence The complete-grade normal control report linear-normal-grades-20260914T053528_685814Z.json passes 78 checks. holomorphic-components-20260914T054737_589091Z.json passes 18 independent high-precision checks of every small canonical component. The full normal stress report holomorphic-normal-stress-20260914T055018_172524Z.json passes 126 checks, including radial refinement, independent Green integrals, the first-order field residual, physical rotations, and the dilation trace. Source versions and raw arrays accompany these reports. holomorphic-force-virial-20260914T072132_349807Z.json passes 90 independent full spatial-force checks. The contracted normal control normal-contraction-20260914T072306_274477Z.json passes 28 checks of both phase curvature and wave momentum, including normal-grade refinement. The later algebraic audit holomorphic-source-compatibility-20260914T074340_237342Z.json also compares all eight stored contracted momentum results with (19). Their maximum absolute discrepancy is about 4.10e-10. The identity itself follows from (17), beyond those sampled velocities. These establish the stated conditional calculations and their resolved signs. They do not establish a physical normal texture, a complete particle inertia, or a derived IDWT mass operator. title: Physical scale accounting for the normal carrier
summary: The spatial frequency unit depends on both radius and hopping, and an exact inverse-matrix bound constrains common physical scales across depths six and ten.
text: The inverse carrier supplies a concrete geometric conversion between its surface radius and its simplex frequency unit. That conversion depends on the normal hopping strength. Equal frequency units therefore do not imply equal radii without an additional relation among the physical coefficients. These are conditional scale constraints on the prescribed operator. The calculation does not determine a physical radius, introduce compactified dimensions, or fit a new particle assignment. The frequency unit includes the spatial matrix factor Let R_n be the ordinary radius of the surface feature, c the common wave speed, and gamma_n the dimensionless hopping coefficient of the gapped normal carrier. Its leading simplex frequency unit is \omega_{0,n}=\frac{c}{R_n}K_n(\gamma_n),\qquad K_n(\gamma)=\frac{n!}{\gamma^{n-1}\prod_{l=0}^{n-2}h_l}. \tag{1} The h_l are fixed spatial integrals. Every occupied degree at one depth uses the same R_n, gamma_n and h_l. Finite-gamma corrections still depend on the degree, and must be checked before using the leading simplex polynomial as an exact spectrum. If G_n denotes the dimensional coefficient multiplying the bounded hopping term, then G_n=\frac{c}{R_n}\gamma_n. \tag{2} G_n is a coefficient of this inverse spatial operator. Its relation to the same-field interaction remains unproved. Holding gamma fixed gives omega_0 proportional to R^(-1). Holding dimensional G fixed instead gives, at leading order, \omega_{0,n}= \frac{n!c^n}{G_n^{n-1}R_n^n\prod_l h_l}. \tag{3} The source law must therefore say which coefficients remain fixed when the cavity scale varies. The conversion from a frequency unit to a radius cannot silently switch between these choices. A shared leading frequency unit across depths Suppose the depth-six and depth-ten constructions are required to share the same leading simplex frequency unit. Define A=\frac{10!\prod h^{(6)}}{6!\prod h^{(10)}} \simeq19461.2049515. \tag{4} Three additional premises give different consequences: Additional premise Required leading relation Equal dimensionless hopping \gamma R_{10}/R_6=A\gamma^{-4} Equal radii R_{10}=R_6 \gamma_{10}^{9}=A\gamma_6^5 Equal dimensional hopping G_{10}=G_6 \gamma_{10}^{10}=A\gamma_6^6 and R_{10}/R_6=\gamma_{10}/\gamma_6 For gamma_6=10000, equal dimensionless hopping requires a radius ratio about 1.94612e-12. Equal radii instead require gamma_10 about 499.80044. Equal dimensional hopping gives gamma_10 about 674.39909 and a radius ratio about 0.0674399. These are alternative conditional relations, not measurements or derived physical source models. A common radius across depths is an additional assumption. Combining it with equal dimensional hopping gives a stronger condition with an exact test. An all-strength bound for equal radius and dimensional hopping Under both equalities, gamma is common. The electron matrix has diagonal entries 13 through 18 and six normal modes. The tau matrix has diagonal entries 23 through 32 and ten normal modes. Their off-diagonal entries are gamma times their respective h_l. For a lower-bidiagonal matrix with positive diagonal d_j and hopping gamma h_j, its inverse has entries (T^{-1})_{ij}=(-1)^{i-j} \frac{\gamma^{i-j}\prod_{k=j}^{i-1}h_k} {\prod_{k=j}^{i}d_k},\qquad i\ge j. \tag{5} Diagonal sign matrices remove the alternating signs without changing the operator norm. The smallest positive canonical frequency is one divided by that norm. Compare the electron inverse with the leading six-by-six block of the tau inverse. The ratio of corresponding positive entries is independent of gamma: R_{ij}= \prod_{k=j}^{i}\frac{23+k}{13+k} \prod_{k=j}^{i-1}\frac{h_k^{(6)}}{h_k^{(10)}}. \tag{6} Let C=max R_ij. For nonnegative matrices, entrywise domination implies domination of the spectral norm. The norm of the tau block is at most that of its full inverse. Consequently, \boxed{\frac{\omega_\tau}{\omega_e}\le C \simeq18.1922701} \tag{7} for every nonnegative common gamma. The assigned simplex-count ratio 64512240/18564 is over three thousand. The equal-radius, equal-dimensional-hopping version of this projected carrier therefore cannot realize that target. This conclusion follows from the inverse entries, beyond the numerical parameter scan used as a check. The result concerns this carrier and these additional scale equalities. It does not exclude common radius when dimensional coefficients differ by depth. Small controlled normal-complement corrections cannot bridge this discrepancy; abandoning their controlled regime would be a different operator test. Finite hopping remains a distinct correction For the equal-radius family in the table, gamma_6=10000 and gamma_10=499.80044 give a muon/electron ratio about 2.79e-5 below the simplex ratio, and a tau/electron ratio about 0.00786 below it. Equating the leading frequency units does not remove these corrections. title: Which normal shapes preserve the simplex frequency polynomial?
summary: Genuine normal-shape deformations independently change the lower frequency-polynomial coefficients, and two source gradients constrain a common restoring-energy completion.
text:
The complete kernel calculation identifies a useful constraint on the inverse mass operator. Each lower holomorphic coefficient of the normal texture supplies a different lower-degree contribution to its frequency polynomial. The correspondence is triangular and has nonzero diagonal coefficients. Consequently, the winding and mode count alone do not protect the specific simplex polynomial: the sustaining dynamics must also control the normal shape. This statement concerns the prescribed spatial carrier, with winding n identified with depth d as an inverse premise. It does not derive that identification or a physical source. It continues the endpoint deformation calculation and retains the complete normal field. Vary every lower holomorphic coefficient Start from W=z^n and consider W(z)=z^n+\sum_{p=0}^{n-1}a_p z^p. 	ag{1} The coefficients can be complex. They describe spatial shape changes, not amplitudes assigned to particle masses. For a sufficiently small deformation the complete index and normal kernel count remain n, while the projected matrix elements can change. Put q=n-1 and s=n-p. The full kernel derivative in direction delta W=a z^p follows from D_n\delta\Phi_l=-\delta D\,\Phi_l,\qquad P\delta\Phi_l=0. 	ag{2} The scalar partner inverse gives an explicit solution. Define A_l=K_{l-p}^{-1}(r^pU_l),\qquad B_l=K_{l-q+p}^{-1}(r^pV_l). 	ag{3} For a real unit deformation, its two nonzero spinor components are  egin{aligned} (\delta\Phi_l)_1={}&-r^nA_l e^{i(l+s)	heta} +(B_l'+(l-q+p)B_l/r)e^{i(l-s)	heta},\ (\delta\Phi_l)_2={}&i(A_l'-(l-p)A_l/r)e^{i(l-p+1)	heta} -i r^n B_l e^{i(l-q+p-n)	heta}. \end{aligned} 	ag{4} For a complex direction a, the terms with angular shift +s multiply conjugate(a), and the terms with shift -s multiply a. Thus both real quadratures are retained. The actual first-order Dirac equation, not only its scalar square, verifies these components. The diagonal polarization is stationary at first order There is an exact cancellation for the projected constant matrix S=sigma_3 tensor I:  oxed{\delta(P S P)=0} 	ag{5} in the parallel kernel frame of (2), for every lower holomorphic direction in (1). This does not follow merely from angular selection; for many p there are allowed angular entries. Use instead the exact inverse of the polarization source, D_n^{-1}(I-P)S\Phi_l = rac r{n+1} \left(e^{i(l-n)	heta}V_l,0,0, i e^{i(l+1)	heta}U_light)^T. 	ag{6} Substitute (6) into the two terms obtained by differentiating the matrix element of S. Each allowed angular entry is the sum of two opposite copies of the same radial integral, with the same complex coefficient. They cancel. This proves (5) without omitting components. Equation (5) is a first-order result at the monomial texture. It does not assert that the polarization spectrum is invariant under arbitrary finite deformations. The hopping has exactly two possible bands For h=z/sqrt(1+r^2), the derivative of a projected matrix entry can be nonzero only when k-l=1-s\quad	ext{or}\quad k-l=1+s. 	ag{7} The first band is on or above the diagonal and multiplies a. The second is below the original adjacent band and multiplies conjugate(a). The constant deformation p=0 leaves only the endpoint-closing entry already calculated in the companion note. There is a useful sign formula for every entry of the first band. Set l=k+s-1, with k=0 through p, and h_z=(1+r^2/2)/(1+r^2)^(3/2). Its coefficient is  egin{aligned} A^{(p)}_{kl}=-\int_{\mathbb R^2}r^p ig[& U_k K_{l-q}^{-1}(2h_zV_l)\ &+V_l K_k^{-1}(2h_zU_k) ig]d^2x<0. \end{aligned} 	ag{8} All radial functions, h_z and the scalar Green kernels are positive. Thus the inequality is strict, and no cancellation of these upper entries is possible. This formula was also evaluated independently of the differentiated kernel fields in (4). Cofactors give a lower-degree frequency polynomial At the undeformed texture, the canonical pair uses the lower-bidiagonal matrix T with diagonal d_j=beta+j-q/2 and adjacent entries gamma h_j. Its leading small frequency is \omega_0( eta)=  rac{\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}d_j} {\gamma^{n-1}\prod_{j=0}^{n-2}h_j}. 	ag{9} For n=d and the assigned relation between beta and surface degree, this numerator is the rising product giving the simplex count. The following calculation keeps those mode assignments fixed. Differentiate the determinant of the complete matrix. The second, strictly lower band in (7) has zero first determinant derivative. Each upper entry A^(p)_(k,k+s-1) instead closes a path containing s-1 existing adjacent links. Its cofactor leaves exactly p diagonal factors outside that path. Dividing by the same leading product of large singular frequencies gives  rac{\partial\omega}{\partial\operatorname{Re}a_p} =\gamma^{1-p}P_{n,p}( eta) \,[1+O(\gamma^{-2})], 	ag{10} at a fixed beta where the leading derivative is nonzero. Explicitly,  egin{aligned} P_{n,p}( eta)= rac{(-1)^{s-1}}{\prod_{j=0}^{n-2}h_j} \sum_{k=0}^{p}&A^{(p)}_{k,k+s-1} \left(\prod_{j=k}^{k+s-2}h_jight)\ &	imes\left(\prod_{j<k}d_jight) \left(\prod_{j\ge k+s}d_jight). \end{aligned} 	ag{11} Empty products equal one. Every term has degree p. Its leading coefficient is nonzero because the A entries are strictly negative and all hopping products are positive. Therefore P_(n,p) has exactly degree p, for each p from zero through n-1. This proves that the map from real lower texture coefficients to the lower coefficients of the leading frequency polynomial is triangular and invertible at first order. It is a geometric constraint within this carrier, not an argument that other dimensional assignments fit the mass relations. Nor does it select a physical restoring law for the a_p. For n=6, the first three response polynomials are approximately P_{6,0}=0.6149315907,\qquad P_{6,1}=-0.8243156254 eta,\qquad P_{6,2}=1.1583120795 eta^2+0.7967533699. 	ag{12} Their frequency derivatives carry the respective factors gamma, one, and gamma^(-1) in (10). The coefficients come from full spatial Green integrals; they have not been chosen to produce a familiar polynomial family. For complex deformations, the leading effective off-diagonal pair amplitude receives the corresponding complex a_p contributions. Its positive frequency is the magnitude of that amplitude. Imaginary directions at a real reference can therefore change the field at first order while changing the positive frequency only at second order. Frequencies alone do not determine all complex shape data, and a zero first frequency derivative does not imply zero coupling. A translation must move all spatial coefficients For p=n-1, the perturbation z^n+a z^(n-1) is, to first order, the translation (z+a/n)^n. The complete kernel derivative in (4) then agrees with partial_x Phi/n or partial_y Phi/n for the two real directions. If h is translated with the same field geometry, its explicit coefficient derivative cancels its kernel-basis derivative:  oxed{\delta(P h P)+P(\delta h)P=0.} 	ag{13} Thus translating the whole set of coefficients leaves the spectrum unchanged, as it should. Moving W while holding h fixed is a relative displacement inside the specified geometry. The p=0 splitting of a multiple zero at n>1 is not a common translation and is not removed by this identity. The small polynomial coefficients quoted in the endpoint note must also be interpreted in spatial terms. For the individual deformation z^n+a_p z^p, its nonzero roots lie at radius |a_p|^(1/(n-p)). For the electron control at gamma=10000, the first-order coefficients that give a frequency change comparable to its original value correspond to radii about 0.00228 through 0.00286 in normal-width units. The muon comparison gives about 0.00555 through 0.00699. These are local sensitivity scales, not a solved finite-deformation spectrum. The constant coefficient 1.42e-16 is therefore not a literal fractional length displacement of 1.42e-16. Its sixth root gives the relevant root-separation scale in that example. What the source must preserve A common translation is already harmless. Genuine changes of the relative normal shape alter the low-frequency polynomial while preserving the winding and normal mode count. A physical source must therefore either restore the required shape or constrain the allowed deformations through the geometry of the same field. For example, requiring several coefficient textures to be functions of one common field geometry would change their variational source: their chain-rule contributions could not be treated as independent. That possibility is different from the simple two-current closure tested earlier. No such common-geometry action or constraint has been derived here, and a mere change of spatial coordinates would not provide one. A common restoring energy must satisfy more than one source equation The first two genuine shape directions already constrain a simple inverse completion. Suppose its energy separates as E_L(a,Q)=E_{m geom}(a)+Q\,\omega_L(a), 	ag{14} where a denotes real shape coordinates, the same geometric energy applies to each occupied surface mode L, and Q is the canonical wave norm. This is a particular trial energy, not a derived nonlinear IDWT action. Allowing Q to vary tests fixed-point consistency; it does not identify amplitude with mass. Mass remains the selected frequency in equivalent units. For the electron and muon to support the same reference shape a=0, stationarity at fixed respective norms would require  egin{aligned} 
abla E_{m geom}(0)+Q_e
abla\omega_e(0)&=0,\ 
abla E_{m geom}(0)+Q_\mu
abla\omega_\mu(0)&=0. \end{aligned} 	ag{15} Consequently, their frequency gradients must be parallel. This necessary condition is independent of the stiffness or higher derivatives of E_geom at that same shape. Take a_0 and a_1 from W=z^6+a_0+a_1 z. Both change the shape; neither is the common translation considered in (13). The complete projected frequency derivatives at gamma=10000 are Occupied branch \partial\omega/\partial a_0 \partial\omega/\partial a_1 Electron,  eta=15.5 6149.27965435 -12.77681687 Muon,  eta=37.5 6149.10817285 -30.91079170 Their ratios of second to first components are approximately -0.00207777 and -0.00502687. Thus these two-dimensional gradients are not parallel. Choosing Q_mu/Q_e=1.0000278872 to satisfy the first source component leaves a second-component difference of about -18.13484 times Q_e. No nonzero scalar normalization choice can satisfy both components of (15). Linear independence also survives any common invertible change of shape coordinates. The leading formula (12) explains why this is not just a numerical coincidence. At large gamma the two components are 
abla_{(a_0,a_1)}\omega_ eta = igl(\gamma A[1+O(\gamma^{-2})], -B eta[1+O(\gamma^{-2})] igr), \quad A=0.6149315907,\quad B=0.8243156254. 	ag{16} For distinct fixed beta values, the determinant of the two gradient rows has leading term -gamma A B (beta_mu-beta_e), which is nonzero. The obstruction persists for all sufficiently large gamma in the controlled regime. The numerical source derivatives were also computed independently from the full normal currents. This conclusion is limited to the separable energy (14), the shared monomial reference texture, and its stated independent deformations. The premise of a common cavity radius within a depth does not require every background shape variable to be identical. A constrained shape, or an action in which W, h and the sustaining oscillation vary together, changes the source equations. Their additional terms would have to be derived from that action. The next inverse calculation should therefore construct the joint same-field source, retaining its oscillation and its momentum and stress. Merely adding a common restoring potential to this prescribed carrier, or adjusting its wave norm alone, does not complete it. title: Homogeneous actions with coherent simplex masses
summary: A specified family of local homogeneous actions gives exact coherent simplex frequencies, canonical energies and full spatial linear stability, while its normalization, master-field carrier and physical selection remain assumptions.
text:
Summary: A specified family of local homogeneous actions gives exact coherent simplex frequencies, canonical energies and full spatial linear stability, while its normalization, master-field carrier and physical selection remain assumptions. A constructive inverse result There is an action-level route to the coherent mass multiplier that does not require a rank-one mass endomorphism. Start with the existing quartic coherent-current integral, take its square root, and supply the explicit product-rank normalization. The resulting nonlinear Dirac action has exact nonconstant coherent solutions on the specified physical spatial geometry. Their frequency and energy per canonical norm are both \mu D_N. This is an inverse construction: the action is specified to meet the mass condition, and its consequences are then derived. The original master interaction has not been shown to produce either this functional or its canonical mode-bundle field. Those are substantive remaining assumptions. Geometry, currents and the proposed action At physical spatial depth d, use W=\mathbf1\oplus(T^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C),\qquad E_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N W,\qquad D_N= inom{N+d}{d},\qquad N=n-1\ge1. 	ag{1} The projective rays of W label local mode data over the physical spatial point. They add no spatial dimensions. The d directions of Q_d remain ordinary macroscopic spatial directions. The coherent localization density is v_z=z^{\odot N},\qquad \Lambda_z=D_N|v_zangle\langle v_z|,\qquad \int\Lambda_z\,d
u(z)=I, 	ag{2} with \|z\|=1 and unit-volume invariant ray measure. For the full field \Psi\in\Sigma\otimes E_N, define j_z=\Psi^\dagger( eta\otimes\Lambda_z)\Psi, \qquad K_p(\Psi)=\int j_z^p\,d
u(z). 	ag{3} Here  eta is the Hermitian scalar-current matrix. Take an even integer p\ge2 and specify the potential density  oxed{U_{N,p}(\Psi)=\mu\,[D_{pN}K_p(\Psi)]^{1/p},\qquad \mu>0.} 	ag{4} The simplest case is U_{N,2}=\mu\sqrt{D_{2N}\int j_z^2d
u}. It is smooth wherever K_p>0. Its spatial action is S=\int dt\left[  rac i2\int(\Psi^\dagger\dot\Psi-\dot\Psi^\dagger\Psi)dV -\langle\Psi,\mathscr D_N\Psiangle-\int U_{N,p}(\Psi)dV ight]. 	ag{5} The canonical kinetic metric in (5) is part of the candidate. In particular, it cannot silently be assigned to a collection of constrained derivatives of one smaller spinor. The derivative-lift test below makes that distinction explicit. The coefficient \mu has dimensions of energy in units \hbar=c=1; (4) is quadratic in field amplitude. Full variation and the occupied eigenvalue Vary every field component in (4), including the current inside its normalizing factor. Put  egin{aligned} \mathcal M_p[\Psi] &=\mu D_{pN}^{1/p}K_p^{1/p-1} \int j_z^{p-1}\Lambda_z\,d
u(z),\ G_p[\Psi]&=( eta\otimes\mathcal M_p[\Psi])\Psi. \end{aligned} 	ag{6} Then \delta U=2\operatorname{Re}\langle G_p,\delta\Psiangle and i\partial_t\Psi=\mathscr D_N\Psi+G_p[\Psi]. 	ag{7} The endomorphism in (6) acts as a scalar in Clifford indices. It is Hermitian, and the action is covariant under the specified unitary mode frames. A complete spacetime-covariant master embedding of those spatial mode components is still required; a spin-scalar contraction alone does not provide that embedding. At a coherent field \Psi_*=\chi\otimes v_{z_0}, let J=\chi^\dagger eta\chi>0 and u=|z^\dagger z_0|^2. The invariant ray measure gives \int u^{pN}d
u =d\int_0^1u^{pN}(1-u)^{d-1}du = rac{d!\,(pN)!}{(pN+d)!}= rac1{D_{pN}}. 	ag{8} Thus K_p=D_N^pJ^p/D_{pN} and U_{N,p}(\Psi_*)=\mu D_NJ. To check the other equations, decompose the mode carrier by the number j of factors orthogonal to z_0, with projectors P_j. Their ranks are  inom{j+d-1}{d-1}. Integrating the normalized occupation monomials gives r_j^{(p)}= rac{(N)_{\underline j}}{(pN)_{\underline j}}, \qquad r_0^{(p)}=1,\qquad  oxed{\mathcal M_p[\Psi_*]=\mu D_N\sum_{j=0}^N r_j^{(p)}P_j.} 	ag{9} For example, the monomial with j transverse occupations contributes  inom Nj u^{N-j}(1-u)^j before averaging its transverse direction. The beta integral weighted by u^{(p-1)N}, divided by the occupied integral, gives (N)_{\underline j}/(pN)_{\underline j}. Consequently every occupied equation gives  oxed{G_p[\Psi_*]=\mu D_N eta\Psi_*.} 	ag{10} All r_j^{(p)} are positive at finite p. The mass endomorphism therefore has full mode rank, although its occupied eigenvalue equals the one from rank-one coherent contact. An occupied mass sequence does not determine the complete endomorphism uniquely. The complete response retains the normalization variation The first derivative (10) does not license freezing the current or its normalization when calculating perturbations. At the coherent field the complete derivative has the especially simple form  oxed{  egin{aligned} \delta G_p&=A_ph,\qquad B_p=0,\ A_p&=\mu D_N\left[  eta\otimes P_0+ \sum_{j=1}^N r_j^{(p)} \left( eta+(p-1) rac{ eta\chi\chi^\dagger eta}{J}ight) \otimes P_jight]. \end{aligned}} 	ag{11} Here B_p denotes the coefficient of \overline h in the general real-linear response. Its cancellation in (11) is a result on the coherent background, not a property of the nonlinear action at arbitrary fields. To see the cancellation, work in the frame z_0=e_0. Before varying K_p^{1/p-1}, the radial response contains 2(p-1) eta\chi\operatorname{Re}(\chi^\dagger eta h_0)/J. Since  rac{\delta K_p}{K_p} = rac{2p}{J}\operatorname{Re}(\chi^\dagger eta h_0), 	ag{12} the derivative of that factor cancels the radial term exactly. Transverse phase integration leaves one ordinary term with coefficient (p-1)r_j^{(p)}; a conjugate term would require two nonnegative transverse occupations to sum to zero and hence occurs only in the radial entry. This proves (11), including every spinor polarization. Each matrix in (11) is Hermitian. The identity p r_1^{(p)}=1 also gives the required unchanged frequency along a moving coherent ray. For a positive-chirality spinor, the response within its occupied spin line in sector j\ge1, divided by \mu D_N, is p r_j^{(p)}. At N=12, its j=2 value is 11/23, 11/47 or 11/71 for p=2,4,6, respectively. Their isolated coherent masses are identical. Exact nonconstant fields on the specified physical CP3 Use the curved coherent mode bundle, with W=\mathbf1\oplus T^{1,0}\mathrm{CP}^3\oplus(T^{1,0}\mathrm{CP}^3)^*, \quad \mathscr D_N=\sqrt2( ar\partial_{E_N}+ ar\partial_{E_N}^\dagger), \quad  eta=(-1)^{	ext{form degree}}. 	ag{13} This is the candidate actual six-dimensional spatial geometry, at undetermined physical radius R and volume \mathcal V. Its mathematically compact topology is a conditional global choice; no directions are compactified or assigned a small extra-dimensional scale. The holomorphic vector field induced by \operatorname{diag}(1,i,-1,-i) gives the nowhere-zero section w=(1,X_A,0). Write h=\|w\|^2, \mathcal Z_N=\int h^Nd
u_Q and dV=\mathcal Vd
u_Q, where d
u_Q is unit spatial measure. The fully normalized physical field is \phi_N=\sqrt{ rac{Q}{\mathcal V\mathcal Z_N}}w^{\odot N}. 	ag{14} Its zero-form holomorphicity, with the full natural Chern connection, gives \mathscr D_N\phi_N=0 and  eta\phi_N=\phi_N. Its ray and amplitude both vary; their covariant derivatives cancel in the holomorphic section. Equations (10) and (14) now prove  oxed{  egin{aligned} \Psi_N(t,q)&=e^{-i\mu D_Nt}\phi_N(q),\ \omega_N&=\mu D_N,\ E_N&=\mu D_NQ. \end{aligned} } 	ag{15} No expectation value is being substituted for an unsolved complementary equation. The kinetic equation and every component of the algebraic source are satisfied. The factors \mathcal Z_N and \mathcal V cancel from E_N/Q, without choosing a separate physical coefficient for each profile. At the unchanged electron and muon assignments, N=12,34,  egin{aligned} D_{12}&=18\,564,\ D_{34}&=3\,838\,380,\  rac{\omega_{34}}{\omega_{12}} &= rac{E_{34}}{E_{12}}= rac{D_{34}}{D_{12}}= rac{3515}{17}. \end{aligned} 	ag{16} at common Q. The equality is the predicted simplex relationship, not an assertion of exact agreement with measured masses. The norm factors are approximately 1694.763120675 and 3.391520233	imes10^9; their different values do not alter (16). The same algebra applies at depth ten, but (15) by itself does not derive the tau sector's physical geometry, shared \mu, occupied branch or cross-sector interaction. Canonical norm Q is not identified here with electric charge or with a quantized particle count. Full spatial linear stability and propagation Linearize (7) around (15) in its rotating frame. Equation (11) gives i\partial_t h=(\mathscr D_N-\mu D_NI+A_p(q))h. 	ag{17} The chosen coherent section is nowhere zero, so A_p(q) is a smooth Hermitian endomorphism. For this positive-chirality field its operator norm is at most \mu D_N: in each transverse sector r_j^{(p)}\le1/p. On the compact physical candidate without boundary, \mathscr D_N is self-adjoint; adding this bounded Hermitian potential preserves self-adjointness. Therefore \|h(t)\|_{L^2(dV)}=\|h(0)\|_{L^2(dV)}. 	ag{18} This includes all spatial modes and spinor components. It does not require the varying projectors P_j(q) to be parallel. It establishes full linear stability, not nonlinear orbital stability of the spatial particle. On a neighborhood where K_p stays positive, (7) is a smooth semilinear Dirac system. Its source has no physical spatial derivatives, so the principal symbol remains Clifford multiplication. For two smooth solutions, their difference obeys the usual local density balance with a source bounded by a local Lipschitz constant times the squared difference. The Clifford flux through a unit normal is bounded by that density. Integrating over a light cone and applying Gronwall's inequality therefore gives finite propagation with the original Dirac speed, for as long as both solutions remain in that smooth domain. This argument is conditional on the independent kinetic carrier in (5). The energy-frequency identity simplifies here: quadratic homogeneity gives \operatorname{Re}\langle\Psi,G_pangle =U_{N,p} pointwise. Thus any sufficiently regular stationary solution of this action satisfies E=\omega Q. Its scale copies retain the same frequency. The action consequently does not select a distinguished norm. A reciprocal coupling diagnostic The same action predicts more than a mass. At one physical point retain two orthogonal positive-chirality spinor polarizations, occupied on the orthogonal mode rays e_0 and e_1, with scalar intensities A,B>0. They are two components of one field. The exact mixed ray moment is t_N= rac1{ inom{2N}{N}},\qquad U_{N,2}=\mu D_N\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2t_NAB}. 	ag{19} The factor follows by integrating |z_0|^{2N}|z_1|^{2N} and dividing by the self moment 1/D_{2N}. Both sources and their reciprocal derivative are fixed:  egin{aligned} \partial_AU&=\mu D_N rac{A+t_NB}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2t_NAB}},\ \partial_A\partial_BU &=-\mu D_N rac{(1-t_N^2)AB}{(A^2+B^2+2t_NAB)^{3/2}}. \end{aligned} 	ag{20} Consequently a very small mixed quartic overlap does not make the root-action response small. At A=B, the occupied coefficient relative to its isolated value is \sqrt{(1+t_N)/2}, tending to 1/\sqrt2. This is a definite consequence of normalizing by the total local moment. Different moment orders give different collective responses despite (16). This comparison concerns coincident polarized components. Fields with disjoint physical spatial support have additive energies because (5) is local in physical space. Neither comparison supplies a completed encounter between particles on different nested sectors. Their full spatial patterns, relative phases, kinetic response and common projected interaction remain necessary for an observed coupling prediction. What the inverse construction still assumes The normalization in (4) is essential. For the general choice U=C_NK_p^{1/p}, the coherent coefficient is C_ND_N/D_{pN}^{1/p}. Requiring \mu D_N determines C_N=\mu D_{pN}^{1/p}. The product rank is an exact geometric integer; choosing this function of it in the physical action remains a premise. For example, a common unnormalized square root gives the assigned-band ratio about 11.706, rather than 3515/17. The action also has a nontrivial singular set. The coherent symbols are informationally complete: j_z=0 for every z is equivalent to \Psi^\dagger eta\Psi=0 as a mode matrix. This follows by expanding the homogeneous polynomial in z and \overline z. That condition can hold for a nonzero spinor. Along a coherent curve with scalar current J=\epsilon, (4) becomes \mu D_N|\epsilon|, which has unequal one-sided derivatives at zero. The construction provides no general continuation through that set and makes no antiparticle identification. At the field vacuum U=O(\|\Psi\|^2) has first derivative zero, but the nonquadratic homogeneous functional has no single quadratic Taylor expansion. A degree-two homogeneous function that is twice differentiable at zero must equal its quadratic Taylor form everywhere. Thus one cannot assume an ordinary smooth vacuum expansion for (4). Finally, cumulative bands are not automatically independent physical branches. Their standard inclusions do not turn the coherent contact family into compressions of one bare operator. A master derivation must supply the carrier, its kinetic norm, the interpretation and selection of N, and the action itself. The conditional result here is an exact spatial mass construction with a derived response, not that missing master derivation. Verification and related calculations The combined-band calculation now puts the distinct occupied mass branches into one root action and varies both currents. Its mixed response remains strongly band dependent; isolated mass agreement does not establish a common coupling group. The geometric current construction instead retains fixed-order tensor currents. It preserves a prescribed simplex mass term and gives a common coherent elastic vertex, with explicit spatial normalization and reciprocal evolution tests. Its master origin and the mass operator itself remain assumptions. The current hierarchy extends the inverse construction to one common action that generates both self-mass and the interaction between grades. Its root endpoint gives an exact common lower-order probe operator on coherent targets. The shell weighting and canonical master-field carrier still need a derivation; the result does not make those premises consequences of the homogeneous action above. coherent_root_action_checks.py compares independent projective quadrature with exact symmetric-tensor contractions, differentiates arbitrary complex eight-component fields, checks the full coherent Hessian in rotated frames, and verifies spatial normalization and both sides of (20). Exact factorial formulas cover the assigned large bands without allocating their full matrices. The peak and smooth comparison treats the limit of increasing moment order and a smooth logarithmic replacement. The constrained-derivative calculation tests whether the field in (5) can simply be interpreted as a canonical jet of one smaller spinor; that specified identification fails finite propagation.

title: A local homogeneous current that closes the spatial mass equation
summary: An explicit local current law generates the adjacent component coupling, preserves an entire spatial eigenspace, and gives exact standing waves of a fully varied positive action; its supporting geometry and physical component channel remain inputs.
text:
A local interaction can preserve the selected spatial frequency without requiring the field density to be spatially constant. The construction below uses the direction of a same-field current, while retaining its complete variation. It supplies exact standing waves of a positive spatial action at every maintained depth. They have not been derived from the original scalar-current master interaction. The construction does not yet select a supporting radius, the physical coupling scales, the required shared six/ten frequency unit, or a complete particle response to motion. A quadratic current, for example, changes the count exponent to 2/(d+1). A common depth coefficient cannot undo that changed dependence on the index. These are leading spectral statements; the finite chain has its separately calculable corrections. There is also a functional version. Under the additional requirement of exact proportionality \lambda=\Lambda_d\mathcal P over a continuous leading-order family, the complete stationary derivative is  rac{d\lambda}{d\mathcal P}=G^{-r}. 	ag{7d} All induced derivatives of G and k cancel. Proportionality therefore requires a constant G on that family, and hence a linear f(k)=Gk over the sampled negative-current interval, with no additive frequency offset. The continuous-family requirement is stronger than matching a finite set of assigned indices, so this is not a uniqueness theorem for every possible interaction. The even square-root law (3) approaches that linear behavior when |k|\gg\eta, while retaining a differentiable generating density through k=0 at nonzero field. Its finite regularizer accounts for the shifts in (6). The competing-branch calculation then tests the dynamics of the small-current alternative under the same specified law. The complete positive action has exact standing waves Define the action on the full spatial field by  oxed{ L_+=\|\dot\Psi\|^2-\|F[\Psi]\|^2, \qquad \ddot\Psi+(DF[\Psi])^*F[\Psi]=0. } 	ag{8} The star here denotes the adjoint for the real Hilbert inner product. It is not a global existence or uniqueness theorem at the non-smooth field origin. The same principal-symbol calculation applies to the actual depth-two differential-form parent. Why a cubic density source behaves differently A conventional local cubic source ho\Psi does not have the closure property of (4).
