Hence the written local scalar interaction has no nonzero bounded smooth stationary field of finite normal norm on the full line within this complete spatial Killing channel, for either sign of \kappa. This result retains all four complex normal amplitudes and their self-consistent current. Its scope is the selected spatial pair and product geometry. Tangentially varying currents, coupling to other spatial modes, different normal geometry and boundary dynamics change the problem. Normal localization itself is not an established requirement of IDWT's cylindrical free continuation. The theorem settles this particular attempted mechanism without selecting a physical geometry. The calculation identifies an explicit spatial origin for |\mathscr D| and follows it through the full spinor and action normalization. Deriving the complete simplex mass operator still requires a normal geometry and boundary or binding law inherited from the master field, together with its consistent nonlinear spatial solution. Verification normal_dirac_extension_checks.py checks every Clifford anticommutator of the rank-sixteen parent, the complete decaying projector and scalar intertwining, and arbitrary complex paired tangential spectra under unitary changes of basis. These paired matrices test operator identities; they are not a replacement for curved spatial multiplicities. Independent normal quadrature verifies the induced kinetic metric, bulk scalar energy and profile moments. Full complex action variations check both bulk and boundary forms and the local quartic source. The last tests differentiate the actual six-dimensional Killing fields in a spatial chart, retain both parent blocks, and measure the complementary normal force in (18). Independent normal Fourier matrices test the full anticommutation and positive square in (20)–(21) with spatially varying scalar profiles and all four complex amplitudes. Those finite periodic matrices verify operator algebra; the full-line nonexistence statement follows from the analytic argument (21)–(24).

title: Translation of the oscillating surface

text:
An oscillation changes the translation response of the conditional surface-bending model. It can give a positive response for one mode, even though the unexcited tension background has a negative longitudinal coefficient. With the assigned electron and muon modes at one common radius and canonical wave action, ordinary tension cannot give both positive inertia and the required frequency ratio within the leading wave calculation. This conclusion concerns the stated geometric surface action. It does not establish a failure of the proposed inertial origin of mass or of multidimensional particles. The full supporting field may carry additional energy, stress and momentum. Those contributions have not been derived from this surface model. title: Phase of a partial wave momentum response
summary: A negative quasistatic partial momentum response can correspond to motion opposite in phase to an imposed velocity, without establishing negative physical particle inertia.
text: A negative signed wave momentum derivative has a precise phase interpretation when the supporting coefficients undergo an imposed oscillatory translation. This calculation concerns a partial response. Positive inertia of a complete particle must be assessed from the momentum of its whole sustaining field. Let a self-adjoint stationary wave operator have a normalized isolated mode phi with selected frequency omega. In coordinates moving with the prescribed profile, a small imposed velocity v(t) contributes -v(t)P to that operator. The first variation satisfies i\partial_t\delta\phi=(H-\omega)\delta\phi-v(t)P\phi. \tag{1} Both frequency components of a real velocity must be kept. Expanding in the complete spectral resolution of H gives the retarded momentum susceptibility \boxed{\chi_{PP}(\nu)= \sum_j\frac{2\Delta_j|\langle j|P|\phi\rangle|^2} {\Delta_j^2-(\nu+i0)^2},\qquad \Delta_j=E_j-\omega.} \tag{2} The sum includes a spectral integral if the operator has continuum modes. Equation (2) requires the stated matrix elements and resolvent limit to exist. The occupied phase direction is removed in the usual linear normalization condition. Here nu is the imposed disturbance frequency; omega remains the particle's selected mass-frequency. At zero driving frequency, (2) is the stationary partial momentum derivative. Away from resonance, a real negative susceptibility gives delta P(t)=chi_PP(nu) v(t), with momentum opposite in phase to the velocity. It does not require a negative inertia for the complete moving structure. It also does not imply a dissipative time lag. An exact unitary two-level control verifies the sign and phase. With Delta=-2 and P=0.7 sigma_x, the linear susceptibilities are -0.50127877 at nu=0.3 and +0.392 at nu=3. Direct time evolution gives respectively phase pi and phase zero. Reducing the velocity amplitude from 0.001 to 0.0002 reduces the nonlinear response error by the expected factor of approximately 0.04, while norm is conserved. The two-level system is a verification control, not an IDWT particle model. The report partial-momentum-phase-20260914T123325_527778Z.json passes ten checks and retains the trajectories and source versions. An actual joint IDWT translation still has to include the sustaining pattern's own response, total momentum and stress.

title: Periodic motion, preserved mass ratios and reciprocal support
summary: Periodic endpoint motion preserves the leading simplex ratios with an explicit uniform error bound, but its reciprocal shape source and positive supporting energy remain essential; exact moving-frame transport gives a separate conditional frequency-preserving action.
text: A supporting pattern can keep moving while retaining a common frequency multiplier across a particle family. This can be demonstrated in the endpoint operator already obtained from the spatial carrier. The same calculation also determines the force exerted on that pattern. Preserving the frequency ratios does not automatically make the supporting motion a solution of its own equations. The results below retain the complete two-state wave evolution, relative phase, a reacting positive geometric oscillator and the temporal frame terms. The reduction from the entire moving normal field is still open. All coordinates describe proposed modes of the same field; no additional interaction particle or particle-exchange mechanism is introduced. Mass remains the selected particle frequency in equivalent units. A Floquet phase of a prescribed periodically varying subsystem is a candidate frequency, not yet the frequency of a complete particle state. Its branch, other temporal harmonics, supporting energy and inertia must also be identified. No frequency is chosen modulo the drive frequency merely to obtain a desired mass. The complete periodically varying endpoint At a fixed depth, rephase the endpoint basis so the reference coupling t=t_{n,d}>0 and the shape coefficient s>0. The existing radial calculation gives t_{n,d} proportional to S(n,d), while s is independent of the occupied index at leading order. The complex deformation has two real directions. Retain a static displacement X in one and a periodic displacement in the perpendicular direction: i\dot c=H(t_{\rm time})c,\qquad H=(t+sX)\sigma_1+sA\cos(\Omega t_{\rm time})\sigma_2, \qquad c^\dagger c=1. \tag{1} Here the \sigma_j are Hermitian Pauli matrices, \Omega is the geometric oscillation frequency and A is its shape amplitude. The wave amplitude is normalized; it is not used to assign mass. The first calculation prescribes this geometric history in order to compute its wave frequency and reciprocal force. Use \tau=\Omega t_{\rm time}, \delta=t/\Omega, a=sA/\Omega and x_0=sX/\Omega. At x_0=0, i c'=[\delta\sigma_1+a\cos\tau\,\sigma_2]c. \tag{2} Transform with R(\tau)=\exp[-ia\sin\tau\,\sigma_2]. Its value is the identity at both ends of a period. Writing c=Rv gives the exact equation i v'=\delta\left[ \cos(2a\sin\tau)\sigma_1+ \sin(2a\sin\tau)\sigma_3\right]v. \tag{3} The norm of this interaction-picture coefficient is |\delta|, independently of the drive amplitude. Its average is \delta J_0(2a)\sigma_1, where J_0(2a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\cos(2a\sin\tau)\,d\tau. \tag{4} The analytic signed Floquet branch continuous from the positive \sigma_1 state therefore has \boxed{\epsilon=\delta J_0(2a)+O(\delta^3),\qquad \epsilon_{\rm physical}=tJ_0(2a)+O(t^3/\Omega^2).} \tag{5} Its magnitude supplies the positive branch comparison. Away from a zero of J_0, a common a,\Omega preserves the leading simplex ratios. The assigned indices at depths 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 are all checked with one drive per depth. The two bottom entries remain component controls; this does not derive their geometric-mean particle branch. An exact half-period identity controls the approximation Let U_h be evolution from zero to \pi. The two identities H(\pi-\tau)=H(\tau)^T and H(\tau+\pi)=\sigma_1H(\tau)\sigma_1 imply U_h=a_hI-i(b_x\sigma_1+b_z\sigma_3),\qquad a_h^2+b_x^2+b_z^2=1, \tag{6} with real coefficients, and \boxed{ U_{2\pi}=(\sigma_1U_h)^2 =(1-2b_x^2)I-2ib_x(a_h\sigma_1-b_z\sigma_2). } \tag{7} The first identity makes U_h symmetric: transposition reverses the ordered product, and the reflected Hamiltonian restores its original order. The second identity then determines the full period. For the branch near \delta=0, \boxed{\epsilon=\frac{\arcsin b_x}{\pi}.} \tag{8} Its initial polarization is the positive eigenvector of a_h\sigma_1-b_z\sigma_2. This remains a regular choice when the small Floquet splitting approaches zero. It avoids extracting a direction by dividing numerical errors by that splitting. Conjugation by \sigma_2 reverses \delta, so b_x has only odd powers of \delta. The first Dyson coefficient from (3) is \pi\delta J_0(2a). Each order has norm at most (\pi|\delta|)^k/k!. Setting z=\pi|\delta| gives |b_x-\pi\delta J_0(2a)|\le\sinh z-z. \tag{9} For z<\operatorname{arsinh}1, it follows that \boxed{ |\epsilon-\delta J_0(2a)| \le\frac{\arcsin(\sinh z)-z}{\pi}, \qquad \left|\partial_\delta\epsilon-J_0(2a)\right| \le\frac{\cosh z}{\sqrt{1-\sinh^2z}}-1. } \tag{10} The frequency bound begins at \pi^2|\delta|^3/3, and the derivative bound begins at \pi^2\delta^2. Both are uniform in the prescribed drive amplitude. They control this complete two-state problem; they do not bound an omitted spatial complement. Direct evolution, an interaction-picture Dyson calculation and (7) independently agree. Near a zero of J_0, the first numerical eigenvector extraction was insufficiently resolved. The refined expansion and the regular formula after (8) resolve that issue. A zero of the leading Bessel factor is not an exact zero at every finite \delta. The static shape force follows from the same Floquet operator Write the periodic state as c=e^{-i\epsilon\tau}u(\tau). The self-adjoint period operator is H-i\partial_\tau, on periodic two-component functions with the cycle-averaged inner product. Differentiating its normalized eigenvalue gives \boxed{ \partial_{x_0}\epsilon=\overline{u^\dagger\sigma_1u}, \qquad \partial_a\epsilon=\overline{\cos\tau\,u^\dagger\sigma_2u}. } \tag{11} The overline denotes an average over the full period. Since x_0 enters exactly like \delta, equations (5) and (10) give \boxed{ \partial_X\epsilon_{\rm physical} =s[J_0(2a)+O(\delta^2)].} \tag{12} For canonical wave charge \mathcal Q, the generalized force is minus \mathcal Q times (12). The positive-frequency branch changes the appropriate sign but leaves its leading nonzero magnitude. Thus a nonzero common frequency multiplier also leaves a nonzero common static source. Cancelling that source by setting the multiplier to zero removes the leading mass frequency. This is a limitation of the common analytic driven branch, not a theorem excluding every self-consistent periodic spatial solution. A different supporting contribution can enter the static shape equation, but must be derived and counted. Cancelling one temporal harmonic does not cancel the full source The complete leading source perpendicular to the original coupling is \boxed{ \langle\sigma_2\rangle =-4\delta\sum_{k=1,3,5,\ldots} \frac{J_k(2a)}{k}\cos(k\tau)+O(\delta^3). } \tag{13} This follows by integrating the Bloch equation \langle\sigma_2\rangle'=-2\delta\langle\sigma_3\rangle using the zeroth-order rotated polarization. Half-period symmetry sets the constant of integration to zero. The odd Bessel harmonics are the Fourier coefficients of \sin(2a\sin\tau). At the first nonzero root of J_1(2a), a\simeq1.91585, the fundamental amplitude source vanishes at this order while J_0(2a)\simeq-0.40276 remains nonzero. However the third and higher force harmonics survive. They cannot all vanish for a nonzero a, since that would require \sin(2a\sin\tau) to vanish for every \tau. The static source in (12) also remains. The time-averaged signed wave energy has the exact derivative expression \overline E_{\rm wave}/\Omega =\delta\,\partial_\delta\epsilon+a\,\partial_a\epsilon, \tag{14} and hence, for unit phase norm, \boxed{\overline E_{\rm wave} =t[J_0(2a)-2aJ_1(2a)]+O(t^3/\Omega^2).} \tag{15} A Floquet phase alone therefore does not account for the wave's energy exchange with its support. A signed partial energy is not negative particle inertia. The complete physical state must satisfy the positive inertia requirement with its sustaining field included. Allow the geometric oscillator to react For a stated local test, give the real geometric mode a positive kinetic coefficient \mathcal M and a harmonic restoring frequency \Omega_g. Normalize c^\dagger c=1, retaining its arbitrary complex polarization, and use L=\mathcal M(\dot y^2-\Omega_g^2y^2) +\frac{i\mathcal Q}{2}(c^\dagger\dot c-\dot c^\dagger c) -\mathcal Qc^\dagger(t\sigma_1+sy\sigma_2)c-E_0. \tag{16} This is an inverse action for retained modes. It does not derive the oscillator or its restoring frequency from the full spatial field. In particular, the earlier curvature calculation supplies no leading pinning coefficient at depths two and three. With \tau=\Omega_gt_{\rm time}, z=sy/\Omega_g, \delta=t/\Omega_g and \lambda=\mathcal Qs^2/(2\mathcal M\Omega_g^3), the exact equations are \boxed{i c'=(\delta\sigma_1+z\sigma_2)c, \qquad z''+z=-\lambda c^\dagger\sigma_2c.} \tag{17} The complete conserved energy, apart from E_0, is \frac{E-E_0}{\mathcal Q\Omega_g} =\frac{z'^2+z^2}{2\lambda} +c^\dagger(\delta\sigma_1+z\sigma_2)c \ge-|\delta|-\frac\lambda2. \tag{18} The inequality uses the fixed wave norm and completes the positive geometric square. The wave and geometry are integrated together at \lambda=0.1,10,100, without prescribing a cosine trajectory. Their common norm and full energy are conserved. Increasing reciprocal response changes the trajectory substantially. These integrations do not establish a periodic particle or balance the separate static deformation X. For a harmonic geometric motion of dimensionless amplitude a, its positive energy obeys the simple identity \boxed{\frac{E_{\rm oscillator}}{\mathcal Q t} =\frac{a^2}{2\lambda\delta}.} \tag{19} At an appreciable drive amplitude, treating \lambda\delta as a small reciprocal-response parameter has a supporting-energy cost. This is not an argument for discarding the geometric kinetic energy. The original geometric normalization tightens that comparison When the metric comes from the previously declared positive geometric action, the normalization calculation gives \mathcal M=E_0M_d/(2\pi d\Lambda^2). Here M_d is its horizontal shape metric, \Lambda=R/L, s=\gamma|\kappa_d| and \gamma=g\Lambda. Put e_0=E_0/(\mathcal Q t). For drive frequency \Omega, \lambda\delta= \frac{\pi d\Lambda^2\gamma^2|\kappa_d|^2} {e_0M_d\Omega^4}. \tag{20} The leading normal carrier has interior frequencies no larger than \gamma\sqrt d. If the drive is required to be slower by a factor \eta<1, then the necessary window \Omega\le\eta\gamma\sqrt d implies \boxed{\lambda\delta\ge \frac{\pi|\kappa_d|^2}{e_0M_d\eta^4 d g^2}.} \tag{21} The separation length cancels from this bound. Both g=0.02,0.05 and all six depths are checked using the complete dressed endpoint coefficients. A chosen weak-response budget also imposes a lower bound on e_0. This is the cost of those stated approximation conditions, not an exclusion of an exact strongly reacting state. Drive-induced mixing with the spatial complement still needs its own estimate; frequency separation alone is insufficient. Exact temporal transport is a separate possible structure Let M(q)=U(q)M_0U(q)^\dagger for a specified unitary mode frame. Instantaneous eigenvalues alone do not determine the actual evolving frequencies. With \mathcal A=\dot U U^\dagger,\qquad D_t=\partial_t-\mathcal A, \tag{22} the positive inverse action L=\|D_t\psi\|^2-\|M(q)\psi\|^2 +\frac I2(\dot q^2-\Omega_g^2q^2)-E_0 \tag{23} reduces exactly under \psi=Uv to fixed wave oscillators plus the positive geometric oscillator. Every eigenfrequency of M_0 is preserved under the complete transport. Removing \mathcal A instead changes the frequencies, despite leaving the instantaneous spectrum unchanged. Independent full-period integrations verify both statements for the maintained frequency controls. This is a useful explicit frequency-preserving structure, with its full time derivatives retained. It is not yet a derived IDWT support. A chosen unitary mixing of modes need not be a physical spatial deformation. If q is only a component-frame choice, it is not physical motion. If it describes a physical geometric mode, its connection, inertia and energy must arise from that mode's action. In (23) the geometric energy is independent of the wave frequency, so their required physical relation has not been selected. Verification periodic_endpoint_checks.py passes 193 checks of full-period evolution, reciprocal derivatives, force harmonics, energy and autonomous local motion. Its periodic report preserves the raw trajectories and exact executed sources. periodic_symmetry_checks.py passes 240 independent half-period, regular-polarization and uniform-bound checks. Its symmetry report tests the analytic bounds at small gaps and at substantially larger frequency ratios. spectral_transport_checks.py passes 147 checks of complete positive temporal transport and the geometric normalization bound. Its transport report keeps the assumed mode frame distinct from a physical geometry.

title: Spatial dimension and component frames of the mass carrier
summary: The round-feature spinor operator extends consistently to the positive tangent dimensions, but its depth-two limit has no harmonic tower; a local phase change also requires transporting the angular lift in the completed mass operator.
text: The completed radial calculation uses a genuine spatial differential operator, but a physical interpretation also requires its surface and component-frame data. Two independent checks clarify those requirements. The round-feature surface operator works in each positive tangent dimension used by the construction, with its correct spinor rank. At depth two, however, the surface has dimension zero and cannot supply the assigned harmonic tower. Separately, the bounded angular completion is written in a specified component frame. A change of local phase must transport its angular operator along with the scalar, connection and wave. These checks concern ordinary spatial dimensions and representations of field components. They introduce no compactified dimensions or new interacting particles. The surface and normal dimensions add to the physical depth The round feature is S_R^m\subset\mathbb R^{m+2}, with two ordinary normal directions and m=d-2. \tag{1} Its intrinsic spinor rank is r=2^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}. For m\ge1, the shifted surface operator is B_K=D_{S^m}-\frac1{2R}. \tag{2} At unit radius, an ambient Clifford representation supplies the complete coordinate formula in a Killing-spinor frame: B_K F=kF-\Gamma_x\Gamma_{\nabla_S}F, \qquad k=\frac{m-1}{2},\qquad \boxed{B_K^2F=\Delta_{S^m}F+k^2F.} \tag{3} For odd m, the ambient Clifford representation in m+1 dimensions has twice the intrinsic spinor rank. The products in (3) preserve ambient chirality; restricting to one chirality gives the correct intrinsic rank. Both chiral copies must not be counted as independent physical directions. At m=1, the induced bounding spin structure gives the usual antiperiodic ordinary spinor; its coefficients in the Killing frame are periodic. The differential identity can be checked without assuming an eigenvalue. Set A_i=-\Gamma_x\Gamma_i+x_iI. Then \partial_iA_j=-\Gamma_i\Gamma_j+\delta_{ij}I, \qquad 2kA_j+\sum_iA_i\partial_iA_j=mx_jI, \tag{4} while the symmetric second-derivative coefficient is -\delta_{ij}+x_ix_j on the unit sphere. These are exactly the coefficients of the positive spherical Laplacian. Independent complex spatial jets verify the identity and its tangent propagation symbol at every maintained positive m. For scalar coefficient harmonic degree L\ge1, the two shifted Dirac branches have RB_K=\pm\beta,\qquad \beta=L+\frac{m-1}{2}, \tag{5} with multiplicities r\binom{L+m-1}{m-1},\qquad r\binom{L+m-2}{m-1}. \tag{6} Their sum equals the complete scalar harmonic multiplicity times the intrinsic spinor rank. Taking the maintained L=n+1 gives \beta=n+(d-1)/2, precisely the value used by the radial carrier. The parity extension therefore introduces no new particle index or separately fitted spectral shift. This validates the reference surface expression at depths three, four, five, six and ten. It does not supply the full curved normal extension, select the physical geometry, or identify the scalar/vector geometric fluctuations with ordinary spinors. Their different full-turn rotation laws remain explicit in the geometric carrier. The depth-two limit needs a different spatial realization For d=2, equation (1) gives m=0. The round feature S^0 consists of two points. It has no tangential derivative and no unbounded sequence of surface harmonics. Its intrinsic Dirac derivative is zero; the shift in (2) supplies only a constant, not a harmonic tower. The same conclusion follows directly from homogeneous harmonic polynomials on \mathbb R^1: \frac{d^2}{dx^2}x^L=L(L-1)x^{L-2}. \tag{7} Only degrees zero and one survive. The assigned boson surface degrees 77, 82 and 96 cannot be obtained by extending this construction to m=0. The earlier depth-two finite matrix, normal profile and polarization checks remain algebraically valid. They prescribe their scalar parameter \beta; they do not derive it from this zero-dimensional feature. Consequently those checks should not be described as a complete spatial realization of the depth-two bosons. A two-dimensional cavity or another actual spatial construction must supply the missing operator before it can be combined with that normal model. Its dimension count must remain two; an extra independent spatial coordinate cannot be added merely to restore a harmonic label. This is a limitation of the codimension-two feature construction. It is not an alternative particle-depth assignment or a failure of the combinatorial mass formula itself. The photon identification is also still separate from the formal zero of the massive matrix. The whole-depth spherical alternative supplies an explicit different spatial construction with a harmonic tower at every maintained depth, including two. It extends the known conformal spectrum to a local signed spinor polynomial at odd depths and supplies a separate actual tangent-vector polarization control at depth two. Its round geometry and component chain remain physical inputs; it is not a repair of the zero-dimensional feature or a derived supporting state. Winding and spatial depth are distinct inputs The normal profile has winding w, which fixes its localized kernel dimension. The construction chooses w=d. Spatial depth determines the surface dimension in (1); it does not by itself force that winding. Keeping the two integers distinct gives the leading angular product \prod_{l=0}^{w-1} \left[n+l+\frac{d-w}{2}\right]. \tag{8} The required degree-d polynomial is recovered when w=d. This makes the role of that choice explicit. It is not a new unrestricted mode search or evidence that another dimensionality reproduces the maintained mass construction. A same-field geometric selection of the winding remains to be derived. The completed angular operator has specified frame data The linked geometric action has the local phase transformation W'=e^{i\lambda}W,\qquad A'=A+\nabla\lambda. \tag{9} Let Q_A=(\tau_3-I)/2 and U=e^{-iQ_A\lambda}, extended over the canonical pair. The full normal Dirac operator obeys D'=UDU^\dagger. The curvature B, and therefore h=zB/2, is unchanged. Independent Cartesian differentiation confirms that the geometric energy density is unchanged. The completed mass operator also uses J=L+\frac12S+\frac d2\tau_3, \qquad L=-i(x_1\partial_2-x_2\partial_1), \qquad K_{\rm nat}=\{D,\mathcal R\}-2J. \tag{10} Write \xi\lambda=x_1\partial_2\lambda-x_2\partial_1\lambda. Since the angular derivative acts on the local phase, \boxed{J'=UJU^\dagger=J+Q_A\xi\lambda.} \tag{11} If W,A and the wave are changed but the literal angular derivative in (10) is held fixed, the raw completed formula instead has the defect \boxed{ H_{\rm raw}[W',A']U-UH_{\rm raw}[W,A] =C\chi_1Q_A(\xi\lambda)U. } \tag{12} The operator here is in the unscaled parent units. The defect is multiplied by \epsilon in the scaled operator (1) of the moving-support calculation. It is a bounded multiplication term for a smooth localized phase change. Transporting J according to (11) removes (12) exactly. This keeps the radial reference operator and its simplex calculation unchanged. It does not establish a master-field origin for the selected angular lift, or turn a component-frame change into an observed force. Equivalently one can describe the lift with a reference connection \mathcal A, whose angular component transforms by a_{\rm ref}'=a_{\rm ref}+\xi\lambda. Then J_{\rm ref}=L+a_{\rm ref}Q_A+\frac12S+\frac d2\tau_3, \qquad K_{\rm ref}=S-d\tau_3+2(a-a_{\rm ref})Q_A. \tag{13} In the original reference frame a_{\rm ref}=0, this is the maintained coefficient. Equation (13) records the operator's frame data; it does not posit a new independently interacting field. Whether that lift is supplied by the ambient geometry, a chosen gauge description, or retained same-field modes must be stated in a complete physical action. The fixed-frame spectral calculations are meaningful within their stated frame. The correction is that an arbitrary phase change cannot be applied to only some coefficients and then interpreted as the same physical operator. Conversely, a claimed gauge redundancy of a proposed joint action needs the complete transformation law, including (11). The frame term can reach the small-frequency endpoints The defect is not necessarily invisible after radial projection. For \lambda=f(r)\sin[(d-1)\theta], the leading endpoint contraction in the stated real radial convention is \boxed{ \langle\psi_-,C\chi_1Q_A(\xi\lambda)\psi_+\rangle =\pi(d-1)\int_0^\infty r f(r)u_-(r)u_+(r)dr>0, } \tag{14} when f is positive away from the origin and decays appropriately. Both endpoint fields include their complete radial dressing. The other component term has angular weight d+1 and drops out of (14). Direct angular quadrature agrees with this independent radial integral at every maintained depth. Thus correct frame transport matters even for the small-frequency subspace. Equation (14) is a leading endpoint matrix element; it is not being used as an unverified complete finite-scale eigenvalue derivative. The normal leading operator is already covariant, so the leading physical shape derivative used for the nearby-zero theorem is unaffected by this order-\epsilon bookkeeping correction. Verification surface_dimension_checks.py passes 194 checks of actual Clifford representations, intrinsic spinor ranks, the complete differential square, tangent symbols, full-turn rotations, multiplicities and the depth-two boundary case. Its surface-dimension report keeps that missing tower explicit. angular_frame_covariance_checks.py passes 156 checks of independent Cartesian derivatives, unchanged geometric energy, the exact raw frame defect and its transported cancellation. The frame-covariance report also retains full radial endpoint contractions and their raw fields.

title: A localized core determined by polarization ratios
summary: A homogeneous current law gives explicit localized common profiles and positive total inertia, but its full formal linearized evolution has unbounded wave-packet amplification.
text: A reconstructed local current action admits a localized spatial core whose shape is determined by polarization ratios. Its defining equation is independent of the overall field magnitude. The same coefficients and profile support every coherent grade of the existing simplex current hierarchy. In that hierarchy the assigned electron and muon frequencies remain different, while their common spatial size is unchanged. This is a specified mathematical model with testable consequences. The binomial current weights, their physical spatial carrier and the common unit of frequency remain premises. This action has not been identified with the separate gapped normal operator. Neither its nonlinear stability nor the physical selection of occupied particle grades is assumed below. Mass remains the selected frequency in equivalent units. One local potential and its complete source Use the doubled Dirac field and partner currents of the localized-current construction on ordinary physical R^d. The matrices satisfy A_a=\sigma_x\otimes\alpha_a,\qquad B_0=\sigma_z\otimes I_r,\qquad B_1=\sigma_x\otimes\beta,\qquad B_2=I_2\otimes\beta, where the Hermitian alpha_a and beta anticommute and square to one. Here r is a representation rank, not a count of physical dimensions. The partner matrix beta_p is the same numerical beta on the right index. For the 2r by r field matrix Psi, define Hermitian currents C=\Psi^\dagger B_0\Psi,\qquad J=\Psi^\dagger B_1\Psi,\qquad K=\Psi^\dagger B_2\Psi. Retain the canonical first-order kinetic term and the spatial operator -i A_a partial_a in units hbar=c=1. For one coherent grade, write \begin{aligned} F_q(C)&=\sqrt{qr\,\operatorname{Tr}(C^2) +(1-q)[\operatorname{Tr}C]^2},\qquad 0<q\le1,\\ U&=\omega_N F_q(C)+m_c\operatorname{Tr}(J\beta_p) -\kappa\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_p K) \operatorname{Tr}(JK)}{\operatorname{Tr}(K^2)}. \end{aligned} \tag{1} The coefficient omega_N in this isolated-grade expression is supplied by the common graded current action described below, rather than an independent parameter for each particle. The core coefficients obey kappa > m_c > 0. The ratio q is the existing trace/exchange current comparison; q=1 and q=1/(r+1) leave the displayed branch unchanged. The last term depends on matrix polarization ratios. It is a local interaction of the retained components of the same field. No independently interacting scalar field, Yukawa coupling or exchanged particle is present. The denominator requires K to be nonzero. Its behavior at a vanishing current remains a domain question for general interacting configurations. Put s=Tr(K^2), b=Tr(beta_p K), w=Tr(JK), and define \begin{aligned} A_C&=\frac{qr C+(1-q)\operatorname{Tr}(C)I_r}{F_q(C)},\\ F(K)&=\frac{bK}{s},\\ Z(J,K)&=\frac ws\beta_p+\frac bs J-\frac{2bw}{s^2}K. \end{aligned} \tag{2} The full local source in the field equation is \mathcal S(\Psi)=\omega_N B_0\Psi A_C +m_c B_1\Psi\beta_p -\kappa[B_1\Psi F(K)+B_2\Psi Z(J,K)]. \tag{3} The second term in the square brackets comes from varying K. It cannot be omitted merely because the particular stationary branch has J=0. All complex and conjugate field variations are retained in (3). Every term of U is homogeneous of degree two in Psi. Consequently S(a Psi)=a S(Psi) for real a>0. Multiplying a solved profile by a common constant changes its canonical norm without changing its frequency, shape, or coefficients. This does not derive a quantized norm. Reduce the spatial equation to a polarization ratio Take the upper-block branch \Psi_N(t,x)=e^{-i\omega_Nt} \begin{pmatrix}\phi(x)\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \phi=f(r_x)I_r+i h(r_x)\alpha_{\hat x},\qquad r_x=|x|. \tag{4} The field is regular at the origin when h(0)=0. Write rho=f^2+h^2. Then phi^dagger phi=phi phi^dagger=rho I_r, J=0, K=rho S with S^2=I_r, and t=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_p K)}{r\rho} =\frac{f^2-h^2}{f^2+h^2},\qquad \beta\phi F(K)=t\phi. \tag{5} The upper field equation gives the selected frequency. The complete lower field equation becomes -i\alpha\cdot\nabla\phi+m_c\beta\phi\beta_p-\kappa t\phi=0, or equivalently f'=-(m_c+\kappa t)h,\qquad h'=(\kappa t-m_c)f-\frac{d-1}{r_x}h. \tag{6} Unlike a density-dependent core law, this potential depends on f and h only through their ratio. Let y=h/f and a=kappa-m_c. Direct subtraction of the two equations gives the Riccati equation \boxed{y'=a(1-y^2)-\frac{d-1}{r_x}y.} \tag{7} Its regular solution is explicit: \boxed{y(r_x)=\frac{I_{d/2}(a r_x)}{I_{d/2-1}(a r_x)}.} \tag{8} The modified-Bessel recurrences in DLMF 10.29 verify (7) by direct differentiation. They are used as mathematical identities, not as an imported physical mechanism. The remaining profile is the positive quadrature f(r_x)=A\exp\left[-\int_0^{r_x} \left(m_c+\kappa\frac{1-y(s)^2}{1+y(s)^2}\right)y(s)\,ds\right], \qquad h=yf. \tag{9} Thus there is no shooting adjustment of the central magnitude to select a localized solution. A controls its canonical norm and is absent from (7). The field's mass is still read from omega_N. Regularity and localization The small-argument Bessel limit gives y(r_x)=\frac{a r_x}{d}+O(r_x^3),\qquad f(r_x)=A\left[1-\frac{(m_c+\kappa)a}{2d}r_x^2+O(r_x^4)\right]. \tag{10} For a>0 the positive Bessel ratio lies between zero and one. Its large-argument expansion gives y=1-\frac{d-1}{2a r_x}+O(r_x^{-2}),\qquad t=\frac{d-1}{2a r_x}+O(r_x^{-2}). \tag{11} Substituting (11) into (6) cancels the coefficient a in the leading power-law prefactor: f(r_x)=C r_x^{-(d-1)/2}e^{-m_c r_x}[1+O(r_x^{-1})], \qquad h/f\longrightarrow1. \tag{12} The norm and all positive spatial moments are finite. Equation (12) is for fixed kappa>m_c; the limit kappa approaching m_c is not uniform. At kappa=m_c the regular ratio is y=0 and the core is constant, so it is not a localized member of this family. A common shape and frequency hierarchy For the complete graded action replace omega_N F_q(C) in (1) by U_{\rm mass}=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k\ge0} \binom{k+d-1}{d-1}F_q(R_k), \tag{13} where R_k is the existing partial-current hierarchy and r in F_q is the partner rank. The binding currents J and K sum over all grades before (1) is varied. On a single coherent grade N, R_k=rho I_r tensor P_(z,k) for k<=N, with a normalized coherent ray z. Their contractions give \omega_N=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k=0}^N\binom{k+d-1}{d-1} =\omega_{0,d}\binom{N+d}{d}. \tag{14} The spatial equation (6) contains neither N nor omega_N. Thus the electron N=12 and muon N=34 at depth six have the same profile at fixed m_c and kappa, while their simplex factors remain 18564 and 3838380. The depth-ten comparison N=22 has factor 64512240. These assignments have not changed. The carrier and the binomial weights in (13) remain model premises. For kappa/m_c=2 the refined unit-norm profile calculations give L_rms*m_c approximately 2.72054 at depth five, 3.21819 at depth six, and 5.21361 at depth ten. The odd-depth comparison uses a sufficient Clifford representation without introducing another spatial coordinate. The independent report below verifies their integration and domain refinement. Restoring units gives L_rms=c times the dimensionless factor divided by m_c. Identifying m_c with the shared frequency unit is an additional common coefficient choice, not a consequence of the profile equation. Energy, phase and complete inertial response Because the full Hamiltonian is homogeneous of degree two, a regular stationary solution with canonical norm Q satisfies E=omega Q. This follows by varying its overall magnitude in the stationary equation; it does not identify that magnitude with mass. For (4), the binding and spatial kinetic energy densities vanish on the solution while their variations sustain (6). The complete stress is T^00=omega_N Tr(phi^dagger phi), with T^0a=T^ab=0. Every B_j anticommutes with A_a, so the displayed scalar currents are invariant under the same spinor boost as in the maintained localized-current action. The boosted solution therefore has E(v)=\gamma\hbar\omega_NQ,\qquad \mathbf P(v)=\gamma\frac{\hbar\omega_NQ}{c^2}\mathbf v. \tag{15} This is the momentum of the full declared action. For Q=1 its positive inertial coefficient is the selected mass-frequency value. The field continues oscillating in its zero-total-momentum frame. The independent report below checks the ordinary spatial derivatives, full source and complete boosted stress of this new binding law. The statement about boosts uses the existing coefficient-frame assumptions. A retained dynamical frame can preserve this branch when its added terms and first variations vanish there, but that does not identify coefficient grades with the actual spatial oscillator spectrum. A complete physical mode carrier, interaction-domain control, stability and occupation selection remain separate tests of the proposed model. A full tail response limits a stability claim The first independent report, polarization-core-20260914T120746_793183Z.json, passes 405 checks of the complete source, its real Hessian, ordinary Cartesian derivatives, profile refinement, relative-phase energy, physical scaling and complete boosted stress. The radius factors above are stable under the documented outer-domain and integration refinements. The relative phase is explicit. For an upper field phi=f I_r+exp(i vartheta) h alpha_(xhat), at fixed f and h, U_{\rm mass}=r\omega_N \sqrt{(f^2+h^2)^2+4q f^2h^2\cos^2\vartheta}. \tag{16} The quadrature values vartheta=+/-pi/2 minimize this restricted energy when q>0. The full radial stationary equation chooses the displayed normalizable branch. Equation (16) does not assign an antiparticle interpretation to the other sign or prove full dynamical stability. A complete frozen tail calculation retains all spinor and partner variations, including directions outside the radial ansatz. At y=1, the binding changes the real Hessian by rank two. Its smallest invariant space under that change, the remaining local terms, and Fourier motion parallel and perpendicular to the radial direction is eight-dimensional. An exact rational-matrix construction verifies that closure. The leading slow disturbance frequencies in that block, at large omega_N and fixed spatial wave vector p, satisfy \nu_\pm^2=q\left[p_\parallel^2+ \left(\sqrt{p_\perp^2+(\kappa-m_c)^2}\pm\kappa\right)^2\right] +O(\omega_N^{-2}). \tag{17} These are frequencies of disturbances to the oscillating pattern; omega_N remains its assigned mass-frequency. In particular, the exact finite-omega generator has a zero eigenvalue when p_\parallel=0,\qquad p_\perp^2=m_c(2\kappa-m_c). \tag{18} At m_c=1, kappa=2 and q=1/9, exact ranks give a one-dimensional kernel and a two-dimensional kernel of the squared generator, including at the electron frequency. This is a nontrivial zero-frequency Jordan block: a frozen linear disturbance can have a secular contribution proportional to time. It is not negative physical particle inertia. The exact characteristic polynomial and full invariant subspace are checked in polarization-tail-20260914T125458_161142Z.json. Its 61 checks include exact Jordan ranks at both assigned depth-six frequencies. Since localization requires kappa>m_c, the critical wave number in (18) is real throughout this family. Moving those two coefficients does not remove that critical direction. The formal full-space linearization is not uniformly bounded The tail calculation can be carried beyond a frozen-point diagnostic. For m_c=1, kappa=2 and p=sqrt(3) e_perpendicular, let A_infinity(p) be the complete frozen generator. Its exact affected subspace contains vectors u and v with A_\infty(p)u=v,\qquad A_\infty(p)v=0,\qquad \langle u,v\rangle=0. \tag{19} The inner product is the canonical real-field norm inherited from the complete spinor and partner space. Exact algebra gives \boxed{\frac{\|v\|}{\|u\|} =c_J=\frac{2(q\omega_N^2+1)}{\sqrt{\omega_N^2+1}},\qquad \frac{\|u+t v\|}{\|u\|}=\sqrt{1+c_J^2t^2}.} \tag{20} The full depth-five and depth-six Hessians give the same expression through their common two-direction Clifford subspace. At q=1/9, omega_N=18564 gives c_J approximately 4125.33 in the stated core time units; omega_N=3838380 gives approximately 852973.33. These are amplification coefficients, not negative inertias or new mass values. Equation (20) also has a nonzero continuous limit at q=0. To connect this result to the localized core, normalize a smooth compact packet chi and put \eta_{R,L}(x,t)=L^{-d/2} \chi\!\left(\frac{x-R e_1}{L}\right) e^{ip\cdot x}(u+t v). \tag{21} Take R much larger than L. On the packet support the radial direction approaches e_1 and h/f approaches one. The Hessian of the degree-two potential is independent of the common magnitude of the background; on this branch its coefficients are smooth bounded functions of those polarization ratios. Their difference from the frozen generator is O((L+1)/R), while derivatives of the envelope contribute O(1/L). For each fixed time interval 0<=t<=T the full linearized residual obeys \|\mathrm{residual}(t)\| \le C\left(\frac1L+\frac{L+1}{R}\right)(1+t). \tag{22} The formal linearized operator has the constant symmetric Dirac principal part plus bounded local coefficients. Its linear evolution therefore exists on the canonical L2 space with an exponential finite-time norm bound. Apply its variation-of-constants formula to (22). Taking L and R sufficiently large for the fixed T makes the difference between the exact linear solution and (21) arbitrarily small. It follows that \boxed{\|e^{T\mathcal A}\|\ge\sqrt{1+c_J^2T^2}.} \tag{23} Real perturbations follow by combining the opposite Fourier vectors. The finite nonzero wave number distinguishes these packets from a global phase change or a common translation. Their overlaps with the finite localized symmetry directions tend to zero as R grows. Equation (23) rules out uniformly bounded formal linearized evolution for the full unbounded spatial core. It is stronger than merely finding a Jordan block in a frozen matrix. The report polarization-packet-20260914T131301_562773Z.json passes 32 exact embedding, norm and amplification checks. The packet argument itself is analytic; the report is not a nonlinear time simulation. A nonlinear stability theorem would additionally have to handle the interaction's current-zero domain. Compact packets can be scaled small relative to the background on their support, but that does not provide uniform nonlinear control of arbitrarily distant tails in the L2 norm. The existence and positive total inertia results remain valid for the stated branch, while a stable physical particle has not been obtained. The physical mode carrier and coefficient frame also remain model inputs. A structural test of more general polarization binding Changing the power of the binding ratio does not automatically repair the response. A broader homogeneous local potential is U_{\rm bind}=-\frac{\sqrt r\,g(t)}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}K^2}} \operatorname{Tr}(JK),\qquad t=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_pK)}{\sqrt{r\operatorname{Tr}K^2}}. \tag{24} For g(t)=kappa t, this is (1). On the same conformal-unitary upper field, the radial equation becomes y'=(1+y^2)[g(t)-m_ct]-\frac{d-1}{r_x}y,\qquad t=\frac{1-y^2}{1+y^2}. \tag{25} A limiting polarization t_infinity in [0,1) satisfies g(t_infinity)=m_c t_infinity. Write s_infinity=sqrt(1-t_infinity^2). The fixed point attracts the radial ratio when g'(t_infinity)>m_c. There is an explicit neutral direction in the full frozen equation at \boxed{p_*^2=m_c s_\infty^2[2g'(t_\infty)-m_c].} \tag{26} To verify it, let alpha_1 point radially and alpha_2 transversely, put Xi=i alpha_1 alpha_2, and normalize the limiting upper field phi. Define the two real-space perturbation coefficients \begin{aligned} F_c&=\phi(2m_ct_\infty I-i m_cs_\infty\alpha_1),\\ F_s&=i\phi\,p_*(t_\infty\alpha_2-s_\infty\Xi). \end{aligned} \tag{27} The upper disturbance F_c cos(p_*x_2)+F_s sin(p_*x_2), with zero lower block, has only a scalar variation of C. The rotating-frame root-current variation therefore vanishes. Substitution into the complete lower equation leaves zero precisely under (26). This retains the sine, cosine, complex-conjugate and local norm variations together. It does not change the assigned background mass-frequency. The canonical symplectic product of these two coefficients is zero. When the full frozen kernel is one-dimensional, that condition supplies a generalized zero vector and hence a secular mode. A degenerate kernel requires its own analysis; (26) alone is not a universal instability theorem for every possible function g. For g(t)=kappa t^p with p=3 or 5 and kappa>m_c, t_infinity=(m_c/kappa)^(1/(p-1)). At m_c=1 and kappa=2 the critical wave numbers are approximately 1.58114 and 1.62359. Both retain the one-dimensional kernel and two-dimensional squared kernel in full depth-six checks. The resolved singular values agree with the explicit vector (27). polarization-power-20260914T134233_510923Z.json passes 63 checks of the complete variational source, real Hessian, homogeneity, explicit neutral vector, symplectic product and numerical Jordan ranks for the linear, cubic and fifth-power laws. These are specified mathematical controls, not additional fitted particle laws. The attracting-tail condition makes (26) real, so this neutral direction is a structural constraint on this polarization-only binding family. A joint model with spatial geometry must address it explicitly. The five exact symbolic identities in polarization_tail_identity.py verify (26)-(27), both real-space quadratures, the scalar current variation and the symplectic product for arbitrary m_c, p and limiting ratio y. title: Generalizing polarization cancellation and testing its inertial meaning
summary: Cancellation is controlled by the available polarization channels and occupied frequencies; extending those channels permits higher-depth source cancellation, while the retained positive action's energy and energy–momentum mass do not cancel.
text: The depth-two result supplies an exact cancellation of coherent shape forces. It motivates a stronger test: can phase or polarization also remove the collective inertia, and does that possibility disappear at higher physical depths? Two calculations separate the relevant effects. Extending the available polarization channels permits force cancellation at higher depths without changing the frequencies. The complete positive quadratic energy of the retained occupied modes nevertheless remains positive and phase independent. Thus the current model supplies a polarization compatibility rule, but does not yet turn that rule into cancellation of inertial mass. The subsequent actual normal-mode classification finds no independent repeated factor in the existing normal chain. Its geometric modes have different rotation weights. The complete linked stress instead supplies a null traveling disturbance above a background with positive inertia, without cancelling positive kinetic contributions. The two-channel threshold is not automatically a dimensional law The actual two-block calculation has two isospectral chiral sectors with different source matrices. At depth two, placing its two occupied frequency bands in opposite blocks removes their beat term. With three or more bands and resolved distinct beat frequencies, the exact endpoint determinant prevents all pair sources from vanishing. To test whether this depends on retaining only two channels, consider a conditional extension with r identical polarization channels of the same retained field. Each channel has the same squared carrier T^\dagger T. No frequency, spatial profile or per-particle coefficient is changed. This extension tests possible component content; it does not derive the physical value of r, or identify it with the spatial depth. Write the normalized polarization of occupied band j as p_j\in\mathbb C^r. For a centered shape source, \boxed{\langle u_i\otimes p_i,K_a(u_j\otimes p_j)\rangle =\langle u_i,K_a u_j\rangle\,p_i^\dagger p_j.} \tag{1} The endpoint pair-source vector is nonzero for every distinct pair in the tested finite matrices. With distinct beat frequencies, its cancellation therefore requires p_i^\dagger p_j=0. Every beat source can vanish if and only if the occupied polarizations can be mutually orthogonal: \boxed{r\ge N_{\rm occupied}.} \tag{2} Here the filled carrier has N_{\rm occupied}=d. Keeping r=2 gives the two-band threshold. Allowing r to grow to d permits cancellation at every tested depth. The same orthogonality cancels every centered source, not just the endpoint used to prove necessity. The frequency-weighted diagonal source sum remains zero. The occupied frequencies and their canonical populations are unchanged, so the same averaged energy function and its tested spatial Hessian are preserved. The extension adds polarization content whose physical origin must still be supplied; it does not repair the energy-normalization problem. This extension is not an assertion that the physical higher-depth field actually contains these independent channels. It shows why that field's polarization content must be derived before a two-only cancellation can be attributed to physical dimensionality. A quantitative bound when there are too few channels Let G_{ij}=p_i^\dagger p_j. Since G\ge0, its trace is N and its rank is at most r. Cauchy's inequality on its nonzero eigenvalues gives \operatorname{Tr}G^2\ge\frac{N^2}{r},\qquad \boxed{\sum_{i<j}|p_i^\dagger p_j|^2 \ge\frac{N(N-r)}{2r}.} \tag{3} Use zero as the lower bound when r\ge N. If w_{ij}>0 is the squared norm of the actual endpoint source for that pair, then \sum_{i<j}w_{ij}|p_i^\dagger p_j|^2 \ge w_{\min}\max\left(0,\frac{N(N-r)}{2r}\right). \tag{4} The six-depth test uses the computed spatial source coefficients in w_{ij}. It tests arbitrary complex polarizations, exact binary assignments and orthogonal constructions with enough channels. Neither (3) nor (4) is a new multiplicative factor in the mass formula. Force cancellation leaves the retained positive energy intact For the explicit action L=\|\partial_t(Bc)\|^2-c^\dagger H_P^2c, hold the geometry fixed and use normalized positive-frequency modes \phi_j. Their orthogonality gives c(t)=\sum_j A_je^{i\theta_j-is_jt}\phi_j, \qquad \boxed{E=2\sum_js_j^2|A_j|^2 =\sum_jq_js_j,\quad q_j=2s_j|A_j|^2>0.} \tag{5} No relative phase occurs in the complete integrated energy. The kinetic Gram matrix is the identity on these independent modes. A positive spatial Gram form can vanish only when the represented field variation vanishes; an algebraic null direction is not automatically a moving massless particle. For the source-balancing populations q_j=s_j/\sum_ks_k, total canonical charge is one and \boxed{E_0=\frac{\sum_js_j^2}{\sum_js_j}>s_{\min}.} \tag{6} This also holds for the exact depth-two opposite-block state. Its shape force cancels, while its positive kinetic and potential energies remain. Direct evaluation of the complete wave and its time derivative verifies (5) for arbitrary phases and polarizations across all six depths. Amplitudes set canonical populations here; they are not particle mass labels. The energy–momentum test is also dimension independent A specified common free propagation extension gives \omega_j^2=c^2k_j^2+s_j^2. In units with wave speed one, its canonical contributions obey E_j=q_j\omega_j,\qquad P_j=q_jk_j, \qquad E_j^2-|P_j|^2=(q_js_j)^2. \tag{7} For positive-energy contributions, the total invariant is \boxed{E^2-|P|^2 =\sum_jm_j^2+2\sum_{i<j}(E_iE_j-P_i\cdot P_j), \quad m_j=q_js_j.} \tag{8} Each pair term is at least m_im_j: align the momenta to minimize it, then write their energies and magnitudes as m_j\cosh\eta_j and m_j\sinh\eta_j. The difference is m_im_j\cosh(\eta_i-\eta_j)\ge m_im_j. Consequently \boxed{\sqrt{E^2-|P|^2}\ge\sum_jm_j.} \tag{9} Positive massive contributions in this additive retained action therefore do not cancel their energy–momentum mass through phase choice or added spatial dimensions. Under a common boost the bound is saturated, and the invariant equals the positive E_0 in (6). For massless contributions the pair term becomes E_iE_j(1-\widehat P_i\cdot\widehat P_j). It vanishes when every occupied component propagates in the same direction, for any number of components. Opposing directions increase the invariant instead of removing it. This zero is compatible with positive energy and continued motion; it does not require negative local inertia. These conclusions are conditional on the stated retained action and free propagation extension. They do not calculate the full master field's binding energy or supporting stress. Those contributions must be obtained before identifying this retained energy with a complete physical particle. What a physical cancellation mechanism must additionally provide The current construction needs a physical polarization module, rather than an assumed channel count. It also needs the complete same-field stress and kinetic normalization. A viable masslessness mechanism must give null total energy–momentum for the photon while preserving its physical motion, and retain the intended nonzero mass-frequencies in the other sectors. The formal depth-two zero is still lifted by an allowed shape deformation, so its protection is a separate unresolved test. The shared and distinct photon-mechanism possibilities remain open. Neither the force-cancellation threshold nor the positive-energy calculation alone settles the complete physical theory. Verification polarized_energy_momentum_checks.py checks the actual retained kinetic Gram matrix, phase-independent energy, canonical charge and common-boost invariant at every maintained massive assignment and both surface signs. polarization_dimension_cancellation_checks.py uses the actual endpoint pair coefficients to test the varying-channel extension, Gram bound, exact orthogonal cancellations and positive energy–momentum inequalities across all six depths. Their 588-check energy report and 484-check channel report record the executed source hashes and exact input spatial report. Both scripts accept that report filename with --input-report.

title: The spatial response of a shape-preserving mass core
summary: A positive scalar/vector shape penalty preserves the mass-frequency and inertia branch while changing the complete local response; spatial angular matching distinguishes finite-basis candidates from localized growing modes.
text: A positive shape term can change the disturbance response of the polarization core without changing its mass-frequency, spatial profile or canonical inertia. The useful distinction is between the background matrix form fI+i h\alpha_{\hat x} and the additional matrix components available to a disturbance. Those components remain physical field variations; none is removed from the equations. The regular current action supplies the complete potential and its nonsingular extension. Its additional term is U_{\rm shape}=\mu\|P_\perp\phi\|_F^2,\qquad P_\perp X=X-\frac{\operatorname{Tr}X}{s}I_s- \frac1s\sum_{a=1}^d\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha_aX)\alpha_a. \tag{1} Here s is the matrix representation rank. The sum runs over the actual d ordinary spatial directions. The complete source of (1) is (\mu P_\perp\phi,0)^T, and its upper-block Hessian is \mu P_\perp. Both vanish on the original radial field except for the Hessian acting on disturbances outside that field's matrix form. Preserving motion and positive inertia Translations and spatial rotations of the core stay in the scalar/vector span. In a retained component frame, an infinitesimal boost of an upper-only core enters the lower block. Consequently the linear map \delta(P_\perp\phi_u) has no frame-only contribution on this branch. The mixed frame-wave and pure frame second variations of (1) are zero. This matters because a binding term that merely preserves the stationary profile can still produce a new reciprocal frame force. The analytic comparison in Holomorphic binding and its responsive-frame test does exactly that. The shape penalty has no such mixed quadratic source. The cutoff terms also have zero added branch variations, since their cutoffs are constant near the core. A positive retained frame kinetic action therefore adds its own linear frame equation without this new wave-frame mixing. For a polarized grade there can also be the existing antisymmetric rotation term; its contribution to the quadratic frame energy derivative is zero. This does not remove the separate nonlinear frame-vacuum problem or derive the physical carrier. The uniformly boosted core still solves the complete branch equations. The canonical translation–boost pairing remains M_{ab}=\omega Q\delta_{ab}>0 in natural units. With Q=1, inertia has the mass-frequency value. Neither a signed shape response nor a complex disturbance frequency is being interpreted as a negative particle inertia. A complete local decomposition across depths Freeze the radial polarization ratio y=h/f at a point, and choose \alpha_1 radially and \alpha_2 in the transverse momentum direction. A Hermitian basis of the full matrix algebra is supplied by Clifford monomials \Gamma_I=i^{|I|(|I|-1)/2}\prod_{a\in I}\alpha_a. Fix the subset outside directions one and two. Toggling membership of those two directions gives four monomials. Upper and lower spinor blocks, and real and imaginary coefficients, make a sixteen-real-component orbit. The complete current Hessian, the shape projector and both principal momentum matrices preserve it. This is a decomposition of the full local matrix equation. It is not a choice of sixteen disturbances with the other components discarded. For even depth, the orbits with k external generators have multiplicity \binom{d-2}{k}. In the chosen odd-depth representation, one additional unused Clifford generator completes the matrix algebra. Its two possible occupancies are both retained; it adds no physical coordinate and is excluded from the physical-vector projector in (1). Physical depth Partner rank s Complete real field dimension 4s^2 3 4 64 4 4 64 5 8 256 6 8 256 10 32 4,096 Explicit full-matrix embeddings verify the decomposition at depths three, four and five. The Clifford algebra, complete dimension count, and direct source closure verify the corresponding orbit classes through depth ten. The common current rule is q=1/(s+1); reusing the depth-six number 1/9 at depth three would change that rule. The center and the tail impose different local tests Use the common illustrative units m_c=1, \kappa=2, and denote the shape coefficient by c=\mu/m_c. In the high-wave-number compression at the center, the full local characteristic polynomial contains 16z^4+8Xz^2+X(X-64),\qquad X=c^2+2c(q-2)\omega+4(1-q)\omega^2. \tag{2} Here z is the local growth-generator eigenvalue after the leading propagation phase is removed, and \omega is in core-gap units. For X>0, this factor has purely imaginary roots only if X\ge64, because z^2=\frac{-X\pm8\sqrt X}{4}. At depths three and four, q=1/5. With c=1, the upper threshold of this particular center test is \omega\ge\frac{9+\sqrt{5121}}{16}. \tag{3} Thus \omega=3 can pass the earlier tail controls while still failing this center control. At \omega=5, the center factor has a positive local growth root of about 0.353. A common scan with c=1 and \omega=6,20,100 has no resolved local growth at any of the tested depths. It retains every orbit, ratios y=0,0.3,0.7,0.95,1, radial and transverse directions, intermediate angles, and momenta from zero through 100. The largest raw real parts remain below the stated numerical tolerance. These are local spectral controls. A frozen center is a finite spatial region of the actual particle, so local amplification there is not by itself a theorem of unbounded whole-particle evolution. Conversely, passing these controls does not prove spatial stability. Equation (3) is a condition for this local test, not a measured cavity-size bound or a universal physical necessity. Choosing \omega_{0,d}/m_c=6 would put every maintained single-grade frequency at six or greater under one common scale rule. This is not an extrapolation of the finite scans to arbitrarily large grade. That ratio is a possible inverse choice, not a derived constant. The bottom two-grade assignment still needs its separate coupled dynamics. No particle is retuned independently in this comparison. Actual spatial angular equations Local Clifford closure does not replace spatial derivatives. For a constant Clifford form T, retain the actual angular family T,\quad i\alpha_{\hat x}T,\quad iT\alpha_{\hat x},\quad \alpha_{\hat x}T\alpha_{\hat x}. \tag{4} The scalar and top-form endpoint families have two independent members. Every member has arbitrary complex radial coefficients in both spinor blocks. The angular Gram matrix follows from the physical sphere average and \sum_a\alpha_aT\alpha_a=(-1)^k(d-2k)T, with the corresponding parity change for an unused representation generator. In an orthonormal angular basis, the spatial Dirac operator is D_r=M\partial_r+\frac{A}{r}. \tag{5} Independent Cartesian finite differences verify (5), and arbitrary complex variations at other physical directions verify the complete current and shape source. These checks include every constant-Clifford form degree at depths 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10, and both representation sectors at odd depth. They do not include all higher spherical-harmonic families. Regular Laguerre radial bases give finite Hamiltonian matrices whose Hermitian structure and physical radial norms are independently checked. Some raw complex eigenvalue pairs occur near the radial basis cutoff. Their appreciable highest-basis weights and changing frequencies make them insufficient evidence of localized unstable modes. Separate central and staggered radial difference controls also show outer-domain and grid sensitivity in that high-frequency region. Testing the outgoing condition For a complex temporal growth value \lambda, the radial equation can be written in canonically weighted variables as Y'=C\left[\lambda I-V(r)-\frac{V_a}{r}\right]Y, \qquad C^2=I. \tag{6} A localized growing mode must belong both to the regular origin subspace and to the decaying far-field subspace. Transport orthonormal bases for those subspaces to a common radius, and form their combined matrix. Its smallest singular value must vanish for a matched mode. Three apparent finite-basis candidates were checked directly: Depth Constant form degree Raw candidate \lambda 3 3 0.017391512+14.23721819i 4 1 0.021315187+12.83363094i 4 2 0.011573507+14.39472328i Their outgoing matching residuals remain nonzero under outer-radius refinement from 30 to 60 to 120. For the first and third candidates, they approach approximately 0.299445 and 0.267559. These candidates therefore do not supply resolved localized growing modes of the radial equation. The known phase/amplitude zero-mode limit supplies an independent positive control of the matching procedure. This is a rejection of those specified numerical candidates, not an exhaustive search for all unstable eigenvalues. It leaves a concrete spatial spectral problem to solve with the full angular hierarchy and appropriate outgoing conditions. The local action now avoids its original current-zero divisions and its specific tested tail defect, while a complete stable physical mass operator remains unestablished. Reproducible calculations The 514-check local report records full source variation, boosted fields, frame quadratic coefficients, complete Clifford embeddings, local scans and the exact factor (2). polarization_angular_channel.py constructs the actual angular and radial operator; polarization_outgoing_match.py implements the independent origin-to-infinity matching test. The 243-check spatial report records the Cartesian angular identities, complete source variations, finite Galerkin spectra, interpolation controls and refined outgoing tests.

title: The supporting multiplet's stiffness depends on the full spatial deformation
summary: The frequency-weighted multiplet has nonnegative stiffness for a linear matrix deformation, but the full nonlinear spatial term changes that conclusion for the density-gradient carrier.
text: The complete positive-frequency multiplet can cancel every centered source after time averaging. That balance alone does not establish an energy minimum. The second variation must include the actual change of the spatial geometry, not only a linear perturbation of its projected matrix. For the separate bounded multiplier h=z/\sqrt{1+r^2}, all tested coordinate curvatures of the balanced averaged energy are positive. For the density-gradient multiplier, the full spatial term produces negative curvatures, including the endpoint direction at every maintained depth. This distinction was absent from the linear matrix model. These are energy curvatures at fixed positive canonical populations. They are not particle inertias or calculated growth rates. The averaged state has not been shown to be a pointwise coherent particle solution. The positive linear-matrix result Let s_j(\alpha) be the positive singular values of T(\alpha). Use the source-balancing populations q_j=s_j(0), kept fixed during a variation. The averaged energy is \mathcal E(\alpha)=\sum_jq_js_j(\alpha). \tag{1} Dividing all populations by \sum_js_j(0) gives unit canonical charge and divides every energy derivative by that same positive number. The complete trace identity gives \mathcal E'(0)=0 for each centered direction. For a strictly linear matrix path T(\alpha)=T_0+\alpha X, twice differentiating \sum_js_j^2=\operatorname{Tr}(T^\dagger T) gives \boxed{\mathcal E''_{ \rm linear}=\|X\|_F^2-\sum_j(s_j')^2\ge0.} \tag{2} To see the sign directly, take T_0=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j)V^\dagger and Z=U^\dagger XV. Then s_j'=\operatorname{Re}Z_{jj}, so \mathcal E''_{\rm linear} =\sum_{i\ne j}|Z_{ij}|^2+\sum_j(\operatorname{Im}Z_{jj})^2. \tag{3} No positivity of a discarded signed wave response is being assumed. Equation (3) is an exact finite-dimensional identity for the stated positive populations. The missing nonlinear spatial term The actual carrier follows T=T_0+\alpha T'+\alpha^2T''/2+\cdots. The same trace calculation now gives \boxed{\mathcal E''= \|T'\|_F^2-\sum_j(s_j')^2 +\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(T_0^\dagger T'').} \tag{4} The last term is not constrained by (3). The complete second spatial calculation computes it from the linked second geometry, moving normal modes and the coefficient's own derivative. At the radial configuration, \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(T_0^\dagger T'') =-\frac12\sum_l\left(\beta+l-\frac{d-1}{2}\right)(K_P'')_{ll} +\gamma^2\sum_lh_lh_l''. \tag{5} The polarization part is fixed independently by (K_P'')_{ll}=-2k(F^{\rm normal}_{x_k y_k})_{ll}. The adjacent h_l'' requires all six terms of the full second hopping derivative. Omitting the nonlinear geometry or the explicit multiplier derivative changes (5). The cross-depth comparison The complete calculation keeps every real centered order k=2,\ldots,d, every maintained particle control and both surface signs. At \gamma=10000, representative endpoint values are: Control Geometric carrier with fixed multiplier Geometric carrier with density gradient Depth-three down 1145.32 -5101.28 Depth-four up 898.35 -3388.67 Depth-five first neutrino 725.02 -2340.16 Depth-six electron 599.61 -1660.55 Depth-ten tau 334.69 -445.78 The entries are \mathcal E''/(\mathcal Q M_d), using the positive actual geometric mode metric. This normalization cannot change a sign. For example, the depth-three density-gradient endpoint has a positive linear contribution about 1.91, but a nonlinear spatial contribution about -4.56\times10^7 before division by \mathcal Q M_d. The omitted term determines the result. All 96 real coordinate curvatures are positive for each fixed-multiplier carrier. The density-gradient case has 94 negative curvatures among the same 96 controls; its endpoint is negative in every control. These statements concern the actual finite hopping value, not an extrapolation from the leading simplex approximation. A positive value in each coordinate direction does not prove that the full mixed Hessian is positive. A negative value in even one direction, however, is enough to exclude a local minimum of this averaged energy under the declared variations. The density-gradient replacement therefore preserves the earlier spectral numerator and first response pattern but loses ground in this supporting-state test. It cannot be treated as a complete simplification of a viable particle action. The retained geometric cost is constant along its exact flat linked moduli. Adding only that constant or a radius-only term cannot change these fixed-radius shape curvatures. Other physical stresses, nonlinear binding terms or curved spatial configurations must be included explicitly before they can alter the result. No such contribution has been inferred from the sign in this table. Verification full_spatial_stiffness_checks.py compares (4) with independent 180-digit finite differences of the complete weighted singular-value energy. Separate finite spatial integrals verify selected adjacent hopping second derivatives, including their explicit coefficient changes. Radial-grid and outer-domain refinements test the sensitive low- and high-depth cases. The 510-check report also verifies the second polarization identity and the full Cartesian second source across all five maintained depths. Raw second geometry and mode data are retained separately with the exact executed source hashes. The depth-two extension repeats these spatial checks over all six active depths. The fixed-multiplier controls retain 102 positive real directions each; the density-gradient control has 100 negative directions among 102. These later totals include W, Z and Higgs controls at depth two.

title: Complete positive-band source balance and its energy cost
summary: Frequency-weighted occupation cancels every centered source in the time-averaged retained multiplet, while an explicit dual inequality prevents such support from preserving the small frequency's energy per canonical charge.
text: The fast bands already present in the spatial carrier can supply a source of the opposite sign. There is an exact constructive way to balance all centered sources after time averaging. It also exposes a normalization problem: the resulting energy per canonical wave charge cannot remain equal to the selected small frequency in the tested model. This calculation retains the full finite carrier, both surface signs, the density-gradient multiplier and all maintained controls at depths 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10. It is an integrated, time-averaged condition. It does not establish a pointwise coherent equilibrium or include the remaining normal continuum. All modes considered here have positive frequency and positive energy in their stated canonical normalization. An exact constructive balance from the full trace Let s_j>0 be the singular values of T, and let f_{jk}=\partial_{x_k}s_j for k=2,\ldots,d. The complete density-gradient derivative has angular shifts 1-k and 1+k. Neither overlaps the diagonal or the adjacent shift already present in T. Therefore \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(T^\dagger\partial_{x_k}T)=0, \qquad \boxed{\sum_j s_j f_{jk}=0.} \tag{1} The second identity is the derivative of \operatorname{Tr}(T^\dagger T)=\sum_js_j^2. The first polarization derivative vanishes independently by the local anticommutator. Equation (1) includes every centered direction, rather than only its strongest source. For positive canonical populations q_j, the averaged source and energy are F_k=\sum_j q_j f_{jk},\qquad E=\sum_jq_js_j, \qquad\mathcal Q=\sum_jq_j. \tag{2} Here \mathcal Q means the action's positive phase normalization, not electric charge. In the first-order positive-frequency model it is the wave norm; in the positive oscillator action it is the sum of its positive circular-mode charges. The explicit choice \boxed{q_j=\frac{s_j}{\sum_rs_r}} \tag{3} gives \mathcal Q=1, every averaged F_k=0, and \boxed{\frac E{\mathcal Q}=\frac{\sum_js_j^2}{\sum_js_j}.} \tag{4} It works within either surface sign separately. At large hopping, (4) is set by the fast frequencies, not the small simplex branch. For example, the geometric density-gradient carrier's lowest controls give values between roughly 3300 and 4400 in the stated dimensionless units at \gamma=10000, whereas their small frequencies are many orders smaller. Distinct frequencies remove their cross terms under time averaging. The opposite surface harmonics are orthogonal in the integrated source. A coherent field can still exert oscillating local forces; (3) has not removed that further dynamical problem. A lower bound for any positive averaged balance The cost is not peculiar to the choice (3). Include every positive band on both surface signs. Separate the two small branches from the fast bands. Write their complete real source vectors as f_j. Choose a real linear source functional a for which both small branches obey a\cdot f_j\ge s>0\quad\text{on the small branches}. \tag{5} Such a functional exists because their source vectors cannot cancel with nonnegative weights in the complete source test. The computation constructs it explicitly: first divide each row by |f_k^+|+|f_k^-|, obtaining vectors p_+,p_-, then take a=p_+/\|p_+\|+p_-/\|p_-\| in those coordinates. Its two contractions are positive unless the vectors are exactly opposite. All of these statements are checked with high-precision signed singular vectors, without changing the physical operator. Define c=\max_{j\ { m fast}}\max(0,-a\cdot f_j),\qquad \omega_F=\min_{j\ { m fast}}s_j,\qquad \omega_L=\min_{j\ { m small}}s_j. Any positive source-balanced population must then satisfy s\mathcal Q_L\le c\mathcal Q_F, \qquad \boxed{\frac{\mathcal Q_F}{\mathcal Q} \ge\frac{s}{s+c}.} \tag{6} It follows that \boxed{\frac E{\mathcal Q}\ge \omega_L+(\omega_F-\omega_L)\frac{s}{s+c} \equiv E_{\rm bound}.} \tag{7} This is a finite-band analytic inequality. It can be checked directly, mode by mode, as a dual certificate. With t=(\omega_F-\omega_L)/(s+c), every retained mode obeys s_j+t\,a\cdot f_j\ge E_{\rm bound}. Summing against positive populations and imposing the balanced source proves (7). The row normalization makes this construction unchanged by positive rescaling of any individual shape coordinate. It is an analysis of a fixed operator, not a new fitting rule for its coefficients. Cross-depth cost At \gamma=10000, examples for the geometric density-gradient carrier are: Control Lower bound on fast population fraction E_{\rm bound}/\omega_L Depth-three down 0.9859 1.18\times10^{10} Depth-four up 0.1239 5.15\times10^{10} Depth-five first neutrino 1.23\times10^{-3} 1.17\times10^9 Depth-six electron 7.65\times10^{-6} 1.47\times10^8 Depth-ten tau 1.23\times10^{-11} 1.19\times10^6 A small fast population can still carry a large energy because its frequency is so high. The inequality exceeds the small frequency for every maintained control and both normal-carrier choices in this test. The explicit balance (3) obeys the bound, as it must. Thus the retained positive bands do provide an averaged supporting source, but cannot preserve the identification E/\mathcal Q=\omega_L under this bare canonical wave model. A complete same-field construction would need a different joint energy and source structure, with any binding contribution and normalization actually derived. The calculation does not assign negative particle inertia or establish a constraint on unspecified modes outside this retained system. Verification positive_band_support.py computes the full band sources and the dual certificate. positive_band_support_checks.py verifies angular orthogonality, the complete weighted trace, positivity, the explicit balanced populations, every dual inequality and independent precision refinements. Its 302-check report uses the independently verified density-gradient matrices and their recorded input hashes. All raw matrices and exact source versions are preserved separately.

title: Positive current matrices and spatial localization
summary: A scalar Dirac identity and spatial virial exclude localized flat-space stationary fields in the positive-current cone of the convex hierarchy, retaining all spinor and coefficient components.
text: Summary: A scalar Dirac identity and spatial virial exclude localized flat-space stationary fields in the positive-current cone of the convex hierarchy, retaining all spinor and coefficient components. A full-field condition on the self-mass action The current hierarchy supplies an isolated self-source and reciprocal interactions from one specified action. Its spatial states still need to exist. The following exact condition tests that question beyond a radial profile or one coherent coefficient ray. Use one grade N on ordinary flat physical space \mathbb R^d, with the trivial connection on its coefficient bundle. Retain every complex spinor and coefficient component. Set \mathscr D=-i\alpha\cdot\nabla,\qquad \{\mathscr D,\beta\}=0,\qquad \beta^2=I,\qquad \mathscr D^\dagger=\mathscr D. \tag{1} The self-mass note defines the reduced scalar currents R_k=\rho_{N,k}, their positive adjoint maps B_{Nk} and the weights h_{k,d}. For r_k=\|R_k\|_{\rm HS}, take the local interaction density u(\Psi)=\sum_{k=0}^N h_{k,d}\Phi(r_k),\qquad \Phi(0)=0, \tag{2} where \Phi is nonnegative, nondecreasing and convex on the nonnegative axis. The quartic, homogeneous root and smooth saturating laws all have these properties for their stated positive coefficients. This is a condition on the written action, not a premise imported from conventional physics. Where the source is defined, its complete variation is \mathcal N(\Psi)=\beta A_\Psi\Psi,\qquad A_\Psi=\sum_{k=0}^N h_{k,d}\frac{\Phi'(r_k)}{r_k}B_{Nk}(R_k). \tag{3} The zero-current values use the smooth limit when available. For a root law, they need a specified subgradient; any use of the theorem must check its positivity hypothesis there as well. The operator A_\Psi acts on the coefficient indices and commutes with \beta. It is Hermitian, but it is not automatically positive for arbitrary signed scalar currents. Let \Psi(t,x)=e^{-i\omega t}\phi(x) be a stationary field with finite positive canonical norm, finite displayed integrals and enough regularity and decay for integration by parts and norm-preserving spatial dilation. These are explicit hypotheses. No ordinary charge interpretation is assigned to this norm. Three exact identities Define the integrated quantities \begin{aligned} Q&=\int\phi^\dagger\phi,& S&=\int\phi^\dagger\beta\phi,\\ T&=\langle\phi,\mathscr D\phi\rangle,& U&=\int u(\phi),\\ P&=\int\phi^\dagger\beta A_\phi\phi =\int\sum_k h_{k,d}r_k\Phi'(r_k),& L&=\int\phi_-^\dagger A_\phi\phi_-, \end{aligned} \tag{4} where \phi_-=(I-\beta)\phi/2. The equality for P follows from the adjoint contraction relation, including every scalar spinor component.
