Multiplication of the stationary equation by \phi^\dagger gives \omega Q=T+P. \tag{5} Under \phi_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{d/2}\phi(\lambda x), the kinetic expectation becomes \lambda T and the local currents become \lambda^d R_k(\lambda x). Differentiation of the interaction therefore gives d(P-U). The spatial virial is T+d(P-U)=0,\qquad \omega Q=dU-(d-1)P. \tag{6} There is also a scalar identity that does not use dilation. The real part of \langle\phi,\beta\mathscr D\phi\rangle vanishes by (1). Multiplication of the same stationary equation by \phi^\dagger\beta therefore gives \boxed{\omega S=\int\phi^\dagger A_\phi\phi=P+2L.} \tag{7} Equations (5) and (7) use the same full field and the same source. Subtracting (7) from (6) yields the decisive identity \boxed{\omega(Q-S)=d(U-P)-2L.} \tag{8} Convexity with \Phi(0)=0 gives r\Phi'(r)\ge\Phi(r) pointwise, so P\ge U. If A_\phi(x) is positive semidefinite almost everywhere, then L\ge0 as well. What positivity excludes Suppose first that \omega>0 and A_\phi\ge0. The left side of (8) is nonnegative, since Q-S=2\|\phi_-\|^2. The right side is nonpositive. Equality forces P=U,\qquad L=0,\qquad \phi_-=0. \tag{9} Projecting the stationary equation onto the negative-\beta space now gives \mathscr D\phi=0. The trivial flat Dirac operator has no nonzero L^2(\mathbb R^d) zero field: its squared Fourier symbol is |p|^2I, so an L^2 zero field would be supported only at p=0. Thus \phi=0, contrary to the assumed positive norm. The quartic and smooth laws give an even more direct contradiction when the currents are nonzero. Their pointwise convexity deficits are \begin{aligned} r\Phi'(r)-\Phi(r)&=\frac\kappa2r^2 &&\left(\Phi=\frac\kappa2r^2\right),\\ r\Phi_\sigma'(r)-\Phi_\sigma(r) &=\mu\sigma\left(1-\frac\sigma{\sqrt{r^2+\sigma^2}}\right)>0 &&\left(r>0,\ \sigma>0\right). \end{aligned} \tag{10} For the root, P=U identically. Equation (8) then supplies the missing restriction on the negative-\beta components and gives the same flat zero-field conclusion. Homogeneity of the self-mass alone does not supply a spatially bound field. A practical sufficient condition for A_\phi\ge0 is positivity of the full scalar mode current C_N(x)=R_N(x)\ge0. \tag{11} Every lower R_k is its partial trace and is therefore positive. The maps B_{Nk}(H)=T_{Nk}^\dagger(H\otimes I)T_{Nk} preserve positivity, and the coefficients in (3) are nonnegative. For nonzero current, (11) also gives S>0 and \int\phi^\dagger A_\phi\phi>0 for the three laws just specified. Equation (7) consequently forces \omega>0. The contradiction covers every real frequency in this nonzero-current cone. A smooth field with every current zero has zero source and would be a free flat Dirac eigenfield, which is also zero. For a coherent coefficient field, C_N=J P_{z,N}. Positive scalar current J is enough for (11). For a general field, positivity of its trace J=\operatorname{Tr}C_N is weaker than (11); a positive trace can conceal negative current eigenvalues. Those fields cannot be excluded by substituting their trace into this theorem. For example, take two orthogonal coherent rays z,w with scalar mode current C_N=2P_{z,N}-P_{w,N}. Its scalar trace is positive. For the root law, however, the insertion on w^N is A_\phi w^N =\mu\left[1-\frac{D_N-1}{\sqrt5}\right]w^N. \tag{11a} It is negative whenever D_N>1+\sqrt5. The order-zero current supplies the first term; every positive current order supplies the second through Hockey-Stick. This is an explicit signed matrix control, not a stationary spatial field. A fixed sign decomposition gives the same obstruction The argument is stronger than positivity in the original coefficient frame. Suppose there is a constant Hermitian coefficient involution Z^2=I such that [Z,A_\phi(x)]=0 and K(x)=ZA_\phi(x)\ge0 at every point. Define \Gamma=\beta Z. Then \Gamma^2=I,\qquad \{\mathscr D,\Gamma\}=0,\qquad \beta A_\phi=\Gamma K. \tag{12} Replacing \beta,A_\phi,S,L in (7)–(9) by \Gamma,K,S_\Gamma,L_K proves the same nonexistence result at positive frequency. A fixed collection of positive and negative coefficient channels is therefore insufficient to evade it. This statement does not assign any particle interpretation to those signs. A spatially changing sign projector contributes a new term Where A_\phi(x) has a smooth spectral sign, put Z(x)=\operatorname{sgn}A_\phi(x), K(x)=|A_\phi(x)| and \Gamma(x)=\beta Z(x). For example, a smooth insertion with a gap about zero has this property. Crossings through zero require a separate analysis; the following derivative formula must not be applied across an unexamined discontinuity. The source still equals \Gamma K\phi, but the kinetic anticommutator now contains the spatial change of its coefficient directions: \{\mathscr D,\Gamma\} =-i\sum_j\alpha_j\beta\,\partial_jZ,\qquad G=\operatorname{Re}\langle\phi,\Gamma\mathscr D\phi\rangle =-\frac i2\int\phi^\dagger \left(\sum_j\alpha_j\beta\,\partial_jZ\right)\phi. \tag{13} The integrand gives a real expectation: \alpha_j\beta is anti-Hermitian and commutes with the Hermitian coefficient derivative. The scalar identity and its combination with the virial become \begin{aligned} \omega S_\Gamma&=G+P+2L_K,\\ \boxed{G}&=\boxed{-\omega(Q-S_\Gamma)-d(P-U)-2L_K}, \qquad L_K=\int\phi_{\Gamma,-}^\dagger K\phi_{\Gamma,-}\ge0. \end{aligned} \tag{14} Thus any positive-frequency stationary solution in this smooth-sign class must supply a nonpositive G. It must be strictly negative if any of the three nonnegative terms on the right is nonzero. A useful quantitative necessary bound is \omega(Q-S_\Gamma)+d(P-U)+2L_K \le\frac12\int\rho(x) \left\|\sum_j\alpha_j\beta\,\partial_jZ(x)\right\|_{\rm op}dx, \qquad \rho=\phi^\dagger\phi. \tag{15} The spatial sign projector is derived from the same field's mass insertion; it is not an added field or mediator particle. Equation (14) identifies where a changing polarization texture can enter a binding calculation. It does not prove that such a texture is dynamically selected or stable. An independent trial illustrates the term without claiming a solution. At depth six and grade one, choose two active coefficient directions and opposite spinors \chi_-=\alpha_1\chi_+ with \beta\chi_+=\chi_+. Let U(\theta) be a real two-by-two rotation through angle \theta/2, \theta(x_1)=t\tanh x_1, and set \phi(x)=e^{-|x|^2/2} \left[\sqrt2\,\chi_+\otimes U(\theta)e_0 +i\chi_-\otimes U(\theta)e_1\right]. \tag{16} The remaining coefficient directions are included with zero field. Its actual current insertion has positive and negative eigenvalues on the two active directions; its sign rotates with U. Direct six-dimensional integration gives G=T=-\sqrt2\,\pi^{5/2} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-x_1^2}\theta'(x_1)dx_1. \tag{17} Reversing the twist reverses this contribution. For nonzero t, the kinetic expectation violates the root stationary virial T=0, so this field is explicitly not a stationary particle. It verifies the geometric term and shows why a texture must solve the complete equations, rather than merely have the desired orientation. The resulting spatial search condition This is a full-field conditional nonexistence result. It retains arbitrary spatial dependence, complex phases, coefficient entanglement and spinor polarizations. It does not assume a radial shape or a coherent ray. It does require the flat trivial connection, the stated local convex interaction and admissible virial variation. At positive frequency, a localized solution of that same action must therefore escape every fixed sign decomposition, or fail another stated hypothesis. An indefinite scalar mode current is insufficient on its own. Spatial change of the sign subspaces, including possible eigenvalue-sign crossings outside the smooth class (13), is a concrete route to examine. The full source, stationary equation and stability still have to be calculated. Removing negative spinor components before doing that search would miss the very directions that could matter. The radial tail calculation gives a different restriction. For smooth scalar contact on a constant coherent ray, it excludes all regular radial finite-norm solutions, including sign-changing ones, without relying on the above current-positivity condition. Its root extension retains the separate virial hypotheses. The known curved coherent fields and smooth spatial controls use different global hypotheses. Their full Dirac operator can have nonzero normalized zero fields, and flat dilation is not their geometric variation. Their conditional actual CP3 geometry is not compactification. The present result neither establishes that geometry nor invalidates its explicitly stated solutions. Verification positive_current_localization_checks.py checks the complete current source, its adjoint contraction, matrix positivity and the convexity deficits with arbitrary complex spinors and coefficient correlations. Independent physical Dirac integration and derivatives of the actual spectral sign check the extra texture term. Indefinite-current controls verify why positive scalar trace alone cannot replace the operator condition. The independent profile dilations in local_self_mass_localization_checks.py check the norm, root energy and scalar virial, including sign-changing profiles. The nonexistence conclusion is the argument (4)–(12), not an inference from numerical shooting.

title: A positive current law with mass and stable pair alignment
summary: One positive three-moment current function preserves the conditional simplex self frequencies, penalizes partner-current distortion and makes aligned prepared pairs an angular energy minimum; a timelike rest-current lift is algebraically covariant, while spatial binding and full stability remain open.
text: The quadratic-root current gives a nonzero self frequency while an aligned pair has zero initial cross energy. Its alignment is an angular maximum for every tested positive current-metric parameter at nonzero shared grade. Here a single different current function changes that sign without changing the isolated simplex frequency. This is an inverse action candidate, not a derivation from the IDWT master interaction. One function of a positive same-field current Let R be a nonzero positive-semidefinite Hermitian retained current, T=\operatorname{Tr}R, p_2=\operatorname{Tr}R^2, and p_3=\operatorname{Tr}R^3. Let r be the partner spinor rank, fixed by the sector's component representation. Define the degree-one function \boxed{\mathcal F_r(R) =T+\frac{T}{2r}-\frac{p_2}{T} +\frac{r p_3}{2T^2}.} \tag{1} This is one local interaction rule for both a state and a pair of states. The three moment coefficients in (1) are fixed by the algebraic construction, not independently fitted to any particle mass. On a coherent rank-r current R_0=\rho I_r\otimes P, with a unit-rank coefficient projector P, one has T=r\rho, p_2=r\rho^2, p_3=r\rho^3, and \mathcal F_r(R_0)=r\rho=T, \qquad (D\mathcal F_r)_{R_0}P=P. \tag{2} The second identity means that its complete first variation acts on the occupied coherent field as the canonical density. In the same shell-current action as the localized construction, use one expression at every order, U_{\rm mass}=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k\ge0} \binom{k+d-1}{d-1}\mathcal F_{r_d}(R_k). \tag{3} On an isolated coherent grade N, equation (2) and the Hockey-Stick sum again give \omega_N=\omega_{0,d}\binom{N+d}{d}. The maintained particle index is n=N+1, so its count is S(n,d)=\binom{n+d-1}{d}. The shell weights and common physical frequency unit are still inverse inputs; (3) does not derive them. The sign of the new current energy is controlled exactly. For a=p_2/T^2 and b=p_3/T^3, Cauchy-Schwarz on the nonnegative eigenvalues gives b\ge a^2. Consequently \frac{\mathcal F_r(R)}{T}-1 =\frac1{2r}-a+\frac r2 b \ge\frac r2\left(a-\frac1r\right)^2\ge0. \tag{4} Equality holds for equal positive eigenvalues of rank r. Thus the isolated coherent current has minimum interaction energy at fixed trace against arbitrary positive current-matrix variations. This is a matrix statement, not a stability theorem for the complete spatial field and its indefinite kinetic energy. For example, split two occupied partner eigenvalues as \rho(1+\varepsilon) and \rho(1-\varepsilon), leaving the other r-2 values equal to \rho. At fixed T=r\rho, \mathcal F_r(R)-T =\frac{\rho}{r}\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^3)>0. \tag{5} Exact pair term and angular sign Prepare two upper-field cores of distinct grades N>M in one depth. At a shared order k\le M, let R_k=I_r\otimes(\rho P_{z,k}+\sigma P_{w,k}) and s=|z^\dagger w|^2. Directly taking the second and third traces in (1) gives the exact mixed density \boxed{\mathcal F_r(R_k)-r\rho-r\sigma =\frac{\rho\sigma}{2(\rho+\sigma)}(1-s^k).} \tag{6} The same function that generates the self frequency therefore gives a reciprocal nonnegative initial pair energy. Alignment s=1 is an angular minimum, not an assumed zero coupling rule. For coincident equal-norm cores with r\int\rho=1, the full prepared-pair value is V(s)=\frac{\omega_{0,d}}{4r} \sum_{k=1}^M\binom{k+d-1}{d-1}(1-s^k). \tag{7} At s=0, its ratio to the smaller isolated frequency is [S(n,d)-1]/[4rS(n,d)], with n=M+1. For a small ray angle s=\cos^2\theta, the coefficient of \theta^2 relative to that frequency is dM/[4r(d+1)]>0 for M>0. These are potential-energy ratios for prepared coincident patterns, not scattering cross sections or encounter probabilities. The depth-three index-one state has M=0, so this mass-current pair term vanishes identically. The six-depth moment batch tests all sixteen maintained indices, random positive current matrices, random pairs and finite boosts. Its report records a maximum pair-formula error of 4.33\times10^{-14}. Selected upper bounds on the coincident pair-energy ratio are about 0.06247 for depth-five index ten, 0.03125 for depth-six index thirteen and 0.0078125 for depth-ten index twenty-three. Those relative values follow from the partner ranks 4,8,32 in this conditional construction. They do not imply that a depth-five neutrino reacts weakly with ordinary matter: that is a cross-depth interaction whose actual field embedding, overlap and dynamics are still missing. A covariant positive-current lift The original scalar mass current is Hermitian but can be indefinite, whereas (4) requires R\ge0. A conditional local lift can obtain a positive matrix from the same field without choosing an external rest frame. With the Hermitian Dirac principal matrices A_a, define j^0=\operatorname{Tr}(\Psi^\dagger\Psi),\qquad j^a=\operatorname{Tr}(\Psi^\dagger A_a\Psi),\qquad u^\mu=\frac{j^\mu}{\sqrt{(j^0)^2-|j|^2}}, \tag{8} where the local current is strictly future timelike. Set H_u=u^0I-u^aA_a and form the retained partner/oscillator Gram matrices from \Psi^\dagger H_u\Psi, with the same spectator trace at each order. Since (A\cdot\hat j)^2=I, the eigenvalues of H_u are u^0\pm|u|>0. Every retained current is therefore positive semidefinite. Under a common Lorentz boost, the spinor and its own u transform together, making \Psi^\dagger H_u\Psi an invariant matrix. No derivatives of \Psi enter H_u, so the spatial principal symbol remains the Dirac one wherever this source is smooth. On the isolated upper-only rest core, j^a=0, H_u=I, and the retained current is exactly \rho I_r\otimes P. Its first field variation also gives the same occupied mass source: the variation of u multiplies \Psi^\dagger A_a\Psi=0 as a matrix there. The executed batch checks finite boosts and that first derivative at all six depths. Maximum matrix boost error is below 2.5\times10^{-15} in its normalized controls. The lift is undefined when the total local current is null or zero. Its full arbitrary-field variation, complete Hessian, local well-posed domain and nonlinear spatial stability have not been established. The finite rest-current checks do not prove a global causal physical carrier or a same-field master origin. Why this is still an inverse candidate Equation (3) has the desired shared self/pair algebra and retains the conditional simplex mass frequency. Its positive matrix excess does not on its own sustain the displayed localized core. On the upper-only coherent branch, its first variation has no lower-spinor source, while the spatial Dirac derivative lies in that lower block. Removing the separate sustaining interaction from the prior localized action would leave -i\alpha\cdot\nabla\phi=0, whose finite-norm flat-space solution is trivial in this ansatz. The previous binding term remains an additional part of the candidate same-field action. A complete one-law derivation must generate the off-diagonal sustaining source, the shell weights, the common normalization, stable spatial states, and cross-depth response from one physical interaction. The current construction isolates a useful algebraic condition: a positive same-field mass current can have a stable aligned-pair direction without sacrificing the assigned self-frequency, provided the current law uses more than quadratic purity and has a physically valid positive-current lift. Frozen-field limitation of the instantaneous rest lift The positive-current algebra above survives, but its algebraic same-field rest-frame lift has a growing high-momentum frozen block. For positive partner-current stiffness A, rank r, and particle frequency \omega, a transverse Clifford block obeys (\Omega^2-c^2p^2)^2+8A\omega^2c^2p^2/r=0. Its growth tends \omega\sqrt{2A/r}. In the displayed law A=1/2, so the limit is \omega/\sqrt r. The separate pair-alignment term does not alter this block. Finite complete frozen matrices at depths two, four and six confirm the limit. Thus the instantaneously selected rest-current lift is not a viable stable carrier as written. The scalar-current alternative keeps the self/pair sign while avoiding this specific frozen defect; its complete spatial stability and current-cancellation boundary remain open.

title: Comparing current positive-response routes on common controls
summary: One calculation compares spectrum shifts, bias compatibility, size curvature and the conditional background Schur cost on the same maintained mode controls at every active depth.
text: The current response proposals should be compared before adding another support term. This calculation puts their immediate algebraic tests in one script, with the same mode assignments and source vectors at physical depths two, three, four, five, six and ten. It distinguishes a diagnostic identity from a complete physical solution. Shared calculation For each maintained mode index i, the algebraic source control and positive inverse stiffness are s_{i,\ell}=\frac{i+\ell+d}{i+2\ell+d+1},\qquad w_{d,\ell}=\frac{d}{(\ell-1)(\ell+d)},\qquad K_{ij}=\sum_{\ell=2,4,\ldots}s_{i,\ell}s_{j,\ell}w_{d,\ell}. \tag{1} These are the existing source controls, not derived particle densities. The cumulative simplex count is \mathcal S(i,d)=\binom{i+d-1}{d}. The single script computes the following tests from (1): The fixed-norm unbiased response changes the standing frequency by -g^2Q_iK_{ii}. At equal Q_i, a common rescaling of a bare simplex spectrum requires K_{ii}/\mathcal S(i,d) to be constant within each depth. A common minimum-norm bias for the selected modes solves Kc=-\operatorname{diag}K. Its selected residuals, the next-mode residual, condition estimate and real-amplitude curvature -4K_{ii} are all computed from the same matrix. For the one-scale energy E=Q c\mu/L-g^2Q^2K_{ii}/(2L^{d-2}), the script records the stationary size curvature and the stationary frequency factor (d-4)/(d-2) when a finite stationary dilation exists. For a spectrally transparent nonzero background, the joint Hessian requires G>F^*A^{-1}F+(M+vN)^*P^{-1}(M+vN). If its metric-force source is normalized to the same s_i, with v=1 and the same inverse w, then F^*A^{-1}F=K_{ii}. The script reports \max_i K_{ii} as a necessary common geometric stiffness at each depth in that unit-control comparison. The actual metric force, field-mixing term and geometric stiffness must come from a same-field action before it can be called a physical pass. Results and decision boundary The infinite harmonic sums were calculated at 50 and 80 decimal digits. The table gives the largest-to-smallest spread of K_{ii}/\mathcal S, the signed next-mode bias residual, and the unit-control lower bound on a shared geometric stiffness. The depth-ten sector has one maintained mode and cannot test within-depth proportionality. Depth Response-to-count spread Next-mode bias residual Unit-control G>\max K_{ii} Size direction 2 1.527 +1.11\times10^{-6} 0.712 No finite extremum 3 561 +2.43\times10^{-5} 0.691 Flat only at equality; negative frequency 4 4.62\times10^4 +4.46\times10^{-4} 0.995 Maximum; zero frequency 5 28.4 +1.21\times10^{-4} 0.928 Maximum 6 176 -7.02\times10^{-4} 1.078 Maximum 10 Single mode +3.61\times10^{-3} 1.225 Maximum The unbiased positive response does not preserve the proposed ratios at equal norm under these source controls. Constraining the norm retains its frequency shift. The fitted common bias cancels selected first derivatives but fails the next mode and has negative response amplitude curvature. The scale-covariant response has no stable finite size by itself at any maintained depth. Thus these variants do not yet give the requested joint mass, size and support mechanism. The nonzero background route remains algebraically possible in the angular sector because it can cancel a metric force without shifting the reference field equation. Its reported stiffness numbers are necessary lower bounds only in the stated unit-control normalization. The subsequent common-background radius calculation specifies one finite-carrier inverse action and derives its radius force, field--radius mixing and radial curvature. It leaves the angular second variation of that carrier, master-field origin and reciprocal pair response unresolved. The separate whole-depth current calculation derives its conformal Hessian from its own action and tests a wider angular basis. The combined check initially passed 108 identities and convergence comparisons. That initial report contains every retained depth and mode; the current script also includes the later radial and conformal-current actions as separate candidates. A passing diagnostic is evidence for the stated equations, not for the physical realization of a candidate. One quick equation comparison for the next decision The later joint candidate script recalculates the equations needed to compare the current routes in one run. For every maintained mode at both common strength controls it places the positive-response Gram norm, linked-carrier radius pressure, whole-depth current frequency, conformal metric force, geometric Hessian and correctly normalized background threshold in one row. The depth-two current row also checks nine form-carrier zonal directions; the higher-depth rows record the pointwise coefficients that establish positive bare spinor curvature for all smooth conformal directions. Its joint report contains 32 rows and common within-depth summaries. The two carrier actions remain separate. The linked radial threshold is reported per unit wave norm. The current model's tested conformal threshold is reported per unit phase charge and is only a lower bound for untested metric directions. The report keeps finite-strength frequency-unit spreads visible; neither carrier has an exact simplex ratio at these finite strengths. The script is a compact decision calculation, while the larger verification script retains the independent precision and quadrature tests. The finite-chain current analysis extends that same quick calculation. It proves that both fixed positive hopping chains have a strictly decreasing frequency per simplex count as the harmonic index rises. It then checks an exact finite-band depth-two current law and a dimension-aware current correction on all maintained modes. A further inverse-depth batch tests finite branches and both shared-gap interpretations of the six-to-ten frequency unit. A component-Hessian batch retains every signed component direction under the fractional correction. Those inverse laws change the reference action, so the saturated current's conformal Hessian and support threshold do not transfer to them.

title: A positive oscillator action and its complete initial shape response
summary: An explicitly defined retained positive action preserves the carrier frequencies but still drives rapid initial deformation; projection and squaring differ by a complementary-mode term that a physical reduction must retain or control.
text: A different canonical action can have the same fixed-geometry frequencies and a different geometric response. A useful explicit comparison is \boxed{L_2=\|\partial_t[B(\alpha)c]\|^2 -c^\dagger H_P(\alpha)^2c.} \tag{1} Here B^\dagger B=I embeds the retained coefficients c in the spatial modes. For a fixed self-adjoint retained carrier H_P, its frequency operator is K_P=H_P^2, so its positive oscillation frequencies are |\lambda_j(H_P)|. The energy is nonnegative. Equation (1) is an alternative inverse construction, not a consequence of the existing first-order master law. Its full physical spatial realization and total inertial response remain open. Mass continues to mean the selected frequency in equivalent units. Projection and squaring do not generally commute. If H_P=B^\dagger H_{\rm full}B and Q=I-BB^\dagger, then \boxed{B^\dagger H_{\rm full}^2B =H_P^2+(QH_{\rm full}B)^\dagger(QH_{\rm full}B).} \tag{1a} Thus (1) explicitly defines the retained effective action. It is not automatically the projection of the full spatial operator's square. A forward reduction must retain the extra term or construct a controlled dressed invariant low subspace before squaring. The calculations below use (1); they do not establish that missing physical reduction. The later spatial complement calculation derives the leading positive kinetic correction from the maintained full parent. The bounded completion and its complete spatial bound then control the small frequency of a specified improved parent. Those results do not retroactively make the particular shape action (1) a derived occupied master-field law. The comparison is useful because the small signed partner that obstructs the first-order slow law is not a gapped negative-frequency excitation of this new positive oscillator. It belongs to a degenerate positive-frequency doublet. Its response must be retained under that different structure. The squared source removes the old partner transition At fixed geometry, writing H=H_P in this finite identity, K_a=\partial_a(H^2)=\{H,H_a\},\qquad \langle r,K_a n\rangle=(\lambda_r+\lambda_n) \langle r,H_a n\rangle. \tag{2} Thus K_a has zero matrix element between the two signed partners \lambda_r=-\lambda_n. Copying the first-order response denominator into (1) would give a wrong answer. For the chiral carrier, H_P=\begin{pmatrix}0&T^\dagger\\T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H_P^2=\begin{pmatrix}T^\dagger T&0\\0&TT^\dagger\end{pmatrix}. \tag{3} If Tu=\lambda v, T^\dagger v=\lambda u, and \|u\|=\|v\|=1, every vector (a u,b v), |a|^2+|b|^2=1, has squared eigenvalue \lambda^2. The projected K_a on this entire doublet is 2\lambda\partial_a\lambda times the identity. Relative phase and population do not remove its first frequency source. Keep all coefficient modes while the spatial basis moves Write \Psi=B(\alpha)c, where B contains the orthonormal normal modes in each chiral block. Expanding the kinetic term of (1) gives L_2=\|B\dot c+(\partial_aB)c\dot\alpha_a\|^2 -c^\dagger K_P(\alpha)c. \tag{4} All retained coefficient modes remain dynamical in (4). It is not a single-eigenray adiabatic action. Choose orthogonal basis transport at the reference configuration, B^\dagger\partial_aB=0, in the same polynomial spatial and temporal-connection convention as the moving normal calculation. Consider a moment with zero shape velocity, while the wave continues its oscillation: c=A\phi, \dot c=-i\lambda A\phi, K_P\phi=\lambda^2\phi, \|\phi\|=1. Define the real positive spatial metric G_{ab}=\operatorname{Re}\langle(\partial_aB)\phi, (\partial_bB)\phi\rangle,\qquad f_a=\partial_a\lambda. \tag{5} The shape Euler equation at this moment is exactly 2A^2G_{ab}\ddot\alpha_b+2A^2\lambda f_a=0, \qquad \boxed{G\ddot\alpha=-\lambda f.} \tag{6} The coefficient modes' acceleration is also retained in the variation; its cross term vanishes here by the orthogonal transport condition. No arbitrary amplitude is being identified with mass. Its common factor cancels from (6). For a fixed circular wave in (1), the positive canonical phase charge is \mathcal Q=2\lambda A^2, and E=2\lambda^2A^2=\mathcal Q\lambda. This charge is the action's phase normalization, not an assertion about electric charge. Rescaling the wave changes both quantities while leaving its frequency unchanged. The instantaneous small branch therefore has \boxed{\frac{\ddot\lambda}{\lambda} =-f^TG^{-1}f\equiv-\Omega_{\rm source}^2.} \tag{7} Equation (7) is a local initial curvature. It does not extrapolate a trajectory beyond the neighborhood where the basis and operator were computed. It tests whether a slowly maintained radial shape is plausible under (4) alone. Every positive-frequency doublet polarization is covered At the real reference point, the real and imaginary metric blocks decouple. For a general doublet polarization the real metric is G(q)=qG_u+(1-q)G_v,\qquad q=|a|^2\in[0,1]. \tag{8} The relative phase drops out because the two chiral blocks are orthogonal. The source vector f is the same for all q. Cauchy's inequality in the positive metric gives f^TG(q)^{-1}f\ge\frac{f_d^2}{G(q)_{dd}}, \qquad \boxed{\frac{\lambda}{\Omega_{\rm source}(q)} \le\frac{\lambda\sqrt{\max((G_u)_{dd},(G_v)_{dd})}}{|f_d|}.} \tag{9} This is a bound over the entire complex doublet, while retaining every centered deformation. It does not rely on a finite scan of polarizations. At \gamma=10000, equal doublet populations give the following local source times relative to the wave time 1/\lambda: Control Geometric carrier, fixed multiplier Geometric carrier, density-gradient multiplier Depth-three down 1.18\times10^{-11} 7.97\times10^{-11} Depth-four up 8.34\times10^{-14} 1.49\times10^{-12} Depth-five first neutrino 6.39\times10^{-15} 4.42\times10^{-13} Depth-six electron 4.00\times10^{-17} 1.48\times10^{-14} Depth-ten tau 9.76\times10^{-26} 5.09\times10^{-19} Each entry is \lambda/\Omega_{\rm source}. The analytic bound (9) is also much smaller than one for all maintained controls, including the original carrier. Choosing another doublet polarization does not restore an initially slow shape under (4). The large-hopping limit has \Omega_{\rm source}\sim|\gamma\kappa_d|/\sqrt{G_{dd}^{\infty}}. Together with \lambda\propto\gamma^{-(d-1)}, this gives \lambda/\Omega_{\rm source}\propto\gamma^{-d}. The density-gradient carrier at depth ten enters this asymptotic regime later because its first adjacent integral is small. The full finite calculation above is retained; the asymptotic check uses higher hopping rather than claiming the leading expression is already accurate there. Do not eliminate a slow radial response prematurely For comparison, restrict a wave to a normalized trial ray \Psi=a e^{-i\theta}\phi(\alpha), with potential energy a^2\lambda^2 in the explicitly retained action. Eliminating only its cyclic phase at fixed \mathcal Q gives the exact Routh expression L_{\mathcal Q}=\dot a^2+a^2g_{ab}\dot\alpha_a\dot\alpha_b +\mathcal Q A_a\dot\alpha_a-a^2\lambda^2 -\frac{\mathcal Q^2}{4a^2}, \tag{10} where g is that ray's positive projective metric and A_a=i\langle\phi,\partial_a\phi\rangle. Its instantaneous radial equilibrium is a^2=\mathcal Q/(2\lambda), with radial oscillation frequency 2\lambda. Substituting this equilibrium into \dot a^2 would produce the positive term \mathcal Q\dot\lambda^2/(8\lambda^3). That substitution is a further slow approximation. It cannot justify slow geometry when the actual initial source acts on the much shorter times shown above. Equation (4) avoids that premature elimination. The alternative action thus changes the signed response structure in a real way, but does not by itself provide the missing sustained particle geometry. A further contribution must be obtained from the same field and tested with its energy, canonical normalization and motion retained. Verification squared_wave_response.py constructs the complete positive normal quantum tensor. squared_wave_checks.py checks its positivity, its independent curvature contraction, the full initial acceleration, the source scaling, spatial refinements and the exact Routh algebra. Its 554-check report passes for all maintained indices and both surface signs, with three carrier/multiplier controls. The polarization bound (9) is additionally checked by squared_wave_polarization_checks.py. Its 936-check report verifies both pure chiral populations, mixed populations and the common analytic endpoint bound at every maintained control. Raw spatial tensors and executed source hashes are preserved separately.

title: Obtain the hopping coefficient from the linked density
summary: The density gradient removes an independent hopping function and preserves the spectral numerator, but its full nonlinear spatial response fails the later averaged supporting-state minimum test.
text: The common normal operator previously used a separately specified bounded function to couple adjacent normal modes. That function can instead be obtained from the linked geometry itself: \boxed{h_{\rm geom}=(\partial_1+i\partial_2)|W|^2.} \tag{1} The same rule works at depths 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10. It removes one independent spatial function. The simplex numerator and grouping of responses within a depth survive; the spatial integrals and response between depths change. Equation (1) is an explicit candidate choice, not a uniquely derived master interaction. Its dimensional coefficient remains to be fixed. All coordinates here are the same dimensionless ordinary normal coordinates used for the linked profile. Restoring physical length gives a derivative an inverse-length factor. That factor must enter the common operator normalization, rather than becoming a separate particle fit. Radial form, boundedness and positive hopping For W=w(r)e^{id\theta}, the linked equations give h_{\rm geom}=f(r)e^{i\theta},\qquad f=2ww'=\frac{2(d-a)w^2}{r}>0\quad(r>0). \tag{2} The coefficient is regular at the center and decays at infinity. It is invariant under changes of the phase representative of W. The profile bounds also give an explicit, conservative estimate \boxed{|h_{\rm geom}|\le2\sqrt{e d}.} \tag{3} For r\ge\sqrt d, use w\le1 and d-a\le d. For r\le\sqrt d, integration of w'/w\ge d/r-r gives w(r)\le(r/\sqrt d)^d\exp[(d-r^2)/2]. Maximizing the resulting r^{2d-1}e^{-r^2} bound proves (3). The number e in (3) is Euler's number, not the connection coefficient in D_{t,e}. With the normalized positive radial carrier components, the adjacent entries become \boxed{h_l=2\pi\int_0^\infty r f(r) (U_{l+1}U_l+V_{l+1}V_l)dr>0.} \tag{4} The geometric carrier gives, for example, (0.39086323,0.46980658) at depth three and (0.12082700,0.26469052,0.38308533,0.43768548,0.39529922) at depth six. These integrals are computed once per depth from the same spatial rule. The projected operator still has T_{ll}=n+l, T_{l+1,l}=\gamma h_l. Consequently \prod_lT_{ll}=d!\binom{n+d-1}{d},\qquad \lambda_{n,d}=\frac{d!}{\gamma^{d-1}\prod_lh_l} \binom{n+d-1}{d}[1+O(\gamma^{-2})]. \tag{5} The finite-hopping correction is still present. A shared charged-lepton frequency unit between depths six and ten is not implied by (5): the products of spatial integrals and the dimensional factors must produce that relation. This calculation preserves the numerator, rather than deriving all sector scales. The full normal complement estimate in the common carrier remains applicable after replacing its perturbation norm by v=\gamma\|h_{\rm geom}\|_\infty+(d+1)/2, bounded using (3). Using the old v=\gamma+(d+1)/2 without checking the new coefficient would be unjustified. The coefficient's own shape derivative must be retained Let P(z)=z^d+\alpha_kz^{d-k}. In the horizontal representation, the real geometric zero mode has \delta W=U_ke^{i(d-k)\theta}. The density variation is \delta|W|^2=s_k(r)\cos k\theta, with s_k=2wU_k. Differentiating (1) gives \boxed{ \delta_{x_k}h= \frac{s_k'+ks_k/r}{2}e^{i(1-k)\theta} +\frac{s_k'-ks_k/r}{2}e^{i(1+k)\theta}.} \tag{6} For the imaginary coordinate, multiply the first coefficient by i and the second by -i. Because the density is phase invariant, this is also its derivative in the polynomial gauge. The full hopping matrix therefore has three terms: \boxed{\delta h_{ij}= \langle\delta\Phi_i,h\Phi_j\rangle+ \langle\Phi_i,h\delta\Phi_j\rangle+ \langle\Phi_i,(\delta h)\Phi_j\rangle.} \tag{7} The last term is substantial. Keeping the multiplier fixed while varying the geometry would not test (1). The complete first polarization derivative still vanishes by the independent anticommutator identity, so the complete first projected source is \delta T=\gamma\delta h. For reproducing the complementary calculation, a general multiplier f(r)e^{i\theta} has positive-chiral Green sources \begin{aligned} h\Phi_l:&\quad ((f'+f/r)V_l,(f/r-f')U_l),\quad j=l+1,\\ \bar h\Phi_l:&\quad ((f'-f/r)V_l,-(f'+f/r)U_l),\quad j=l-1. \end{aligned} \tag{8} They follow by applying the full D to the multiplied zero mode. The independent computation instead differentiates the modes using -D L_+^{-1}\delta D\Phi_l and contracts them directly in (7). Responses within and between depths The endpoint still has a single matrix entry \delta h=\kappa_d\alpha_d|0\rangle\langle d-1|. Its positive-frequency derivative is 2\gamma\kappa_d\operatorname{Re}(v_0^*u_{d-1}). For a fixed surface sign, the endpoint product tends to a common value across the assigned indices at each depth. Different masses can therefore retain similar geometric response under this simplified rule. Using the actual geometric metric M_d, the endpoint values are: Depth Original normal carrier Geometric normal carrier 3 -0.07113624 -0.19700886 4 -0.08668439 -0.22799161 5 -0.08371570 -0.23597486 6 -0.07155973 -0.23228880 10 -0.02285616 -0.19268416 Each entry is \kappa_d/\sqrt{M_d}. These values are spatial response coefficients, not encounter rates. They do not derive special neutrino suppression or a physical normalization across sectors. All centered sources were also checked under mixtures of the two positive surface-sign branches. To avoid dependence on rescaling a coordinate, the test minimizes \min_{0\le q\le1}\max_k \frac{|qF_k^++(1-q)F_k^-|}{|F_k^+|+|F_k^-|}. \tag{9} Every tested mixture leaves a nonzero residual. The smallest residual in the geometric-carrier controls is about 0.0230 at depth three; other depths remain near 0.5. The fixed-multiplier source sign theorem must not be copied to this new calculation: the explicit term (6) changes some penultimate signs. Equation (9) records the newly tested scope. The later second-variation test The preserved spectral numerator and first response are insufficient for the supporting-state calculation. The complete nonlinear spatial Hessian has negative energy curvature in the endpoint direction at every tested depth for this gradient rule. It therefore fails that averaged local-minimum test. These energy curvatures are not negative particle inertia. The curvature-moment rule removes the same independent spatial function and passes the complete centered mixed-Hessian test under its stated retained-action assumptions. Verification profile_gradient_hopping.py implements the density-derived multiplier and its full derivative. profile_gradient_checks.py checks Cartesian differentiation, two independent Green contractions, all maintained controls and surface signs, positive hopping, the exact polarization spacing and the complete source mixtures. Its 362-check report also includes radial-grid and outer-domain refinements. Raw arrays are preserved separately with the exact executed source versions.

title: Canonical norm of the projective derivative lift
summary: The complete projective holomorphic jet lift has a calculable kinetic norm that changes its reduced simplex coefficient, while canonical compression keeps the local scalar response bounded on any fixed smooth background.
text: Summary: The complete projective holomorphic jet lift has a calculable kinetic norm that changes its reduced simplex coefficient, while canonical compression keeps the local scalar response bounded on any fixed smooth background. The geometric polynomial needs its parent-field norm The projective covariant derivative has an exact simplex adjoint square on the specified CP3 line bundle: P(X)=\frac{X(X+4)(X+6)}{720}, \qquad X=\left.\frac{R^2\mathscr D_2^2}{4}\right|_{\text{zero forms}}. \tag{1} One possible route to a master-field origin is to represent the lower field and its derivatives by components of a larger field. For the natural projective holomorphic jet lift, that route has an explicitly nonconstant kinetic metric: \boxed{Z(X)=\frac{X^2+12X+40}{40}.} \tag{2} If this lifted field carries the canonical time derivative, the reduced coefficient of the derivative energy is P(X)/Z(X). The metric cannot be omitted while retaining that physical lift. The following calculation derives it without discarding any component or adjusting the occupied indices. The geometry remains conditional physical CP3 with unknown radius R, ordinary macroscopic spatial directions and no compactification. The finite jet carrier describes derivatives of the same spatial field. Its mathematical rank adds no physical spatial directions, and its realization as components of the master spinor is a further hypothesis. The full osculating polynomial Work first on \mathbb{CP}^m with L\ge0. Let \mathcal H_L=H^0(\mathbb{CP}^m,\mathcal O(L)), \qquad D_L=\dim\mathcal H_L=\binom{L+m}{m}. \tag{3} Give \mathcal H_L its invariant norm from unit-volume spatial integration. For a smooth section f and a point x, there is a unique polynomial section whose holomorphic derivatives through order L at x agree with those of f. Define \mathcal J_Lf(x) to be its complete coefficient vector in \mathcal H_L. This is the osculating polynomial: it matches the entire holomorphic jet, not just the value or one coherent direction. In an affine chart, the monomials of degree at most L form a basis of the same number of jets. Their derivative matrix is invertible. Projective coordinate covariance makes the construction global. For a holomorphic section, the same polynomial works at every point, so its coefficient vector is constant over the base. The degree L here is the line degree of the physical spatial section. For CP3 and L=2, D_L=10. It is not the auxiliary mass-band rank S(n,6) and does not relabel the electron or muon mode. Derive the pointwise metric on all derivatives At the origin of an affine chart, write f(z)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le L}f_\alpha z^\alpha +\text{terms of higher holomorphic order}. An orthonormal basis of the polynomial carrier is e_\alpha(Z)= \sqrt{\frac{D_LL!}{(L-|\alpha|)!\,\alpha!}}\, Z_0^{L-|\alpha|}Z^\alpha. \tag{4} The coefficient of e_\alpha in the osculating polynomial is f_\alpha\sqrt{(L-|\alpha|)!\alpha!/(D_LL!)}. At this point the holomorphic connection coefficients vanish. Contracting every tensor index and grouping by j=|\alpha| gives \boxed{ |\mathcal J_Lf(x)|^2 =\frac1{D_L}\sum_{j=0}^{L} \frac{(L-j)!}{L!\,j!} \left(\frac{R^2}{2}\right)^j |\mathcal B_jf(x)|^2. } \tag{5} Here \mathcal B_j is the complete symmetric covariant derivative defined in the derivative note. Both norms use the physical Hermitian metric. Physical SU(m+1) isometries move any point to this origin and act unitarily on \mathcal H_L. Thus (5) holds globally. The factors in (5) are fixed by polynomial interpolation and the actual section norm. They are not optional weights for independent derivative coordinates. A field of jets still obeys the derivative compatibility conditions. Integrate the induced kinetic operator The derivative norm identity gives, on the degree-n zero-form family, \frac{\|\mathcal B_jf_n\|^2}{\|f_n\|^2} =\left(\frac2{R^2}\right)^j (n+L)_{\underline j}(n+m)_j. \tag{6} Since X=n(n+L+m) on that family, integrating (5) yields \boxed{ \mathcal J_L^\dagger\mathcal J_L=Z_{m,L}(X) =\frac1{D_L} \sum_{j=0}^{L}\frac{(L-j)!}{L!\,j!} \prod_{k=0}^{j-1}[X+(L-k)(m+k)]. } \tag{7} The empty product is one. Every coefficient of this polynomial is positive, and Z_{m,L}(X)\ge1 for X\ge0. The identity holds on the full section space because each irreducible spatial family has the eigenvalue obtained in (6). There is an exact use of the Hockey-Stick Identity here. At n=0 the derivative factors in (6) reduce (7) to Z_{m,L}(0) =\frac1{D_L}\sum_{j=0}^{L}\frac{(m)_j}{j!} =\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{L}\binom{m+j-1}{j}} {\displaystyle\binom{m+L}{m}} =1. \tag{8} The combinatorial sum verifies the correct norm of a holomorphic section and its constant polynomial lift. It does not supply a mass enhancement. For m=3,L=2, (7) is Z(X)=\frac1{10} \left[1+\frac{X+6}{2}+\frac{(X+6)(X+4)}4\right] =\frac{X^2+12X+40}{40}, \tag{9} which proves (2). Vary the action with the same time-kinetic norm Suppose the physical reduction uses Y=\mathcal J_Lf and gives that complete field its ordinary positive kinetic norm. The time-kinetic term for f is then \operatorname{Re}\langle f,iZ\partial_tf\rangle. If its specified derivative energy is \mu\langle f,P(X)f\rangle, variation gives iZ(X)\partial_tf=\mu P(X)f. \tag{10} Defining the canonically normalized amplitude u=Z^{1/2}f gives \boxed{i\partial_tu=\mu\,\frac{P(X)}{Z(X)}u.} \tag{11} This is the contribution of the stated derivative energy to this specified reduced component. It is not a complete spatial Dirac dispersion relation or an observed rest mass. The full spinor construction separately retains the first-order kinetic operator and both signs. At the unchanged assigned indices: Spatial index n S(n,6) Derived norm Z_n Canonical coefficient P/Z 13 18\,564 \frac{14\,401}{10} \frac{185\,640}{14\,401}\approx12.891 35 3\,838\,380 49\,421 \frac{3\,838\,380}{49\,421}\approx77.667 Their coefficient ratio is approximately 6.025, rather than the simplex ratio. Rescaling the whole carrier by a constant does not remove its dependence on n. More generally, at L=m-1 the leading terms in (7) and in the normalized derivative polynomial give \boxed{\frac{P(X)}{Z_{m,m-1}(X)} \sim\frac{X}{2m^2}\qquad(X\longrightarrow\infty).} \tag{12} For CP3 this is X/18. The complete derivative lift accounts for four of the six powers of the high spectral degree in its kinetic norm. This conclusion depends on using the lifted field as the canonical parent. If f itself is the canonical field of a separately specified action, its kinetic norm is the one in that action. Equation (7) is a constraint on this concrete lift, not a change to the valid geometric identity (1). Compress the actual algebraic scalar current The same norm issue applies directly to the written local scalar interaction, without introducing the derivative energy. Let T be the specified linear field lift, Z=T^\dagger T its positive kinetic operator and U=TZ^{-1/2},\qquad U^\dagger U=I. \tag{13} For the projective jet lift, (7) computes Z explicitly. Equation (13) is its isometric form on the canonical retained field. Retain the full parent spinor and its scalar matrix \beta^\dagger=\beta, \beta^2=I. At a fixed smooth background Y_0, set J_0=Y_0^\dagger\beta Y_0. The complete real-linear derivative of the cubic scalar source is \mathcal V_{Y_0}h =g\left[J_0\beta h +2\operatorname{Re}(Y_0^\dagger\beta h)\,\beta Y_0\right]. \tag{14} All complex amplitudes and their conjugate response are present. Since |J_0|\le|Y_0|^2, its pointwise operator norm obeys \|\mathcal V_{Y_0}\| \le3|g|\,|Y_0|^2. \tag{15} On a fixed bounded smooth spatial background, multiplication by this response is a bounded real-linear operator. Canonical compression gives \boxed{ \|U^\dagger\mathcal V_{Y_0}U\| \le3|g|\,\|Y_0\|_\infty^2. } \tag{16} The derivatives in T do not invalidate the bound: the same derivatives occur in Z, and their canonical combination U is an isometry. A constant scalar contribution M\|\mathcal J_Lf\|^2 in the selected component similarly becomes M\|u\|^2. Thus this canonical compression of the algebraic scalar source cannot equal a nonzero constant times the unbounded polynomial P(X) on all degrees of one fixed smooth background. This is a statement about the specified linear lift and fixed-background response. It does not impose a uniform bound across different self-consistent particle backgrounds, whose densities may differ. It also does not replace a nonlinear, frequency-dependent elimination of other spatial components. Those require the full complementary variation. The geometric simplex operator remains a concrete candidate. The natural osculating-polynomial lift, by itself, does not derive it as a canonically normalized physical mass interaction. Verification projective_jet_norm_checks.py constructs and inverts the complete polynomial interpolation matrix. Arbitrary complex spatial jets verify (5) against independent full tensor contractions at nonzero projective coordinates. Exact arithmetic checks the norm polynomial, the Hockey-Stick normalization and the unchanged assigned indices. Independent curved quadrature verifies the full Gram matrix through degree 35; complex action variations verify the canonical coefficient. Complete real-linear scalar variations with every spinor polarization check the compression bound (16).

title: Spatial source preservation for an exact linear branch
summary: Exact preservation of a holomorphic spatial section forces a constant real scalar potential. If a covariant kernel preserves a coherent section, every normalized section in that band has the same frequency.
text:
Summary: Exact preservation of a holomorphic spatial section forces a constant real scalar potential. If a covariant kernel preserves a coherent section, every normalized section in that band has the same frequency. The spatial condition behind exact linearity The nonlinear mass reduction gives, for a normalized analytic chiral branch, \omega(g)=gA-4g^3C+O(g^5),\qquad C=A\|\eta\|^2+\langle\eta,V_\chi\etaangle, \quad \eta=-\mathscr D_\perp^{-1}(I-P)(V_\chi\chi). 	ag{1} Here P retains the whole zero space in the stated problem. Under A>0 and V_\chi\ge0, C=0 precisely when the complementary source vanishes. An exact linear frequency near g=0 must therefore satisfy that source-preservation condition. This note determines its spatial meaning for the specified CP3 Dirac geometry. The physical electron directions remain six ordinary macroscopic spatial directions. CP3 and its Fubini–Study metric are conditional hypotheses about their global spatial geometry, with an undetermined physical radius. There is no compactification. Its holomorphic section degree L is an input to this comparison and is not the cumulative mass-band label N=n-1. Use the canonical Spin^c bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L), L\ge0, and \mathscr D_L=\sqrt2( ar\partial_L+ ar\partial_L^\dagger). For the following formulas the geometry is CPm, with m=3 in the six-dimensional comparison. The zero space is the positive-chirality holomorphic section space H_L=H^0(\mathcal O(L)). Use unit spatial measure d
u and unit norm for \chi\in H_L. The radius, physical volume and canonical norm are restored as in the spatial branch note. Preserving a holomorphic section forces a constant potential Let V be a smooth real scalar function on this connected spatial manifold, and let \chi be a nonzero holomorphic section. Then  oxed{V\chi\in H_L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad V 	ext{ is spatially constant}.} 	ag{2} To prove the nontrivial direction, take a local holomorphic frame away from the zero set of \chi. There 0= ar\partial_L(V\chi)=( ar\partial V)\chi, so  ar\partial V=0. Because V is real, its conjugate derivative also vanishes. A nonzero holomorphic section has a zero set with empty interior. Smoothness therefore extends dV=0 over that set, and connectedness makes V constant globally. The converse is immediate. The argument concerns a scalar multiplication operator on actual spatial sections, not an arbitrary matrix on their coefficient space. Suppose now that V=K|\chi|^2, where K is real, reciprocal and normalized by K1=1. Reciprocity and unit norm imply \int V\,d
u=\langle1,K|\chi|^2angle =\langle K1,|\chi|^2angle=1. Thus the constant in (2) must be one. The unchanged field then solves (\mathscr D_L+gV eta)\chi=g\chi,\qquad \omega=g,\qquad \mathcal E_g(\chi)= rac g2. 	ag{3} For local contact K=I and L>0, this cannot hold: every nonzero holomorphic section of this line bundle has zeros. Restrict its homogeneous polynomial to a projective line on which it is not identically zero; a positive-degree homogeneous polynomial in two complex coordinates has a projective zero. Its squared norm therefore cannot be a positive spatial constant. The field must acquire a complementary spatial response if it continues as a stationary solution of that local equation. Equation (2) does not say that the kernel itself must be spatially constant. A nonconstant kernel can send a particular source to a constant. Its action on the full source family is the next question. Preserving a coherent section with a covariant kernel makes the band degenerate Assume K commutes with all physical Fubini–Study isometries. On scalar spatial harmonics it has real multipliers k_\ell: K=\sum_{\ell\ge0}k_\ell\Pi_\ell,\qquad k_0=1. 	ag{4} The spatial harmonic calculation derives their dimensions, normalized zonal functions and coherent convolution eigenvalues. Define  egin{aligned} h_\ell&= inom{\ell+m}{m}^2- inom{\ell+m-1}{m}^2, \quad h_0=1,\ Z_\ell(t)&= rac{P_\ell^{(m-1,0)}(2t-1)}{ inom{\ell+m-1}{\ell}},\ b_\ell(L)&= rac{L!(L+m)!}{(L-\ell)!(L+m+\ell)!} \quad(0\le\ell\le L), \end{aligned} 	ag{5} with b_\ell(L)=0 for \ell>L. For a normalized coherent section centered at the spatial point a, put t=|a^\dagger Z|^2 using unit representatives. Its density has the complete expansion ho_a(Z)=D_Lt^L =\sum_{\ell=0}^Lh_\ell b_\ell(L)Z_\ell(t),\qquad D_L= inom{L+m}{m}. 	ag{6} This follows from the zonal orthogonality \int Z_\ell^2d
u=1/h_\ell and the beta integral giving b_\ell(L). Every coefficient through L is nonzero. Consequently  oxed{Kho_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k_1=k_2=\cdots=k_L=0.} 	ag{7} Covariance makes this condition independent of the chosen center a. More strongly, the density of every \varphi\in H_L lies in scalar harmonics 0 through L: it is the restriction of a polynomial of bidegree (L,L), with successive traces giving those harmonic degrees. Therefore (7) implies K|\varphi|^2=\|\varphi\|^2, \qquad \mathcal E_{\mathrm{int}}(\varphi)= rac g2\|\varphi\|^4 \quad (\varphi\in H_L). 	ag{8} Every unit holomorphic shape is then an exact branch with the same frequency and energy. This interaction cannot select a coherent shape from other complex superpositions in that band. It may still act nontrivially on higher spatial harmonics outside the band's densities. The coherent-section assumption in (7) matters. A noncoherent holomorphic section can have vanishing low harmonic moments even when the kernel retains those harmonics. Its potential can then be constant without forcing the kernel to annihilate every other section's density. Equation (2) still applies, but the whole-band degeneracy conclusion need not. The balanced spatial branch realizes this possibility explicitly for the smooth first-moment kernel. Noncoherent holomorphic sections with an isotropic spatial moment give exact linear frequencies, and their complete spatial linearization has no exponential modes. Their density remains nonconstant. For example, K(Z,W)=1+\alpha Z_{L+1}(|Z^\dagger W|^2),\qquad 0<\alpha<1, 	ag{9} is positive pointwise because |Z_\ell|\le1. It is a nonconstant, reciprocal, covariant kernel satisfying (7). Its only nonzero multiplier above the constant is \alpha/h_{L+1}. This example prevents inferring that preservation of one finite band forces K=\Pi_0 everywhere. If one fixed bounded covariant kernel preserves coherent sections for unbounded degrees L, however, (7) forces all k_\ell=0 for \ell\ge1, so K=\Pi_0. Smooth coherent kernels retain a spatial correction The normalized spatial kernel family K_p(Z,W)=D_p|Z^\dagger W|^{2p},\qquad D_p= inom{p+m}{m},\qquad p=0,1,2,\ldots 	ag{10} has multipliers b_\ell(p) from (5). title: Rank-one common anchor
summary: A conditional source-cancellation mechanism fixes output ratios but not their physical identification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A conditional source-cancellation mechanism fixes output ratios but not their physical identification. NOT A PHYSICS MODULE OR COMPLETED SCALE DERIVATION. The source-cancellation calculation below is exact for a specified rank-one response. Its identification with the actual V2 projected reference-frequency dynamics remains unproved. 1. The constructive possibility The earlier work treated a coupling matrix as though it had to act directly on wave-mode coefficients, then diagonalized it or took its square root. A different role is possible: the matrix can map scalar source currents to scalar Dirac self-energies. In that role, its rank-one image fixes ratios of output coefficients without determining the source magnitudes. This provides a concrete sufficient mechanism for the square-root coupling ratios. It does not require an oscillator frequency-squared matrix, and it does not require an amplitude measurement. The remaining physical identification is substantial and is kept explicit below. 2. Exact source elimination Consider a finite, compatibly normalized common source space. The test interaction is \mathcal L_{\rm int}=-\frac12\mathbf J^TG\mathbf J, \qquad G=vv^T, \qquad v_d=\sqrt{g_{dd}}>0. This is an algebraic candidate after choosing common units and integration conventions. Any common dimensional prefactor is suppressed here and can be absorbed in the common response scalar. A physical cross-depth action must establish the compatible measures and maps; the displayed finite expression does not do that automatically. Writing U=(1/2)\mathbf J^TG\mathbf J, its scalar self-energy coefficients are \Sigma_d=\frac{\partial U}{\partial J_d} =\sum_eG_{de}J_e =v_dC, \qquad C=\sum_ev_eJ_e. For arbitrary symbolic source entries, the row relations give \boxed{v_6\Sigma_d-v_d\Sigma_6=0.} On a nonzero electron-reference branch, \boxed{\frac{\Sigma_d}{\Sigma_6}=\frac{v_d}{v_6} =\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}.} No J_d has been assigned a measured value, fitted, or solved for. The source vector and any common multiplier cancel. This is elimination of an unneeded source, not an amplitude-domain reconstruction. The positive choice of v specifies the adopted sign convention. Relating these scalar coefficients to positive rest frequencies still requires the appropriate common mass-sign branch. A zero response cannot serve as the electron anchor. 3. Coefficient ratios are not automatically pole ratios The exact result above concerns \Sigma_d. To conclude \frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e}=\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}, one must establish that \Sigma_d is the relevant complete occupied scalar rest-frequency coefficient after canonical kinetic normalization and the prescribed mode projection. Different kinetic factors, additional mass terms, noncommuting operator pieces, spatially varying backgrounds, or frequency-dependent self-energies can prevent this coefficient ratio from being the ratio of physical poles. A common local scalar function is not automatically a common constant in every sector's eigenvalue problem. The self-contact source, Section 9.1, currently introduces the common-anchor relation conditionally and says the master equation must supply it. The present calculation offers a sufficient response mechanism to test against that obligation. It does not change that documentary status into a completed theorem. 4. The decisive reference-band versus primitive-unit test Use the specified references (n_3^\star,n_4^\star,n_6^\star)=(1,3,13), whose contact multipliers are (D_3^\star,D_4^\star,D_6^\star)=(1,15,18564). The ordinary contact law gives \omega_d^\star=D_d^\star\varpi_d. There are two inequivalent ways to place the rank-one response relative to this multiplication. Case A: response already gives the occupied reference frequencies If \Sigma_d=Cv_d already denotes \omega_d^\star, then \frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e}=\frac{v_d}{v_6}, \qquad \boxed{\frac{\varpi_d}{\omega_e} =\frac{v_d}{D_d^\star v_6}.} For the adopted g_{33}=8\sqrt7, g_{44}=12/\sqrt7, g_{66}=1/4, this gives: Depth Occupied reference frequency divided by \omega_e Primitive unit \varpi_d/\omega_e 3 9.201306535164823 9.201306535164823 4 4.259377267212064 0.28395848448080424 6 1 1/18564\approx0.0000538677009265245 This reproduces the proposed anchor architecture, conditional on the Case A identification. The calculation does not independently derive the adopted coupling values. Case B: response gives the coefficient before contact multiplication If instead \varpi_d=Cv_d is the pre-contact unit, the occupied reference frequencies obey \boxed{\frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e} =\frac{D_d^\star v_d}{D_6^\star v_6}.} The same numerical couplings now give: Depth Occupied reference frequency divided by \omega_e 3 0.0004956532285695337 4 0.0034416429114512473 6 1 The discrepancy is not a rounding error or a choice of MeV units. Case A divided by Case B is exactly 18564 at depth three and 18564/15 at depth four. The response and the simplex multiplier cannot be composed in an unspecified order. This distinction is directly motivated by self-contact Sections 6.4 and 9: the source first defines the projected coefficient \mu_d, then multiplies it by S(n,d). Its separate common-anchor statement concerns M_d^\star=\mu_dS(n_d^\star,d). A rank-one law for the former is not automatically a rank-one law for the latter with the same vector. 5. What two-sided reference-count weighting would do Let D_\star=\operatorname{diag}(1,15,18564). A symmetric primitive response matrix \widetilde G=D_\star^{-1}GD_\star^{-1} =\widetilde v\widetilde v^T, \qquad \widetilde v=D_\star^{-1}v, has diagonal entries \boxed{\widetilde g_{dd}=g_{dd}/(D_d^\star)^2.} If this were the primitive response, multiplying its outputs by D_d^\star would give a vector proportional to v, recovering the Case A reference ratios. This is a correct algebraic construction and retains rank one. It is not a derived V2 normalization. The primitive matrix is no longer the original G with the original diagonal entries. Dividing only one side would also change the action's symmetric response interpretation. Calling the two-sided transformation a harmless field redefinition would require transforming the kinetic form, currents, measures, and the meaning of the quoted couplings consistently. No such projection/kinetic-normalization theorem was established in the inspected passages. The reference counts must not be inserted solely because they recover the desired numbers. 6. Why cross-depth geometry is still an obstruction to automatic factorization The reciprocity source, Section 5, writes the two variations of the same cross-depth interaction as a lower-depth response to the higher-depth marginal and a higher-depth response to the lower-depth field extended across the additional fibre. The polarization-coupling source, Section 6, separately assigns pushforward to contact, invariant brackets to polarization selection, and the coupling coefficient and field equations to dynamics. These are valuable geometric and variational structures. They do not automatically make every sector's full response proportional to the same source functional after projection. Even when the numerical coefficients factor as g_{de}=v_dv_e, the full operator can contain sector-dependent kernels, fibre maps, spinor contractions, and kinetic normalizations. Factorization of the coefficient matrix is not yet factorization of all those maps together. The common-source cancellation is therefore sufficient when the projected response has the proved finite form. Checking that premise in the actual source geometry is indispensable. The reported bounded searches did not establish an independent full projected reference-response action; that search result is not a universal absence theorem. 7. Proof obligations before promoting the mechanism The immediate task is an identification calculation, not a source-amplitude solve. It must show that the projected scalar interaction has the needed common response after the cross-depth measures and kernels are included; track every D_d^\star through projection and variation; put the kinetic term into the same normalization used for the frequency extraction; and connect the resulting scalar coefficient to the complete reference pole on the appropriate branch. If those steps establish Case A, the reference ratios follow without determining C. If the action instead establishes Case B, the different ratios are a real consequence of that prescription and must not be hidden by relabeling \Sigma_d. If additional kernels destroy the common response, their frequency effects have to be calculated rather than silently absorbed into a universal source. Closing the reference law would still not solve the baryon problem by itself. A composite operator, its color-singlet constraint, and any induced frequency-dependent interactions remain to be derived. The signed color-pair coefficient and exact block reduction in the review note are tools for that next stage, not missing mass factors that can simply be multiplied together. 8. Reproducible status The regression script differentiates the symbolic quadratic interaction, proves the row annihilator identities for arbitrary sources, calculates both reference prescriptions, and verifies the two-sided count weighting. The independent checks are packaged for repetition. Established: a rank-one scalar response can give the desired square-root coefficient ratios with complete cancellation of unmeasured source magnitudes. Not established: that the written V2 master action realizes this response for canonically normalized occupied reference frequencies, that the reference-count weighting is dynamically selected, that the self-consistent branch exists and is stable, or that a nucleon pole has been predicted. This is the principal constructive lead from the latest calculations. Its conditional status is part of the finding, not a reason to discard it or to claim more than has been shown. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and correction guidance. Common field response — derives the full response-profile criterion for rank one and its static coupling bound.

title: A rank-independent current excess for same-field pair response
summary: A smooth polynomial excess preserves an isolated coherent source at every projector rank and gives a calculable prepared-pair angular cost, but it still requires an independent strength and spatial binding law.
text: The cubic current excess gives a positive prepared-pair angular cost but changes the isolated source when a lower-rank current is simply inserted in a larger matrix. The following polynomial removes that algebraic defect without choosing a rank in its definition. The insertion is a conditional map of representation coefficients; the physical spatial map between nested sectors remains undetermined. Polynomial and source For a Hermitian Lorentz-scalar current C, put T=\operatorname{Tr}C and p_j=\operatorname{Tr}C^j. Define \boxed{K(C)=T p_3-p_2^2 =\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i\lambda_j(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^2,} \tag{1} where the eigenvalues include zeros. Thus K\ge0 on positive semidefinite currents. It can be negative on indefinite currents; for eigenvalues 2,-1, it equals -18. It is nevertheless a smooth polynomial through C=0. Its complete matrix gradient is \boxed{\nabla K=p_3 I+3T C^2-4p_2 C.} \tag{2} For any occupied-rank s projector P_s, C=\rho P_s gives K=0 and (\nabla K)P_s=0, independent of the surrounding matrix rank. The gradient on the unoccupied complement is s\rho^3 I; thus the complete field Hessian may change, even though the occupied isolated mass source does not. The joint calculation and report check (1), (2), their full noncommuting derivatives, and all maintained representation depths 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10. The largest relative gradient-derivative error in the random indefinite controls is below 2.4\times10^{-9}. There is an exact minimality result within unitary-invariant polynomials of this one current. Evaluate a homogeneous polynomial on C=\rho P_s for every positive occupied rank s. Up to degree three, the invariant bases evaluate respectively as s, (s^2,s), and (s^3,s^2,s), times the appropriate power of \rho. Their Vandermonde matrices have full column rank, so no nonzero combination vanishes on all projector rays. At degree four the basis (T^4,T^2p_2,p_2^2,Tp_3,p_4) evaluates as (s^4,s^3,s^2,s^2,s)\rho^4. Its nullspace is exactly the span of Tp_3-p_2^2. Thus (1) is the unique lowest-degree nonzero projector-transparent invariant polynomial of a single current, up to its coefficient. Since C is quadratic in the field, this correction is eighth order in the field. This result does not exclude lower-order laws using the other currents, spatial derivatives or nonpolynomial functions. The batch verifies these evaluation-matrix ranks exactly using rational arithmetic. An inverse action trial can add one coefficient \eta K(C_k) to each shell's existing trace current. Since K is fourth order in C, \eta has units of inverse current cubed. The common shell weights, frequency unit, canonical norm, and separate nonlinear binding remain premises. No master equation here fixes \eta or unifies it with the trace term. Same-depth prepared pair For two currents sharing a partner frame, let C_k=I_r\otimes(\rho P_z+\sigma P_w), s=|z^\dagger w|^2, and L=\rho+\sigma. The two ray eigenvalues have product P=\rho\sigma(1-s^k). Direct substitution in (1) yields \boxed{K(C_k)=r^2P(L^2-4P)\ge0.} \tag{3} For s=\cos^2\theta, its small-angle term is r^2\rho\sigma L^2 k\theta^2. Thus alignment is an angular minimum for every positive-order shared shell. The exact response has a useful decomposition. With u=s^k, K=r^2\rho\sigma(\rho-\sigma)^2(1-u) +4r^2(\rho\sigma)^2u(1-u). \tag{3a} For equal densities, only the second term remains. Since \|[P_z^k,P_w^k]\|_{\rm HS}^2=2u(1-u), its prepared-pair energy is 2r^2\rho^4\|[P_z^k,P_w^k]\|_{\rm HS}^2. The current therefore penalizes noncommuting ray projectors in this restricted preparation. Orthogonal equal-density rays also have K=0, whereas unequal orthogonal rays have K=r^2\rho\sigma(\rho-\sigma)^2. Therefore this algebraic energy alone does not guarantee that two freely evolving patterns align; it can have another stationary configuration and a barrier. For equal densities the barrier occurs at \cos^{2k}\theta=1/2 and has height r^2\rho^4 per shell. On the alignment side of this angle the energy slope tends to restore alignment; on the orthogonal side it tends toward orthogonality. If two ray angles are allowed to respond in one plane, their derivatives of this shared energy are equal and opposite. Their actual angular kinetic terms and spatial coupling have not been derived. Spatial overlap, phases in the full fields, and reciprocal shape motion must be included before interpreting a rate or force. Conditional cross-depth insertion Suppose a rank-s lower current \sigma P_s is zero padded in a rank-r parent. Equation (2) gives zero source on the occupied lower subspace for every s\le r, unlike the cubic excess. For a nested commuting prepared pair C=\rho P_r+\sigma P_s, the exact cross term is \boxed{K(C)=s(r-s)\rho(\rho+\sigma)\sigma^2.} \tag{4} The batch checks the isolated identity and (4) for all fifteen ordered depth pairs. The largest absolute formula error in those double-precision controls is below 2.3\times10^{-13}. This is an algebraic condition on a specified representation embedding. It is not a derivation of how independent physical particle patterns in nested spatial sectors couple. In particular, (4) begins quadratically in the lower amplitude and has no orientation dependence for rotations entirely inside a filled parent projector. With equal local amplitudes, the rank factor in (4) is 12 for a depth-two rank-2 current inside depth six's rank 8, but 16 for a depth-five rank-4 current there. The rank-only comparison therefore does not yield weak neutrino engagement. Different spatial support, occupied modes or a derived geometric map would have to carry any such suppression. Frozen partner threshold and physical limit At a unit-density coherent rank-r current, the traceless partner-split Hessian of \operatorname{Tr}C+\eta K(C) matches the earlier trace-current metric with q=2\eta r. At local density \rho, q_{\rm loc}=2\eta r\rho^3. Its frozen high-momentum partner block therefore requires \boxed{2\eta r\rho(x)^3<1} \tag{5} for the bounded real-frequency side of that block. This is a local necessary condition, not a whole-core stability theorem. Complete finite real-linear controls at depths 2, 4 and 6, with one or two oscillator columns, core gaps 0 and 1, and momenta 0.1, 1 and 10, found no resolved imaginary frequency above 9\times10^{-15} at one quarter and three quarters of the threshold. At 1.25 times the threshold, the largest imaginary frequency was about 0.484666 in particle-frequency units at each tested depth, approaching the analytic high-momentum limit 0.5. The polynomial is a stronger conditional coupling lead because the same expression preserves isolated occupied sources across projector ranks and gives a nonzero angular pair cost. It is not the physical coupling law or mass operator. The relative strength, the complete cross-depth spatial embedding, permitted polarization states, and encounter dynamics are unselected. The inherited upper-only localized core still has the constrained energetic saddle: its coherent energy is flat under norm-preserving dilation while the lower-spinor mixed source is nonzero. In fact, any correction that vanishes on every coherent current \rho P is identically zero along this full upper-only dilation, so it contributes no scale-scale curvature. Its occupied first derivative also vanishes when it is projector-transparent. No strength of (1) can cure that particular energetic saddle without changing the occupied core or another part of the action. A complete same-field law must also supply spatial support and a positive full response in one normalization.
