title: Coulomb angular response
summary: A six-coordinate Kepler model with reciprocal source angular momentum has exact signed-rose trajectories, including repelling two-electron solutions, but the pair is unstable and magnetic quadratic completion changes the motion.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A six-coordinate Kepler model with reciprocal source angular momentum has exact signed-rose trajectories, including repelling two-electron solutions, but the pair is unstable and magnetic quadratic completion changes the motion. What is restored, and what is a new premise The visualization history contains Coulomb binding plus a prescribed precession construction, not a single implemented force-law integration joining them. The old c50ef57 prose used a visible 1/r potential plus a separate sector Hamiltonian; it did not derive the subsequent frequency lock. This test supplies actual Cartesian positions and canonical momenta q_i,p_i in R6, without appending another independent six-dimensional electron position. Flat R6 is a mechanical diagnostic geometry, not a derived replacement for the candidate physical CP3 metric. Use the explicitly chosen Kepler kernel -k/|q| as a control. It is not silently identified with the Green function of an unrestricted six-dimensional field, nor with the unresolved interaction of a flat nucleus and a depth-six electron. A radial potential -k/r^a has circular effective-potential curvature a k (2-a)/r^(a+2). Thus a=1 has stable radial circular motion, whereas the unrestricted six-dimensional inverse-fourth-power potential does not in this flat point-particle model. Kernel and geometry selection remain explicit. The responding source is now a real skew 6 by 6 angular-momentum matrix C on a fixed coadjoint orbit. This is a new source phase-space premise, motivated by angular-momentum-bearing response, not a relabeling of the previous singlet-plus-gapped-amplitude source. No equivalence between the two source models or identification with a measured nuclear current is claimed. In particular C=0 remains zero: this source can reorient a prepared angular momentum but cannot induce its magnitude from an initially zero source. The petal preparations require nonzero source angular momentum as input. One autonomous Hamiltonian Define L=sum_i(q_i p_i^T-p_i q_i^T), pairing <A,B>=-tr(AB)/2, and H_0=\sum_i\left(\frac{p_i^2}{2m}-\frac{k}{|q_i|}\right) +\sum_{i<j}\frac{\gamma}{|q_i-q_j|},\qquad H=H_0+\lambda\langle C,L\rangle+\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I}. Use canonical brackets for q,p and the angular-momentum Lie-Poisson bracket for C. The equations are \dot q_i=p_i/m-\lambda Cq_i,\qquad \dot p_i=F_i(q)-\lambda Cp_i,\qquad \dot C=\lambda[C,L]. Here F is the full attraction-plus-pair-repulsion force from H0. The source energy is a Casimir and adds no orientation torque. The source is not frozen: C and L generally precess, with dot L=-dot C. Total J=C+L, energy, the spectrum of C, and the spectrum of total orbital L are conserved. The source and orbit exchange angular momentum. There are no prescribed time-dependent fields in these equations. They describe classical actual trajectories. The two-electron version includes direct repulsion, but is not an antisymmetric quantum many-body state and does not replace the separate Pauli-compatible carrier tests. The canonical p is not m dot q when the angular coupling is present. Exact reduction to Coulomb motion plus reciprocal precession Let Q_i(t),P_i(t) solve the uncoupled rotationally invariant H0 problem, with conserved total L0 and the same initial Cartesian data. Then R(t)=e^{-\lambda Jt}e^{\lambda L_0t},\qquad q_i(t)=R(t)Q_i(t),\quad p_i(t)=R(t)P_i(t), \qquad C(t)=e^{-\lambda Jt}C_0e^{\lambda Jt} solve the coupled equations. Indeed dot R R^T=-lambda C(t), and the central and pair forces are rotation-covariant. This is an exact autonomous backreaction solution, not an imposed precession schedule. It also shows a limitation: this interaction only rotates the ordinary Coulomb configuration; it does not repair its radial or pair instabilities. Prepared signed-rose family Set radius and mass to one, k=1, lambda=0.2. For N=1 choose q=e1,p=ell e2 with ell=1. For N=2 take an antipodal pair with opposite momenta and gamma=0.4. Both remain separated by distance two, and their canonical circular momenta obey ell=sqrt(k-gamma/4)=sqrt(0.9). In either case define beta=ell/m-N lambda ell. Choose conserved total angular momentum J=j(E14+E25), where Eab is the unit skew generator; indices here run from one to six. These planes mix the first two visible axes with the fourth and fifth axes. Set lambda j=l beta and C0=J-L0. Then the first electron has the exact Cartesian path q(t)=(\cos(l\theta)\cos\theta,\ \cos(l\theta)\sin\theta,\ 0, \ \sin(l\theta)\cos\theta,\ \sin(l\theta)\sin\theta,\ 0), \qquad\theta=\beta t. Its full radius is one, so projected center crossings are not collisions with the nucleus. The source backreaction is nonzero. The second electron, when present, is its antipode. The computed clocks are beta=0.8 for N=1 and beta=0.569209978830 for N=2. Neither clock is imposed in the RHS. However, the integer ratio is selected by the initial conserved J, not dynamically attracted or quantized by this Hamiltonian. The source coadjoint spectrum changes when this preparation changes. No shell index or nuclear response spectrum has been derived from choosing integer l. Relation to the visualization The direct planar projection is the smooth signed rose w=cos(l theta) exp(i theta). For even integer l it has 2l distinct petals and the same planar image as the demo's |cos(l theta)| exp(i theta). Thus l=2 and l=4 yield actual four- and eight-petal projected paths. Their time parametrization differs from the modulus-folded demo at center crossings; the demo's additional height readout is not derived here. For odd l the signed curve instead has l distinct petals. In particular l=1 is an offset circle and l=3 is a three-petal rose, not the demo's two- and six-petal images. The absolute-value detector map cannot be silently substituted for this linear spatial projection. Matching selected even-l images is a concrete partial match, not reproduction of the entire display. Perturbation and two-electron instability Independent integration agrees with the exact prepared paths over a full clock turn for N=1,2 and l=1,2,3,4. For one electron, perturbed bound Kepler motion stays radially bounded because R is orthogonal. Small changes can alter the clock ratios and lose exact recurrence; the periodic petal path is not an attractor. For the l=2 test, changing one unobserved position component and one canonical tangential momentum component by 0.0001 or 0.001 gives the following maximum position deviations over two intended clock turns: N Perturbation Position deviation Radius deviation 1 0.0001 0.00488624 0.000400115 1 0.001 0.0487993 0.00401144 2 0.0001 4.48656 2.31761 2 0.001 4.92009 4.02402 The repelling pair has an analytic exponential instability, not merely a poor numerical trajectory. Its common-displacement mode has no first-order change in total orbital angular momentum and therefore is not stabilized by the reciprocal rigid rotation. In the ordinary co-rotating Coulomb frame its 4 by 4 Jacobian is [-W,I; diag(2k,-k),-W], with W=[[0,-Omega],[Omega,0]] and Omega²=k-gamma/4. In the tested units, \sigma^2=\frac{k-2\Omega^2+\sqrt{9k^2-8k\Omega^2}}2>0. The growth rate is 0.520404067288 in the test's time units, predicting amplification 64.2789706 over eight units. The checker computes this eigenvalue and tests its predicted growth in a full coupled integration from a 1e-7 perturbation. Consequently the exact two-electron family is an existence result, not a stable atomic model. Magnetic quadratic completion must not be omitted The linear angular coupling can stand as a phenomenological gyroscopic Hamiltonian, but calling it a complete magnetic minimal coupling requires the quadratic term. For a spatially uniform linear connection, the completed kinetic Hamiltonian is H_{\rm min}=\sum_i\frac{|p_i-m\lambda Cq_i|^2}{2m} -\sum_i\frac{k}{|q_i|}+\sum_{i<j}\frac{\gamma}{|q_i-q_j|} +\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I}. This adds m lambda² sum |Cq|²/2. The source equation must change as well: dot C=[C,lambda L-m lambda² sum(q wedge Cq)]. Both versions are checked against their own energy gradients, with conserved total angular momentum. This is a consistency test for this uniform-connection interpretation, not a uniquely derived nuclear electromagnetic field. On the prepared trajectories, the initial quadratic/uncoupled-kinetic energy ratios are: N l=1 l=2 l=3 l=4 1 0.68 2.60 5.80 10.28 2 0.52 1.60 3.40 5.92 The term is not perturbatively small for the complex petal examples. Adding it reciprocally changes the old l=2 preparation: over one intended turn the one-electron position error reaches 1.86827 with radius change 0.595951; the pair position error reaches 2.53216 with radius change 0.527079. These are tests of the same initial data, not an exclusion of other solutions of the completed equations. The subsequent completed relative-equilibrium calculation finds different exact solutions of the completed Hamiltonian, including one-electron four- and eight-petal branches without resolved exponential linear modes. Thus this initial-data failure is not a no-petal conclusion. Conclusion Actual autonomous petal-shaped projections with reciprocal source motion now exist in an explicit Coulomb-plus-angular-response Hamiltonian, including an exact repelling two-electron family. The source, coupling, and preparation are explicit, and the even-l planar matches are checked, not drawn by an assigned clock. The remaining problems are specific: the pair is unstable; the integer frequency ratio is prepared rather than selected; odd-l and height readouts do not match the visualization; and the magnetic quadratic completion is large and changes these trajectories. That next calculation has now found bound relative equilibria of the completed Hamiltonian; see Completed Coulomb petals. Source induction, integer selection, and stable many-electron motion remain unfinished. Reproduction and related notes Final normal and optimized runs completed 9,812 evaluations across 28 conditions. Independent integration matched the exact prepared motion within 1.88e-9; full-turn energy drift was at most 6.02e-9. Perturbed trajectory energy drift was 3.94e-9, and the quadratic-completion energy drift was 1.01e-8. Predicted unstable-mode amplification agreed with the coupled integration to relative error 1.66e-8. Reversing source backreaction, omitting the quadratic force, or reversing pair repulsion each failed an independent gradient or angular-momentum conservation check. All 50 diagnostic scripts and source checks passed in the regression run; the final zero-source control also passed the separate normal and optimized reruns. coulomb_angular_response_checks.py — actual six-coordinate integrations, exact solution, reciprocal gradients, pair instability, and quadratic completion. Full response extension — preceding response-only model; its negative result is not overwritten. Actual orbit research correction — provenance of the Coulomb-plus-precession target. Two-electron shared response — separate antisymmetric carrier model, not this classical Cartesian calculation. Research status — current proof boundaries.

title: CP3 response selection
summary: At fixed electron depth six, an explicit filled-band response selects equal nonzero skew strengths and CP3 minimum components, with positive stiffness for normal variations in matrix space but unresolved source occupation and first-order dynamics.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: At fixed electron depth six, an explicit filled-band response selects equal nonzero skew strengths and CP3 minimum components, with positive stiffness for normal variations in matrix space but unresolved source occupation and first-order dynamics. Fixed-depth question The particle depths supplied by the mass formula are fixed inputs to this investigation. In particular the electron has six spatial dimensions. The question here is whether a six-dimensional interaction selects the complex-structure geometry, not whether the electron should be reassigned to a different depth. Allow an unconstrained real antisymmetric 6x6 variable B. Its three signed canonical plane strengths are lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3. We do not impose B squared proportional to minus the identity. Introducing B as a collective electron order parameter is itself a modeling premise; its microscopic definition remains to be derived. An arbitrary six-dimensional particle does not automatically have this order parameter as its configuration. A specified matrix response rather than a prescribed CP3 penalty Introduce two six-component vector response bands with gap Delta>0 and coupling g!=0. Their real symmetric one-particle operator is h(B)=\begin{pmatrix}0&gB\\-gB&\Delta I_6\end{pmatrix}. Under B -> R B R^T it transforms by conjugation with diag(R,R); no rotation plane is distinguished. Twelve is the number of source states, not a particle depth. This is a new candidate self-response model, distinct from the earlier singlet-plus-nine nuclear-contact model. Neither its source carrier nor its occupation is claimed to follow already from the V2 master kernel. For each plane, the source eigenvalues are e_\pm(y)=\frac{\Delta\pm\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}}2, \qquad y=\lambda_i^2, each with multiplicity two. Assume all six lower-band states are occupied, and add a positive bare cost mu times the squared skew norm, with mu>0. Equivalently use the lower-band trace as an explicitly specified effective energy. The fixed six-occupation interpretation is a possible source model, not a claim that an electron has six constituent particles. With <B,B>=−tr(B squared)/2=sum lambda_i², the total energy is exactly E(B)=\mu\langle B,B\rangle+\operatorname{Tr}_{-}h(B) =\sum_{i=1}^3 f(\lambda_i^2),\qquad f(y)=\mu y+\Delta-\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}. The source force in each plane is bounded at large strength, while the positive quadratic cost makes the total energy coercive. Thus the energy is not an unstable truncated expansion. Near B=0 its expansion is (mu−2g²/Delta) sum lambda_i²+(2g^4/Delta³) sum lambda_i^4 plus higher orders. The equalizing quartic sign follows from this source spectrum, not a fit. Exact global minimum: the complex-structure constraint emerges For y>=0, f'(y)=\mu-\frac{2g^2}{\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}},\qquad f''(y)=\frac{4g^4}{(\Delta^2+4g^2y)^{3/2}}>0. Strict convexity makes equal squared strengths the unique minimizer at any fixed sum of squared strengths. Allowing that sum to vary gives: If mu>=2g²/Delta, the minimum is B=0, not CP3. If 0<mu<2g²/Delta, each squared strength has the same positive minimum \rho^2=\frac{4g^4/\mu^2-\Delta^2}{4g^2}. Consequently every global minimum obeys B^2=-\rho^2 I_6,\qquad J=B/\rho,\qquad J^2=-I_6. The full minimum set is O(6)/U(3). It has two connected components, distinguished by Pfaffian sign. Each component is SO(6)/U(3), hence CP3. The response energy does not select one component or a handedness. The orthogonal-complex constraint has been obtained by minimization rather than inserted into the definition of B. For the dimensionless diagnostic mu=Delta=g=1, rho²=.75 and E_min=−.75. The stationary states with one or two nonzero plane strengths have energies −.25 and −.5; they do not minimize the full energy. Full fluctuation calculation Here "normal variations in matrix space" means changes away from the CP3 minimum family in the auxiliary matrix B, not extra spatial directions. A skew 6x6 matrix has 6(6−1)/2=15 independent rotation-plane components: six variations are tangent to the CP3 family and nine are normal to it in this parameter space. The electron's assigned spatial depth remains six. The gradient in the skew pairing is \nabla E=2\mu B-4g^2B(\Delta^2 I_6-4g^2B^2)^{-1/2}. At B=rho J, skew perturbations H split into six matrix-space variations satisfying HJ+JH=0 and nine satisfying HJ−JH=0. The first are tangent to the CP3 component. The Hessian is zero on them and is a positive scalar on the nine normal variations in matrix space: k_\perp=\frac{16g^4\rho^2}{(2g^2/\mu)^3}>0. This tests all fifteen skew coordinates, not just the three canonical strengths. The diagnostic has six zero eigenvalues and nine eigenvalues equal to 1.5. Flat orientation directions are expected along a family of minima; they do not imply attraction to a unique orientation. What dynamics this energy can and cannot supply A commutator-only equation dot B=[F(B,t),B] preserves all spectral invariants tr(B^n). It cannot turn unequal strengths into equal ones. For this invariant energy, [gradient E,B]=0 identically. Thus simply substituting E into the earlier coadjoint equation would give no amplitude-selection dynamics. As an explicit additional kinetic assumption, introduce canonical momentum Pi for B and Hamiltonian <Pi,Pi>/(2M)+E(B). This allows strength fluctuations. Near the selected family the nine oscillation modes for normal variations in matrix space have frequency sqrt(k_perp/M). Direct evolution verifies their linearized oscillations and total-energy conservation. There is no damping and no claim of relaxation from arbitrary initial states. Low-energy confinement near the minimum manifold is distinct from dissipative capture into it. Restricting the flat kinetic term to B=rho J gives an induced CP3 metric. For a normalized geometric ray Z and horizontal dZ, the existing Pauli map obeys <dJ,dJ>=8||dZ||². With the convention ds_FS²=dZ dagger dZ−|Z dagger dZ|², the kinetic term is therefore 4M rho² ds_FS²/dt². The metric is proportional to Fubini–Study under this specific kinetic assumption, rather than separately named by fiat. This is still a collective-coordinate construction. If B is a field over an already chosen particle base, CP3 is its target/order-parameter space, not automatically that base. Identifying these collective coordinates with the actual six-dimensional electron configuration requires a microscopic reduction that does not double-count spatial variables. The source does not generate the needed first-order term The filled-band projector of h(B) is real symmetric. Its derivative is real symmetric, so the determinant-band Berry curvature i tr(P[dP,dP]) vanishes: a symmetric matrix has zero trace against a real antisymmetric commutator. The calculation checks this using independent projector differences in all skew directions. Therefore this filled real source cannot by itself supply the nonzero first-order symplectic term used in the previous CP3 precession equation. The canonical kinetic example is an inertial model, not a derivation of that first-order equation. An existing electron action term or a suitable complex/chiral response would have to provide it. Geometry selection and the origin of the precession action must not be conflated. Occupation is a substantive premise: counterexample Keep the same h(B) but occupy only its lowest state. The source energy depends only on the largest squared plane strength. All other strengths cost positive mu energy without lowering that occupied level. When the coupling exceeds its corresponding threshold, this version prefers rank two B, not three equal nonzero strengths. For mu=.5, Delta=g=1, the single occupied state gives one squared strength .75 and minimum energy −.125. Both the global bound and the cost of adding other planes are checked. This is not an alternative particle-depth assignment. It shows precisely why the filled-band premise must be derived: rotational symmetry and the displayed source operator alone do not select CP3. Verification and next derivation cp3_geometry_selection_checks.py checks the complete twelve-state spectrum, exact energy, global bounds, finite-difference gradient, full Hessian, pure-ray metric, zero filled-band Berry curvature, partial-rank stationary states, threshold behavior, single-occupation counterexample, and canonical dynamics of normal variations in matrix space. All tests use explicit runtime failures and remain active under Python -O. Normal and optimized runs each completed 631 evaluations across 24 runtime conditions. Reversing the gradient in memory was rejected by the independent energy-gradient check in both modes; no mutated source was saved. The next source-level task is to derive or reject this response operator, its filled-band occupation, and an amplitude kinetic term from the V2 master interaction. Then determine the first-order electron term and the identification with physical spatial coordinates. The result already obtained is a conditional forward mechanism selecting CP3 components at fixed depth six, not a completed physical identification of the electron geometry. Related Research status — fixed-depth scope and current results. Sector geometry premise audit — separates assigned depth from geometry assumptions. Geometric response operator — Pauli map used to check the induced metric. Gapped contact source — earlier bounded-source method, with a different carrier and role. Flat nucleus precession — first-order dynamics not supplied by the present real filled source.

title: Cylindrical molecular shape stability
summary: The prescribed three-petal route gives a strict trigonal ligand minimum, while the nominal tetrahedral quarter-turn rays carry transverse force and relax to a strict disphenoidal minimum.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The prescribed three-petal route gives a strict trigonal ligand minimum, while the nominal tetrahedral quarter-turn rays carry transverse force and relax to a strict disphenoidal minimum. Question beyond radial balance The finite cylindrical profile calculation found restoring roots when every ligand was constrained to share one radius. That only tests the breathing coordinate. A molecular candidate can be restoring in that coordinate and still buckle or shear. This check holds the central nucleus and prescribed 6D electron route fixed, but varies every supported-space coordinate of every ligand independently. For ligand centres R_a\in\mathbb R^3, it evaluates U(R_1,\ldots,R_n)=Z_L\left\langle \sum_a V_{r_N}(|q_{\rm vis}(t)-R_a|)\right\rangle_t +\sum_a\frac{Z_0Z_L}{|R_a|} +\sum_{a<b}\frac{Z_L^2}{|R_a-R_b|}, using the finite uniform-ball cylindrical profile V_{r_N} and the same diagnostic values as the radial calculation. The gradient is analytic; the Cartesian Hessian is a centered difference of that gradient and is checked against an independent second energy difference. Three-petal trigonal result At nuclear profile radius r_N=0.3, (Z_0,Z_L)=(1,0.1), and R=0.937604839, the three petal-axis centres are stationary to 3.97\times10^{-14}. The nine Cartesian ligand Hessian eigenvalues are (0.548468,0.557117,0.557117,0.585964,0.585964,0.598115, 0.652028,0.652028,0.659033). They are all positive. Thus the frozen-route energy diagnostic gives a strict trigonal local minimum against arbitrary independent ligand displacement, not merely a restoring common radius. The same conclusion holds at r_N=0.1 and 0.6: the minimum pair angle remains exactly 120^\circ, and the smallest Hessian eigenvalues are 3.17715, 0.548468, and 0.0588992 respectively. The declining stiffness with profile width is quantitative, but no shape mode changes sign. Four-centre correction The four quarter-turn rays of the (1,2) route have the Gram matrix of a regular tetrahedron. That kinematic fact does not make the regular tetrahedron a force equilibrium after the entire route is time averaged. At the radial root R=0.901811770, the largest Cartesian energy-gradient component is 2.996\times10^{-2} and is transverse to the assigned ray. Unconstrained relaxation of all twelve ligand coordinates converges to \begin{aligned} &(\phantom{-}0.771577,0,\phantom{-}0.462280), &&(0,\phantom{-}0.771577,-0.462280),\\ &(-0.771577,0,\phantom{-}0.462280), &&(0,-0.771577,-0.462280). \end{aligned} This is a disphenoid rather than a regular tetrahedron: four pair angles are 105.31619^\circ and two are 118.14528^\circ. Its final gradient is below 10^{-10}, and all twelve Hessian eigenvalues are positive, ranging from 0.183516 to 0.608247. The route therefore supports a strict nearby 3D four-centre minimum, but its present time weighting predicts a distortion away from the regular tetrahedral angles. Boundary of the result This remains a prescribed-route diagnostic with a fixed central nucleus and fixed nuclear support planes. The electron route has not been solved or relaxed as a function of the ligand coordinates, so this is not a derived Born--Oppenheimer energy surface. It establishes a local ligand minimum only for that restricted energy. It does not establish recurrence or Floquet stability of the reciprocal system, where the electron route, angular source, nuclear motion, and plane rotors all respond together. Conversely, the regular-tetrahedron correction should not be erased by calling the calculation incomplete: within the stated approximation, the transverse force is nonzero and the stable minimum is the reported disphenoid. The displacement is robust but profile-dependent: r_N four repeated angles two repeated angles minimum Hessian eigenvalue 0.1 108.69956^\circ 111.02582^\circ 0.456196 0.3 105.31619^\circ 118.14528^\circ 0.183516 0.6 99.06970^\circ 133.21424^\circ 0.0500167 The r_N=0.6 row retains point-centre nuclear repulsion even though some uniform-ball nuclear profiles overlap. It is therefore a hybrid diagnostic, not the result for consistent finite-density pair interactions. The r_N=0.3 reported minima have no such profile overlap. Listed Hessian digits are numerical output, not an error-certified continuum precision. Angle data could constrain profile width only after the electron route, charges, nuclear interaction, and averaging law are independently fixed. Angles alone do not identify a unique nuclear density. title: Cylindrical petal continuation
summary: Fixed-Casimir shooting supplies near-recurrent candidates, but independent integration refinement rejects the saved nonzero checkpoints at the stated closure tolerance.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Fixed-Casimir shooting supplies near-recurrent candidates, but independent integration refinement rejects the saved nonzero checkpoints at the stated closure tolerance. Independent numerical correction Follow-up: Accurate cylindrical correction revisits these states with a new independently tested corrector. The rejection below applies to the original saved states, not to every nearby solution. The earlier claim that this calculation certified a periodic micro-branch is withdrawn. Reintegrating the same saved states and periods without fitting at tighter tolerances gives: h original closure norm refined closure norm last endpoint refinement 0.0064 4.25\times10^{-7} 2.41423\times10^{-6} 1.50\times10^{-9} 0.0096 2.49\times10^{-7} 7.43896\times10^{-6} 3.24\times10^{-9} 0.0128 5.24\times10^{-7} 5.31450\times10^{-6} 9.89\times10^{-11} All three fail the stated 10^{-6} closure threshold. Source Casimirs remain preserved to roundoff. The candidates are near-recurrent trajectories, not accepted periodic solutions. Earlier smaller steps have not independently been certified either. This rejects the prior numerical acceptance, not the existence of a nearby periodic orbit. The refinement uses DOP853 at (\mathrm{rtol},\mathrm{atol})=(10^{-12},10^{-14}) with maximum step T/1200, then (2.5\times10^{-14},10^{-15}) with T/2400. Agreement between those endpoints is an error diagnostic, not a rigorous global error bound or an existence theorem. The force is continuous but its derivative changes at the nuclear-profile boundary; endpoint accuracy must be checked separately from the integrator's local error control. The original states, parameters, and source-file hashes are preserved in archived candidates. Independent audit checks regenerate the refinement report. The continuation acceptance gate now requires a complete finite integration, fixed Casimirs, and independently refined closure before saving a checkpoint. Reduced recurrence problem The exact completed-Coulomb L=3 orbit occupies only coordinates (q_0,q_1,q_3,q_4) and the corresponding 4\times4 skew-source block. This sector remains invariant under both the full-4D Coulomb potential and the finite cylindrical potential supported on (q_0,q_1). Reducing to it leaves four positions, four momenta, six skew components, and the period. The shooting residual contains full-state recurrence, the phase condition q_1(0)=0, and the family condition q_0(0)=1. Fixed energy is another legitimate family constraint; it was not mathematically inappropriate. Neither constraint guarantees that the desired family exists. The section q_1(0)=0 is not by itself a radial turning-point condition. At homotopy h=0, the exact orbit has T=20.99780573,\qquad \|X(T)-X(0)\|=1.86\times10^{-12}. Thus the reduced dynamics and recurrence equations reproduce the analytic start. Why ordinary continuation stalled For V_h=(1-h)(-1/|q|)+hV_{r_N}(|q_{\rm vis}|),\qquad r_N=0.3, ordinary least-squares steps of h=0.05 and 0.005 stagnated with recurrence residuals 0.459 and 0.151 respectively. These are rejected numerical shoots, not evidence that a cylindrical periodic orbit does not exist. The Jacobian at the exact start is rank deficient, with symmetry and source-invariant structure. Not every unresolved direction has been proved to be a removable gauge direction. Ordinary whole-orbit finite differences misleadingly reported ranks from 8 to 12. This has now been replaced by local complex-step differentiation and simultaneous integration of the 14\times14 fundamental matrix. The local Jacobian agrees with an independent centered derivative to 5.53\times10^{-11}. The analytic shooting Jacobian has exactly eight resolved singular values, (94.7368,14.6897,5.94203,5.87715,1.37876,0.928496,0.838421,0.197030), with the other seven at 1.5\times10^{-12} or below. A separately integrated parameter-sensitivity equation gives kernel forcing norm 52.5150. Its component outside the resolved Jacobian range is only 2.70\times10^{-8}, and the minimum-norm tangent has norm 6.20934. Therefore there is no resolved first-order obstruction to continuing the petal orbit toward the cylindrical kernel. The h=10^{-4} tangent predictor has recurrence residual 8.59\times10^{-6}. Truncating newly split soft singular values rather than inverting them gives rank-aware correction residuals 4.87\times10^{-7} and 2.23\times10^{-7}. The corrected period is 20.99091657. These are the original, unrefined shooting diagnostics. They do not establish a periodic micro-branch or continuation to the fully cylindrical endpoint h=1. The unconstrained correction changes the source's quadratic and Pfaffian Casimirs by 2.19\times10^{-3} and 1.08\times10^{-3}. Continuing those values freely is mathematically allowed across a family of source orbits, but is not appropriate if V2 fixes the electron's source coadjoint orbit. Adding both Casimirs raises the resolved shooting rank from 8 to 10. Its analytic first-order equation is still solvable to 2.70\times10^{-8}, with tangent norm 7.32359, so fixed source invariants present no first-order obstruction. The first attempt to impose the Casimirs as extra residuals stalled at 4.49\times10^{-6}. The corrected formulation instead uses \mathfrak{so}(4)\cong\mathfrak{so}(3)_+\oplus\mathfrak{so}(3)_- and parameterizes the fixed coadjoint orbit as the product of the two spheres with the original self-dual and anti-self-dual radii. This removes both Casimir-normal directions identically. The chart reconstructs the initial source to 2.78\times10^{-17} and gives a rank-8-of-13 shooting Jacobian. At h=10^{-4}, rank-aware correction reduces the recurrence residual from 1.37\times10^{-5} to 2.44\times10^{-7}, with T=20.99128584 and maximum Casimir error 1.78\times10^{-15}. The Casimir parameterization is valid, but this unrefined closure estimate does not certify continuation. Continuation with the previous residual included in each predictor originally reported the following unrefined values, retained as a diagnostic record: h period T recurrence residual maximum Casimir error 1\times10^{-4} 20.99128584 2.44\times10^{-7} 1.78\times10^{-15} 2\times10^{-4} 20.98482005 1.75\times10^{-7} 0 4\times10^{-4} 20.97204284 2.01\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} 8\times10^{-4} 20.94710312 3.94\times10^{-7} 0 1.6\times10^{-3} 20.89958488 6.03\times10^{-7} 0 3.2\times10^{-3} 20.81331458 6.31\times10^{-7} 8.88\times10^{-16} 6.4\times10^{-3} 20.67292125 4.25\times10^{-7} 8.88\times10^{-16} 9.6\times10^{-3} 20.56750468 2.49\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} 1.28\times10^{-2} 20.48965107 5.24\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} The optimizer reached h=0.0128 using an intermediate h=0.0096 candidate, but the independent check above rejects its accuracy. Neither an accepted 1.28% continuation branch nor a branch termination follows. First-order solvability at a rank-deficient start also does not, alone, imply nonlinear continuation. Required continuation method First correct candidates using integration accuracy independently adequate for the desired closure tolerance. Pseudo-arclength continuation is a candidate improvement, not a guaranteed remedy. Multiple-shooting nodes can be placed at the six cylindrical-support encounters, where the profile changes curvature most rapidly. The existing fixed SO(4) source chart already uses self-dual and anti-self-dual two-spheres and removes the two Casimir-normal directions. Time phase, amplitude/arclength, and the remaining visible/unobserved rotation gauges must also be fixed explicitly. Only after reaching h=1 should the full reciprocal moving-nucleus system be continued from the fixed-centre solution and its Floquet multipliers computed. Reproduction cylindrical_petal_continuation_checks.py reproduces the exact start, verifies its local analytic Jacobian, integrates the monodromy and parameter sensitivity, tests first-order solvability, and performs two rank-aware corrections of the nonzero microstep. fixed_casimir_petal_continuation_checks.py constructs the two-sphere source chart and attempts continuation. It must reject a candidate that fails its independent integration-quality gate. Related Completed Coulomb petals — supplies the exact analytic branch at h=0. Reciprocal cylindrical molecule — supplies the conservative target dynamics after fixed-centre continuation. Cylindrical molecular shape stability — gives stable nuclear configurations for the later moving-centre solve.

title: Dimensional magnetic kernel comparison
summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route. Same kernel, different spinor moments Use the existing magnetic bridge: a fixed square-integrable density envelope, one uniform pure polarization, positive magnetic cost, and the leading Pauli coupling. At nonzero Fourier wavevector k, the closed-field projector on skew matrices is \mathcal P_kJ=P_kJ+JP_k,\qquad P_k=\frac{kk^T}{|k|^2}. This formula is valid in either ambient dimension. Its amplitude-space rank is d-1 and its isotropic angular average is (2/d)I on bivectors. In particular the average factor is 2/5 in five dimensions and 1/3 in six. An average projector factor is not itself a particle-depth measurement. With \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2, \|\mathcal P_kJ\|^2=\frac{|Jk|^2}{|k|^2}. The selected moments derived from the explicit spinors obey J_5^2=-I_5+nn^T,\quad |n|=1, \qquad J_6^2=-I_6. Therefore their directional response strengths are \|\mathcal P_kJ_5\|^2=1-(n\cdot\widehat k)^2, \qquad \|\mathcal P_kJ_6\|^2=1. There is a genuine zero-response direction in five dimensions. No rescaling of the coupling removes it. More generally every skew matrix in an odd-dimensional real space is singular, since \det J=\det(-J)=(-1)^d\det J. Thus a nonzero isotropic response for every wavevector at one fixed polarization is impossible for any odd-dimensional bivector in this kernel. Four-dimensional invertible skew matrices exist, so this parity result alone does not establish exactly six. Envelope anisotropy changes the minimum family differently Write f(k)=|\widetilde n(k)|^2\geq0 for the prescribed envelope weight, using a consistent Fourier convention, and define W=\int f(k)\,dk,\qquad T=\int f(k)\widehat k\widehat k^T\,dk,\qquad\operatorname{tr}T=W. After constrained field minimization, the polarization energies are E_5(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}\left(W-n(z)^TTn(z)\right), \qquad E_6(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}W. For an isotropic five-dimensional envelope, T=(W/5)I_5, the whole CP3 polarization family still minimizes and the magnitude is (4/5)g^2W/(2Z_B). For a generic anisotropic envelope with a simple lowest eigenvalue, n instead aligns with either sign of its lowest-eigenvalue axis. For any unit n, the condition \gamma(n)z=z defines a complex two-dimensional eigenspace, and its normalized rays form CP1. The explicit spinor identity gives precisely these rays the prescribed n. Hence a simple lowest envelope eigenvalue leaves two CP1 minimum families, one over each sign of the selected axis, not the full CP3. At either family, four ray directions acquire positive curvature and two remain flat. In six dimensions all six ray directions remain flat under this spin-magnetic energy for any such fixed envelope. If the lowest eigenvalue of T has multiplicity m, its allowed unit vectors form S^{m-1} and each has a CP1 ray fibre. The minimum family therefore has real dimension m+1; this dimension count does not assert that the bundle is globally a product. The m=1 case is the two CP1 components above, and m=5 restores all of CP3. In particular, an envelope respecting a three-visible-plus-two-unobserved split has T=\operatorname{diag}(t_V I_3,t_H I_2), with 3t_V+2t_H=W. If t_H<t_V, the minimum family has dimension three; if t_V<t_H, dimension four; if they are equal, dimension six. This symmetry-respecting comparison is more relevant to a fixed nuclear three-plane than assuming an arbitrary five-distinct-eigenvalue envelope. The corresponding six-dimensional pure-spinor magnetic energy remains ray-independent within the stated uniform-polarization approximation. For T=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,2,1,1)/8, a separate finite-difference check gives ray Hessian (0,0,0,1,1,1) to 4\times10^{-8}, as the dimension count predicts. The fibre argument is explicit: \gamma(n)^2=I and \operatorname{tr}\gamma(n)=0 give a two-complex-dimensional positive eigenspace. A ray in it has n(z)\cdot n=1; the already proved unit norm of n(z) forces n(z)=n. Rotational covariance gives the same smooth two-real-dimensional fibre over every axis. An exact axis-weight quadrature with five-dimensional weights (5,4,3,2,1)/15 yields the ray Hessian eigenvalues \left(0,0,\frac8{15},\frac{16}{15},\frac{24}{15},\frac{32}{15}\right), for energy normalized by g^2/(2Z_B)=1. Numerical derivatives reproduce these values. With six-dimensional weights (6,5,4,3,2,1)/21 every ray Hessian eigenvalue is zero analytically and below 1.2\times10^{-8} in the finite-difference calculation. This is a structural prediction of two competing kernels, not a fit of their coupling constants. The five-dimensional null axis and the envelope are explicit variables; no V1 choice of S5 or CP2 spatial base was used. Relation to the spectral discriminator The spectral comparison assumed an isotropic unrestricted bivector cost. For an isotropic envelope, the integrated magnetic projector merely rescales that coupling, preserving the corresponding gap multiplicities. For an anisotropic envelope the selected field is generally not proportional to J. Consequently the six-dimensional frozen-field excited gaps need not remain triply equal for an anisotropic envelope, even though its joint field-plus-ray minimum family remains CP3. These are different statements. Do not demand the isotropic-source singlet-triplet spectrum of every anisotropic magnetic preparation. The existing scalar-exchange bridge supplies the escape channel The operator-class restriction is substantive in the project's other source proposal. In five dimensions the sixteen Hermitian matrix directions are the identity, five \gamma_a, and ten bivectors H_{ab}, orthogonal with trace norm four. For any Hermitian density matrix \varrho, write N=\operatorname{tr}\varrho,\quad v_a=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho\gamma_a), \quad b_{ab}=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho H_{ab}). Completeness gives 4\operatorname{tr}(\varrho^2)=N^2+|v|^2+|b|^2. The same explicitly assumed Gaussian scalar-exchange reduction used in the scalar bridge therefore becomes E_G=\frac\kappa2\left(N^2-\operatorname{tr}\varrho^2\right) =\frac{3\kappa}{8}N^2-\frac\kappa8\left(|v|^2+|b|^2\right). It supplies both a vector and a bivector channel. Dropping the vector channel would not preserve that exchange identity. For a pure ray, S(b)+v\cdot\gamma=4zz^\dagger-I, exactly the operator that evades the five-dimensional bivector-only spectral no-go. Thus the leading Pauli/magnetic proposal and the full scalar-exchange proposal do not have the same dimension-discrimination power. No spectral exclusion of the full five-dimensional exchange competitor has been proved. The existing exchange caveats—Gaussian closure, statistics, normal ordering, and absence of exact one-particle two-body self-interaction—remain unchanged. Physical scope and next test This calculation tests a concrete part of the response kernel already in the archive. It omits orbital magnetic energy, electric response, radiation, spatial profile relaxation, nonuniform polarization, and the nucleus. Anisotropy should next be generated by the coupled envelope/nucleus solution, rather than chosen only as a diagnostic Fourier weight. The useful discriminant is polarization response to controlled envelope anisotropy, or a preparation-resolved directional magnetic response. Whether the electron exhibits either specified response still needs a derived observable map. The mathematics does not identify an electron from CP3 geometry or an averaged cloud alone. Verification dimensional_magnetic_kernel_checks.py performs 500 runtime checks, including kernel projection, directional responses, envelope minimization, the CP1 family, numerical Hessians, and the mixed-density exchange identity. Evidence: dimensional-magnetic-kernel.json. Related Frozen magnetic texture test — subsequent predeclared test that relaxes uniform polarization while leaving this kernel unchanged. Magnetic bivector master bridge — the same constrained field projector and fixed-envelope approximation. Master scalar exchange bridge — the same Gaussian closure, whose five-dimensional decomposition has an extra channel. Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination — explicit spinor moments and operator-class spectral theorem. Dimensional necessity from response — separates kernel-specific discrimination from general dimensional lower bounds.

title: Dimensional necessity from response
summary: A fixed-preparation unobserved-response rank theorem gives a conditional six-dimensional lower bound, while exact five-dimensional dynamics and averaging counterexamples identify what the existing constructions do not require.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A fixed-preparation unobserved-response rank theorem gives a conditional six-dimensional lower bound, while exact five-dimensional dynamics and averaging counterexamples identify what the existing constructions do not require. Scope and timing These counterfactual models test which mathematical structures require six spatial dimensions. They do not reassign the mass-formula electron index. No particular sphere or projective spatial geometry is assumed for the competing models. The corrected orbit has an exact five-dimensional realization Write the tested model on \mathbb R^d as q,p\in\mathbb R^d, C\in\mathfrak{so}(d), with a fixed rank-three nuclear projector P. Its potential depends on |q| and |Pq|; its other operations are matrix products, commutators, and the bivector q\wedge p. Let E:\mathbb R^5\to\mathbb R^6 include the first five coordinates, keeping all three visible coordinates. Set q_6=Eq_5,\qquad p_6=Ep_5,\qquad C_6=EC_5E^T. Since E^TE=I, P_6E=EP_5, and radii are unchanged, substitution into every equation gives F_6(\iota s)=\iota F_5(s), where \iota is the corresponding state inclusion. No force drives the omitted coordinate or its mixed source entries. Differentiation gives DF_6(\iota s)\iota=\iota DF_5(s) and the same relation for the tangent flow. This holds on both nuclear-profile branches and across their continuous join, away from the remaining full-radius singularity. The corrected orbit already lies in this subspace. Fresh five-dimensional integration, retaining the third visible perturbation, gives: h full-state closure error against restricted six-dimensional monodromy 0.0096, turning-point section 3.85\times10^{-13} 7.61\times10^{-12} 0.0128 5.64\times10^{-13} 2.39\times10^{-12} 0.100 2.47\times10^{-11} 6.01\times10^{-12} At h=0.0128 the growing multiplier is still 1.138471302788. At h=0.100, five dimensions give maximum modulus 8.54765518819; six dimensions give 9.18464295801 because an additional instability occurs in the third-unobserved-coordinate block. Thus identical invariant orbits do not imply identical responses to all six-dimensional disturbances. At the weak turning-point sample neither transverse block has a resolved exponential instability; neutral splitting does not prove nonlinear stability. This is stronger than a similar display: it preserves the interaction and the complete five-dimensional tangent dynamics. It does not reproduce an arbitrary six-dimensional preparation, every molecular configuration, or the CP3-constrained source model. The source here is a general skew matrix with a rank-four prepared spectrum, not an invertible complex structure. The active trajectory plane has dimension four and intersects the fixed visible three-plane in two dimensions. Their span has dimension five. Deleting another coordinate cannot preserve this particular full trajectory and that visible plane isometrically. This is a minimum for this embedding, not a theorem excluding every four-dimensional model of the visible curve. A sharp local lower-bound theorem Let x\in\mathbb R^3 be visible displacements and y\in\mathbb R^k the only eliminated spatial displacements. At a fixed preparation suppose E_2(x,y)=\tfrac12x^TAx+x^TBy+\tfrac12y^TKy,\qquad K>0. Eliminating y gives y_*=-K^{-1}B^Tx and E_{\rm eff,2}=\tfrac12x^T(A-R)x, \qquad R=BK^{-1}B^T. The factorization R=(BK^{-1/2})(BK^{-1/2})^T proves R\geq0,\qquad\operatorname{rank}R=\operatorname{rank}B\leq k. Consequently a rank-three unobserved-mediated response at one fixed preparation requires k\geq3, hence d=3+k\geq6. The bound is sharp: any positive semidefinite rank-r response has an r-coordinate realization by taking its positive-eigenvalue square root and K=I_r. To infer exactly six, rather than at least six, additionally require a minimal realization with no unobserved spectator coordinates. This is also a local theorem for nonlinear energies: if the unobserved equilibrium is unique nearby and its Hessian E_{yy}=K is positive definite, implicit differentiation gives the same Schur complement for the effective Hessian at that preparation. No globally quadratic energy is needed. Singular unobserved Hessians require a separate treatment. For a stationary linear response with fixed coordinate coupling B, unobserved inertia M, and damping \Gamma, the frequency-dependent mediated matrix is R(\omega)=B\left(K-\omega^2M-i\omega\Gamma\right)^{-1}B^T. Where the inverse exists, its complex rank is still at most k; positive semidefiniteness need not survive at nonzero frequency. Direct feedthrough must again be separated. This formula does not cover a periodically rotating coupling B(t): sidebands and period averaging can mix different directions, as the rank-one averaging counterexample demonstrates. An orbit's cycle-averaged susceptibility cannot simply be treated as the stationary matrix above. A response-state count also does not become a spatial count without identifying the eliminated variables as physical coordinates. The sign matters: minimizing a stable unobserved coordinate reduces the visible energy Hessian by R. Positive definiteness of the total visible Hessian neither implies nor requires rank-three R. A symmetry version of the theorem Suppose the fixed preparation is rotationally invariant, the unobserved linear displacements carry a representation U(R_0), and the mixed map obeys BU(R_0)=R_0B for every visible rotation R_0\in SO(3). Then \operatorname{im}B is an invariant subspace of the ordinary visible vector representation. Every nonzero vector has a rotation orbit spanning \mathbb R^3, so a nonzero B is surjective and k\geq3. This does not assume three unobserved directions at the start. It assumes that a nonzero mixed linear coupling exists at a symmetry-preserving state. Covariance of a family of oriented states is weaker and does not give this result. At k=3, orthogonal unobserved representations make the nonzero coupling a scalar times an orthogonal identification: BB^T commutes with every visible rotation and is therefore b^2I_3. Exact counterexamples to weaker proposed tests Direct visible response. For k=1 or 2, choose B=(e_1,\ldots,e_k) and positive diagonal K. The unobserved response has rank k, but adding the direct matrix D=I_3-R gives total response D+R=I_3. Total rank is not unobserved-channel rank. Averaging. With one unobserved coordinate and K=1, choose the prescribed rotating coupling b(t)=\left(\sqrt{2/3}\cos t,\sqrt{2/3}\sin t,1/\sqrt3\right)^T. Every b(t)b(t)^T has rank one, but its exact period average is I_3/3. This example includes a prescribed changing orientation; it does not claim that its orientation clock is generated for free by that one unobserved displacement. It disproves the inference from averaged rank to instantaneous unobserved rank. Additional representation variables in a comparison model. The same rank proof counts whatever variables were eliminated. Calling polarization or source-matrix entries spatial directions would change the theorem's physical meaning. Additional directions of the same physical manifold. Appending uncoupled coordinates preserves a model's responses on its original invariant subspace. A lower-bound argument alone cannot exclude such higher-dimensional extensions. These are limits of the inference, not alternative IDWT sectors. In IDWT all physical directions already belong to the one infinite manifold, and all particle sectors are nested submanifolds of it. Source-matrix components are representations of fields, not independently postulated spatial dimensions. The current cycle-averaged molecular Hessians do not yet isolate R under these conditions. Three molecular axes and petal counts therefore do not supply the missing rank-three premise. Verification and next discriminating target dimensional_necessity_checks.py checks exact rank and averaging identities, equivariance examples, random full-equation and derivative intertwinings, and optional fresh five-dimensional orbit integrations. The first full run completed 171 runtime checks; its evidence is dimensional-necessity.json. The productive next target is a physically derived, preparation-resolved response with its direct contribution separated, not another unperturbed petal image. A proof that its unobserved-mediated part is necessarily nonsingular would activate the lower-bound theorem. That nonsingularity is not yet proved. Work-block verification record The final regression run completed 63 finite diagnostic scripts, with no failures. It excluded the two original expensive shooting searches explicitly; it included the archived-state rejection audit and the fresh ten-candidate cross-method verification. The new corrector and full-orbit stability tools were exercised separately with the saved arguments and states described in the orbit note. The complete suite output is in diagnostic-suite-final.json. Three deliberate in-memory mutations were rejected: adding 10^{-4} to the five-dimensional velocity field failed equation intertwining; doubling one spinor-bivector operator failed the universal moment-norm polynomial; replacing reciprocal matrix evolution by identity failed the independent nonlinear response comparison. No mutated source was saved. The four new dimensional diagnostic scripts also passed under Python -O: their explicit runtime checks are not disabled with ordinary assertions. These finite numerical checks do not upgrade numerical recurrence to an interval existence proof or identify the physical electron from the conditional theorems. Related Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination — stronger operator-class no-go theorem and a CP3 counterexample developed during the same work block. Accurate cylindrical correction — supplies the corrected orbit and full-coordinate perturbation calculations. Five-depth orbit comparison — earlier kinematic compression, distinct from the same-equation dynamical inclusion proved here.

Question and measured input The now-rejected unobserved-localized multicentre control found a trigonal cycle-averaged force-balance radius with positive radial force slope F'(R_*)=0.0485176186. Writing a displacement as x, its uncoupled local equation is \ddot x=\sigma^2x with \sigma=\sqrt{F'(R_*)}=0.2202671528. This slope and every numerical threshold derived from it belong only to that control. They must not be transferred to the selected cylindrical bound-within/free-without kernel. Passive relaxation is a no-go Let y be one small plane-orientation coordinate with positive stiffness \kappa and reciprocal potential coupling bxy. The quadratic potential is V(x,y)=-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}x^2+bxy+\frac\kappa2y^2. Static elimination gives y=-bx/\kappa and V_{\rm eff}''=-\sigma^2-\frac{b^2}{\kappa}<0. Equivalently, the Hessian determinant is -\sigma^2\kappa-b^2<0. Thus a passive positive-energy orientation mode makes the relaxed curvature more negative and the autonomous coupled system retains a real exponential eigenvalue. Runtime checks cover twelve (\kappa,b) pairs and positive orientation inertias. The driven susceptibility \chi_N(\omega)=\frac1{\kappa-I\omega^2} does reverse sign above resonance. That fact alone is not a stability proof: the autonomous static Hessian remains indefinite. Treating the sign reversal as stabilization would confuse forced response with the spectrum of the closed electron--nucleus system. A plane coordinate alone is not a phase space The configuration space of rank-three planes in six dimensions is \operatorname{Gr}(3,6),\qquad \dim\operatorname{Gr}(3,6)=3(6-3)=9. The tangent variations of P_0=\operatorname{diag}(I_3,0) are \delta P=[K,P_0] for K\in\mathfrak{so}(6); the checked linear map has rank nine. Every antisymmetric bilinear form on a nine-dimensional real space is degenerate. Hence the plane coordinate by itself cannot carry a nondegenerate Hamiltonian/Berry two-form. A complete flexible-plane model must use at least the cotangent phase space T^*\operatorname{Gr}(3,6), of dimension eighteen, or supply additional field variables derived from the same master geometry. These are parameter counts for spatial orientation and angular momentum, not additional physical dimensions or separate sectors. Its conjugate momentum is not optional bookkeeping: it is where the plane stores angular momentum between electron encounters. A first-order precession equation written only for P_a would necessarily be a reduced/presymplectic law and must identify the degrees of freedom already eliminated. Gyroscopic stabilization is possible A rotating nuclear three-plane has at least a two-component transverse normal mode. The minimal conservative gyroscopic normal form is \ddot{\mathbf x}+2\Omega J\dot{\mathbf x}-\sigma^2\mathbf x=0, \qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. The antisymmetric term does no work, so E=\frac12|\dot{\mathbf x}|^2-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}|\mathbf x|^2 is conserved. The characteristic equation is (\lambda^2-\sigma^2)^2+4\Omega^2\lambda^2=0. All four roots are imaginary exactly when \boxed{|\Omega|\ge\sigma}. Below threshold there is a real part. Above threshold the two positive oscillation frequencies are \omega_\pm=|\Omega|\pm\sqrt{\Omega^2-\sigma^2}. This is spectral gyroscopic stabilization of an indefinite-energy equilibrium, not a positive potential minimum. Control-only comparison with the actual trigonal clock The completed signed L=3 orbit has clock \beta_3=0.2992305666. Numerically, \frac{\beta_3}{\sigma}=1.35849>1. Therefore a reciprocal plane rotation acting with gyroscopic rate equal to the existing orbit clock would lie above the local threshold. A deterministic 100-turn integration of this normal form remains bounded, with maximum norm amplification 3.26186 and energy error below 2.5\times10^{-15}. This comparison is only a scale observation inside the rejected unobserved-localized control; it is not evidence that the cylindrical molecular branch is stable. The full nuclear-plane equations must derive the coefficient 2\Omega J and identify its \Omega with the orbit clock. Substituting \Omega=\beta_3 by hand would merely hide the missing lock in the linearized equation. Rotating coordinates are not the mechanism There is a decisive adversarial control. Expressing an ordinary unstable lab equation \ddot q=\sigma^2q in coordinates rotating at rate \Omega produces \ddot x+2\Omega J\dot x-(\sigma^2+\Omega^2)x=0. The Coriolis-looking term comes with the centrifugal \Omega^2 contribution. Its spectrum retains real growth \sigma for every \Omega; changing frames does not stabilize anything. Runtime tests confirm this at four rates, including the trigonal clock. Consequently the stabilizing normal form of the preceding section requires a physical antisymmetric term without the compensating coordinate artifact. Candidates include a Berry-curvature term on the dynamical orientation space, a magnetic bivector coupling, or a spinning-rotor relative equilibrium whose energy--momentum Hessian supplies the needed block. Merely declaring that the nuclear plane co-rotates with the electron is insufficient. Next proof obligation Introduce an orientation frame U_a(t)\in SO(6), P_a=U_aP_0U_a^T, and a conjugate skew momentum \Pi_a. Derive both the torque and electron backreaction from one Hamiltonian. Linearization about the trigonal relative-periodic branch must then reproduce a transverse block of the form above with a calculated \Omega. Summary: The fixed nuclear three-plane and an invariant CP3 binding energy yield an exact conditional precession flow, with conserved misalignment and no automatically selected petal lock. Premises: follow the lower-dimensional nucleus A depth-three nucleus is lower-dimensional relative to a six-dimensional electron. The existing binding module represents its depth-three structure by a fixed projector P onto O in V6 = O direct-sum H. This is not a literal two-dimensional disk, nor an assumption that the nucleus is isotropic in all six directions. The bound/free module extends lower-depth modes cylindrically across their unstructured directions. It does not replace that extension with delta-function sheet support. This calculation uses the electron's physical spatial position, represented by the orthogonal complex structure J in SO(6)/U(3) = CP3. It does not substitute a stationary orbital or a coefficient ray for that point. Three premises are retained explicitly: a fixed nuclear frame, its SO(3) times SO(3) symmetry, and Hamiltonian evolution on the invariant symplectic CP3 orbit. Additional electron kinetic/field variables and nuclear motion are not included in this reduced flow. Flatness alone does not prove this reduction. From the existing energy to motion Write J=\begin{pmatrix}A&Q\\-Q^T&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad J^T=-J,\quad J^2=-I,\quad P=\operatorname{diag}(I_3,0). The binding module gives AQ + QC = 0 and s=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}A^2\in[0,1],\qquad V_N=V(s). Use the invariant matrix pairing ⟨X,Y⟩ = −tr(XY)/2. Fix the Hamiltonian sign and normalization by \dot J=\frac1{\mathcal I}[\nabla_J V,J],\qquad \mathcal I>0. Here the action scale I (written as mathcal I in equations) is a symplectic normalization, not a nuclear mechanical moment of inertia. It is not fitted or identified with a physical constant in this diagnostic. The natural coadjoint-orbit symplectic construction supplies this commutator form; see Karshon's Hamiltonian group-action notes. The following specialization and solution are derived here. Reversing the symplectic sign reverses precession, not the conservation or closure results. Direct variation gives \delta V=-V'(s)\operatorname{tr}(A\delta A),\qquad \nabla_J V=2V'(s)PJP. Consequently \dot J=\frac{2V'(s)}{\mathcal I}[PJP,J],\qquad \dot A=0,\quad\dot C=0,\quad \dot Q=\frac{2V'(s)}{\mathcal I}AQ. Both s and V(s) are conserved. V'(s) is therefore constant along each trajectory even when V is nonlinear. The exact solution is Q(t)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2V'(s_0)}{\mathcal I}A_0t\right)Q_0. Equivalently the full J is conjugated by diag(exp(2V'(s0)A0 t/I),I3). Antisymmetry, J² = −I, and the chosen CP3 component are preserved. This is actual motion on the proposed electron-sector manifold, not motion created by changing the observer coordinates. At s0 = 1, Q has rank one and AQ = 0, so J is also stationary even if the matrix exponential rotates its unused plane. If V'(s0) = 0, the motion is stationary at any s0. Any relative-position variables must be derived from that same spatial geometry, without counting the electron position twice. Nuclear response can subsequently be included reciprocally, without confusing an electric-polarization calculation with magnetic feedback. A spatial revolution within O does not itself rotate the projector onto O. Making P(t) rotate at an assigned orbital rate would therefore insert a drive, not derive synchronization from “flatness.” The nucleus-to-electron direction inside O may supply additional position-dependent invariants, but those must come from the source map and kernel. Equivalently the leading oscillator response has \chi(0)=2/\Delta,\qquad M_X=\hbar^2/(2\Delta),\qquad \Omega_X=\Delta/\hbar. This relates the response inertia and susceptibility instead of choosing them independently once the gap and operator normalization are specified. It introduces no phenomenological damping. This remains a finite effective contact model, not the full spatial electron–nucleus field equations. A solved collective rotation without the harmonic approximation Take a=.6, q=.8, hbar=2, Delta=4, and g²=25/32. These are dimensionless diagnostic choices. Let the O plane rotate at rate omega, and denote the source's rotating-frame eigenvalue by epsilon. Put d=Delta−epsilon and den=d²−(hbar omega)². The singlet occupation p0 and two consistency equations are p_0=\left[1+g^2\left( \frac{2q^2(d^2+(\hbar\omega)^2)}{\mathrm{den}^2} +\frac1{d^2}\right)\right]^{-1}, \epsilon=-g^2\left(\frac{2q^2d}{\mathrm{den}}+\frac1d\right),\qquad \omega=\frac{4g^2a p_0d}{\mathcal I_e\mathrm{den}}. These equations come respectively from the contact-state eigenproblem and the electron precession equation. Solving them gives approximately epsilon=−.41150923 and omega=.40069857. The rate is an output for these chosen parameters and preparation, not an observed atomic frequency or a fitted integer lock. For the same kappa and response frequency, the harmonic-response model has the low branch omega=.5. The difference is a concrete finite-response correction from the explicit bounded source; replacing the exact source with its linear susceptibility is not harmless in this example. The linear-stability result for the harmonic model does not automatically transfer to this full contact-state solution. Full source stability diagnostic An additional check linearizes the coupled projective equations on all six real CP3 tangent directions and eighteen real CP9 source directions. The two common phases are excluded. The analytic 24x24 Jacobian agrees with independent centered finite differences to approximately 3.5e-10. Its largest computed real eigenvalue is about 1.3e-8, associated with the near-zero sector; the computed nullities of the matrix and its square are three and four at threshold 1e-9. The decomposition can be checked state by state: \begin{array}{c|c} |++\rangle & \frac14+\frac14+\frac34=\frac54,\\ |+-\rangle & \frac14-\frac14-\frac34=-\frac34,\\ |-+\rangle & -\frac14+\frac14-\frac34=-\frac34,\\ |--\rangle & -\frac14-\frac14+\frac34=\frac14. \end{array} 72.2 Axial one-body generators are insufficient Trying to represent \widetilde G using only I, \qquad \sigma_z\otimes I, \qquad I\otimes\sigma_z has no solution. This initially made the coefficient 3/4 look like an independent two-frame bilinear that might have to be related to 3g_{66}. There is a cleaner exact formulation. Define the total axial generator of the diagonally locked spin frames, \boxed{ J_z =\frac12\left(\sigma_z\otimes I+I\otimes\sigma_z\right). } Since J_z^2 =\frac12\left(I+\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z\right), the orbit generator is exactly \boxed{ \widetilde G =-\frac34I +\frac12J_z +\frac32J_z^2. } The scalar -3I/4 is projectively invisible, so the projective generator is equivalently \boxed{ \widetilde G_{\rm proj} \sim \frac12J_z+\frac32J_z^2. } 74.1 Diagonal-spin basis Under the locked subgroup, (\mathbf2,\mathbf2) \downarrow_{Spin(3)_{\rm diag}} =\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf1. Use the standard coupled basis |1,1\rangle, \quad |1,0\rangle, \quad |1,-1\rangle, \quad |0,0\rangle. Then J_z =\operatorname{diag}(1,0,-1,0), while the orbit generator becomes \boxed{ \widetilde G =\operatorname{diag} \left( \frac54, -\frac34, \frac14, -\frac34 \right) } up to the ordering of the two zero-m states. The two m=0 states — the triplet |1,0\rangle and singlet |0,0\rangle — have exactly the same orbit-generator eigenvalue. Therefore the generator does not need the total-spin Casimir J^2 to distinguish the \mathbf3 and \mathbf1 sectors. Indeed, solving \widetilde G =aI+bJ_z+cJ_z^2+dJ^2 forces \boxed{d=0.} So the orbit generator depends only on the axial quantum number m, not separately on whether the state lies in the singlet or triplet representation. 74.2 Why this is stronger than the 3g_{66} interpretation The coefficient 3/4 in the product basis is not an invariantly separate physical coupling. It is partly a consequence of rewriting the quadratic axial operator J_z^2 back into the uncoupled tensor-product basis. Therefore the relation \frac34=3g_{66} must not be interpreted as evidence that three copies of the depth-six coupling are dynamically summed into an axial bilinear. Section 73 already showed that an actual isotropic three-axis sum produces the Heisenberg exchange operator instead. The more invariant statement is \boxed{ \widetilde G_{\rm proj} \sim \frac12J_z+\frac32J_z^2. } This shifts the proof obligation away from deriving an isolated coefficient 3g_{66} and toward deriving a linear-plus-quadratic function of the total locked axial generator. 74.3 Representation-theoretic origin of the four weights For m\in\{1,0,-1,0\}, the polynomial f(m) =-\frac34+\frac12m+\frac32m^2 gives \boxed{ \left( \frac54,-\frac34,\frac14,-\frac34 \right), } which is precisely the traceless orbit spectrum up to ordering. Passing to \Lambda^2\mathbf4 then produces the positive real rotation rates \boxed{ \frac12,\frac12,\frac32. } Thus the 1{:}1{:}3 vector spectrum can be viewed as descending from a quadratic axial polynomial on the diagonally locked (\mathbf2,\mathbf2) spinor. 74.4 What remains unexplained This reformulation removes a misleading candidate coupling identification, but it does not yet derive the polynomial coefficients \boxed{ \frac12,\qquad\frac32. } The existing amplitude/clock uniqueness theorem fixes an equivalent generator once its five premises are assumed. What has not yet been shown is that the scattering-selected locked electron must realize precisely that polynomial of J_z. The next useful test is therefore whether primitive projective closure, time-reversal/orientation reversal, and the required unit clock gap uniquely determine the lowest-degree polynomial f(J_z)=a+bJ_z+cJ_z^2 on the four locked spin states. If those physical constraints force b:c=1:3, the factor three will have been derived from the locked-spin spectrum without invoking g_{66} at all. summary: An explicit quadratic nuclear-plane kernel reproduces the precession flow, while inverse-rate reconstruction exposes nonuniqueness and the oriented source required for the full petal generator.

Summary: An explicit quadratic nuclear-plane kernel reproduces the precession flow, while inverse-rate reconstruction exposes nonuniqueness and the oriented source required for the full petal generator. What is being reverse engineered The target is first the fixed-nucleus sector precession just derived, and then the stronger target of the visualization's selected rotation generator. These are distinct inverse problems. Constructing a kernel that yields a specified motion proves compatibility, not independent physical selection. No measured masses, fields, or conventional atomic-orbital densities are used in the construction below. Retain J in SO(6)/U(3), the nuclear three-plane projector P, and the symplectic convention dot J = [grad V,J]/I of the precession note. The scale I is an action normalization. The common 6-vector frame and projectors are the binding module's geometric premises, not new coordinates added to the particle. 1. An explicit nuclear-plane interaction kernel Let u denote a nuclear configuration, P(u) its rank-three projector in the shared frame, and gamma(u) a scalar coefficient. Define \boxed{ K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J) =\frac{\gamma(u)}2\|P(u)JP(u)\|_F^2 =-\frac{\gamma(u)}2\operatorname{tr}(P(u)JP(u)J). } This is a smooth, quadratic orientation interaction. Under a simultaneous SO(6) rotation of both arguments it is invariant. It measures how much the electron complex structure rotates nuclear-plane directions within that plane instead of into its complement. It does not model the nucleus as a point or a thin charged sheet. For a normalized nuclear density with a common projector P(u)=P0, V_N(J)=\int\rho_N(u)K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J)d\mu_N(u) =\bar\gamma s(J;P_0),\qquad \bar\gamma=\int\rho_N(u)\gamma(u)d\mu_N(u). It gives precisely the previous V(s)=kappa s with kappa=mean gamma. Thus the previously unspecified orientation kernel now has an explicit candidate. For varying P(u), the integral remains well defined but generally does not collapse to one scalar times s; its anisotropy must be retained. The coefficients, density, and identification of the shared frames are still physical inputs. This kernel is the orientation channel only. It does not supply radial Coulomb binding, spatial falloff, retardation, a field propagator, or a definition of physical separation on the sector. Adding a J-independent term leaves the reduced J flow unchanged, but cannot be advertised as solving the separate relative-position dynamics. 2. Reciprocity is available from the same energy For fixed u and the skew pairing −tr(XY)/2, \nabla_J K=2\gamma PJP. For projector variations, with the ordinary symmetric trace pairing, \delta_P K=\operatorname{tr}(G_P\delta P),\qquad G_P=-\gamma JPJ. The latter expression is an ambient gradient restricted to allowed tangent variations delta P = [B,P], B skew; it is not by itself a nuclear velocity. Simultaneous rotation of both arguments gives \delta_J K\big|_{\delta J=[B,J]} +\delta_P K\big|_{\delta P=[B,P]}=0. Hence a joint dynamical model can use this single interaction to obtain reciprocal orientational forces. A nuclear kinetic or symplectic action is still needed for the response equation; no mechanical inertia or magnetic susceptibility is silently supplied by this identity. 3. Invert an entire precession-rate function For 0<s<1 the previous flow gives the signed rate \omega_{\rm p}(s)=\frac{2V'(s)\sqrt{s}}{\mathcal I}. Therefore a prescribed rate function determines the reduced potential up to a constant on an interval: \boxed{ V(s)=C+\frac{\mathcal I}{2} \int^s\frac{\omega_{\rm p}(v)}{\sqrt v}\,dv. } For example, omega_p(s)=a sqrt(s)+b s^(3/2) gives V(s)=C+I a s/2+I b s²/4. Substituting s(J;P(u)) into this expression gives a higher-order orientation-kernel candidate, for a fixed common plane. A single trajectory at conserved s0 gives much less information: it fixes only V'(s0)=I omega_p(s0)/(2 sqrt(s0)). Adding lambda(s−s0)² changes the kernel away from that trajectory without changing its motion. Likewise, any delta K with zero nuclear marginal leaves V unchanged. Thus neither one precessing orbit nor an entire reduced V identifies a unique microscopic kernel. 4. A nonzero universal rate has a regularity cost Demanding omega_p(s)=omega0 at every 0<s<1 gives V(s)=C+\mathcal I\omega_0\sqrt{s}. This is not smooth at the aligned configuration. Along the smooth signed-coordinate curve A=epsilon K, Q=diag(sqrt(1−epsilon²), sqrt(1−epsilon²),1), C=−epsilon K, it becomes proportional to |epsilon|. The two directional derivatives disagree at zero. This is a property of the inverse construction, not a prohibition on precession. A smooth alternative is V_\eta(s)=\mathcal I\omega_0(\sqrt{s+\eta^2}-\eta),\qquad \omega_{{\rm p},\eta}(s)=\omega_0\sqrt{\frac{s}{s+\eta^2}},\quad\eta>0. It approaches the desired rate away from alignment and tends to zero near alignment. Eta is an additional model parameter, not a derived nuclear width and not the visualization's imbalance parameter. Matching one selected s0 to an orbital clock instead only calibrates a coefficient; it does not establish a dynamically attracting frequency lock. 5. Reverse engineering the full chosen rotation For a prescribed skew generator B_star with units of inverse time, the linear potential V_{\rm target}(J)=\mathcal I\langle B_\star,J\rangle =-\frac{\mathcal I}{2}\operatorname{tr}(B_\star J) gives exactly dot J=[B_star,J] and J(t)=exp(t B_star)J0 exp(−t B_star). Choose the 1:1:3 vector-plane generator corresponding to the existing magnetic construction and this supplies its base rotation. Its specified spin/section lift can then be tested against the existing coefficient flow; the physical observer map and preparation are still required for petals. An inverse source kernel is consequently K_{\rm drive}(u,J)=\mathcal I\langle B(u),J\rangle,\qquad \int\rho_N(u)B(u)d\mu_N(u)=B_\star. This identifies the source tensor that would be needed, rather than deriving that tensor from a scalar nuclear density. It is a separate candidate from the quadratic plane kernel; summing them generally changes the target flow. No claim is made that the sum preserves the desired petals automatically. 6. What a bare nuclear plane can and cannot select A kernel depending only on the unoriented plane P and J must respect the stabilizer SO(3)_O times SO(3)_H. No nonzero fixed skew matrix B_star commutes with this whole group: each diagonal skew 3x3 block must commute with all SO(3) rotations and is therefore zero; the off-diagonal block cannot be invariant under independent rotations of O and H either. Thus a bare plane cannot select that particular linear drive. This does not contradict the quadratic kernel's precession: its effective generator 2 mean(gamma) PJP/I also depends on the electron's prepared J. The result does not exclude a joint symmetry-breaking electron–nucleus solution. It says that an oriented nuclear current, a relational electron–nucleus tensor, or another dynamically selected structure must supply the missing orientation if the full fixed generator is to follow from the source. Flatness already provides the split; it does not provide every axis and relative rotation rate inside that split. Status and next test We have constructed a smooth quadratic inverse kernel, derived both orientation variations, and inverted general precession-rate functions. We have also identified an exact linear source kernel for the stronger target and the extra source information it requires. None is a unique first-principles interaction or a completed electron–nucleus binding model. Next, use the actual projected nuclear/electron currents to calculate the allowed source tensors and their energy cost. Test whether the quadratic orientation channel and a selected linear drive emerge together with the same orbital clock, rather than fitting their sum to the displayed curve.
