Its radial force derivative is +0.0485176, so it is unstable rather than restoring. For the orbit-aligned tetrahedral curve with central and ligand effective charges 0.1, no noncollision root occurs on the tested ranges R\in[0.2,0.95] and R\in[1.05,4]. Thus the alternative embedded-point 1/r kernel does not turn the available conservation geometry into a stable molecule. Conservation and equivalence derive the angles, but a derived lower-depth interaction/response kernel—or a materially retuned electron trajectory—is still required for stable reciprocal closure. Flexible nuclear three-planes Let a nucleus carry a rank-three orthoprojector P_a in the electron's six-coordinate space. A minimal anisotropic distance family is d_{\eta,P}^2=\Delta q^T\bigl(P+\eta(I-P)\bigr)\Delta q. The unobserved-localized point-kernel control is \eta=1, while bound-within/free-without is the cylindrical limit \eta=0. Allowing P to relax instantaneously with no orientation cost does not retain an anisotropic force. A rank-three plane in six dimensions can always be chosen either to contain the one separation vector \Delta q or to lie wholly perpendicular to it. Therefore \min_{\operatorname{rank}P=3}d_{\eta,P}^2 =\min(1,\eta)|\Delta q|^2. For \eta>0 the relaxed interaction is only a constant rescaling of 1/|\Delta q|. In the selected cylindrical limit \eta=0, the minimum is zero and the ideal Coulomb kernel becomes singular: a freely reorienting plane can turn until it intersects the electron. Complete cost-free flexibility is therefore unusable in either case. Finite inertia or stiffness is essential. The physically useful interpretation of flexibility must be finite response. The nuclear plane needs rotational inertia, an orientation stiffness relative to its lower-depth structure, or a nonzero response time. It can then lag the electron, store angular momentum, and return it through backreaction. This is the same kind of dynamical susceptibility already isolated by the response modules, now applied to molecular closure. A fixed projector and an instantaneously minimized projector are the two controls on either side of that finite-response problem. Correct next solve: reciprocal closure The nuclei must now be dynamical variables rather than fixed scenery. For a candidate period T, solve simultaneously for electron and nuclear initial data, the response source, and the nuclear scale, subject to X(T)=gX(0),\qquad P(T)=gP(0), where g is the appropriate trigonal or tetrahedral permutation-rotation, together with energy and total bivector conservation. Equivalently, in a Born--Oppenheimer reduction require zero cycle-averaged force on every nucleus, \frac1T\int_0^T F_a(t)\,dt=0. This formulation tests the proposed spatial mechanism: near-straight electron motion, deflection at the lower-depth nuclear structures, and a molecular shape selected partly by closure and conservation in six dimensions. It also makes the proposal falsifiable: if no stable reciprocal periodic branch exists for the derived kernel, geometrical availability alone is insufficient. Summary: A finite-inertia rank-three nuclear plane coupled reciprocally to a 6D electron preserves its projector constraints, energy, visible momentum, and combined rotational charge while undergoing nontrivial orientation response. Purpose The plane-response audit showed that a nuclear three-plane needs conjugate momentum. This note constructs that missing finite-inertia system before any molecular periodic orbit is sought. It is a consistency model for reciprocal orientation dynamics, not a microscopic identification of the nuclear kernel. Hamiltonian variables and interaction Let q,p\in\mathbb R^6 describe the electron, let R,P_R\in\mathbb R^3 describe the lower-depth nuclear centre, and let P^T=P,\qquad P^2=P,\qquad\operatorname{tr}P=3 be its oriented three-plane. A skew matrix \Omega\in\mathfrak{so}(6) is the plane's angular velocity and carries kinetic energy I\langle\Omega,\Omega\rangle/2, with \langle A,B\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(AB)/2. For the selected bound-within/free-without ontology use the cylindrical distance s=d^TPd, \qquad d=q-(R,0), and V=-Zs^{-1/2}. Coordinates perpendicular to the nuclear plane do not increase separation from its cylindrical support. The numerical consistency run uses dimensionless M_N=12, I=2.3, and Z=0.7. These values are not fitted to an atom. An earlier \eta=0.35 interpolation gave the nucleus finite unobserved localization and has been removed as inconsistent with this ontology. Reciprocal equations Write G=\partial V/\partial P. Variation under \delta P=[K,P] fixes the plane equations \dot P=[\Omega,P], \qquad I\dot\Omega=2[P,G]. The electron receives -\nabla_qV. The three-coordinate nuclear centre receives the opposite visible component +(\nabla_qV)_{1:3}. This respects the depth mismatch: the nucleus is not assigned unobserved translational momentum. The torque factor and sign are fixed by differentiating the common energy. They are also required for the visible rotational Noether charge \mathcal J_O =q_O\wedge p_O+R\wedge P_R-I\Omega_{OO} to be conserved. The minus sign reflects the angular-velocity convention in \dot P=[\Omega,P]. A nonlinear integration over 18 model time units gives: quantity maximum error total energy 2.57\times10^{-10} projector idempotence 1.01\times10^{-11} visible total momentum 2.05\times10^{-15} visible rotational charge 5.12\times10^{-11} Symmetry of P, skewness of \Omega, and \operatorname{tr}P=3 remain preserved. The final projector differs from its initial value by more than 0.1 in norm, so conservation is not a consequence of a frozen plane. What this changes The project now has an energy-conserving mechanism by which a flexible lower-depth nucleus can store orientation momentum and return it to a 6D electron. This closes the phase-space consistency gap identified in the finite-response note. It does not yet establish gyroscopic stabilization of the trigonal saddle. The next calculation must duplicate this rotor for all symmetry-related nuclei, regularize the supported-plane Coulomb singularity using the derived finite nuclear profile, and compute the full monodromy matrix. Summary: A scalar geometric potential reproduces the orbit generator after compression but necessarily leaks from the holomorphic sector, while frame changes alone do not establish physical motion. Physical evolution versus a moving description The precession mechanism predates this diagnostic. In the visualization history, ce71f75 explicitly assigns precession rates and locks them to the orbital frequency; 1f8a54a replaces that recipe with Hamiltonian exchange and clock evolution, and c6d6bcf–4701c3a place both in one representation action. This note tests a possible physical source for that existing flow. It does not introduce precession for the first time, nor show that a new scalar potential is necessary to obtain petals. The Coulomb-binding-plus-precession construction remains the baseline; the compression below is an inverse diagnostic, not its derived electron–nucleus force law. The selected-line current construction added ℏνĜ as a candidate physical drive. It did not establish whether the master action supplies this term relative to the nucleus and electromagnetic observer. Conversely, evolving c by e^{-iνGt} while keeping the physical D fixed generally gives a changing measurement. Transforming that active evolution to a stationary state makes D time-dependent; it does not remove the signal. Thus the ability to remove G by a time-dependent basis change is not a no-motion theorem. The physical test is relative evolution of electron, nuclear frame, and probe. The action must specify all three. A transformed coordinate current cannot be inserted into an inertial radiation formula while leaving the observer and electromagnetic field untransformed. A scalar potential can reproduce the compressed generator Consider the candidate spinor line carrying H⁰(CP3,O(L)), with its unit-volume FS measure and orthogonal holomorphic projector P_L. This is a condition on the physical orbit, not a choice of an orbital quantum number. Conservative evolution preserves s_x and does not relax an arbitrary initial preparation onto that orbit. 3. A full projective recurrence therefore requires both ΩT and νT to be integer multiples of 2π. If Ω/ν = p/q in lowest positive integer terms, its period is 2πq/ν. Its selected representation gives the correct weights exactly; the problem is not to replace those weights with fitted frequencies. The projected action must select and preserve that representation and prepared orbit, fix the nuclear frame, and control the relative phases not visible in the readout. summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation.

Summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation. Why the first combination failed The completed petal Hamiltonian was originally written about a fixed nuclear origin. Adding moving nuclei without changing that source makes its magnetic completion depend on the absolute electron coordinate and destroys visible translation invariance. A failed momentum-derivative check exposed this before the model was used for shooting. The correction is to define the source coupling using the electron--central- nucleus relative coordinate s=q-(R_0,0). The completed kinetic term is then H_e=\frac1{2m_e}|p-m_e\lambda Cs|^2 +\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I_C}. The central nucleus receives the opposite visible component of the source force. It receives no unobserved translational momentum because it remains a depth-three object. Full diagnostic Hamiltonian For nuclear centres R_a\in\mathbb R^3, momenta P_a, rank-three planes \Pi_a, and skew plane velocities \Omega_a, use H=H_e+\sum_a\frac{|P_a|^2}{2M_a} +\sum_a\frac{I_a}{2}\langle\Omega_a,\Omega_a\rangle +\sum_a V_a\bigl(|\Pi_a(q-(R_a,0))|\bigr) +\sum_{a<b}\frac{Z_aZ_b}{|R_a-R_b|}. Here V_a is the finite uniform supported-space profile of the preceding note, extended cylindrically through unsupported coordinates. The source coadjoint equation uses s\wedge p and s\wedge Cs, not q\wedge p about an external origin. Each plane obeys \dot\Pi_a=[\Omega_a,\Pi_a], \qquad I_a\dot\Omega_a=2[\Pi_a,\partial_{\Pi_a}V_a]. Every force and torque is obtained from this one energy. The executable originally specialized the equations to m_e=1 while exposing a configurable mass. The September 7 audit restores the factors of m_e in the completed square, velocity, magnetic force, and source gradient; the reported unit-mass run is unchanged. Nuclear mutual repulsion is a separately assumed centre-charge interaction here. It is not the mutual interaction of overlapping finite cylindrical charge profiles, particularly when their support planes differ. The full skew rotor also permits angular momentum in the plane stabilizer; a pure Grassmannian plane rotor requires horizontal initial angular velocity or an explicit reduction. Conserved quantities The visible total momentum is \mathcal P_O=p_O+\sum_aP_a. The visible rotational charge is \mathcal J_O=q_O\wedge p_O+C_{OO} +\sum_aR_a\wedge P_a-\sum_a I_a(\Omega_a)_{OO}. Ten random states independently check the differential conservation of H, \mathcal P_O, and \mathcal J_O. A nonlinear example contains one central cylinder plus three trigonal ligand cylinders with moving centres, four flexible planes, and a nonzero electron angular source. Over eight model time units its maximum errors are: quantity maximum error energy 7.93\times10^{-8} visible momentum 3.59\times10^{-15} visible rotational charge 2.87\times10^{-10} projector idempotence 2.18\times10^{-11} The differential energy residual is below 8.9\times10^{-10}. Thus the finite profile, moving lower-depth centres, plane rotors, and completed source are mutually compatible at the Hamiltonian level. Remaining periodic-orbit problem This calculation establishes the system to shoot; it does not claim that the arbitrary nonlinear example is molecularly periodic. The next solve should start from the exact trigonal orbit and the restoring finite-profile radius, fix centre-of-mass and global-rotation gauge directions, and solve a relative-periodic boundary condition. The monodromy calculation must retain electron, source, nuclear-centre, and plane-rotor perturbations. Stable radial force balance alone is not sufficient. The uniform-ball nuclear profile and dimensionless masses, charges, and inertias remain diagnostic inputs. A successful branch would establish existence within that controlled model, not yet derive those inputs from V2. Reproduction reciprocal_cylindrical_molecule_checks.py checks the relative-source energy gradient, visible translation and rotation charges, nonlinear integration, all four plane constraints, and a nonzero source preparation. Related Finite cylindrical nuclear profile — prerequisite: supplies the finite encounter law and restoring candidate radii. Nuclear-plane rotor — prerequisite: supplies the finite-inertia projector dynamics and torque normalization. Cylindrical petal continuation — begins fixed-centre periodic continuation and diagnoses the soft shooting directions.

title: Ring section embedding
summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector. What can be unified algebraically The demo uses a separate ring coefficient generator ν diag(0,−1,0), with initial state (A,B/√2,B/√2), and a constant-radius readout whose angle is the relative clock phase. Its projective orbit is not generated by the one-dimensional H⁰(O(0)) space. There is nevertheless a simple embedding in the same section spaces used for the petalled cases. Denote the section degree by k here, keeping it distinct from the demo's ring label L = 0. For every k ≥ 2 choose normalized monomials proportional to s_0=Z_1Z_2Z_4^{k-2},\qquad s_-=Z_3Z_4^{k-1},\qquad s_r=Z_4^k. They are distinct sections of O(k). Under the same generator Ĝ_k = N₁−N₂−N₃ their weights are exactly (0,−1,0). Hence \Phi(t)=A s_0+\frac B{\sqrt2}e^{i\nu t}s_- +\frac B{\sqrt2}s_r has precisely the demo's three-state coefficient evolution and returns after 2π/ν. The prescribed ring readout Γ_x+iΓ_y = R times the normalized clock coherence is Re^{iνt}. This is an actual time-dependent coefficient orbit in a selected section subspace, not a stationary field substituted for the ring. The selected spinor-line construction lifts this field into Σ⊗O(k+2), just as it lifts the degree-k petalled orbit. At k = 2, the 10-dimensional section space therefore contains both the ring's three-state generator and the four-state generator used for four petals. No new generator weights or electric charge have been fitted to obtain this fact. What this does not unify This is not a degree-zero construction. The earlier dimension obstruction for H⁰(O(0)) remains intact, and the k ≥ 2 ring cannot be declared the physical L = 0 atomic state without a separate identification. It shows that the generator algebra need not require an unrelated carrier space; it does not derive which carrier the physical circular state occupies. The ring and petalled prescriptions select different mode subspaces and readout rules. An algebraic embedding alone does not derive a single apparatus response that selects between those rules, a nuclear preparation mechanism, energies, or transition strengths. In particular, the petal-count rule 2k applies to the prepared extremal exchange construction, not to every trajectory in O(k). Degree alone does not force a petalled outline. The smooth geometric clock dipole from the probe calculation also exists here, but it already gives circular dipole signals for some petalled preparations. It cannot by itself distinguish those detector images. Research consequence A single positive-degree field sector may support multiple coefficient-orbit families under the same Killing action. This supplies a concrete candidate bridge for the ring, with no change to the displayed petals or their code. The remaining problem is physical family selection and the degree/flux interpretation, not merely finding three suitable abstract frequencies. The scalar effective-drive route also applies algebraically in this space, but inherits the omitted-mode leakage and locking corrections audited in the companion note. The embedding is not a stability proof. Reproduction orbit_drive_origin_checks.py checks the three weights, normalized evolution, clock readout, and full recurrence for k = 2, 3, 4, while retaining the one-dimensional degree-zero check. title: Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination
summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class. Why this comparison matters The six-dimensional selection uses one pure normalized irreducible spinor, a real skew source, positive quadratic source energy, and linear spinor-bivector coupling. Here the same construction is performed for a five-dimensional Euclidean carrier. No inherited V1 spatial geometry is assigned to that carrier. An irreducible Spin(5) spinor has four complex components, as does either irreducible half-spin representation of Spin(6). The general dimensions are 2^n for Spin(2n+1) and 2^{n-1} for each half-spin of Spin(2n). See Woit's representation construction. The explicit five-dimensional representation and its quaternionic structure are also discussed in Niedzialomski's five-dimensional spinor analysis. The following energy and spectrum calculations are explicit local derivations, not claims taken from those references. Exact five-dimensional construction Using Pauli matrices, take the Hermitian Clifford generators \gamma=(\sigma_1\otimes I,\sigma_2\otimes I, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_1,\sigma_3\otimes\sigma_2, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_3). They obey \{\gamma_a,\gamma_b\}=2\delta_{ab}I_4. For z^\dagger z=1, define H_{ab}=-i\gamma_a\gamma_b,\quad b_{ab}=z^\dagger H_{ab}z,\quad n_a=z^\dagger\gamma_a z, \quad S(b)=\sum_{a<b}b_{ab}H_{ab}. Let J be the skew matrix with upper entries b_{ab}, with \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2=\sum b_{ab}^2. Direct Clifford calculation gives |n|^2=1,\qquad \|J\|^2=2,\qquad J^2=-I_5+nn^T,\qquad Jn=0. Thus the source has two unit rotation planes and one null axis. It is not an invertible complex structure on an odd-dimensional vector space. Furthermore S(b)z=2z,\qquad zz^\dagger=\frac{S(b)^2}{8}+\frac{S(b)}4. The last identity reconstructs the ray from the bivector, so no ray degree is lost. These identities are verified as polynomials in eight independent real spinor components, without assuming normalization numerically. For an initially unrestricted skew B, take E(B,z)=\mu\|B\|^2-g\langle B,J(z)\rangle, \qquad \mu,g>0. With \rho=g/(2\mu), completion gives E(B,z)=\mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2-\frac{g^2}{2\mu}. All normalized rays minimize at B=\rho J(z), and the injective reconstruction makes their minimum family CP3. This does not require assuming CP3 as the carrier's spatial base. It is the collective polarization/source family of this specified five-dimensional model. The Berry term i\hbar z^\dagger\dot z is the same nonzero projective symplectic structure as in the six-dimensional construction. Adding M\|\dot B\|^2/2 gives reciprocal dynamics and the exact conserved bound \mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2+\frac{\|\Pi\|^2}{2M} =E_{\rm total}-E_{\min}. This controls departure from the minimum family, not spatial localization or an electron-nucleus orbit. The ten-component source-space Hessian after ground-ray elimination has six flat directions and four positive normal directions 2\mu; these are matrix-space counts, not extra spatial axes. The Hessian statement also follows analytically: minimizing the completed square over rays gives E_{\rm eff}(B)-E_{\min}=\mu\,operatorname{dist} (B,\rho J(\mathrm{CP}^3))^2. In a tubular neighborhood of this smooth embedded orbit, the squared-distance Hessian is twice the normal projector. The numerical Hessian is an independent finite-difference check of that result. What differs from six dimensions At the selected source, the five-dimensional spinor Hamiltonian has \operatorname{spec}h_5(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-2,0,0,2), whereas the six-dimensional chiral model has \operatorname{spec}h_6(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-3,1,1,1). Their gaps above the selected ray are respectively (2,2,4)g\rho and (4,4,4)g\rho. Thus “CP3 minima, a gap, a Berry term, and conservative confinement” do not distinguish them, while the full gap multiplicity does. Their induced source kinetic metrics also differ. For Fubini–Study unit horizontal tangents at z=(1,0,0,0), the five-dimensional squared bivector derivative has weights (4,4,4,4,8,8); the six-dimensional construction has weight 8 in all six directions. The five-dimensional CP3 family is not being claimed to have the same induced metric or every same response. A genuine no-go theorem for the five-dimensional competitor Every real skew 5\times5 source is orthogonally reducible to two rotation blocks and a zero direction. The corresponding irreducible spinor Hamiltonian has eigenvalues \{\alpha+\beta,\alpha-\beta,-\alpha+\beta,-\alpha-\beta\}, up to an overall scalar shift and coupling scale. Order the positive block strengths \alpha\geq\beta\geq0. If its ground state is nondegenerate, the three gaps are \Delta_1=2\beta,\qquad\Delta_2=2\alpha, \qquad\Delta_3=2(\alpha+\beta)=\Delta_1+\Delta_2. Consequently three equal positive gaps are impossible for any source in this operator class, not just for the selected minimum or a sampled parameter range. Equivalently, the ordered eigenvalues always obey \lambda_1+\lambda_4=\lambda_2+\lambda_3. This is robust: a target with eigenvalues (E_0,E_0+\Delta,E_0+\Delta, E_0+\Delta), \Delta>0, has operator-norm distance at least \Delta/4 from every scalar-plus-five-dimensional-bivector Hamiltonian, even allowing arbitrary spinor bases. If the norm error is \epsilon, each ordered eigenvalue differs by at most \epsilon. The two pair sums of the target differ by \Delta, so the competitor's equality forces \Delta\leq4\epsilon. The bound is attained: for target \operatorname{diag}(-3,1,1,1), the aligned canonical bivector spectrum (-2,0,0,2) is at distance one. Conditional exact-six theorem Assume all of the following are independently justified: The relevant polarization is one fundamental complex spatial spin module, or one irreducible half-spin module in even dimensions, of a Euclidean d-dimensional carrier. It has exactly four complex components. This means the module supplied by the spatial Clifford construction, not an arbitrary higher-spin representation, multiplicity space, or four-level internal system. Its source Hamiltonian is linear in spatial bivectors, apart from a scalar shift; no extra vector or higher-degree operator is present. A selected ray has one nondegenerate energy and three exactly equal higher energies separated by a nonzero gap. The spin-representation dimension formula restricts d to five or six. The spectral sum rule excludes five. Within these premises, d=6. Unlike a theorem that assumes chirality from the start, this argument uses the spectrum to discriminate the two four-component irreducible spinors. It does not establish that an actual electron satisfies premises 1–3. In the existing archive the six-dimensional operator produces this spectrum, but deriving a physical requirement for it independently of that operator remains necessary to avoid circular identification. Frozen-source gaps versus reciprocal response frequencies The preceding spectra hold the source fixed during a spinor variation. They are not the normal frequencies of the entire coupled source-spinor system. The flat minimum family supplies six zero modes in that larger system. This distinction can be followed through exactly. For one complex tangent u, choose the corresponding normalized complex source displacement b. If the squared moment-map derivative weight is w, then \Delta=g^2w/(4\mu) and the linearized equations are M\ddot b=-2\mu b+g\sqrt w\,u, \qquad i\hbar\dot u=\Delta u-\frac{g\sqrt w}{2}b. With time dependence e^{-i\omega t} the characteristic polynomial is \omega\left(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar\right)=0. Apart from the zero mode, the positive frequency pair is \omega_{\rm high,low} =\frac{\sqrt{\Delta^2+8\mu\hbar^2/M}\ \mathord{\pm}\ \Delta}{2\hbar}. In particular \omega_{\rm high}-\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{\Delta}{\hbar}, \qquad\omega_{\rm high}\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{2\mu}{M}. Thus reciprocal source motion changes the frequencies but preserves the gap as a pair separation in this quadratic, isotropic-inertia model. Five dimensions have two identical pairs and one different pair; six dimensions have three identical pairs. The remaining source-normal modes have frequency \sqrt{2\mu/M}, with multiplicity four and nine respectively. These are additional source degrees of freedom, not spatial dimensions. At \mu=1.3,g=0.7,M=0.4,\hbar=2, the five-dimensional pairs are (2.45701979,2.64548133) twice and (2.36800433,2.74492741) once. Six dimensions give the latter pair three times. Direct full nonlinear projective evolution matches the analytic tangent response: reducing perturbations from 10^{-4} to 10^{-5} reduces the scaled prediction error by a factor of ten in both models. This is a calculable response target, not a demonstrated experimental access route. Other source inertias, extra couplings, damping, nuclear interaction, and detector selection require their own calculation. For the explicitly specified drive “force on the source tangent” and readout “the same source displacement,” the complex-helicity susceptibility is \chi_b(\omega)=\frac{\Delta-\hbar\omega} {\omega(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar)}. Its nonzero mode poles have nonvanishing numerators, so they are not dark to this input/output pair. The full linear-system resolvent reproduces this formula at fifteen off-resonant probes in each dimension to below 1.8\times10^{-15}. The frozen-source value \omega=\Delta/\hbar is an antiresonance of this helicity response, not a coupled-system pole. These are ideal model controls and observations; their laboratory access has not been derived. Operator-class escape route: why the hypotheses matter The same five-dimensional matrices obey S(b)+\sum_a n_a\gamma_a=4zz^\dagger-I_4. Allowing an additional vector source therefore reproduces the singlet-triplet operator exactly in five dimensions. The no-go theorem is a theorem about linear bivector coupling, not arbitrary five-dimensional interactions. Scalar nonlinearities in the bivector operator could also alter its spectrum. A microscopic derivation must justify the allowed operator class before this discriminator can decide spatial dimension. None of these source-polarization energy gaps have yet been identified with measured atomic excitation energies. Their multiplicities should not be relabelled p/d/f shell counts. Verification spin5_selection_checks.py checks universal Clifford polynomial identities, moment-map injectivity, the completed-square minimum, all six projective tangent directions, the selected spectrum, normal Hessian, induced metric, Berry curvature, and reciprocal conservation. The first run completed 501 checks. Later spectral-distance and vector-channel checks extend that run; saved reports retain their separate counts. spinor_response_poles_checks.py checks the reciprocal frequency calculation against the full variational matrix and nonlinear evolution. Evidence: extended selection checks and reciprocal response checks. The forced-response extension completes 93 runtime checks, including source-pole observability. Chiral CP3 selection — six-dimensional construction compared under the same type of source energy. Dimensional necessity from response — independent rank theorem and dynamical five-dimensional competitor.

What is established The finite response model has a two-electron collective rotating family. Both occupied modes drive the same source, and that source acts back on both. The second electron cannot be omitted while retaining this solution. This is a positive existence result in a specified reciprocal model, not two noninteracting copies of the one-electron calculation. Electron depth remains six. The four complex components below are the existing chiral carrier, not four spatial dimensions. Nor do the four available carrier modes set atomic shell capacities: spatial and other degrees of freedom have not been supplied in this truncation. Shared variational system Let U be a complex 4 by 2 occupied frame with U†U=I2. Its two columns define a normalized antisymmetric Slater state. Put D=UU†, so D²=D and tr D=2. Apply the existing linear moment map to D and take its mixed block Q. Thus Q is the sum of the two individual mixed blocks; D is a number-density matrix, not a trace-one single-electron state. For the normalized ten-state contact-source vector n, use the existing response X=2 Re(n0* n_exc), arranged as a 3 by 3 matrix. The energy is E(U,n)=\Delta\|n_{\rm exc}\|^2-g\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}Q_{ij}. Varying this energy with the occupied-state and source Berry terms gives i\hbar\dot U=h_e(X)U,\qquad i\hbar\dot n=h_N(Q)n, \qquad h_e(X)=g\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}\sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j. The source Hamiltonian has excited diagonal Delta and singlet-to-excited matrix entries -g Qij. The interaction appears once in the joint energy, not once in each subsystem energy followed by double counting. Hermiticity preserves U†U and n†n. Reciprocity conserves E. This is a variational Slater-times-source product-state model. It includes shared-source feedback but not unrestricted electron-source entanglement, general electron correlation, or direct spatial electron-electron repulsion. Explicit collective family For 0<a<1, define q=sqrt(1-a²), c=sqrt((1+a)/2), s=sqrt((1-a)/2), u_1=(0,c,-s,0)^T,\qquad u_2=(c,0,0,s)^T. These vectors are orthonormal and their total Q is diag(0,2q,0). With d=Delta-epsilon and b=d²-(hbar omega)², solve p_0=\left[1+4g^2q^2\frac{d^2+(\hbar\omega)^2}{b^2}\right]^{-1}, \qquad \epsilon=-\frac{4g^2q^2d}{b},\qquad \omega=\frac{4g^2a p_0 d}{(\hbar/2)b}. The source initial state is proportional to (1, g[(Delta-epsilon)I9-i hbar omega KN_exc]^{-1}vec Q). It is an eigenvector of hN-i hbar omega KN with eigenvalue epsilon. The initial occupied subspace is invariant under he-hbar omega Ze; call its 2 by 2 restriction Lambda. Then U(t)=e^{-i\omega t Z_e}U(0)e^{-it\Lambda/\hbar},\qquad n(t)=e^{-i\epsilon t/\hbar}e^{\omega t K_N}n(0) solve the coupled equations. These are relative equilibria, not imposed forcing of a frozen source. The previous one-electron a=0.6 example has rate 0.4006985724 with the same Delta, g, and hbar. The pair changes both total preparation and source response; this is not a universal electron-count scaling law. Physical reading and remaining test U and U R for any unitary 2 by 2 matrix R describe the same occupied projector and the same Slater ray. Individual occupied-column paths are therefore not uniquely labeled electron trajectories. The gauge-invariant collective projector evolves nontrivially; a physical position readout must respect this frame freedom. This does not replace the intended actual orbits by stationary orbitals: it identifies what the present carrier calculation can establish about them. The proven extension is shared-source collective precession with two electrons. The source has not yet generated the visualization's complete petal generator and position readout, for either one or two interacting electrons. No stability conclusion follows from existence or an unperturbed integration. Next is a gauge-consistent spatial many-electron readout and interaction, followed by perturbation tests and shell observables. Neither p/d/f capacities nor a helium spectrum has been derived here. The subsequent petal response residual makes the generator mismatch explicit: the prescribed demo lift varies s at three times the clock frequency, whereas every orientation-only V(s) conserves s. Full finite-source inverse tests also find nonzero residual bounds at the tested parameters. The existing selected map already produces the radial modulation from the prescribed lift; its source dynamics, not the algebraic readout formula, is the newly tested missing connection. It checks energy, source normalization, occupied orthogonality, projector rank, Slater normalization and exchange antisymmetry. Random preparations test reciprocity and occupied-frame invariance. Mutation testing exposed that conservation on a relative equilibrium alone does not detect a doubled energy coupling. This is an exploratory research record, not an independently established V2 result. Read the related later audits before using an intermediate conclusion. 45. Canonical free-pair operator from two electron complex structures To test whether a free electron pair can generate the locking map Q without importing a nucleus-selected 3+3 split, construct the most immediate pair operator from the two orthogonal complex structures,  oxed{ R_{12}=-J_1J_2. } Since J_i^T=-J_i, \qquad J_i^2=-I_6, one has R_{12}^TR_{12}=I_6, so R_{12}\in SO(6) for the explicit electron-sector realization. Using the diagonal-SU(4) canonical pair Z_1=e_1, \qquad Z_2=\cos	heta\,e_1+\sin	heta\,e_2, the exact gamma-matrix calculation gives  oxed{ R_{12}=I_2\oplus R(2	heta)\oplus R(-2	heta), } up to ordering of the real basis, where R(\varphi) is a real planar rotation. Equivalently,  oxed{ \operatorname{tr}R_{12}=2+4\cos(2	heta), } and the characteristic polynomial is  oxed{ \chi_{R_{12}}(\lambda) =(\lambda-1)^2 \left(\lambda^2-2\cos(2	heta)\lambda+1ight)^2. } Thus, for generic pair separation, the real six-dimensional representation has a canonical decomposition  oxed{ \mathbb R^6 =E_{m fix}^{(2)}\oplus E_{m rot}^{(4)}. } In a convenient canonical basis the four-dimensional rotating block can be displayed as two planar rotations R(2	heta)\oplus R(-2	heta), but that planar 2+2 refinement is not itself uniquely selected by the pair invariants. The invariant content is the fixed two-plane plus the active four-space. 45.1 Consequence for the free-pair locking problem This is a genuine pair-defined frame structure: it depends only on (J_1,J_2) and therefore requires no external nucleus or observer-selected 3+3 decomposition. However, it is not the previously used \mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3 split. The generic free pair naturally gives the invariant split  oxed{2+4,} not 3+3. A displayed 2+2+2 block form is basis-dependent inside the active four-space. Therefore the exact 3+3 Schur-lock model cannot yet be promoted to an SU(4)-invariant free-electron theorem merely by replacing the nucleus with the second electron. This is an important negative result: the pair geometry itself selects canonical planes, but their dimensions differ from the nucleus-relative decomposition. 45.2 Relation to the single pair invariant The spectrum of R_{12} is completely determined by the Fubini--Study separation 	heta, hence by

Instead it is whether the master interaction dynamically correlates the three pair-defined two-planes supplied by R_{12} in such a way that the observer's resolved three-dimensional motion becomes correlated with the unresolved directions. Its instantaneous marginal is \int \delta(x-X(t))\delta(y-Y(t))\,d^3y=\delta(x-X(t)). Unobserved-coordinate marginalization does not spread a point. Convolution with an apparatus response additionally assumes the relevant spatial response is translation invariant. title: Frequency-domain review
summary: Corrected frequency-domain conclusions and the remaining hadronic proof target.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Corrected frequency-domain conclusions and the remaining hadronic proof target. RESEARCH NOTES, NOT A PHYSICS MODULE. This is a record of calculations, corrections, and unresolved hypotheses. It does not assert a completed hadronic-mass derivation or a validated replacement for the V2 master dynamics. 1. Where the investigation stands The most useful progress was not another numerical factor close to a nucleon residual. Several earlier exclusions depended on confusing a static matrix, an observed projection, or an operator coefficient with a frequency generator. Those exclusions were narrowed or withdrawn after exact checks. Two later results had not yet been recorded in the inspected ledger. First, the point-contact construction and a smooth coherent-density construction have different spectra; the latter does not automatically replace or disprove the graph-supported prescription explicitly chosen in V2. Second, a rank-one source-to-scalar-self-energy response supplies a concrete sufficient mechanism for the common-anchor ratios without measuring or solving for the sources. The unresolved issue is whether that response applies to complete occupied reference frequencies or to coefficients before the simplex multiplier. The companion contact-kernel note and rank-one-response note contain those previously undocumented calculations. They are live possibilities and exact comparison tests, not a numerical baryon prediction. The last inspected hadronic ledger ends at Section 76. Its Sections 67--76 contain the earlier saved corrections. The returned execution report confirmed that write and its verification. Later read-only tests did not, by themselves, save the additional findings. This notes package preserves them separately rather than extending an exploratory ledger as though it were a finished module. 2. Observable and notation discipline The target is a rest-frequency ratio, ultimately z_B=\frac{\omega_B}{\omega_e}, \qquad \omega_e=\frac{m_ec^2}{\hbar}. Use \varpi_d=\mu_d/\hbar when \mu_d denotes the sector energy unit, and distinguish it from an oscillator frequency produced by a constriction model. On the hypothesized ordinary contact branch, \omega_{n,d}=\varpi_d S(n,d), \qquad S(n,d)=\binom{n+d-1}{d}. A specified occupied reference frequency is \omega_d^\star=\varpi_d S(n_d^\star,d), not generally \varpi_d. In particular, the depth-four reference has count 15, while the electron reference has count 18564. The pre-prism source-phase proposal \Omega_{n,d}=S(n,d)-1 is yet another object; its identification with time-dependent physical dynamics remains conditional in the contact-resonance source, Section 3. No independently calibrated field amplitude is an input to these notes. Arbitrary normalization of an eigenvector cannot move the eigenvalues of a fixed linear operator. However, replacing an unknown coefficient by an unknown frequency ratio does not determine it, and a nonlinear background dependence cannot be erased by renaming its variables. Genuine coefficients, projected kernels, kinetic metrics, and boundary conditions still need a derivation or a demonstrated cancellation. 3. Corrected static and spectral matrix results For the adopted test values G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a=8\sqrt7,\quad b=4\sqrt6,\quad c=12/\sqrt7, one has b^2=ac. The three quantities previously conflated are \underbrace{a-b^2/c}_{\text{actual static Schur complement}}=0, \qquad \underbrace{b^2/c}_{\text{removed relaxation contribution}}=a, \qquad \underbrace{a}_{\text{clamped principal block}}. The frequency-dependent matrix elimination instead uses f(z)=a-z-\frac{b^2}{c-z}, \qquad (c-z)f(z)=\det(G-zI)=z(z-a-c). This is exact away from the excluded complementary denominator. That excluded value must be checked in the original problem. The full matrix eigenvalues are 0 and a+c, not the removed static contribution considered in isolation. The operator square root also does not commute with projection. Here \sqrt G=\frac{G}{\sqrt{a+c}}, \qquad \frac{\langle3|\sqrt G|3\rangle}{\sqrt a}=\sqrt{14/17}, \qquad \frac{\sqrt{\langle3|G|3\rangle}}{\sqrt a}=1. The reference-band law (\omega_d^\star/\omega_e)^2=g_{dd}/g_{66} alone does not identify the full interacting frequency generator with \sqrt{G/g_{66}}. Consequently the earlier universal prohibition on a term linear in a dimensionless coupling was too strong. The particular matrix prescriptions were checked; a different operator map was not disproved. These corrections are already recorded in the hadronic ledger, Section 73. 4. Projection of a signal is not replacement of its generator For a time-independent linear map P and the same clock, P\bigl(u e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)=(Pu)e^{-i\omega t}. A nonzero projected line retains its frequency. A zero projection removes the line. This is different from physically imposing a new closed dynamics generated by PHP on a subspace that does not reduce H. The exact diagnostic used u=\begin{pmatrix}1/\sqrt6\\\sqrt{5/6}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad H=64uu^\dagger, \qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0). The compressed matrix has its observed entry 32/3, but the exact projected resolvent is P(z-H)^{-1}P =\left[\frac{1}{6(z-64)}+\frac{5}{6z}\right]P. The factor 1/6 is the residue at the unchanged frequency 64. The corresponding exact reduced generator is H_{\rm eff}(z)=\frac{32z}{3z-160}. This resolves the earlier color-projection error: the ordered rank-one contact gives 64/6 under compression, but that is not a universal frequency penalty. If color and orbital factors separate as I_{\rm color}\otimes A_{\rm mode}, singlet restriction leaves the allowed orbital eigenfrequencies unchanged. Likewise, annihilation of an identical color-vector product does not exclude a shared orbital mode with a separate antisymmetric color state. These results do not establish that 64 is a physical baryon eigenvalue. See ledger Section 74. 5. A genuine color coefficient, with its sign retained With fundamental generators normalized by \operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2, the directly constructed pair operator is C_{ij}=\sum_aT_i^aT_j^a =\frac12\left(X_{ij}-\frac13I\right). On the normalized determinant singlet \epsilon\in\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3, X_{ij}\epsilon=-\epsilon. Hence C_{ij}\epsilon=-\frac23\epsilon, \qquad \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\epsilon=-2\epsilon. All eight generators, their trace normalization, and all three pair operators were checked explicitly. For a derived interaction of the form \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\otimes K_{ij}(z), the singlet restriction is -(2/3)\sum_{i<j}K_{ij}(z). It becomes -2K(z) only when the remaining pair operators actually coincide. This is not a frequency prediction. The radial, spin, and normalization content of K_{ij} is still required. A numerical equality with the 2/3 in 28/9=(2/3)(g_{33}/g_{44}) does not identify the two constructions. The adopted sector couplings must not silently be equated with the coefficient of a gauge-current pair interaction. The source generator convention appears in the contact-resonance module, Section 14; the diagnostic is recorded in ledger Section 76. 6. What the earlier numerical searches actually tested These searches used preselected illustrative prescriptions, not a derived composite generator. Their failures therefore do not falsify all V2 hadronic constructions. For the committed quark contact counts D_u=15, D_d=1, D_s=20, raw constituent products give 225 for uud, 15 for udd, and 300 for uds. This shows why that unqualified product prescription is unsuitable as a common nucleon bulk contribution; it does not establish how physical composite frequencies combine. A separate carrier-size scan gave: Candidate carrier Dimension W^{\otimes3}, \dim W=4 64 \operatorname{Sym}^3W 20 \Lambda^3W 4 U^{\otimes3}, \dim U=3 27 \operatorname{Sym}^3U 10 \Lambda^3U 1 W^{\otimes2} 16 \operatorname{Sym}^2W 10 \Lambda^2W 6 The number 64\varpi_3 lay about 2.77 percent below the chosen approximately 309.5 MeV per-constituent residual when the conditional sector scale was used. That proximity does not choose a baryon carrier. Its previous suppression-based exclusion was withdrawn, not replaced by a derivation. Another scan tried S(n,6)/S(13,6) for 35\le n\le47. The values bracketing the selected residual ratio near 605.676 were approximately 578.408 at n=42 and 661.038 at n=43. No operator identification justified borrowing the electron-sector scale for a composite. Scalar S^5 harmonic degeneracies were also scanned; their initial values are 1,6,20,50,105,196. Degeneracy is not automatically a frequency. These are records of unsuccessful exploratory identifications, not universal spectral exclusions or statistical null tests. The approximately 309--310 MeV quantity itself was a residual allocated per constituent after subtracting chosen quark contributions. It is not, absent an additional decomposition theorem, a separately measured pole that a correct operator must contain. The primary target is the whole baryon rest frequency. 7. The constructive spectral target Three positions in a common observed three-space give six relative Jacobi coordinates after center-of-mass removal. A fixed Euclidean hyperradius has an S^5 angular surface. This is useful effective three-body kinematics, not proof that the baryon is the depth-six electron sector or the depth-five neutrino sector. Native higher-depth coordinates, spinor bundles, and eliminated channels must be accounted for. Ledger Section 75 records the corrected distinction. For a specified stationary generator \mathsf H in electron-frequency units and an orthogonal model-space projector P_B, let Q_B=I-P_B. Exact reduction gives \mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z)=P_B\mathsf HP_B+ P_B\mathsf HQ_B(z-Q_B\mathsf HQ_B)^{-1}Q_B\mathsf HP_B, and seeks \ker\left[z_BI_{P_B}-\mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z_B)\right]\ne\{0\}. The complementary inverse has a specified domain; at its excluded values the original problem is checked. This is an exact block identity for a given generator, not a derivation of the missing blocks. A covariant Dirac operator must first be related to a stationary time generator. An off-diagonal map P_3D_\infty P_4 has no standalone ordinary frequency spectrum without further structure. The common-anchor law remains conditional on deriving the projected reference response from the action. The composite blocks and their induced spectral terms are also unresolved; amplitude fits do not supply those derivations. 8. Scope of verification The packaged regression checks reproduce finite algebra, the illustrative resolvent, color contractions, moving-projector identities, smooth-symbol spectra, and the source-cancellation/count-normalization distinction. They are not Monte Carlo significance tests, a full variational derivation, or a proof of empirical agreement. The source audit covers the cited passages and reported bounded searches. An unsuccessful search is not a proof that no suitable formula exists. The packaged checks do not include extensive statistical null tests. 9. title: Independent correctness audit
summary: Independent recurrence refinement exposes false numerical acceptance, while scope corrections separate valid conditional geometry and conservation tests from physical identification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Independent recurrence refinement exposes false numerical acceptance, while scope corrections separate valid conditional geometry and conservation tests from physical identification. Verdict and scope Not everything was correct. There are valid conditional constructions and reproducible diagnostics, but the periodic-continuation acceptance and several physical-inference statements exceeded their evidence. This audit corrects those statements rather than counting earlier successful script exits as proof of the full theory. The audit inspected the core module statements and recent orbit, response, geometry, mass-operator, and conservation calculations. The initial sweep ran 57 existing diagnostic scripts, excluding the two expensive continuation searches, and all exited successfully. Independent checks then reintegrated saved continuation candidates and found the failure below. The mass-spectrum program also reproduces its stated fixed-index depth sequence. These are finite checks, not an end-to-end independent proof of every theorem in the historical archive. Earlier research notes not individually rederived remain historical records with their existing correction links. After the corrections, a fresh suite run completed 58 diagnostic scripts, including the new independent audit, with no failing exit status. The saved suite report contains every script's output, exit status, timing, interpreter version, and the two explicit continuation-search exclusions. The independent audit performed 84 checks and classified all three archived candidates as not accepted. The mass-spectrum program also passed its stated checks. These finite numerical checks are not mathematical proof. Corrections with explicit witnesses Periodic continuation was accepted at inadequate integration accuracy. The three archived candidates at h=0.0064,0.0096,0.0128 have refined closure errors 2.41423,7.43896,5.31450 times 10^{-6}, respectively, rather than the reported sub-10^{-6} values. Their Casimirs are correct. The optimizer's residual was not a reliable independent error estimate. See Cylindrical petal continuation for pinned states, numerical settings, and the withdrawn acceptance claim. The fully cylindrical centre had a removable implementation singularity. At h=1, the coefficient of the old Coulomb potential vanishes, but the implementation still evaluated that potential at q=0. The corrected code omits the discarded term and returns V(0)=-3/(2a) and zero central force. This fixes an endpoint evaluation; it does not remove the actual Coulomb singularity when h<1. Projection does not establish a smeared physical electron. The delta-distribution calculation and experimental distinction are in Electron detection and shape. An additional normalization mistake is corrected in Bound within, free without: a uniform probability density normalized in a fibre box of volume V gives an overlap proportional to 1/V, not an automatically volume-independent coupling. A cylindrical field and a normalized uniform wavefunction are different objects; the action must specify which is intended. A frozen-route ligand minimum is not full molecular stability. The positive ligand Hessians are meaningful for the specified frozen route, fixed centre, and fixed planes. The regular tetrahedral snapshot has nonzero transverse force in that energy and relaxes to a disphenoid. At nuclear radius 0.6, overlapping profiles are still assigned point-centre repulsion, so those entries are hybrid-model controls. See Cylindrical molecular shape stability. Configurable electron mass had inconsistent factors. The completed kinetic energy is |p-m_e\lambda Cs|^2/(2m_e). The reciprocal executable previously used the unit-mass factors even when m_e changed. Corrected velocity, force, and source equations now pass independent Hamiltonian-derivative and conservation checks at m_e=0.7,1,2.3, including nonaligned nuclear planes. The original unit-mass trajectory is unchanged. See Reciprocal cylindrical molecule. A classical angular source is not automatically the CP3 electron. The continued orbit occupies an invariant four-coordinate subspace of the six-coordinate model. Random-state checks verify the exact embedding of its h=0 field, including zero inactive derivatives, to roundoff. It therefore is not an independent dimension witness. This does not reassign the electron: depth six remains the working mass-formula input. Also, a generic skew C need not obey C^2=-c^2I_6, whereas an orthogonal complex structure representing CP3 does. A classical coadjoint source, a CP3 spatial point, and a spinor field are not identified merely because their symmetry groups are related. See Sector geometry premise audit. Several module summaries omitted necessary premises. Base-coordinate locality does not force a rank-one contact operator: band-compressed identity remains identity, whereas a specified point evaluation can be rank one. The occupied-ray and normalization assumptions are now explicit in the self-contact module. See Contact-kernel audit. A generation-blind charged-current vertex is identity in a common basis, but its mass-basis matrix is U_{u,L}^\dagger U_{d,L}; obtaining identity there additionally requires aligned left mass bases. The CKM module now says so. The coherent CPd submanifold is also distinguished from the full projectivization of the cumulative mode bundle. Energy preference and representation realization were overstated. A positive lock-energy coefficient is not dynamical capture: for H=V(s), \dot s=\{s,V(s)\}=0. A small observer-space motional magnetic estimate does not prove that additional curvature supplies the missing lock. Constructing a group action with the desired generator does not derive its physical electromagnetic current. The visualization prose now makes these distinctions without changing its petal rendering. The photon module also states that spatial polarization and normal propagation are premises of its orthogonality theorem, not consequences of dimensional counting alone. What survives and what comes next The exact representation algebra, specified analytic orbit constructions, fixed-source chart, and checked conservative equations remain useful. They are positive mathematical results for defined models. They are not a completed derivation of the physical electron, chemistry, or a unique CP3 geometry. Known unstable and rejected branches must remain in the record. The September 7 audit recommended correction and independent closure tests of the fixed-Casimir cylindrical candidates, followed by moving-nucleus recurrence and perturbation stability. This is a historical recommendation; the excerpt does not establish whether those tasks were subsequently completed. The active September 28 research target is the physical mass operator, its canonically normalized spatial source map and frequency selection. A common action and measurement law connecting spatial patterns, reciprocal response and detections remains necessary for physical identification. Neither chain can substitute for the other. Reproduction From the repository root (use a fresh report filename for a new run): OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/independent_audit_checks.py OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/reciprocal_cylindrical_molecule_checks.py OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/run_checks.py --skip-continuation --jobs 3 --report experiments/results/audit-2026-09-07/reproduction-suite.json python3 -B experiments/idwt-v2.py python3 -B scripts/validate-kb.py The independent script consumes archived states without re-fitting them and regenerates its report. Its successful diagnostic checks and the candidates' computed acceptance fields are separate: passing the audit does not mean the orbit candidates passed. Integration-failure negative controls reject failed, partial, and nonfinite trajectories. Full long-run continuation has not been rerun as part of this independent saved-state test.

title: Mass-operator controls at depths three and four

The full small frequency still has the previous finite-hopping correction: \omega_{N,d}= \frac{d!\binom{N+d}{d}}{\gamma^{d-1}\prod_l h_l} \left[1-\frac{(L-1)^2/h_0^2+(L+d-2)^2/h_{d-2}^2} {2\gamma^2}+O(\gamma^{-4})\right]. The actual lower-dimensional surface The normal calculation uses one ordinary plane at every winding. By itself, changing that winding would not test the full physical dimension. For odd m, construct the ambient Clifford matrices in m+1 directions and restrict their even products to one ambient chirality. Both choices of ambient chirality are checked; neither is assigned a particle charge or antiparticle meaning. Arbitrary complete spatial spinor jets verify B_K^2=\Delta_S+k^2, and a separate stereographic calculation with the actual spin connection agrees. On the unit circle, in one of the two equivalent ambient realizations, B_K=-i\partial_\theta,\qquad \mathscr D=B_K+\frac12. Here the specified bounding spin structure has antiperiodic spinors \psi=e^{i\theta/2}F, with periodic coefficient F. The modes F=e^{\pm iL\theta} have B_K eigenvalues \pm L. Both are retained for L\ge1. At L=0, B_K=0; a formula dividing by \beta must not be used there. All assigned depth-three controls have L\ge2. The depth-three link product is B_K(B_K^2-1). It is odd in B_K, so its two surface signs give opposite signed products. The complete canonical Hamiltonian H_P=\begin{pmatrix}0&T^\dagger\\T&0\end{pmatrix} reads positive frequency from a singular value and gives the same positive frequency on both branches. More generally, if R reverses the chain and J=\operatorname{diag}((-1)^l), reflection symmetry of the actual hoppings gives T(-\beta)=-JRT(\beta)^TRJ. Thus both signs have the same complete singular spectrum at finite hopping, including at odd depth. The signed product alone is not the physical frequency or an inertia sign. Complete partner phases and geometric response For diagonal links D_l=\beta+l-(d-1)/2, let u_l,v_l be the positive singular vectors obtained from the absolute scaled inverse. Their canonical phases must obey s_0=1,\qquad s_l=-\operatorname{sgn}(D_l)s_{l-1},\qquad t_l=\operatorname{sgn}(D_l)s_l. The positive-frequency state is (s_lu_l,t_lv_l)/\sqrt2. An alternating-sign formula is sufficient only when all D_l>0. The implementation now retains the correct partner phases on negative and mixed-sign controls. This correction leaves the previously tested positive-branch frequencies unchanged. The complete geometric source gives the constant-polynomial deformation response F_{N,d}=2\gamma\kappa_d \operatorname{Re}(v_0^*u_{d-1}), where \kappa_d is one spatial integral shared by all grades. Here \kappa_d denotes the endpoint integral, not the core binding coefficient. Thus the depth-three surface partners have opposite signed response, whereas the depth-four partners have the same signed response. Their positive mass-frequencies agree exactly. At normal orientation angle \vartheta, the derivatives with respect to the real and imaginary geometric coefficients are (F_{\mathrm{Re}},F_{\mathrm{Im}}) =F_{N,d}(0)(\cos(d\vartheta),\sin(d\vartheta)). The full reciprocal source verifies both components independently. Cross terms vanish by the actual circle integral. Equal weights cancel this particular response for every relative phase, while other spatial deformation channels remain. Such balance is a state choice here, not a derived occupation rule or a general absence of interactions. The same parity rule applies to other odd depths and cannot by itself single out neutrinos. The sign of a geometric force depends on orientation and polarization; it is not a sign of particle inertia. The full occupied support still has to respond to the complete spatial source. The bottom assignment adds a dynamical constraint A normal deformation constant over the circle commutes with the surface operator. It cannot mix the bottom components L=17 and L=18: \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} e^{-17i\theta}e^{18i\theta}\,d\theta=0. A first surface harmonic can access that channel, since the same integral with \cos\theta inserted is 1/2. Using the previously derived normal endpoint deformation and the actual two canonical states gives a nonzero first-harmonic matrix element, approximately -1647.10475 at \gamma=10^4. This identifies a spatially allowed channel, not a stationary occupied shape or a derived bottom mass. Ordinary mixing of the two positive branches is insufficient. For 0<a<b, retain their frequencies on the diagonal and add any Hermitian off-diagonal coupling: M=\begin{pmatrix}a&g\\\bar g&b\end{pmatrix}. At \lambda=\sqrt{ab}, \det(M-\lambda I) =-\sqrt{ab}(\sqrt b-\sqrt a)^2-|g|^2<0. Consequently \sqrt{ab} is never an eigenfrequency of this matrix. In fact no eigenvalue lies strictly between a and b. The two uncoupled frequencies also give an ordinary difference frequency, not their geometric mean. The maintained bottom count therefore requires a different coupled block, changed diagonal dynamics, or an explicitly derived relation between the two canonical quadratures. Merely inserting the target off-diagonal singular value would assume the missing result. The full signed parent and its same-field nonlinear response remain available to test; this exclusion concerns the stated two-positive-branch reduction. The full core limitation persists at the new depths The separate polarization core has the same radial rule at each physical depth: \frac{h(r)}{f(r)} =\frac{I_{d/2}((\kappa-m_c)r)} {I_{d/2-1}((\kappa-m_c)r)},\qquad \kappa>m_c>0. With m_c=1,\kappa=2, its dimensionless root mean squared radii are 1.73035154 at depth three and 2.22415436 at depth four. Within each depth, all listed single-grade controls have the same profile. Constructing its exact invariant tail block gives the same finite-wave-number Jordan chain at p_\perp=\sqrt3, with \|e^{tA}u\|/\|u\|=\sqrt{1+c_J^2t^2},\qquad c_J=\frac{2(q\omega^2+1)}{\sqrt{\omega^2+1}}. title: Research status
summary: Current mass and coupling research: spatial support, internal-motion inertia, conditional frequency selection, count scaling and reciprocal field evolution, with explicit assumptions and corrections.
text: Research Update: 4 October 2026 The expanded evidence for the sector structure brings together the mass comparisons and the reviewed spin, helicity, neutrality and nested lepton geometry. It includes the exact depth-six and depth-ten count polynomials for one specified projective connection and the available half-spin states in those spatial families. The same quadratic law leaves higher-spin states degenerate, so availability is not an energy-based selection of observed particles. The paper gives its numerical inputs, geometric assumptions, shared derivations and reproducible checks. Recent spatial work has also produced full-field solutions in a common saturated-current action at depths two, four, six and ten. Complete conserved stress gives the isolated boost inertia E/c^2. These are particle-construction results within that action, rather than independent evidence selecting those depths. The tested stability windows do not establish unrestricted stability, and no observed particle or complete mass-frequency selection law has been identified. Independent-clock pair preparations retain the two isolated resonance frequencies; short projected evolution does not yet establish a persistent interaction or a measured coupling. The dated entries below describe their own actions and assumptions. Their favorable results require a checked common-action construction before they can be combined. The physical mass operator, occupation rule and common polarization-sensitive interaction remain open. Research Update: 28 September 2026 The latest work develops localized wave support, complete inertia and reciprocal contact alongside the earlier spatial simplex operator. These are conditional candidate actions. A physical mass operator, a selected particle spectrum and a common cross-depth coupling law remain open. Counting, frequency selection and internal-motion inertia derives Pascal phase weights, supported profile identities and the complete boost response. Conditional phase-action quantization supplies discrete roots, with restrictions from spatial depth and stability. A scale-covariant action for count scaling and shared contact gives exact complete-energy scaling under one coefficient rule. A projected source supplies an analytic exterior stability bound; a shared density square supplies both self-contact and reciprocal pair contact. Reciprocal contact with deforming spatial patterns evolves the two-grade field equations at depths three and five. Contact changes through deformation while momentum is exchanged reciprocally, with mesh, timestep and domain controls. The count family in those graph calculations is 3,10,35,126,\ldots; it is not the full maintained particle assignment spectrum. The graph's physical spatial origin, photon polarization, cross-depth contact and absolute frequency selection remain unresolved. Its amended action has promising isolated-state controls, but finite-volume occupied spectra are not a nonlinear stability theorem. The recent standing spatial support, current support ledger and canonical contact bounds qualify earlier surface and current constructions. Results below retain their stated action and date; a later repair does not retroactively validate a different earlier action. Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Spatial mass operators, polarized reciprocal coupling and the sustaining-source and inertia requirements, with correction routes through the earlier localized actions. Spatial mass operator and source: 14 September 2026 The current spatial investigation has a complete finite normal Dirac kernel and a positive gap to every other normal mode. Under its stated winding and surface assumptions, the projected frequency approaches the assigned simplex product with one coefficient per depth. The carrier calculation retains the full normal spectrum; its coefficient texture and physical source remain inverse inputs. The complete polarized pair keeps mixed currents, actual surface overlaps and reciprocal separation forces. A defined common probe gives a muon/electron response ratio about 1.11 while their frequency ratio is about 207. This is a conditional example of different frequencies with comparable responses. It is not an observed coupling, a photon identification or a neutrino suppression mechanism. The normal stress audit gives, at unit canonical norm, M^{\mathrm{wave}}_{ij}=\omega\delta_{ij}+T_{ij}. One directional response is negative in the tested simplex regime. Independent spatial-force integrals and the exact contracted boost confirm the stress contribution. This is the partial wave response in a prescribed background. The supporting field must contribute its own energy, momentum and stress before this is a complete particle calculation. Mass remains the selected frequency in equivalent units. The shape-source constraints show that a common restoring energy and scalar norm adjustment alone cannot support both assigned branches at the same reference texture in the tested separable completion. A joint same-field source changes those equations and remains the next physical requirement. The scale audit also keeps the normal hopping and ordinary cavity radius in the frequency conversion. The earlier localized-current construction below has a different conditional inertia result. Its retained spatial frame now repairs a particular polarized principal defect, but this extension has not been combined with the new normal carrier into one physical mass operator. Localized mass and coupling: 13 September 2026 The earlier reconstructed current action has actual localized spatial solutions under its stated inverse premises. Its frequency and inertia calculation gives \omega_N=\omega_{0,d}\sum_{k=0}^{N}\binom{k+d-1}{d-1} =\omega_{0,d}\binom{N+d}{d},\qquad E_0=\hbar\omega_NQ,\qquad M_{ab}=\frac{\hbar\omega_NQ}{c^2}\delta_{ab}. Here N is the occupied coefficient grade and Q the canonical field norm. The depth-six electron and muon retain N=12 and N=34. Their continuously oscillating solutions share one spatial core and, under the common Q=1 condition, have the corresponding mass-frequency inertia. Field magnitude enters the spatial fixed-point equation; it is not used as a separate mass variable. These are exact results of an inverse action. The shell weights, its physical spatial mode carrier, and the common norm have not been selected by the master field. The common-gap core calculation also gives an explicit radius law L_{\mathrm{rms},d}=\gamma_d c/m_c, with a dimension-dependent factor \gamma_d determined by that binding law. Equating its core frequency m_c with \omega_{0,d} remains an additional inverse identification. Different masses with a common initial coupling response The same action gives identical lower-grade probe energies and complete probe sources for different larger target grades at the same depth and common profile. The calculation retains both polarizations and reciprocal initial forces. Two independently solved cores realize that identity, while the target's full deformation can still depend on its grade. Their binding currents can cancel even when each isolated core is regular; a smooth binding comparison removes this specific fractional-current singularity without changing the frequency hierarchy. These are initial same-depth pair results. A complete encounter, cross-depth vertices and the observed photon and neutrino coupling pattern have not yet been derived. What the stability calculations establish A trace contribution to the mass current preserves the same core, frequency and inertia: F_q(R)^2=qr\operatorname{Tr}(R^2) +(1-q)[\operatorname{Tr}R]^2,\qquad 0<q\leq1. Here r is a component rank, not a spatial dimension. The original norm has q=1. It has a nilpotent high-momentum compression with secular amplification despite real limiting frequencies. For 0<q<1 and a nonzero gap, the complete constant far-field linearization instead admits a positive conserved perturbation norm and a bound uniform in time and momentum. Equal trace and exchange contractions give the explicit comparison q=1/(r+1), hence 1/9 at depth six; this contraction is an inverse choice rather than a uniquely derived interaction. The higher angular response classifies the even-depth matrix angular blocks and checks 200 finite electron and muon spectra across two radial refinements and both current norms. No exponentially growing mode is resolved within those ranges. This is not a theorem for all radial wavelengths, all angular labels, or nonlinear disturbances of the spatially varying core. Separately, the field-carried spatial frame has defective principal blocks for complex polarized rays. Changing the mass potential does not repair that kinetic issue. How this connects to the preceding calculations The moving-cavity inertia control and common-size balance isolate the kinetic and sustaining-stress requirements. title: Sector geometry premise audit
summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification. Current physical hypotheses All sectors are nested submanifolds of the one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. This is the current IDWT hypothesis. Every sector direction is macroscopic and spatial. In particular, CP3 denotes the electron's six-dimensional physical submanifold, not an internal state space. Three are shared with us, but that makes none of the six different in kind. Similarly, the electron's six dimensions are six of the tau's ten; the electron is lower-dimensional, or “flat,” relative to the tau. Neither comparison gives the containing particle an inherent physical split. The three-dimensional nuclear sector is the proposed basis of ordinary matter's three-dimensional experience. A particular observer-adapted frame calculation does not establish that general claim. The earlier attribution of three-dimensional experience to nuclear 3+3 locking is withdrawn. Under these hypotheses, a candidate construction must supply the stated spatial nesting. A proposed revision of a scientific premise must be named explicitly and tested for mathematical consistency and agreement with observations. Silently relabeling physical directions as internal coordinates does not supply an embedding. The audit below tests the specified geometry; its obstructions retain that scope when alternative premises are explored. Nesting is a geometric requirement The named candidate list in the polarization module does not establish its required smooth inclusions. There is a concrete obstruction in that list. Suppose an embedding of CP2 into S5 existed. Both are oriented, so its real normal line would be trivial. Restricting the sphere tangent bundle would give i^*TS^5=T\mathbb{CP}^2\oplus\mathbf1. The sphere tangent bundle is stably trivial, hence its second Stiefel–Whitney class vanishes. The Whitney sum formula would then require the same for the CP2 tangent bundle. This contradiction rules out that smooth nesting of the proposed CP2 and S5 assignments. The characteristic-class tools are given in Ralph Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles, chapter 3. Within that ansatz, retaining phase gives S(2r−1), and quotienting it gives CP(r−1). The dimension arithmetic is valid. Globally, the same argument uses a fibre bundle projection \pi_{ba}:\Xi_b\longrightarrow\Xi_a. A depth-a mode has a normalizable bound factor \chi_a(x) on its own sector. Its continuation to depth b is the cylindrical pullback (\pi_{ba}^{*}\chi_a)(x,y)=\chi_a(x). Therefore \partial_{y^j}(\pi_{ba}^{*}\chi_a)=0 \qquad (j=1,\ldots,b-a). The lower-depth particle has no profile that must be aimed at a point of the extra fibre. It spans that fibre because nothing in its spatial mode distinguishes one fibre point from another. The same state is compatible with, but not forced by, a free outer Hamiltonian. In a direction with no binding potential, H_{\mathrm{free}} =- rac{\hbar^2}{2\mu}\partial_y^2. Its generalized momentum eigenfunctions e^{iky} have uniform magnitude. The zero-momentum member is constant; a nonzero-momentum member has changing phase but still no localized body being carried along the coordinate. A finite wavepacket may have a localized envelope, but it is then a superposition of outer momenta. Thus the translation eigenmode gives the spatial “already-there” sector state, while outer localization represents additional dynamical preparation.
